postings.text: "Impact Evaluation of an IFC / GAFSP PrSW Project in Pakistan: Baseline and Follow-up Survey " --> --> Working for a World Free of Poverty Who We Are Corporate Procurement Business Opportunities "Impact Evaluation of an IFC / GAFSP PrSW Project in Pakistan: Baseline and Follow-up Survey " SOLICITATION NUMBER:  0002024426 INSTITUTION:   IFC ASSIGNMENT LOCATION:  Pakistan ISSUE DATE AND TIME:  Nov 10,2026 13:20 CLOSING DATE AND TIME:  Nov 23,2026 23:59 These Terms of Reference (ToR) cover two complementary components: 1.Impact evaluation research: Evaluate the impact of IFC-supported financial inclusion interventions implemented through HBL Microfinance Bank; including expanded access to credit for agricultural borrowers; women entrepreneurs; microenterprises; and smallholder farmers. 2.Job quality measurement study: With support from the Jobs MDTF; develop and test innovative approaches to measuring monetary and non-monetary dimensions of job quality in informal and semi-formal employment; particularly among self-employed workers; entrepreneurs; and agricultural households. postings.title: Monitoring and Evaluation Officer (Anticipatory Action), SC9 WFP - World Food Programme Nairobi SB-4 (SC8/SC9), Service Contract, Local Contractors Agreement - Consultancy
postings.text: Monitoring and Evaluation Officer (Anticipatory Action), SC9 | WFP - World Food Programme Skip to main content Monitoring and Evaluation Officer (Anticipatory Action), SC9 WFP - World Food Programme Nairobi National SB-4 (SC8/SC9), Service Contract, Local Contractors Agreement level Speaks English, French, Portuguese Application deadline: November 30, 2026 (14 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Monitoring and Evaluation Officer at WFP will provide technical support and oversight for monitoring and learning activities across Country Offices in Eastern and Southern Africa. This role involves designing, implementing, and overseeing monitoring and evaluation frameworks for various programs, ensuring quality evidence generation to inform program design and decision-making. The officer will collaborate with program teams and contribute to building M&E capacity among staff and partners. The position requires a strong background in M&E, data analysis, and experience in humanitarian or development contexts. Candidate Requirements: Minimum three years of relevant work experience in M&E Advanced degree in social sciences, statistics, or related fields Fluency in English; knowledge of French/Portuguese is a plus Experience in quantitative and qualitative data analysis Knowledge of Anticipatory Action approaches Experience in capacity strengthening of partners Proven skills in developing monitoring frameworks DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS 30 November 2026-23:59-GMT+03:00 East Africa Time (Nairobi) WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability. ABOUT WFP The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks. At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves. To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org  and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube , LinkedIn , Instagram , Facebook , Twitter , TikTok . WHY JOIN WFP?   WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate. WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment. WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities. A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe. We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement). Position Title: Monitoring and Evaluation Officer Grade: SC9 Duty Station: WFP ESARO, Nairobi, Kenya Unit: Programme Monitoring and Reporting Type of Contract: Service Contract ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT : The position is based within the outposted Global HQ (GHQ) Monitoring Team in the WFP Eastern and Southern Africa Regional Office (ESARO). Reporting to the Regional Monitoring Officer, the incumbent provides technical support and oversight for monitoring and learning activities across Country Offices (COs), working closely with the Programme Team – particularly the Resilience, Anticipatory Action (AA) and School Feeding teams – and CO M&E focal points to strengthen evidence generation, reporting and learning on AA, integrated resilience, and home-grown school feeding (HGSF) programming across ESARO. JOB PURPO SE: Support the design, implementation and oversight of monitoring and learning activities for AA, integrated resilience, and HGSF programmes across Eastern and Southern Africa, ensuring the generation of quality evidence to inform programme design, implementation, learning, advocacy and corporate reporting. The role provides technical support to COs and contributes to monitoring, reviews, and other evidence-generation initiatives in line with WFP corporate standards. The position will specifically support regional projects, such as the Building Climate Resilience for Food Security in the Fragile Setting of the Horn of Africa and Transforming Local Food Systems through Home-Grown School Meals in Eastern Africa (THRIVE) initiatives. KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority): Monitoring and Evaluation 1. Provide inputs to the development of Monitoring, Review and Evaluation plans that will provide the most relevant and strategic information toward achieving expected results (as set out in the Country Strategic Plan (CSP) and other global and regional plans), while being compliant with WFP evaluation and monitoring requirements. 2. Budget for M&E costs and advocate through line manager for both appropriate financial and human resourcing. 3. Provide feedback on the formulation of the Regional Monitoring and Evaluation Strategies and support their operationalization. 4. Contribute to evidence-based decision-making on programme design and implementation, notably through making monitoring, review and evaluations findings accessible, developing innovative, user-friendly and informative products. 5. Support WFP Management in addressing recommendations from monitoring, reviews and evaluations to ensure that follow-up actions are taken as required. 6. Contribute to building M&E capacity of WFP staff and partners through training and information sharing. Manage junior staff members and guide as required to enable high performance. 7. Provide inputs to line manager regarding the development and implementation of national government and inter-agency monitoring, reporting and evaluation frameworks, including United Nations Development Assistance Framework (UNDAF) aligned with nationally owned sustainable development goals. 8. Take responsibility for integrating protection and gender perspectives in all areas of work, to ensure equal participation of women and men. Specific to the monitoring function 9. At Country Strategic Plan (CSP) design stage, support the Head of M&E or Head of Programme in developing a Theory of Change outlining how the expected results are likely to occur and listing key assumptions and risks. 10. Support line manager in ensuring that CO monitoring systems and tools are in place and compliant with corporate standards including the minimum monitoring requirements (MMR), standard operational procedures (SOP) and establishment of baselines and targets in alignment with the updated corporate results framework (CRF). 11. Draft regular monitoring reports on status of results and implementation progress and contribute to the data analysis. 12. Support mid-term reviews and thematic reviews which are intended for internal learning, strategic and operational decision-making. OTHER SPECIFIC ACCOUNTABILITIES: 13. Ensure compliance of integrated resilience, home –grown school feeding and AA monitoring systems with corporate standards, including CRF requirements, SOPs, monitoring guidance, and data protection and privacy policies. 14. Support COs in the design and implementation of integrated resilience, home-grown school feeding and AA Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) frameworks, including MEL plans, logframes, indicators and evidence-generation strategies. For AA, this will involve support to COs to develop or revise MEL plans captured in the Anticipatory Action Plans (AAPs) and guiding them on implementing M&E plans during activations. 15. Coordinate and provide technical guidance on quantitative and qualitative data collection, analysis and reporting activities, including monitoring, assessments, surveys and evaluations. For THRIVE, this will also involve strengthening the use of qualitative data to assess results across programme components and capture outcomes not fully reflected in quantitative indicators. 16. Work closely with Programme teams to develop and maintain a THRIVE performance dashboard, integrating country- and regional-level monitoring data and using effective data visualisation to track implementation progress, results and key programme trends and support timely management decision-making. 17. Support the development and implementation of context-appropriate monitoring approaches, including remote and third-party monitoring arrangements where required. 18. Strengthen linkages between programme monitoring data and research and evaluation activities, including through the THRIVE research component, by aligning monitoring indicators with relevant research questions, facilitating the triangulation and joint analysis of monitoring and research data, and ensuring that evidence generated through both streams informs programme adaptation, learning and decision-making. 19. Lead the synthesis, reporting and dissemination of integrated resilience, home-grown school meals and AA evidence and learning products, ensuring findings inform programme design, policy development, resource mobilisation and decision-making. 20. Facilitate regular review of monitoring findings with WFP and partner stakeholders and support the follow-up of agreed actions and recommendations. 21. Support COs in customising monitoring plans to prepare for AA activations, including the development of tools, systems and reporting mechanisms. 22. Strengthen monitoring and evaluation capacities of WFP staff, cooperating partners and government counterparts through training, coaching and knowledge sharing. 23. Identify opportunities to improve monitoring systems, methodologies and field processes to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of Anticipatory Action interventions. 24. Other duties as required. DESIRED EXPERIENCES FOR ENTRY INTO THE ROLE: • Previous experience in humanitarian or development contexts. • Proven knowledge and skills in M&E, including analytical skills and experience in developing and implementing Monitoring frameworks and analysing and compiling M&E data for management decisions, programme adjustments, and donor reporting. • Experience in quantitative and qualitative data analysis, including the synthesis and interpretation of evidence to assess programme results and inform learning. • Knowledge of Anticipatory Action (AA) approaches and frameworks, as well as the broader disaster risk management workstream in food security and nutrition. • Experience in data visualisation and the development of dashboards or other tools to support programme monitoring, analysis and decision-making. • Experience in capacity strengthening, including of government counterparts and in-country partners. STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Experience : Minimum of three years of relevant professional work experience including monitoring and evaluation activities. Experience using a variety of quantitative and qualitative analytical tools and methods. Education : Advanced University degree in social sciences, statistics, development economics, performance management, monitoring and evaluation or other related fields, or First University degree with additional years of relevant work experience and/or training/courses. Language : Fluency (level C) in English language. Knowledge of French and/or Portuguese is an asset. WFP LEADERS

postings.title: Senior MEAL Associate IOM - International Organization for Migration Ankara GS-6, General Service - No need for Higher Education - Locally recruited position - Administrative support
postings.text: Senior MEAL Associate | IOM - International Organization for Migration Skip to main content Senior MEAL Associate IOM - International Organization for Migration Ankara National GS-6, General Service - No need for Higher Education - Locally recruited position level Speaks English, Turkish Application deadline: November 30, 2026 (14 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The G-6 Senior MEAL Associate will coordinate field monitoring visits and oversee data collection and analysis to ensure quality monitoring and evaluation practices. This role involves capacity building for enumerators and implementing partners, drafting reports, and supporting accountability mechanisms. The associate will also participate in proposal development and facilitate the integration of humanitarian standards in MEAL functions. The position requires strong analytical skills and the ability to train others in MEAL systems. Candidate Requirements: University degree in Social Science, Statistics, or Development Studies Four years of relevant professional experience or six years with a High School degree Advanced skills in Excel, PowerPoint, SPSS, kobotoolbox, ODK, Power BI Experience with international humanitarian organizations Knowledge of monitoring and evaluation principles Strong analytical and report writing skills Fluency in English and Turkish Ability to train others and facilitate meetings Willingness to travel up to 70% of the time Job Description Applications are welcome from internal candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal candidates are considered first-tier candidates.   Context Under the direct supervision of the Senior National MEAL Officer, the incumbent will be responsible for coordinating field monitoring visits, quantitative and qualitative data collection, enumerator and implementing partners capacity building, monitoring data quality assurance, participating in quantitative and qualitative data analysis, drafting M&E reports, supervising MEAL Assistants and enumerators, supporting development and implementation of context-appropriate accountability to affected populations mechanisms, supporting utilization of monitoring and evaluation findings and participating in proposal development sessions. Responsibilities 1.Support preparation of project proposals and concept papers, paying attention to SMART indicators, realistic MEAL budgets, MEAL Plans, and evidence-based project designs. 2.Ensure all approved projects have a standard log frame, M&E plan with defined indicators, Results Monitoring Framework, Indicator tracking table (ITT), field-level data collection tools in line with donor requirements. 3.Ensure direct implementations and risks are monitored regularly in line with MEAL standards and humanitarian standards through schedule visits, data quality assurance, spot check/verification visits against reports, and reports reviews (as per agreed schedule with donors, project managers, and MEAL Plan). 4.Update all MEAL system standard documents and data on a monthly basis. 5.Consolidate, analyze and draft quantitative and qualitative MEAL reports in line with MEAL plans, highlighting project outcomes and impact. 6.Support in the facilitation of integration of IASC principles, cross-cutting issues (gender, protection), and core humanitarian standards in MEAL functions. 7.Support Senior National MEAL Officer in sharing learning and tools with other agencies and use the experience of other agencies to improve IOM Türkiye MEAL practices and participate in inter-agency MEAL coordination meetings  8.In coordination with the Senior National MEAL Officer, guide and build capacity of supervised MEAL staff (CFAs, MEAL Assistants & enumerators) in order to facilitate delivering ofhigh-quality outputs especially during assessments, PDMs, FGDs, KIIs. 9.Train and provide technical guidance to project partners on project MEAL systems and provide ongoing routine coaching and mentorship of partners MEAL staff. 10.Support Senior National MEAL Officer in developing/adapting contextually appropriate accountability tools and systems to enable response staff to better include communities in program planning, implementation, and monitoring. 11.Support in the process of information sharing, Consultation, Participation & Complaints and response of affected people is being conducted by MEAL and Community feedback assistants. 12.When end line evaluations are run by external parties, support drafting ToR according to IOM quality standards and donor requirements. 13.Ensure all M&E data, reports, and records are clearly organized archived in a central location for future reference. 14.Support in documentation to share M&E findings with relevant stakeholders and provide timely and updated data to be used in discussions in appropriate forums. Follow up on the utilization of the Monitoring results stated in the “Monitoring Utilization matrix. 15.Ensure an end-line measurement of the outcome level indicators is conducted to understand the change IOM projects contributed to and results are documented, and management response collected for all internal and external evaluations. 16.Participate in project review and learning events for direct & partner implemented projects before the closure of the project in order to document learnings and best practice for future programs. 17.Perform such other duties as may be assigned. Qualifications Education University degree in Social Science, Statistics or Development Studies or a related field from an accredited academic institution with four years of relevant professional experience; or Completed High School degree from an accredited academic institution with six years of relevant professional experience. Accredited Universities are those listed in the  UNESCO World Higher Education Database . Experience  Computer/software literate, preferably advanced skills in Excel, PowerPoint, SPSS, kobotoolbox, ODK, Power BI, and report writing Experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-governmental or governmental institutions/organizations in a multi-cultural setting; Knowledge of principles and current approaches to monitoring and evaluation to emergency conflict contexts using quantitative and qualitative methodologies Strong knowledge of monitoring and evaluation tools and methodologies and excellent analytical and report writing skills. Communicates with integrity to different stakeholders (strong interpersonal skills). Experience in data processing or analysis (Excel, etc.) is required Ability to train others on MEAL and effectively facilitate meetings is required. Proven strong organizational skills and practical experience of how to multi-task, prioritize, and work independently. Willingness to travel up to 70% of the time. Languages Fluency in English and Turkish is required IOM’s official languages are English, French and Spanish. Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at  this link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these three values: Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies – behavioural indicators (Level 2) Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators (Level 2) (applicable only if position is with direct reports) Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential. Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty. Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction. Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings. Notes Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This post is subject to local recruitment. Only those holding a valid residence and work permit for the country where this position is based will be eligible for consideration. IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts. postings.title: RESEARCH TEAM LEADER M&E UNIRMCT - United Nations International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals Nairobi BG09
postings.text: RESEARCH TEAM LEADER M&E | UNIRMCT - United Nations International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals Skip to main content RESEARCH TEAM LEADER M&E UNIRMCT - United Nations International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals Nairobi BG09 level Speaks English, French Application deadline: November 20, 2026 Closing soon Apply Summary by Impactpool The Research Team Leader for Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) at IITA Kenya will provide technical and coordination support for the TAAT Programme's M&E functions. This role involves designing, implementing, and managing M&E systems to track and report on programme performance across multiple countries and partners. The leader will ensure data quality, facilitate evidence-based learning, and support the preparation of analytical reports and dashboards. The position requires strong expertise in M&E methodologies, data management, and stakeholder engagement. Candidate Requirements: Master’s degree in relevant field 8+ years in agricultural research coordination 10+ years in M&E and data analysis Experience with multi-country projects Strong data management and analytical skills Proficiency in digital data collection tools Technical writing and reporting experience Capacity strengthening experience Ability to work in multicultural teams Excellent English communication skills Job Description RESEARCH TEAM LEADER- M&E IITA KENYA THE ORGANIZATION The Alliance of Bioversity International delivers research-based solutions that harness agricultural biodiversity and sustainably transform food systems to improve people’s lives. Alliance solutions address the global crises of malnutrition, climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental degradation. The Alliance works with local, national and multinational partners across Latin America and the Caribbean, Asia and Africa, and with the public and private sectors. The Alliance is part of CGIAR, a global research partnership for a food-secure future, dedicated to reducing poverty, enhancing food and nutrition security, and improving natural resources and ecosystem services. THE INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTE OF TROPICAL AGRICULTURE (IITA) The International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA) is a not-for-profit institution that generates agricultural innovations to meet Africa’s most pressing challenges of hunger, malnutrition, poverty, and natural resource degradation. Working with various partners across sub-Saharan Africa, we improve livelihoods, enhance food and nutrition security, increase employment, and preserve natural resource integrity. IITA is a member of CGIAR, a global agriculture research partnership for a food secure future. Please visit http://www.iita.org/ for more information on IITA. ABOUT THE POSITION The Research Team Leader- M&E role is established to provide hands-on technical and coordination support for the monitoring, evaluation, learning, and performance management functions of the Technologies for African Agricultural Transformation (TAAT) Programme. The Research Team Leader will support the design, implementation, coordination, tracking, analysis, and reporting of TAAT results, ensuring that programme activities, outputs, outcomes, and impacts are systematically measured and documented in line with the TAAT results framework and reporting requirements. Given the breadth, complexity, and multi-country nature of the TAAT portfolio, the role combines strong expertise in monitoring and evaluation, data management and analysis, results measurement, and performance reporting with effective programme coordination and stakeholder engagement. The role will work closely with the TAAT Programme Management Unit, Compacts, country teams, implementing partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen the quality, timeliness, and use of programme data; track progress against targets and key performance indicators; identify implementation gaps and emerging risks; and facilitate evidence-based learning and adaptive management. The role will contribute to ensuring that TAAT has credible, timely, and actionable evidence on programme performance, including the adoption and scaling of agricultural technologies, beneficiary reach, productivity and production outcomes, employment and livelihood effects, gender and youth results, and other programme-level indicators. The post holder will also support the preparation of high-quality M&E products, dashboards, analytical reports, performance updates, and donor reports, helping ensure coherence, accountability, and evidence-based decision-making across the TAAT portfolio. MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE: STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS AND PROGRAMME COORDINATION The position will work across a complex, multi-country and multi-partner portfolio, requiring close coordination with the TAAT Programme Management Unit, TAAT Compacts, implementing CGIAR Centers and non-CGIAR international agricultural institutions, the TAAT Clearinghouse, National Agricultural Research and Extension institutions, government agencies, private-sector partners, and other implementing partners. The Research Team Leader - M&E will help ensure that reliable and timely evidence on programme implementation, outputs, outcomes, and impacts is generated, quality-assured, analyzed, and effectively used for programme management and decision-making. The role will: Lead the translation of TAAT results frameworks into actionable M&E plan and elaborate Performance Indicator Reference Sheets (PIRS) including indicator definitions, data sources, collection methods, reporting schedules, responsibilities, milestones, and verification requirements. Contribute to the implementation of TAAT's M&E system, applying appropriate M&E approaches, tools, methodologies, and digital data systems aligned with the TAAT Results Framework. Track programme performance across all TAAT Compacts and countries, monitoring progress against set baselines, targets, and milestones for the programme’s indicators. Coordinate the collection, compilation, validation, analysis, and reporting of data, ensuring that data submitted by Compacts and implementing partners are complete, accurate, consistent, timely, and adequately supported by evidence. Provide technical guidance on data quality assurance and verification processes, including consistency checks, field-level verification, and other appropriate data quality assessment mechanisms to strengthen the credibility and reliability of reported results. Maintain and continuously update TAAT performance tracking systems, databases, dashboards, and other M&E tools for real-time visibility of implementation progress. Prepare periodic performance reports on TAAT outputs and outcomes indicators and submit them within stipulated donor and programme timelines. Provide technical guidance to Compacts and implementing partners on M&E methodologies and tools, including indicator measurement, data collection, digital data management, sampling, surveys, outcome monitoring, technology adoption measurement, beneficiary tracking, and results reporting. Support the design and implementation of outcome case studies, impact assessments, and other M&E studies as required to generate credible evidence of TAAT's contribution to agricultural transformation. Contribute to programme reviews, learning events, supervision missions, and performance discussions, providing evidence and analytical insights to inform management decisions and adaptive implementation. Lead capacity strengthening of Compact and partner M&E teams, including development and use of M&E tools, indicator guidance, data collection protocols, reporting templates, data quality procedures, and results. Contribute to the coordinatiom of M&E activities of TAAT addendums and country engagement initiatives to ensure their alignment to TAAT’s Result Framework. M&E LEADERSHIP AND PROGRAMME COORDINATION The M&E Lead will serve as a key coordination and technical focal point for monitoring, evaluation, learning, and results measurement across the TAAT programme. The role will facilitate effective engagement and information flow between the TAAT Programme Management Unit, Compacts, country teams, implementing partners, technical institutions, the TAAT Clearinghouse, national stakeholders, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure timely generation, validation, use, and reporting of programme results. The role will: Coordinate routine M&E engagement across TAAT Compacts and participating countries, ensuring that M&E requirements, reporting schedules, indicators, targets, and evidence requirements are clearly understood and consistently applied. Lead the flow of M&E information between implementing partners, Compacts, the TAAT PMU, the TAAT Clearinghouse, and other relevant stakeholders. Provide technical guidance and constructive feedback to implementing teams and partners on indicator measurement, data collection, reporting formats, evidence requirements, and compliance with the TAAT Results Framework. Support coordination with the TAAT Clearinghouse and relevant technical partners on the tracking and verification of technology dissemination, adoption, scaling, beneficiary reach, and other key TAAT results. Contribute to cross-Compact learning and knowledge exchange, facilitating sharing of M&E approaches, lessons, good practices, and innovative tools across compact teams and countries. PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND PERFORMANCE MONITORING The M&E Lead will deliver timely, credible, and actionable monitoring, evaluation, and performance information to support effective implementation, accountability, learning, and evidence-based decision-making across the TAAT programme. The role will: Lead the consolidation and synthesis of routine M&E updates from TAAT Compacts, countries, and implementing partners, ensuring that progress against indicators, targets, milestones, and deliverables is accurately captured. Prepare and maintain programme performance dashboards, trackers, databases, and analytical tools that provide up-to-date information on TAAT implementation and results. Ensure the completeness, accuracy, consistency, and quality of reported results through systematic data validation, quality assurance, verification, and follow-up with Compacts and implementing partners. Lead the preparation of annual, quarterly, and other periodic reports, ensuring that results across all Compacts and countries are accurately consolidated. Document and synthesize lessons, good practices, innovations, and emerging evidence from programme implementation to support learning, knowledge management, and adaptive management. Provide timely M&E inputs for programme reviews, supervision missions, management meetings, donor engagements, and strategic planning processes. Maintain an organized and auditable repository of M&E data, reports, tools, supporting documentation, and evidence, ensuring that programme results can be readily verified and traced to their sources. REQUIREMENTS: Education and Experience A Master’s degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Agricultural Economics, Development Studies, Statistics, Data Science, Agricultural Sciences, Social Sciences, or a related field from a recognized university.At least eight years of progressively responsible experience coordinating agricultural research for development, extension, agribusiness, digital agriculture, innovation scaling, or related programs. At least 10 years of professional experience in monitoring, evaluation, learning, results measurement, performance management, data analysis, or related fields, preferably within agricultural development or international development programmes. Demonstrated experience in designing, implementing, and strengthening M&E systems and Results Measurement Frameworks. Proven experience in coordinating M&E functions for complex, multi-country and multi-partner projects or portfolios, involving multiple implementing institutions and diverse stakeholders. Strong expe

postings.title: MEAL Officer - Accountability IRC - International Rescue Committee Bangladesh Mid - Mid level
postings.text: MEAL Officer - Accountability | IRC - International Rescue Committee Skip to main content MEAL Officer - Accountability IRC - International Rescue Committee Bangladesh International Mid level Speaks Bengali, English Application deadline: September 30, 2027 (11 months) Apply Summary by Impactpool The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is seeking a MEAL Officer - Accountability to oversee the Client Feedback and Response Mechanism (CFRM) in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh. This role involves managing client feedback, supervising accountability volunteers, and ensuring compliance with IRC and donor requirements. The officer will also conduct capacity-building sessions and maintain communication with various stakeholders to enhance client responsiveness. The position is crucial for strengthening the organization's accountability framework and improving service delivery to affected populations. Candidate Requirements: Bachelor's degree in social science or related field At least 3 years of experience in Accountability or MEAL Experience supervising community-based volunteers Good command in Excel, Power BI, and ODK Strong written and spoken English and Bengali skills Ability to handle sensitive information confidentially Willingness to travel to field locations The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Program Brief The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities, helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future, and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity, and hope to millions. If you're a solution-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people worldwide for a better future. Since 2017, IRC has supported Rohingya Refugees and Bangladeshi national communities in Cox's Bazar, Khulna, Barisal, and Chattogram with integrated services. The organization also addresses climate change impacts by building resilience and promoting economic recovery, education, and protection. Purpose of the Role The Officer - Accountability runs the day-to-day operation and continuous improvement of the Client Feedback and Response Mechanism (CFRM) across the IRC Cox's Bazar program. The post-holder makes sure client feedback and complaints are recorded, referred and closed on time. The role also manages, builds the capacity of and fairly pays the pool of Accountability Volunteers (IWs), and keeps CFRM tools and reporting aligned with IRC and donor requirements. The officer will work closely with accountability volunteer, CFRM Focal Persons, facility focal points, program and partner staff and the line supervisor to strengthen client responsiveness and institutionalize the CFRM policy framework. Contract length : Till 30 September 2027 (with high possibility of extension) Work Location: IRC-Bangladesh, Ukhiya Office Reporting to: Manager - Accountability and Learning Scope of Work The work is built around five core tasks: CFRM activities implementation; follow up Accountability Volunteers, updated CFR toolkit in Commcare with the programmatic responses; the Annual multi-sectoral Client Satisfaction Survey (CSS); and logistics support for CFRM team. Highlights of Key Responsibilities Strengthening and institutionalizing the CFRM policy framework Review and update the Client Feedback Registry tools regularly to reflect the current context. Review and revise Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA) awareness and reporting tools across all IRC and partner programmes. Review and update the standardized CFRM FAQ toolkit regularly. Follow up on and renew the Feedback Boxes, including their operational guidelines. Maintain and update the engagement plan for Incentive Volunteers supporting CFRM and process monitoring. Maintain the CFRM Focal Person list by location, grant and sector. Integrate newly endorsed global and country accountability strategies, guidelines and management directives into existing CFRM systems, and conduct staff orientations as needed. Capacity building and Incentive Worker (IW) management Supervise, coordinate and monitor accountability volunteers, onboard new personnel as required, and prepare yearly consolidated work plans. Monitor daily attendance and track performance of all active accountability volunteers against their work plans, keeping regular contact with facility focal points, CFRM focal and partner staff. Prepare and process accountability volunteer payment sheets accurately within timeline. Hold bi-monthly coordination meetings and targeted capacity-building sessions for accountability volunteers, based on identified learning needs. Conduct data management, safeguarding and compliance orientations for accountability volunteers. Facilitate CFRM integration initiatives for IRC and partner staff and align them with Project Implementation Plans. Liaise regularly with HR and Safeguarding on volunteer management and operations. Brief facility focal points on new grants, locations and facilities, and integrate newly onboarded donors into the CFRM plan. CFRM case management, coordination and closure Record, track and follow up on 100% of client feedback and complaint cases in line with CFRM guidelines. Download and clean CFR data weekly, correct mismatches, share with respective CFRM focal. Enter CFRM Focal Person responses into the CFR tool to close cases on time and share responses with IWs and clients daily and weekly by mobile, WhatsApp and email. Maintain the CFRM Focal Point database and run at least 2 CFRM orientation sessions a year for focal people and relevant staff. Make at least 48 weekly follow-up communications (emails and coordination updates) with focal points and programme teams to speed up case closure. Follow up weekly on overdue or pending cases until they are resolved and closed.Refer the high-priority and urgent cases to the respective departments within 24 hours of receipt and monitor them until action is taken. Ensure action taken against all complaints programme complaints by focal and reply to the feedback on assigned CFRM cases. Make 50% field monitoring and supervision visits a month (at least 2 days in a week), and identify and mitigate day-to-day challenges in activities, cases, conflicts, the CFRM system and coordination. Keep grant, sector and location-based service mapping 100% updated and accessible. Develop and implement grant-specific CFRM operational plans and budgets, including monthly IW plans by location, grant and sector, with timely tracking and supporting documentation. Prepare and share monthly action-track reports covering case status, response rates, pending actions and closure performance, and share CFRM database and narrative reports with the line supervisor for donor reporting. Client assessments, evaluations and logistics management Assist to provide support the annual Client Satisfaction Survey (CSS): planning, budgeting, sampling, tool contextualization, IW orientation, data collection, cleaning, quality assurance, analysis, reporting and dissemination. Support MIS manager in annual Data Quality Audit (DQA).Provide 100% logistical, administrative and financial documentation support for MEAL-led training, workshops, learning sessions, assessments and meetings. Coordinate all CFRM-related events on time, including budget tracking, finance processing, visibility messaging, draft design preparation and internal/external approvals. Ensure uninterrupted availability, asset management and distribution of CFRM logistics, visibility materials and communication tools across all sites.Submit monthly expense claims for Accountability and Learning activities and support colleagues with theirs. Assist in developing and reviewing strategic plans and guidelines on Client Responsiveness. Other Promote and actively participate in initiatives and efforts to build team engagement, inclusion and cohesion in IRC [team/office] Foster ongoing learning, honest dialogue and reflection to strengthen safeguarding and to promote IRC values and adherence to IRC policies. Requirements   Proposed qualifications and experience Bachelor's degree in social science, development studies, disaster management, statistics or a related field, Masters preferrable. At least 3 years of experience in Accountability to Affected Population or CFRM, MEAL, safeguarding, preferably in a humanitarian setting. Experience supervising community-based volunteer or incentive workers, and handling case and complaint data.  Proposed skills and competencies Good command in Excel, power bi and ODK based data collection tool, familiarity with CFR/CFRM databases and reporting templates. Strong written and spoken skill in English and Bengali; Rohingya or Chittagongian dialect is must. Clear communication, coordination and follow-up skills, and attention to detail. Ability to handle sensitive information with confidentiality and sound judgment.Willingness to travel to IRC field locations. Specific Educational Qualification Bachelor's degree in social science, development studies, disaster management, statistics or a related field, Masters preferrable. Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct . Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding , Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. postings.text: Temporary Junior Policy Analyst – Research and Statistics | OECD - Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development Skip to main content Temporary Junior Policy Analyst – Research and Statistics OECD - Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development Paris International T6 level Speaks English, French Application deadline: December 20, 2026 (about 1 month) Apply Summary by Impactpool The OECD is seeking several Junior Policy Analysts for temporary positions focused on education policy analysis and research. Candidates will conduct policy research, data analysis, and contribute to the development of policy advice while supporting knowledge-sharing initiatives. Responsibilities include drafting reports, managing projects, and engaging with countries and partner organizations. The role requires collaboration within teams and the ability to work independently in a multicultural environment. Candidate Requirements: Advanced degree in economics, education, public policy, or social sciences At least one year of applied research and policy analysis experience Knowledge of education policy issues and research Proven quantitative and qualitative research skills Strong statistical skills and/or knowledge of statistical software Fluency in English and knowledge of French Proficiency in Microsoft Office Package Experience with data analysis software (e.g., STATA, R, NVivo) is an asset Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate effectively Temporary Junior Policy Analyst – Research and Statistics Full-time Directorate: EDU Grade: T6 Company Description The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world.  Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The  Directorate for Education and Skills  (EDU) leads the Organisation’s work to help member and non-member countries achieve high-quality learning for all, design better skills policies, and turn them into jobs and growth. The Directorate carries this out by providing statistics, analysis and policy advice to countries on a wide range of educational topics. Within the Directorate, the Policy Advice and Implementation Division (PAI) co-ordinates advice on education policy to OECD members and other countries, both collectively and individually, across all sectors of education. Outputs include both cross-country and country-specific analysis. They typically bring together quantitative and qualitative analysis and can support the entire policy process from design through to successful implementation, including data development at the system level.  We are looking for several Junior Policy Analysts for one-year temporary staff positions starting in early 2027. Selected candidates will undertake education policy analysis, education research and data analysis. Available positions cover a range of education policy areas such as assessment and certification, digital education and AI, secondary education, higher education, teachers and school leaders, equity and inclusion, basic and foundational skills, curricular reform, policy evaluation and implementation advice and international comparative research. Selected candidates will work in one or two of these areas in the relevant team(s) under the supervision of a Senior Analyst, and the direction of the Head of the PAI Division. Job Description Main Responsibilities The selected candidate(s) will conduct policy research, data analysis, contribute to the development of policy advice and support knowledge-sharing, including through peer-learning events. They will assist countries with the implementation of education policy; preparing reports and publications; and effectively communicating findings. They will also contribute to the management and delivery of projects and engagement with countries and partner organisations. Analysis and drafting Contribute to the identification and development of policy issues by reviewing, synthesising and interpreting available evidence, and analysing the policy implications.  Draft chapters and parts of reports, country reviews, policy briefs, case studies and working papers to present evidence, analysis and policy advice. Data collection and analysis Extract and analyse data and information from national and international datasets (e.g. OECD datasets, labour force surveys, longitudinal surveys, administrative data) and other information (e.g. questionnaires, country policies and practices, and case studies) to undertake statistical and qualitative analysis. Identify and develop appropriate figures, tables and other visualisations to communicate and disseminate findings. Coordination and planning Contribute to the organisation of review missions, peer learning discussions, policy dialogues, webinars, conferences and workshops, in collaboration with countries. Support the coordination of country-specific activities, including managing relations with the concerned country, organising activities and steering the associated analysis. Representation, liaison and dissemination Engage in dissemination activities and developing communication materials such as agendas, presentations and summary notes. Support coordination with partners and experts and ensure professional relationships are maintained internally and externally.            Qualifications Ideal Candidate Profile Academic Background An advanced university degree in economics, education, public policy, social sciences, or a similar discipline. Professional Background At least one year of applied research and policy analysis in education or public policy acquired in an international organisation, national administration, higher education or research institution or think tank. Knowledge of education policy issues and education research is desirable. Expertise in one or more of the following areas is an advantage: assessment and certification, digital education and AI, secondary education, higher education, teachers and school leaders, equity and inclusion, basic and foundational skills, curricular reform, policy evaluation and implementation advice and international comparative research. Proven quantitative and qualitative research skills, analytical capacity and drafting skills. Strong statistical skills and/or knowledge of statistical software is desirable (for some of the available positions). Capacity to write well-organised, clear and precise prose in English. Capacity to work with independence and flexibility, identifying priorities, tasks and timelines, and a demonstrated commitment to delivering excellence in work outputs. Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate effectively within and across teams. An ability to work autonomously and in a multicultural and international environment. Tools Proficiency with the Microsoft Office Package (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint etc.). Experience with quantitative and/or qualitative analysis data software (e.g., STATA, R, NVivo) would be an asset. An understanding of the potential application and limits of AI tools in a policy research environment. Core Competencies OECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of the hiring process: Vision and Strategy (Level 1); Enable People (Level 1); Ethics and Integrity (Level 1); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 1); Achieve Results (Level 1); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 1). To learn more about the definitions for each competency for levels 1-3, please refer to OECD Core Competencies . Languages Fluency in one of the two OECD official languages (English and French) and knowledge of the other, with a commitment to reach a good working level. Additional Information Closing Date This vacancy should be filled as soon as possible, and applications should reach us no later than  Sunday 20 December 2026, 23h59 (Paris time) . Contract Duration 12 months, renewable up to a maximum of 24 months. Assignment based in Paris, France. Ideal start date: January-March 2027. Salary information For temporary staff, salary starts at 3 240 EUR. The Corporate Salary Framework for Temporary staff members can be found here . Selection Process For short-listed candidates, the selection process may include a video-recorded interview, job-based assessment and panel interviews. The OECD is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes the applications of all qualified candidates, irrespective of their racial or ethnic origin, opinions or beliefs, gender, sexual orientation, health or disabilities. Temporary appointments are open to applicants irrespective of nationality. In accordance with OECD practice, priority will be given to candidates who are nationals of OECD Members, or, where applicable, to countries participating in the relevant programme or body.  The OECD promotes an optimal use of resources in order to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. Staff members are encouraged to actively contribute to this goal. postings.text: National Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist | FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Skip to main content National Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Port Moresby National Consultant - Contractors Agreement level Speaks English Application deadline: November 30, 2026 (14 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The National Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist at FAO will oversee the monitoring and evaluation of projects aimed at enhancing pandemic preparedness in Papua New Guinea. This role involves ensuring effective partner coordination, sound planning, and compliance with FAO and donor requirements. The specialist will contribute to the design and implementation of monitoring and evaluation plans, facilitate data collection and analysis, and prepare reports for various stakeholders. The position requires collaboration with national authorities and technical partners to strengthen pandemic response systems. Candidate Requirements: University Degree in relevant field At least 5 years of experience in monitoring and evaluation Working knowledge of English National of Papua New Guinea or resident with work permit Experience with intergovernmental bodies and multidisciplinary teams Experience in designing monitoring and evaluation systems Experience in results-based management Experience in data collection and analysis Experience using monitoring information systems Experience with UN or international development projects Ability to draft technical documents and reports Excellent communication skills IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that Closure Date and Time displayed above are based on date and time settings of your personal device FAO is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, background and culture Qualified female applicants, qualified nationals of non-and under-represented Members and person with disabilities are encouraged to apply Everyone who works for FAO is required to adhere to the highest standards of integrity and professional conduct, and to uphold FAO's values FAO, as a Specialized Agency of the United Nations, has a zero-tolerance policy for conduct that is incompatible with its status, objectives and mandate, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks All applications will be treated with the strictest confidentiality FAO’s commitment to environmental sustainability is integral to our strategic objectives and operations. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) contributes to the achievement of the 2030 Agenda through FAO Strategic Framework by supporting the transformation to MORE efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agrifood systems, for better production, better nutrition, a better environment, and a better life, leaving no one behind. Organizational Setting The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations leading international efforts to eradicate hunger, improve food security and nutrition, reduce rural poverty, and promote the sustainable management of natural resources. Through the FAO Strategic Framework 2022–31, the Organization supports the transformation to more efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agrifood systems for better production, better nutrition, a better environment and a better life, leaving no one behind. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) is implementing its component of Papua New Guinea's Pandemic Fund Project All Aboard for a Systematic Approach to Pandemic Preparedness in Papua New Guinea (ASAP-PNG) under GCP/PNG/020/PAF as well as a multi-country Pandemic Fund project Data to Action: Stronger Pandemic Preparedness and Response Systems in the Western Pacific Region (GCP/RAS/421/PAF). The projects strengthen pandemic prevention, preparedness and response through zoonotic disease risk assessment and mitigation, animal health surveillance and early warning, One Health workforce capacity, Risk Communication and Community Engagement, and strengthened One Health coordination. The project is implemented with national and subnational authorities, One Health stakeholders, implementing entities and technical and development partners. Reporting Lines The National Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist will work under the overall guidance of the FAO Head of Office in Papua New Guinea (PNG), and the direct supervision of the International Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist. The incumbent will receive technical and functional guidance from the Lead Technical Officer (LTO), the Lead Technical Unit (LTU), and relevant FAO technical and operational units. The incumbent will also work in close coordination with relevant divisions, teams and officers within FAO PNG, the FAO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific (RAP), and FAO Headquarters. Technical Focus Monitoring and evaluation of the FAO component of GCP/PNG/020/PAF and GCP/RAS/421/PAF, ensuring coherent and timely delivery, effective partner coordination, sound planning and monitoring, and compliance with FAO rules and applicable donor requirements, including M&E technical inputs across the One Health and Livestock team. Tasks and Responsibilities • Contribute to the formulation, implementation, monitoring and reporting of FAO's activities under relevant Animal Health and One Health projects and programmes, including Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR). • Provide technical assistance to the monitoring and evaluating of GCP/PNG/020/PAF and GCP/RAS/421/PAF project outputs, outcomes and impacts through data collection, analysis and reporting, contributing to informed decision-making on strengthening critical pandemic prevention, preparedness, and response capacities (PPR) and ensuring alignment with SDG indicators. • Help design, validate, and implement the project’s M&E Plan, to enable tracking of progress toward objectives, targets, and budget performance, in accordance with the Project’s Logical Framework Matrix (LFM), Project Environmental and Social Management Plan, Gender Action Plan, and the Annual Work Plan and Budget. • Facilitate the management and maintenance of web-based M&E systems, ensuring timely and accurate data collection, entry, validation, quality assurance, analysis, and reporting. • Provide technical support to the PMU during the Project Inception providing inputs and mainstreaming M&E elements into the updated Project Theory of Change and other relevant elements for the project implementation. • Help integrate and manage the project logical framework and budget into the FAO Field Programme Management Information System (FPMIS), ensuring timely updates throughout implementation. • Identify and implement early warning mechanisms for risks and continuous improvement, anticipate potential implementation challenges and assess risk mitigation measures and adjustments to improve coordination and implementation at national and regional levels. • Participate in field monitoring missions undertaken by the PMU, Lead Technical Officer and Pandemic Fund representatives, ensuring documentation of findings, follow-up actions and lessons learned. • Provide technical inputs and advise tot the International M&E Specialist to prepare monitoring data, performance analysis and documentation required for the Project’s Annual Performance Report (APR) for the Pandemic Fund. • Provide M&E data and technical inputs to the Communications Specialists by providing data for the development of evidence-based communication products. • Prepare materials and participate in external audit processes, the Mid-Term Evaluation, and the Final Evaluation of the Project, and design strategies to address recommendations and findings resulting from such audits and/or evaluations. • Coordinate actions related to project completion and closure, including the timely resolution of outstanding commitments, final disposition of project assets, and submission of the final report. • Coordinate with FAO's M&E officers at regional and headquarters levels and ensure compliance with FAO corporate monitoring standards and protocols from PNG Government and Pandemic Fund. • Provide technical inputs and advice to the to the International M&E Specialists and Head of Office-PNG on any other M&E matters related to the FAO-PNG’s programme delivery. • Contribute to FAO’s inputs and feedback to Pandemic Fund documents and guidelines developed by the Pandemic Fund Secretariat. • Coordinate the preparation and submission of timely reports on the ASAP-PNG project implementation in collaboration with the Pandemic Fund teams at sub-regional, regional and headquarters levels • Perform any other duties as required. CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING Minimum Requirements • University Degree in Economics, Environmental Science, Veterinary Science, Public Health, One Health, Natural Resource Management, Development Studies, Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, or a related field. • At least 5 years of relevant experience in monitoring and evaluation, results-based management, or performance monitoring of development projects, preferably donor-funded programmes. • Working knowledge (C1) of English. • National of Papua New Guinea or resident of the country with a valid work permit. FAO Core Competencies • Results Focus • Teamwork • Communication • Building Effective Relationships • Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement Selection Criteria • Experience in working with intergovernmental bodies and multidisciplinary teams. • Experience in designing and implementing monitoring and evaluation systems for development • programmes and projects. • Experience in results-based management, including the development of logical frameworks, indicators and results frameworks. • Experience in data collection, analysis, performance monitoring and preparation of donor reports, preferably for UN agencies or other international development partners. • Experience using monitoring information systems and project management platforms, including FPMIS or similar systems. • Experience working with UN or other international development projects is highly desirable. • Demonstrated experience in establishing and maintaining partnerships, including government institutions and agencies. • Demonstrated ability to formulate, draft and finalize clear technical and policy documents, guidelines and manuals, in English. • Demonstrated ability to analyse data, prepare technical reports, and communicate monitoring results to diverse stakeholders. • Excellent communication skills and ability to present complex topics to a variety of technical and non-technical audiences. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION FAO does not charge a fee at any stage of the recruitment process (application, interview meeting, processing) Applications received after the closing date will not be accepted Please note that FAO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU) / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.  IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at  IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration   Project Context and Scope Through this assignment, the consultant will contribute to the Government of Ethiopia's ongoing efforts to strengthen and institutionalize the NRM by developing practical tools and frameworks that support evidence-based planning, monitoring, reporting, and decision-making. The outputs of the consultancy will enhance the capacity of MoWSA, NPC, relevant line ministries, regional structures, and other NRM stakeholders to effectively monitor the performance and impact of the NRM, improve interagency coordination, and strengthen protection and assistance outcomes for vulnerable migrants, victims of trafficking, returnees, and other persons in need of protection. The assignment will be implemented under the Strengthening Safe Labour Migration, Reintegration, and Protection Systems in Ethiopia Project.    Responsibilities Tasks to be performed under this contract Deliverable 1: Inception Report and Desk Review- 30% Payment Conduct a review of NRM documents, reporting systems, referral tools, SOPs, and relevant policy frameworks. Hold consultations with key stakeholders including government institutions, service providers, and development partners. Submit an inception report outlining methodology, workplan, stakeholder engagement approach, and deliverables. Timeline: Within 2 weeks of contract commencement. Quarterly reporting template  to support consolidated reporting on referral performance among various service providers, referral outcomes, service utilization, stakeholder engagement, and emerging gaps. Service provider reporting template to capture service delivery statistics, referral caseloads, capacity constraints, and implementation challenges. Consolidated reporting dashboard format. Guidance notes on reporting requirements and data management outlining reporting responsibilities, reporting timelines, indicator definitions, and quality assurance measures. Outcome and output indicators. Indicator reference sheets. Data collection and reporting procedures. Data quality assurance mechanisms. Roles and responsibilities of stakeholders. Reporting timelines and accountability matrix. Risk and assumption matrix. Monitoring tools and templates. Timeline: End of Month 2.  Deliverable 4: Validation Workshop and Final Package - 20% Payment Facilitate a stakeholder validation workshop. Revise draft tools and framework based on comments received. Submit final standardized reporting templates and M&E framework. Provide a brief user guide for implementation. Timeline: End of Month 3. Performance indicators for the evaluation of results Timely submission of all deliverables according to agreed schedule. Quality and technical soundness of reporting templates and M&E framework. Alignment with the National Referral Mechanism and relevant national policies. Practical applicability and user-friendliness of developed tools. Incorporation of stakeholder feedback. Approval of final deliverables by IOM and relevant government counterparts. Demonstrated experience in developing M&E frameworks, reporting systems, and data management tools. Experience working with government institutions, development partners, and UN agencies. Knowledge of migration, trafficking in persons, protection, and referral mechanisms in Ethiopia is highly desirable. Proven experience facilitating stakeholder consultations and validation workshops.
