postings.title: Senior Research Associate (PSA) UNU - United Nations University Dresden Senior
postings.text: Senior Research Associate (PSA) | UNU - United Nations University Skip to main content Senior Research Associate (PSA) UNU - United Nations University Dresden Senior level Speaks German, English Application deadline: November 29, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Senior Research Associate at the United Nations University (UNU) will contribute to research on the Resource Nexus, focusing on sustainability assessments and resource management. The role involves designing and managing research activities, coordinating methodologies, and publishing findings in scientific journals. Additionally, the associate will mentor students and staff, support grant proposals, and engage with stakeholders to enhance research impact. This position requires collaboration with a diverse team to address global sustainability challenges. Candidate Requirements: PhD or Master's degree in relevant field At least 2 years of relevant experience Experience with Life Cycle Assessment software Proven record of publications Experience in quantitative analysis and/or modelling Strong planning and organization skills Fluency in English United Nations University (UNU) The United Nations University (UNU) is a global think tank and postgraduate teaching organization within the United Nations System. UNU engages in policy-relevant research, capacity development, and knowledge dissemination in furtherance of the purposes and principles of the United Nations. The work of UNU contributes to solving pressing global problems that are the concern of the United Nations and its Member States. For the past five decades, UNU has been a source of impartial research on sustainability, human security, and economic development. With hundreds of researchers working at institutes in 12 countries, UNU's expertise spans the full breadth of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals, generating policy-relevant knowledge to effect positive global change. UNU collaborates closely with other UN entities and leading research institutions across the globe. For more information, please visit . About United Nations University Institute for Integrated Management of Material Fluxes and of Resources (UNU Resource Nexus) UNU Resource Nexus is one of 13 research and training Institutes that comprise the think tanks in the UNU system. UNU Resource Nexus develops strategies to resolve pressing issues in the sustainable use and integrated management of environmental resources such as water, soil, waste, energy, and other geo-resources that are of concern to the United Nations and its Member States – particularly in developing and emerging economies. Based in Dresden, Germany, the Institute engages in research, capacity development, postgraduate teaching, advanced training, and knowledge dissemination to advance the Resource Nexus. For more information, please visit .  Sustainability Assessment for the Resource Nexus The short and long-term implementation of Sustainability Assessment is fundamental to the comprehensive understanding of the Resource Nexus and for driving policy creation for resource management that considers social, economic, and environmental dimensions, without disregarding other facets, such as technical, institutional, and cultural. The integration of the multi-dimensional concept of resilience in sustainability assessments is also emphasized, considering the complementary character and synergetic potential of these perspectives. In general, Sustainability Assessment has been highlighted as a valuable analytical viewpoint that can support the operationalisation of the Resource Nexus concept. However, due to the various definitions and methods available, there is a challenge to find the suitable direction in which Sustainability Assessment can support Resource Nexus research. The overall objective is to assess sustainability from its initial design to its application in a comprehensive analysis, namely by interconnecting different resources and addressing their dimensions of sustainability. Considering the plethora of methods for Sustainability Assessment, a multi-metric approach based on the screening of data, context analysis, integration of stakeholders' perspectives, and the selection of the most appropriate assessment method to support the solution is envisioned. Additionally, to tackle the Nexus problem, an analysis across multiple scales and in a transdisciplinary manner, by integrating stakeholder and wickedness analyses, is recommended. Sustainability Assessment supports a Resource Nexus Approach for all relevant environmental resources, including water, soil, waste, energy, and other geo-resources, as well as biodiversity. Sustainability Assessment promotes research beyond the siloed biophysical-oriented view of a resource by involving all three dimensions, namely, social, economic, and environmental. This aligns with the comprehensive and holistic view proposed by the Resource Nexus perspective. The Senior Research Associate will contribute to this research theme and associated research and will be responsible for coordinating designated project/s within the context of Resource Nexus assessment. Responsibilities Under the authority and supervision of the Director of UNU Resource Nexus and in close collaboration with the academic team at the Institute, the successful candidate will contribute to: 1. Research and Innovation Development on the Resource Nexus Advance UNU Resource Nexus’ projects by designing, implementing, and managing research activities related to the designated project/s; Coordinate, advance and ensure alignment of Resource Nexus assessment methodology across the designated project/s; Contribute to publications and publish articles in peer-reviewed renowned scientific journals, books, and policy briefs, actively represent the Institute by presenting papers where appropriate; Conduct research studies and prepare management reports based on the scientific methods such as systematic literature review, inductive and deductive qualitative content analysis, grounded theory, design science research and case study research; Contribute to addressing emerging issues advancing the Resource Nexus that are of interest to the United Nations, its Member States, the United Nations University, and relevant policymakers; Provide substantial support in the development of grant proposals and resource mobilization efforts for research activities; and Identify opportunities and build strategic partnerships and networks to expand research impact. 2. Education and Capacity Development Mentor, supervise, and/or provide guidance to students writing their master’s thesis; Co-supervise and mentor staff, doctoral researchers, fellows, scholars, and interns; Contribute to the Institute’s teaching activities, especially e-learning and capacity development related to the designated project/s; and Prepare presentations, tools and other materials, and support organization of capacity development activities, related to the designated project/s. 3. Governance and Administration of the Institute Coordinate working groups related to the designated project/s, focusing on Resource Nexus assessment, such as Young PRISMA; Identify and pursue funding opportunities; prepare, coordinate and write research proposals, and communicate with partners and donors; Implement administrative regulations and policy framework relevant to respective activities and projects; Coordinate and contribute to reports for donors and partners; Coordinate input to the creation of vacancy announcements and support the selection process for recruitment activities; and Maintain research tools and platforms, and handle communication with suppliers and service providers. 4. Outreach, Advocacy and Impact Maintain networks with stakeholders and research institutions relevant to the designated project/s; Act as a focal point for activities related to the designated project/s; Actively participate and represent UNU Resource Nexus in local and international conferences, networking events and science communication events, including engagement with non-scientific audiences, present knowledge and findings acquired from the Institute’s research, education and capacity development activities; and Prepare outputs to be shared on the UNU Resource Nexus websites and other relevant platforms. 5. Perform other duties as assigned by the Director. Key Performance Indicators In relation to UNU Resource Nexus’ KPI categories and 4 Pillar structure as follows: Research and Innovation Development : Successful submission and publication of at least one (1) first-author publication per year as author or co-author of UNU Resource Nexus (KPI 1.1.0); At least one (1) joint research product (for example papers) with academic institutions located in the Global South annually (KPI 1.4.1); and Contribution to at least one (1) new collaboration in new regions OR at least one (1) new research topic (KPI 5.1.0) in the area of research annually. Education and Capacity Development At least five (5) hours of delivered capacity-building initiatives on annual basis; At least one (1) set of educational materials or modules to the KARE platform or similar knowledge-sharing tools delivered; and Contribution to at least one (1) new collaborations in new regions OR at least one (1) new education topic (KPI 5.1.0) in the area of education. Governance and Administration Contribution to the positive reputation of UNU Resource Nexus as a reliable and trustworthy partner among research partners, governments, donors and civil society. Outreach, Advocacy and Impact Maintain/participate in at least one (1) active collaborations on annual basis; Contribution to at least one (1) UN/ Member State organized conferences or policy-dialogues on annual basis; Contribution to at least one (1) event organised by the Institute with participation of policy makers on annual basis; and Contribution to at least one (1) public event and high-level speaking engagements on annual basis. Competencies Values: Inclusion — take action to create an environment of dignity and respect for all, regardless of age, culture, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, gender expression, geography, grade, language, nationality, racial identity, religion, sex, sex characteristics, sexual orientation, social origin or any other aspect of identity Integrity — act ethically, demonstrating the standards of conduct of the United Nations and taking prompt action in case of witnessing unprofessional or unethical behaviour, or any other breach of UN standards Humility — demonstrate self-awareness and willingness to learn from others Humanity — act according to the purposes of the United Nations: peace, dignity and equality on a healthy planet Behaviours: Connect and collaborate — build positive relationships with others to advance the work of the United Nations and work coherently as One UN Analyse and plan — seek out and use data from a wide range of sources to understand problems, inform decision-making, propose evidence-based solutions and plan action Deliver results with positive impact — hold oneself and others accountable for delivering results and making a positive difference to the people and causes that the United Nations serves Learn and develop — pursue own learning and development and contribute to the learning and development of others Adapt and innovate — demonstrate flexibility, agility and the ability to think and act in novel ways 1) Education and certification PhD or Master 's degree or equivalent in Environmental, Natural, Social, Economic or Political Sciences, Environmental Ecology, or a related field. 2) Required skills and experience At least two (2) years of relevant experience related to sustainability, on a topic(s) relevant to the Resource Nexus; Experience with Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) software solutions, such as open Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), SimaPro, LCA for Experts or similar sustainability assessment softwar

The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) contributes to the achievement of the 2030 Agenda through FAO Strategic Framework by supporting the transformation to MORE efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agrifood systems, for better production, better nutrition, a better environment, and a better life, leaving no one behind. Organizational Setting The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations leading international efforts to eradicate hunger, improve food security and nutrition, reduce rural poverty, and promote the sustainable management of natural resources. Through the FAO Strategic Framework 2022–31, the Organization supports the transformation to more efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agrifood systems for better production, better nutrition, a better environment and a better life, leaving no one behind. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) is implementing its component of Papua New Guinea's Pandemic Fund Project All Aboard for a Systematic Approach to Pandemic Preparedness in Papua New Guinea (ASAP-PNG) under GCP/PNG/020/PAF. The project strengthens pandemic prevention, preparedness and response through zoonotic disease risk assessment and mitigation, animal health surveillance and early warning, One Health workforce capacity, Risk Communication and Community Engagement, and strengthened One Health coordination. The project is implemented with national and subnational authorities, One Health stakeholders, implementing entities and technical and development partners. Reporting Lines The National Animal Health/One Health Specialist will work under the overall guidance of the FAO Head of Office in Papua New Guinea (PNG), and under the direct supervision of the Livestock Development Officer. The incumbent will receive technical and functional guidance from the Lead Technical Officer (LTO), the Lead Technical Unit (LTU), and relevant FAO technical and operational units, while maintaining close coordination with relevant teams and officers within FAO PNG, the FAO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific (RAP), and FAO Headquarters. international partners and One Health stakeholders to facilitate the introduction of internationally recognized tools for One Health zoonotic disease prioritization, Joint Risk Assessment and surveillance evaluation. • Provide technical inputs to the multi-country Pandemic Fund supported project activities relating to FAO’s Assessment Tool for Laboratories and AMR Surveillance Systems (FAO-ATLASS), laboratory proficiency testing for priority disease of concern and a Field Training Program for Wildlife, Ecosystem, Biodiversity and Environment (FTP-WEBE). • Coordinate activities contributing to the establishment of One Health coordination in PNG through a governance framework, policy mapping One Health emergency response planning. • Coordinate the monitoring of project presentations, communication materials and other knowledge products related to Animal Health and One Health activities. • Liaise with national and provincial authorities, One Health structures, implementing entities and development partners. • Contribute to project reviews of pilot Animal Health and One Health activities and revise approaches based on feedback. • Contribute to FAO’s inputs and feedback to Pandemic Fund documents and guidelines developed by the Pandemic Fund Secretariat. • Coordinate the preparation and submission of timely reports on the ASAP-PNG project implementation in collaboration with the Pandemic Fund teams at sub-regional, regional and headquarters level. Support to country programme/project development and management • Provide technical guidance in the preparation of project concept notes and documents as required, in areas of FAO’s mandate; • Liaise and coordinate with relevant government ministries, donors, and implementing partners, for FAO activities and project implementation, as required; • Carry out other programmatic tasks for the FAO PNG Office in Papua New Guinea, as well as for FAO programme/ projects in Papua New Guinea, as required; and • Perform other related duties as required. postings.title: IT Operations SC G WFP - World Food Programme Cairo SB-3 (SC6/SC7), Service Contract, Local Contractors Agreement - Consultancy
postings.text: IT Operations SC G | WFP - World Food Programme Skip to main content IT Operations SC G WFP - World Food Programme Cairo National SB-3 (SC6/SC7), Service Contract, Local Contractors Agreement level Application deadline: November 30, 2026 (14 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The IT Associate - Product Adoption and Support at WFP will provide operational and technical support for corporate IT solutions across Country Offices. This role involves troubleshooting, requirements analysis, user enablement, and service performance monitoring. The incumbent will also engage with Country Offices to understand their needs and improve the adoption of digital solutions. The position requires strong problem-solving skills, customer focus, and the ability to manage multiple priorities. Candidate Requirements: Experience supporting digital platforms Knowledge of ITIL-aligned service management practices Ability to analyze service and operational data Experience in user training and product demonstrations Strong documentation skills for technical issues DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS 30 November 2026-23:59-GMT+02:00 Eastern European Standard Time (Cairo) WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability. ABOUT WFP The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks. At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves. To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org  and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube , LinkedIn , Instagram , Facebook , Twitter , TikTok . WHY JOIN WFP?   WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate. WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment. WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities. A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe. We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement). ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) is the world's largest humanitarian agency, fighting hunger worldwide. The WFP Technology Division (TEC) is the digital business engine of the World Food Programme, providing the business with multi-pronged and resilient technical capabilities able to respond with the agility required in humanitarian operations, be they manmade or in a natural disaster setting. TEC’s Digital Solutions Branch (TECD) oversees all solution development activities for WFP, covering the full technology stack and delivering changes to existing solutions. This function manages all aspects of development, from understanding business requirements to designing and building solutions, and overseeing quality assurance. TECD is expanding their service offering into the support and adoption of corporate tools used on the front line of WFP’s operations. TECD’s Global Beneficiary Services (GBS) team supports the adoption and effective use of corporate IT solutions that enable Programme delivery across WFP operations. GBS provides guidance, training, and Tier 2 support to Country Offices (CO) adopting these tools. Members of the team are spread across WFP’s five Regional Offices (RO) to provide follow-the-sun support in the time zone and language of our COs. BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT Under the direct supervision of the Head of GBS, the IT Associate - Product Adoption and Support will provide independent operational and technical support for the adoption, rollout and sustained use of corporate IT solutions across Country Offices in the region. Compared with an assistant-level role, the SC-6 function carries greater responsibility for Tier 2 troubleshooting, requirements analysis, implementation support, user enablement, service performance monitoring, knowledge management and coordination with Regional Office and HQ product teams. The incumbent will analyse incidents and recurring service issues, recommend corrective actions, support deployments and adoption activities, coach local support teams, and contribute to measurable improvement in service quality and user experience. The role requires sound judgement, customer focus, structured problem solving and the ability to manage several priorities with limited supervision. KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES / DUTIES 1. Product support and service management ·       Provide Tier 2 functional and technical support for assigned corporate products, resolving incidents and service requests within agreed service targets and escalating complex defects to product or engineering teams with complete diagnostic evidence. ·       Perform structured troubleshooting using error information, logs, configuration checks, user scenarios and available knowledge articles; identify root causes or contributing factors for recurring issues and recommend sustainable corrective actions. ·       Monitor assigned support queues, priorities, ageing tickets and SLA performance; follow up on escalations and keep users and stakeholders informed through resolution. ·       Identify recurring incidents and service improvement opportunities; contribute to problem records, knowledge articles, standard operating procedures and reusable troubleshooting guidance. ·       Support access, configuration, data-quality and integration-related investigations within the incumbent's authorised scope, applying established information-security and data-protection requirements. 2. Product adoption and country-office readiness ·       Advise Country Offices on the appropriate use of corporate digital solutions supporting programme delivery, including SCOPE, SugarCRM, NEST, CIAM, School Connect, Partner Connect, CODA and PIT, in line with approved product guidance. ·       Engage Country Offices to understand operational requirements, business processes, readiness gaps, user groups and support needs; consolidate findings and provide structured inputs to product and GBS teams. ·       Develop or adapt adoption materials, user guidance, checklists and support resources to improve readiness and consistent use of digital products. ·       Track adoption issues, user feedback and implementation risks, and coordinate follow-up actions with relevant Country Office, Regional Office and HQ stakeholders. 3. postings.text: UN Women National Consultant – WEPs Corporate Action Lab Programme Facilitator (ICT, Technology and Business Services Industries) (Philippines) | UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Skip to main content UN Women National Consultant – WEPs Corporate Action Lab Programme Facilitator (ICT, Technology and Business Services Industries) (Philippines) UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Remote | Philippines National Mid level Speaks Filipino, English Application deadline: November 23, 2026 (7 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool UN Women is seeking a National Consultant to facilitate the WEPs Corporate Action Lab Programme in the Philippines, focusing on gender-responsive and inclusive skills development in the ICT, Technology, and Business Services sectors. The consultant will provide technical guidance, coaching, and documentation support to participating companies as they develop and implement solutions for gender equality challenges. This role involves collaboration with UN Women and participating companies to ensure effective implementation and learning throughout the programme. The consultant will also document progress and insights to inform future initiatives. Candidate Requirements: Master’s degree in relevant field At least 1 year of experience in gender equality or women's economic empowerment Experience providing technical advice to private sector companies Strong coaching and organizational consulting skills Fluency in English and Filipino Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action, and peace and security. Women’s Economic Empowerment (WEE) is central to UN Women’s Strategic Plan 2026–2029, contributing to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly those related to gender equality, decent work, poverty reduction and inclusive economic growth. In Asia and the Pacific, UN Women works with governments, the private sector and other partners to advance gender-responsive business practices, strengthen women’s economic participation and leadership, transform the care economy, support women entrepreneurs, and promote gender-responsive markets, including in the context of climate action and the green and digital transitions. The Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs) are a key framework through which UN Women engages businesses and wider ecosystem actors, including chambers of commerce, business associations and government bodies, to accelerate progress on gender equality. Launched in 2010 by UN Women and the UN Global Compact, the WEPs comprise seven principles that guide private sector action for gender equality across the workplace, marketplace and community, beginning with corporate leadership and underpinned by accountability and transparent reporting. The Gender Action Lab (GAL): Innovation and Impact for Gender Equality in Asia-Pacific , established by UN Women in partnership with the Government of Australia through the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), aims to foster private sector innovation and concrete action that advances gender equality and women’s empowerment and contributes to more inclusive economies across the region. In collaboration with the private sector, GAL identifies, pilots and supports the scaling of multi-stakeholder initiatives aligned with and leveraging the WEPs. This includes thematic innovation labs at country and regional levels, incubators and accelerators, policy labs, applied research and other partnership support initiatives. GAL also generates evidence and provides technical assistance to advance policy, investment and ecosystem development for gender-transformative innovation. One of GAL’s key implementation modalities is the WEPs Corporate Action Lab (WEPs CAL), a cohort-based approach that supports companies to identify gender equality challenges and develop, test and refine practical solutions in a selected thematic area utilizing innovation and human-centered design methodologies. Guided by UN Women’s gender equality expertise and tailored resources, WEPs CAL provides participating companies with a structured process for experimentation, peer learning and the development of solutions tailored to their own organizational contexts, priorities and workforce needs. The first WEPs CAL in the Philippines focused on Advancing Women’s Leadership in Technology, with particular attention to strengthening women’s leadership pipelines and addressing mid-career drop-off points. Building on this experience, the current cohort focuses on gender-responsive and inclusive skills development in the context of the green and digital transitions. This initiative forms part of a larger regional collaboration between UN Women’s Gender Action Lab and the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) Regional Cooperation on Labour Market Policy and TVET for a Twin Transition in ASEAN (RECOTwin) project . RECOTwin promotes practice-oriented skills development through Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), including reskilling and upskilling, to support an inclusive response to changing labour markets shaped by the green and digital transitions. The collaboration seeks to strengthen gender responsiveness in TVET systems, particularly through engagement with the private sector on in-company training and skills development. A key component is the review and revision of the Standard for In-Company Trainers in ASEAN Countries (In-CT Standard) and its supporting training materials through a WEPs and Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) lens. The WEPs CAL in the Philippines – Business Action for Gender-responsive and Inclusive Skills Development: Advancing Equitable Career Pathways for Women and Diverse Talent for the Green and Digital Transition – brings together 11 companies to develop and test approaches to more gender-responsive and inclusive skills development. The programme has already been launched, and participating companies have completed the Ideation Workshop, where they identified key challenges and began developing potential solutions. The companies will now move forward with refining and implementing these solutions, while also contributing to the testing of the uptake, applicability and inclusivity of relevant training pathways, standards and resources, including the revised In-CT Standard and related materials. Lessons and evidence generated through the process will help inform the further refinement of these resources and contribute to broader knowledge exchange and regional dialogue. Against this background, UN Women is seeking to hire one (1) National Consultant – WEPs Corporate Action Lab Programme Facilitator under this Terms of Reference to provide targeted technical support for the implementation of the WEPs CAL, with particular responsibility for the preparation, technical guidance, coaching and documentation of assigned participating companies within the cohort. The objective of the consultancy is to support UN Women in the implementation of the WEPs Corporate Action Lab by providing targeted technical guidance to select participating companies as they identify and refine gender-responsive and inclusive skilling solutions, translate these solutions into practical implementation approaches, and document their progress, challenges, lessons and emerging results. Technical guidance and coaching should be anchored in a human-centered design methodology and designed to foster co-creation, innovation, and solutions contextualized to the lived realities of diverse talent the solutions seek to impact. The consultant will work closely with the UN Women team and provide hands-on support to assigned companies at relevant stages of the WEPs CAL journey. The consultancy will also contribute to capturing learning from company experiences, including insights related to the practical application of the revised In-CT Standard and related resources.  Under this TOR, the consultant will be assigned three (3) to four (4) participating companies, as determined by UN Women, and will provide hands-on support to these assigned companies at relevant stages of the WEPs CAL journey. This TOR focuses on participating companies operating in the ICT, Technology and Business Services industries. Description of Responsibilities/ Scope of Work Under the supervision of the Country Programme Coordinator and guidance of the Regional Programme Manager of the Gender Action Lab, and working closely with the UN Women Philippines Presence Office, the consultant will undertake the following tasks: Review relevant WEPs CAL materials and submissions from select participating companies and prepare for company-level consultations and technical guidance sessions. Provide tailored technical guidance to select companies to refine their challenges, proposed solutions, implementation approaches, stakeholder engagement, and indicators for measuring progress. Participate in and support company check-ins and other relevant WEPs CAL sessions (2-4 cohort-wide WEPs CAL sessions, which may include progress meetings and learning exchanges), providing practical feedback and follow-up recommendations as needed. Support select companies in the application and testing of relevant components of the revised In-Company Training Standard and related resources, and gather feedback on their relevance, usability, and applicability. Coordinate with assigned companies and follow-up regularly to ensure that solution trackers are complete and up to date, relevant supporting materials are uploaded, and progress data and evidence are documented to feed into the consolidated tracker Document company discussions, progress, challenges, technical recommendations, agreed actions, and next steps throughout the WEPs CAL process. Develop a case study for each assigned company, documenting the solution, implementation process, emerging results, challenges, lessons, and recommendation, and consolidate key insights and emerging practices to inform overall WEPs CAL implementation, learning, and relevant programme documentation. Coordinate regularly with the UN Women team and other technical experts supporting the WEPs CAL to ensure alignment and complementarity of support provided to participating companies. Expected Output/s: Upon approval of the following:  Preparatory review and assessment of relevant WEPs CAL materials and submissions from select participating companies, including identification of key areas for technical guidance and follow-up. Technical guidance and support to select participating companies in refining their challenge statements, proposed solutions, stakeholder engagement approaches, implementation plans, and indicators or measures of progress. Periodic progress updates and documentation of technical guidance sessions, company check-ins, and other relevant WEPs CAL engagements, including key discussion points, recommendations, agreed actions, and next steps. Review and feedback on relevant company outputs and documentation developed throughout the WEPs CAL process, as applicable. Documentation and consolidation of feedback from select participating companies on the relevance, usability, and practical application of the revised In-Company Training Standard and related resources, as applicable. Selected synthesis or learning notes capturing emerging challenges, good practices, lessons, and recommendations from the supported companies. End-of-assignment summary note consolidating key outputs delivered, lessons from company engagements, and practical recommendations for future WEPs CAL implementation. postings.title: UN Women : Assessment Study on Low Female Labour Force Participation Rate and the Measurement of Female Labour Force Participation in Labour Force Surveys Across the Arab Region with priority in Egypt, Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Remote | Rabat Senior
postings.text: UN Women : Assessment Study on Low Female Labour Force Participation Rate and the Measurement of Female Labour Force Participation in Labour Force Surveys Across the Arab Region with priority in Egypt, Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia | UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Skip to main content UN Women : Assessment Study on Low Female Labour Force Participation Rate and the Measurement of Female Labour Force Participation in Labour Force Surveys Across the Arab Region with priority in Egypt, Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Remote | Rabat International Senior level Speaks Arabic, English, French Application deadline: November 23, 2026 (7 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool UN Women is seeking an International Consultant to conduct an assessment study on low female labour force participation (FLFP) in Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, and Tunisia. The consultant will lead a mixed-methods assessment to analyze the underlying drivers of low FLFP and evaluate how labor force surveys capture women's economic activities. The study aims to generate robust evidence and policy recommendations to improve measurement and increase women's economic participation in the region. The consultant will work closely with UN Women’s Regional Office and various stakeholders to deliver actionable insights. Candidate Requirements: Master’s degree or PhD in Labour Economics, Econometrics, Statistics, Demography or related field At least 10 years of experience in labour economics data and research Experience in gender and labour market analysis Proficiency in quantitative and qualitative research methods Strong data analysis and visualization skills Fluency in English; knowledge of Arabic or French is desirable Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security.  UN Women’s Regional Office for the Arab States (ROAS), established in Cairo in 2012, covers 17 countries across the Arab States region. ROAS exercises UN Women’s triple mandate—normative standard-setting, regional programme delivery, and inter-agency coordination—and serves as a regional knowledge hub to strengthen multi-stakeholder efforts on gender equality . Female labour force participation (FLFP) in the Arab region remains among the lowest globally despite significant improvements in female educational attainment, health outcomes, and demographic indicators. Across many Arab countries, women continue to face barriers that limit their participation in economic activities, including social norms, legal and institutional constraints, caregiving responsibilities, labour market segmentation, limited access to childcare, mobility restrictions, occupational segregation, and inadequate employment opportunities. These barriers are compounded by the region’s high informality, conflict and fragility in some settings, and persistent gender gaps in paid employment and wages. At the same time, evidence suggests that the measurement of female labour force participation may not fully capture the range of economic activities undertaken by women. Women's work in family enterprises, agriculture, home-based production, informal employment, seasonal work, and unpaid contributing family work is often underreported or inconsistently measured. Differences in labour force survey (LFS) methodologies, questionnaire design, interviewer practices, reference periods, proxy reporting, and application of International Labour Organization (ILO) standards can significantly influence FLFP estimates across countries. Given the policy importance of increasing women's economic participation and the growing emphasis on evidence-based policymaking, there is a need for a comprehensive assessment examining both: The underlying drivers of low female labour force participation in Arab countries; and How female labour force participation is measured and captured in labour force surveys across the region, including methodological limitations and implications for comparability. The study is jointly commissioned by SWEI (Supporting Women’s Economic Empowerment) programme , which provides a policy reform platform and sectoral focus on job creation for women and Women Count programme , which provides methodological expertise in measuring unpaid care work, informal employment, and gender statistics. The combined approach will deliver diagnostic evidence and actionable recommendations to ensure that women’s economic activities are fully captured in labour force surveys and that SWEI’s policy reforms and progress tracking are grounded in accurate data rather than statistical artefacts. It is within this context that UN Women Regional Office for the Arab States is recruiting an International Consultant to Conduct an Assessment Study on Low Female Labour Force Participation Rate and the Measurement of Female Labour Force Participation in Labour Force Surveys Across the Arab Region — Egypt, Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia. Reporting to the Director for Women’s Employment in the Green, STEM, and Care Economy, with support from the Regional Gender Statistics Specialist at RO Arab States, the International Consultant will lead a mixed-methods assessment combining evidence review, trend analysis, comparative survey assessment and stakeholder interviews to diagnose why female labour force participation remains low across Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, and Tunisia and whether labour force surveys adequately capture women's economic activity—ultimately producing policy recommendations that strengthen measurement Purpose of the Study The purpose of this study is to generate robust evidence and policy recommendations on the structural, social, economic, institutional, and measurement-related factors influencing female labour force participation in Egypt, Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia. The study will assess the extent to which current labour force surveys adequately capture women's economic activities and identify opportunities for improving measurement in line with international standards and regional realities. To achieve the objective of this study, generating robust evidence on the structural barriers to women’s economic participation and assessing whether labour force surveys accurately capture women’s work.  By combining Women Count’s methodological expertise in measuring unpaid care work, informal employment, and gender statistics with SWEI’s policy reform platform and sectoral focus, the two programmes will jointly deliver the diagnostic evidence and actionable recommendations needed to ensure that women’s economic activities are fully captured in labour force surveys and that SWEI’s policy reforms and progress tracking are grounded in accurate data rather than statistical artefacts. Objectives of the study Overall Objective To examine the determinants of low female labour force participation in Arab countries and assess how female labour force participation is measured through labour force surveys in Egypt, Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia. Specific Objectives A. Understanding Low Female Labour Force Participation Analyze trends and patterns of FLFP across Arab countries over the past two decades. Identify key drivers of low female labour force participation, including:  Social and cultural norms; Gender roles and unpaid care responsibilities; Educational attainment and skills mismatches; Labour market structure and job availability; Public versus private sector employment dynamics; Legal and regulatory frameworks; Transportation and mobility constraints; Availability of childcare and eldercare services; Informality and vulnerable employment; Digitization and emerging forms of work. Examine variations by:  Age; Marital status; Education level; Residence (urban/rural); Household income; Nationality and migration status; Disability status where data permit. Assess how intersecting factors (e.g., age, marital status, education, residence, nationality, and disability) interact to produce differentiated FLFP outcomes, with attention to the most disadvantaged groups of women. B. Assessment of Labour Force Survey Measurement Review labour force survey methodologies used across Arab countries. Assess consistency with latest ILO labour force concepts and definitions. Examine how surveys capture:  Employment; Unemployment; Labour underutilization; Informal employment; Family work; Agriculture and subsistence production; Home-based work; Gig and platform work; Unpaid contribution to family work. Evaluate gender-related measurement issues in labour force surveys. Identify methodological limitations that may contribute to underestimation of women's economic participation. Assess comparability of FLFP estimates across countries. Develop recommendations for strengthening labour force surveys and improving measurement of women's work. Identify good practices and innovations in LFS design and implementation that could be adapted across the four countries. Scope of Work The consultant shall undertake the following tasks: Task 1: Literature and Evidence Review Conduct an extensive review of: Academic literature; Regional studies; National policy documents; Labour market assessments; Gender analyses; ILO methodological guidance; United Nations reports; National statistical office documentation. The review should be structured around a clear conceptual framework that links structural drivers, measurement issues, and policy implications, and should identify evidence gaps and areas of contestation. Task 2: Trend Analysis Analyze available labour market data from: National labour force surveys; ILOSTAT; National Statistical Offices; Arab labor market databases; World Bank sources; Other relevant datasets. The analysis should examine: FLFP trends; Employment; Unemployment; Labour underutilization; Gender gaps; Sectoral employment patterns. Where feasible, the analysis should include decomposition analysis to disentangle the contributions of demographic, educational, structural, and behavioral factors to changes in FLFP over time. Task 3: Comparative Review of Labour Force Surveys Review labour force survey instruments and methodologies in selected Arab countries (Egypt, Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia) covering: Survey Design Sampling methods; Sample size; Survey frequency; Data collection modes. Measurement Framework Definitions of employment; Definitions of labour force participation; Reference periods; Classification standards. Data Collection Practices Proxy versus self-response; Respondent selection procedures; Interviewer instructions; Gender-sensitive interviewing practices. Questionnaire Content Assessment of modules that capture: Family businesses; Informal employment; Home-based production; Agricultural activities; Subsistence work; Temporary work; Digital platform work. Task 4: Key Informant Interviews Conduct interviews with: National Statistical Offices; Labour Ministries; Gender machinery institutions; Labour market experts; ILO specialists; Regional organizations; Survey practitioners. Task 5: Assessment of Measurement Limitations Analyze key challenges potentially affecting the accurate capture of women's economic activity, including: Conceptual Limitations Narrow interpretation of work; Exclusion of certain productive activities; Differences between labour force and broader work concepts. Operational Limitations Inadequate probing; Respondent misunderstanding; Cultural perceptions of women's work; Enumerator bias. Statistical Limitations Small sample sizes; Limited subgroup disaggregation; Seasonal fluctuations; Non-response bias. In partnership with the Government of Luxembourg, GGGI is preparing the Climate Nexus Finance Facility (CNFF), a five-year global programme (2026–2030) with an estimated budget of EUR 20 million. The Facility aims to strengthen fiscal, financial and public investment frameworks to align financial systems with climate, nature and resilience objectives. Its work includes supporting Ministries of Finance and regulators, National Development Banks, public investment and public–private partnership systems, and the development of bankable climate-resilient and nature-positive investments. The Facility targets mobilization of USD 5 billion toward Climate Nexus objectives, alongside capacity building, investment frameworks, resilient infrastructure projects and climate risk insurance products. Position Summary The Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Associate will support results monitoring, reporting, evidence management and learning for the Climate Nexus Finance Facility (CNFF) and other GGGI Global Sustainable Finance Programs. As part of the Project Support Unit (PSU), the Associate will work closely with the Project Management Unit (PMU), Project Technical Unit (PTU), country teams and GGGI's corporate MEL functions to ensure accurate results tracking, quality reporting and alignment with GGGI's Corporate Results Framework (CRF). postings.text: National Consultant B for Capacity Building of Safe Migration Hotline and Frontline Operators on the UK Seasonal Worker Scheme | IOM - International Organization for Migration Skip to main content National Consultant B for Capacity Building of Safe Migration Hotline and Frontline Operators on the UK Seasonal Worker Scheme IOM - International Organization for Migration Tashkent Both national and international UG - Ungraded level Speaks English, Uzbek Application deadline: December 01, 2026 (15 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool IOM is seeking a qualified Expert to conduct capacity-building training for government-funded Safe Migration Hotline and frontline operators under the UK Seasonal Worker Scheme. The training aims to enhance knowledge on UK SWS regulations, ethical recruitment practices, and identification of recruitment fraud risks. The Expert will prepare training materials, deliver the training, and assess participants' knowledge through pre- and post-training tests. A comprehensive training report will be submitted, documenting the training outcomes and recommendations for future improvements. Candidate Requirements: Advanced degree in migration studies, law, social sciences, or related field Minimum 5 years of experience in labour migration or related field Knowledge of UK Seasonal Worker Scheme and ethical recruitment standards Experience with SOPs, case management, and referral mechanisms Strong facilitation, presentation, and report-writing skills Fluency in Uzbek and strong written English skills Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.  IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at  IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Project Context and Scope The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is implementing the UK International Development-funded project, "Central Asia Safe Migration", which aims to promote safe, orderly, and regular labour migration from Central Asia, with a particular focus on Uzbekistan, under the UK Seasonal Worker Scheme (UK SWS). The project strengthens migrants’ preparedness by improving access to accurate, timely, and practical information throughout the migration cycle, enabling prospective migrants to make informed decisions and supporting a safe, regular, and dignified migration experience. Government-funded Safe Migration Hotline and frontline operators are often the first point of contact for prospective and current seasonal workers and their families seeking information, reporting concerns or requesting assistance. Their ability to provide accurate, up-to-date guidance on the UK SWS, recognize recruitment fraud and protection risks, and refer migrants safely to the appropriate services is therefore essential to the project’s aim that migrants know where to access SWS-related, gender-sensitive resources and services. Under Activity 1.1 of the project, IOM will conduct capacity-building training for 20 government-funded hotline and frontline operators. The training will cover UK SWS regulations and recent policy changes, ethical recruitment practices, and the identification of recruitment fraud risks. Technical support will also be provided to strengthen case management practices, the application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and referral pathways for migrants requiring assistance. IOM seeks to engage a qualified Expert to review the existing SOPs and IOM-produced SWS content, design and deliver the training, measure participants’ knowledge gains through pre- and post-training tests, and document the training results, participants’ discussions and recommendations in a training report.  The training is planned for February 2027. Objectives •    Strengthen the knowledge of hotline and frontline operators on UK SWS regulations and recent policy changes, ethical recruitment practices and the identification of recruitment fraud risks, so that they can provide accurate and up-to-date guidance to prospective and current seasonal workers. •    Strengthen the application of SOPs, case management practices and referral pathways for migrants requiring assistance, including referrals involving UK stakeholders. •    Measure the change in participants’ knowledge through pre- and post-training tests, and document participants’ discussions and feedback on SWS processes to inform future capacity building and technical support. Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing •    Labour Mobility Division, IOM Uzbekistan The Consultant will work under the direct supervision of the Head of Labour Mobility Division and in close coordination with the relevant IOM project staff, including the project’s Monitoring and Evaluation focal point for the pre- and post-training tests. Responsibilities Tasks to be performed under this contract Category B Consultants: Tasks to be performed under this contract: The selected Expert will be responsible for preparing, delivering and reporting on a training for approximately 20 government-funded Safe Migration Hotline and frontline operators, building on the existing SOPs and IOM-produced SWS materials. The assignment will include the following key tasks: Preparation •    Review the SOP used by hotline and frontline operators, including those on case management and referral pathways, as well as IOM-produced SWS content, including pre-departure orientation (PDO) materials, SWS factsheets, anti-fraud and anti-scamming materials, and other materials shared by IOM. Identify outdated information, gaps and practical challenges in applying the SOP and referral pathways, and reflect them in the training content. •    Develop a training plan, presentation and agenda for IOM’s review and approval. The training should be interactive and practice-oriented, using case studies, role plays based on typical hotline calls and group discussions, and should cover, at a minimum, the following modules: - UK SWS regulations, recent policy changes (e.g., National Living Wage, Statutory Sick Pay, accommodation offset) and workers’ rights and obligations; - Refresher on the SWS process, from recruitment and visa application to employment in the UK and return; - Ethical recruitment practices and the identification of recruitment fraud and scam risks; - Application of the SOP, case management practices and referral pathways, including referrals involving UK stakeholders. •    Prepare the training presentation(s) and supporting materials (e.g., handouts, case studies and exercises) in the language(s) agreed with IOM and submit them to IOM for review at least two weeks before the training. The Expert shall incorporate all feedback received before the training. •    Develop pre- and post-training tests (the same or equivalent 10 questions, covering all training modules), together with an answer key and scoring method, for IOM’s review and approval before the training.   Delivery •    Deliver in person training to approximately 20 hotline and frontline operators in February 2027 (exact dates, venue and duration to be agreed with IOM). •    Administer the pre-test at the start and the post-test at the end of the training, using unique participant codes so that each participant’s results can be matched. •    Facilitate and systematically document participants’ discussions during the training, including questions and concerns raised about SWS processes, common issues raised by callers, challenges in applying the SOP, case management and referral pathways, and participants’ suggestions for improvement. Reporting •    Analyse the pre- and post-test results, including average scores before and after the training, the change in scores, the share of participants whose scores improved, and results by module or question to identify topics that need further reinforcement, disaggregated by sex and other variables as relevant. •    Prepare and submit a training report to IOM, including, at a minimum: -    a summary of the training, its objectives, agenda and methodology; -    participation data, disaggregated by sex and institution; -    pre- and post-test results and analysis; -    documented discussions among participants on SWS processes, including key questions, concerns and challenges raised; -    key findings on the application of SOPs, case management practices and referral pathways; -    recommendations for future training, updates to SOPs and materials, and further technical support; -    annexes: agenda, presentation(s), pre- and post-tests with answer key, attendance list and photos. •    Incorporate IOM’s feedback and submit the final training report, together with all training materials, in editable electronic format. Deliverables and Timeline All materials shall be reviewed and validated by IOM Uzbekistan prior to finalization. The Expert shall incorporate consolidated comments and make necessary revisions within the agreed timeframe. Coordination and quality assurance The Expert shall work in close coordination with IOM Uzbekistan throughout the assignment, and shall: Maintain regular communication with IOM Uzbekistan on progress; Ensure that all training content is accurate and consistent with the latest UK SWS rules and IOM-approved materials, and consult IOM where information is unclear or may have changed; Administer the pre- and post-training tests using participant codes rather than names, and protect all personal data in line with IOM Data Protection Principles; Incorporate consolidated feedback from IOM in a timely manner. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience The Expert must demonstrate strong technical, training and analytical capacity, including: •    Advanced degree in migration studies, law, social sciences, social work, public policy or a related field; •    Minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience in labour migration, migrant protection or a related field, including designing and delivering training for government officials or frontline staff; •    Sound knowledge of the UK Seasonal Worker Scheme, ethical recruitment standards and recruitment fraud risks; •    Experience with SOPs, case management and referral mechanisms for migrants or other vulnerable groups; experience with hotline or helpline services is an advantage; •    Experience in designing pre- and post-training tests and reporting on training results; •    Strong facilitation, presentation and report-writing skills; Languages For this consultancy, Fluency in Uzbek; strong written English skills for report preparation are required. postings.text: Evaluation Consultant for Terminal Evaluation of the UNEP project Leveraging transformational change through coherent and synergistic implementation of Environmental Treaties | UNEP - United Nations Environment Programme Skip to main content Evaluation Consultant for Terminal Evaluation of the UNEP project Leveraging transformational change through coherent and synergistic implementation of Environmental Treaties UNEP - United Nations Environment Programme Remote | Nairobi International CON level Speaks English, French Application deadline: November 30, 2026 (14 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Evaluation Consultant will conduct a Terminal Evaluation of the UNEP project focused on enhancing policy coherence and synergies among Multilateral Environmental Agreements. This role involves managing the evaluation process, including data collection, analysis, and report writing, while ensuring stakeholder participation and maintaining independence. The consultant will work closely with the Evaluation Manager and other team members to deliver a comprehensive evaluation report. The position is home-based with field visits and is expected to last for six months on a part-time basis. Candidate Requirements: Advanced university degree in environmental sciences or related field Minimum of seven years of technical expertise in relevant areas Good understanding of environmental treaties and collaboration Evaluation experience using a Theory of Change approach Fluency in oral and written English Result of Service The Evaluation Consultant will submit a concise evaluation report. Work Location Home based with field visits Expected duration 6 months (part time) Duties and Responsibilities ORGANIZATION SETTING The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the United Nations systems designated entity for addressing environmental issues at the global and regional level. Its mandate is to coordinate the development of environmental policy consensus by keeping the global environment under review and bringing emerging issues to the attention of governments and the international community for action. This consultancy is located at Headquarters in the Evaluation Office which reports directly to the Executive Director. The consultant reports to the Evaluation Manager and the Director of the Evaluation Office. THE EVALUATION In line with the UNEP Evaluation Policy and the UNEP Programme and Project Management Manual, the Terminal Evaluation is undertaken at operational completion of the project to assess project performance (in terms of relevance, effectiveness and efficiency) and determine outcomes and impacts (actual and potential) stemming from the project, including their sustainability. The Evaluation has two primary purposes: (i) to provide evidence of results to meet accountability requirements, and (ii) to promote operational improvement, learning and knowledge sharing through results and lessons learned among UNEP and parties to the MEAs, as well as the MEA Secretariats. Therefore, the Evaluation will identify lessons of operational relevance for future project formulation and implementation, especially where a second phase of the project is being considered. Recommendations relevant to the whole house may also be identified during the evaluation process. The Terminal Evaluation will be an in-depth evaluation using a participatory approach whereby key stakeholders are kept informed and consulted throughout the evaluation process. Both quantitative and qualitative evaluation methods will be used as appropriate to determine project achievements against the expected outputs, outcomes and likelihood of impacts. It is highly recommended that the consultant maintains close communication with the project team and promotes information exchange throughout the Evaluation implementation phase in order to increase their (and other stakeholders') ownership of the evaluation findings. Where applicable, the consultant will provide a geo-referenced map that demarcates the area covered by the project and, where possible, provide geo-reference photographs of key intervention sites. THE PROJECT The UNEP Mid-Term Strategy 2022 – 2025 (MTS) recognised that Multilateral Environmental Agreements (MEAs) were central to its achievement and that a lack of coherent and synergistic implementation, characterised by the absence of a 'whole of government approach' at the national level, was a significant factor impeding current progress. The project intervention strategy was based on the needs and priorities as expressed by national governments who are Parties to the MEAs, clear instructions from the United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA) and from the governing bodies of the biodiversity-related MEAs and the MEAs in the chemicals and waste cluster, calling for more integration, as well as from extensive feedback from stakeholders. UNEP's comparative advantage in working in this area includes its universal mandate, convening power among the MEAs and their Parties, and a well-established track record in the subject area. The project focused on enhanced policy coherence, synergies, and cooperation between the MEAs globally and at national level, between their secretariats, and South-South and triangular cooperation among Parties to the MEAs. THE EVALUATION TEAM For this Evaluation, the Evaluation Team will consist of an Evaluation Consultant who will work under the overall responsibility of the Evaluation Office represented by an Evaluation Manager, in consultation with the UNEP Project Manager and the Subprogramme Coordinator of Environmental Governance. SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES In close consultation with the Evaluation Manager, the Evaluation Consultant will be responsible for the overall management of the Evaluation and timely provision of its outputs, data collection and analysis and report-writing. The Evaluation Team will work together to undertake the following: Inception phase of the Evaluation, including: • preliminary desk review and introductory interviews with project staff; • draft the reconstructed Theory of Change of the project; • prepare the evaluation framework; • develop the desk review and interview protocols; • draft the survey protocols (if relevant); • develop and present criteria for country and/or site selection for the evaluation mission; • plan the evaluation schedule; • prepare the Inception Report, incorporating comments until approved by the Evaluation Manager Data collection and analysis phase of the Evaluation, including: • conduct further desk review and in-depth interviews with project implementing and executing agencies, project partners and project stakeholders; • interview project partners and stakeholders, and ensure independence of the Evaluation and confidentiality of evaluation interviews. • regularly report back to the Evaluation Manager on progress and inform of any possible problems or issues encountered and; • keep the Project Manager informed of the evaluation progress. Reporting phase, including: • draft the Main Evaluation Report, ensuring that the evaluation report is complete, coherent and consistent with the Evaluation Manager guidelines both in substance and style; • liaise with the Evaluation Manager on comments received and finalize the Main Evaluation Report, ensuring that comments are taken into account until approved by the Evaluation Manager • prepare a Response to Comments annex for the main report, listing those comments not accepted by the Evaluation Consultant and indicating the reason for the rejection; and • (where agreed with the Evaluation Manager) prepare an Evaluation Brief (2-page summary of the evaluand and the key evaluation findings and lessons) Managing relations, including: • maintain a positive relationship with evaluation stakeholders, ensuring that the evaluation process is as participatory as possible but at the same time maintains its independence; • communicate in a timely manner with the Evaluation Manager on any issues requiring its attention and intervention. The Evaluation Consultant shall have had no prior involvement in the formulation or implementation of UNEP projects and programmes and will be independent from the participating institutions. The consultant will sign the Evaluation Consultant Code of Conduct Agreement Form. The Evaluation Consultant will be selected and recruited by the UNEP Evaluation Office through a consultancy contract. Comprehensive Terms of Reference will be shared with the consultant separately. Qualifications/special skills Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in environmental sciences, international development or other relevant political or social sciences area is required. A first level university degree (Bachelor's degree or equivalent) in the same areas in combination with two (2) additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced degree. A minimum of seven (7) years of technical expertise in environmental sciences, environmental governance, international development or relevant social or political sciences is required. A good understanding of environmental treaties, partnerships and collaboration among environmental institutions is desirable. Evaluation experience, preferably including evaluating national, regional or global programmes and using a Theory of Change approach, is an added advantage. Working knowledge of the UN system and specifically the work of UNEP is desirable. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this consultancy, fluency in oral and written English is required. Additional Information Not available. No Fee THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS.
