postings.text: Senior Officer, Research & Innovation Partnerships | IRC - International Rescue Committee Skip to main content Senior Officer, Research & Innovation Partnerships IRC - International Rescue Committee Remote | New York City International Senior level Speaks Arabic, French, Spanish Apply Summary by Impactpool The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is seeking a Senior Officer for Research & Innovation Partnerships to enhance funding for its research and innovation initiatives. This role involves collaborating with high-value fundraisers and technical experts to create compelling donor-facing materials and manage funding proposals. The officer will also maintain communication between teams, track funding opportunities, and ensure compliance with donor requirements. The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in fundraising and excellent writing skills to translate complex research into accessible content. Candidate Requirements: 6-7 years of experience in fundraising or partnerships Experience securing multi-million-dollar funding Outstanding writing skills for non-expert audiences Experience managing complex proposals and grants Knowledge of fundraising and grants management processes Excellent relationship management and communication skills Experience working with global, cross-cultural teams The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised. Job Background/Overview: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people affected by humanitarian crises to survive, recover and rebuild their lives. The Airbel Impact Lab is the research and innovation arm of the IRC. Airbel designs, tests, and scales cost-effective solutions for people affected by conflict and disaster, from new tools and technologies to cost analysis and rigorous research on what works. To keep innovating and deliver on its annual operating budget of about $25 million, Airbel relies on flexible private funding as well as project funding for impact and cost evidence generation in areas such as nutrition and immunization. We are seeking a Senior Officer, Research & Innovation Partnerships to help raise this funding. This role supports the IRC’s high-value fundraising teams, who work with major individual donors, corporate partners, and foundations, to secure  funding for research and innovation (R&I). It also helps Airbel put its work in front of the right donors without pulling the Airbel team away from their core work. You will turn technical findings into compelling, accurate donor-facing material, guide each opportunity from first lead to proposal submission, and keep both sides informed as awards are delivered.  Major Responsibilities: You will work alongside the IRC’s high-value fundraisers, Airbel innovation project leads and researchers, program and technical experts, and finance and support teams to raise the profile of, and increase private funding for, the IRC’s research and innovation work. This role coordinates and connects technical expertise from Airbel’s experts with donor strategy and relationships led by fundraisers. Your job is to make sure both teams have what they need, when they need it, and to own the quality of what is produced along the way. The major responsibilities will include: Turn research and innovation into donor-ready content (30%) Draft donor-facing materials in partnership with Airbel teams, including pitch decks, one-pagers, briefing notes, and proposal narratives, tailored to each audience (individual philanthropists, corporate partners, foundations and trusts) so that what reaches reviewers is close to final rather than a blank template. Get involved at the start of each product, helping decide whether the audience needs a punchy high-level pitch or deeper technical content and shaping a clear outline, and at the end, rewriting dense technical content for external readers and polishing the final format. Build clear, evidence-based arguments that read as both visionary and grounded, using facts and figures accurately and without losing what is actually true about the work. Help fundraisers and Airbel leaders position Airbel’s funding priorities (core funding, pooled funds, and project funding) with the donors most likely to care about each, and shape project ideas and funding pitches that are ready for donor conversations. Share knowledge and build the pipeline (20%) Be the fundraisers’ go-to source for what is happening in R&I right now: innovation opportunities, evidence generation priorities, project milestones, funding needs, and results worth sharing. Give fundraisers a heads-up on wins or risks before important donor conversations. Maintain and regularly update the tracker of private funding opportunities and awards for R&I, and flag new opportunities as soon as they are identified. Pass donor interest, feedback, and trends back to Airbel so teams know where to focus their pitch and proposal effort next. Support donor mapping, targeting, and briefings for R&I prospects, and help fundraisers track donor activity and progress toward revenue goals, including linkages with the organizations Impact at Scale funding priorities and other strategic initiatives. Work with Airbel leaders and fundraisers on strategy and pipeline development for priority areas, such as cost analysis, evidence generation, and innovative approaches that are ready to scale. Stay current on developments in humanitarian research and innovation, and on trends in private philanthropy, to inform fundraising efforts. Manage opportunities and proposals from first lead to submission (30%) Run the go/no-go process (the decision on whether to pursue an opportunity) for R&I-linked funding opportunities: gather what the fundraiser knows about the gift, such as its value, timeline, donor restrictions, and likelihood; present it to Airbel in a format that supports a quick, clear decision; and start the internal approval workflow once a decision is made. Project-manage private donor proposals and reports from start to finish, including timelines, reviewers, and inputs from program, finance, and technical teams. Take ownership of content quality and the overall outcome, not just the workplan and reminders. Check draft proposals, budgets, and agreements against donor and IRC requirements before they go to the fundraiser, and confirm that internal approvals, waivers, and sign-offs happen at each stage so nothing stalls further down the line. Coordinate answers to donor questions and any revisions after a proposal is submitted. As needed, join donor meetings to provide technical expertise and strategy support. Ensure strong coordination with other Program Services team members and program units for decision-making and shared workflows on complex cross-departmental or multisectoral proposals Connect teams, improve how we work, and support active grants (20%) Connect the right people at the right time. When a donor question, pitch, or site visit comes up, quickly route fundraisers to the right Airbel colleague, and route Airbel colleagues to the right fundraiser, setting up direct conversations between program leads and account managers rather than acting as a go-between. Help prepare Airbel colleagues for donor meetings. Help develop and document simple, clear ways of working between fundraising and Airbel teams, such as when each side should expect to hear from or update the other, and coordinate effective cross-team meetings with timely follow-up on decisions. For active awards, work with Airbel teams and fundraisers to track implementation and spending, and flag risks, delays, or amendment needs early. Coordinate reporting inputs and amendment documentation so donor reports are timely and high quality. Contribute to long-term donor relationships by ensuring donor requirements and compliance obligations are met throughout the life of a grant. Work closely with other Program Services team members to ensure ways of working for R&I fundraising are aligned with those of other departments such as Crisis Response, Recovery, and Development (CRRD), Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI), et al.  Essential Qualifications: 6-7 years of related work experience in fundraising, partnerships, program development, or communications, preferably with a mission-driven organization Experience contributing directly to securing multi-million-dollar funding for evidence generation, innovation, or other technical programming, including with private philanthropy, such as major donors, corporate partners, or foundations, Outstanding writing skills, with a demonstrated ability to quickly get up to speed on technical content and turn highly technical or research content into clear, compelling material for non-expert audiences (a writing sample may be requested). Experience managing complex proposals, grants, or similar projects from start to finish, with a track record of delivering high-quality results under tight deadlines Experience with fundraising and grants management processes, including budgets, donor requirements, and reporting Excellent relationship management and communication skills, including the ability to build trust and influence senior colleagues without direct authority over them Experience working across diverse contexts with global, cross-cultural teams, including collaborating remotely Desired Qualifications: Familiarity with how social innovation, evidence generation, or cost-effectiveness analysis is used in humanitarian or global development work Experience with customer relationship management (CRM) or pipeline tracking tools Knowledge of other IRC languages (Spanish, French, Arabic) would be an asset We strongly encourage applications from candidates who have lived experience in the contexts where the IRC operates Working Environment:  This role may require working remotely, and occasional travel. If remote, applicants must have a home or alternate workspace they can effectively complete their work from during regularly scheduled hours. Compensation: (Pay Rate: $93,000-$106,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget.  Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.  Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct . Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding , Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients. postings.text: Cryogenic Materials Engineer (EN-MME-MM-2026-175-GRAP) | CERN - European Organization for Nuclear Research Skip to main content Cryogenic Materials Engineer (EN-MME-MM-2026-175-GRAP) CERN - European Organization for Nuclear Research Geneva Mid level Speaks English, French Application deadline: December 06, 2026 (20 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Cryogenic Materials Engineer will contribute to materials characterization and qualification activities for various CERN projects. Responsibilities include planning and executing studies on materials, overseeing quality control for particle accelerator construction, and investigating the properties and failure mechanisms of engineering materials. The role requires advanced analytical techniques and mechanical testing at cryogenic temperatures. Candidates should have a strong background in materials engineering and experience in a multidisciplinary laboratory setting. Candidate Requirements: Experience in materials engineering Background in experimental materials characterization Mechanical testing experience at cryogenic temperatures Hands-on experience in mechanical testing in liquid helium Ability to integrate materials characterization methods Proficiency in scientific software and scripting tools Strong organizational skills Clear technical communication skills Analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities Ability to work independently and collaboratively Spoken and written English, commitment to learn French Master's degree with 2-6 years experience or PhD with up to 3 years experience National of a CERN Member or Associate Member State Company Description Job Description As an Experienced Project Graduate, you will contribute to materials characterisation and qualification activities supporting a wide range of CERN projects and technologies. Your responsibilities will include supporting, planning and executing studies on materials and components, covering materials procurement, fabrication and assembly qualification, as well as overseeing quality control activities for the construction of particle accelerators. Working within the Materials & Metrology team, you will investigate the microstructure, chemical composition, properties and failure mechanisms of metallic and other engineering materials using the section's advanced characterisation capabilities, including light microscopy, Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), microanalysis, X-ray diffraction (XRD), hardness testing and instrumented indentation. You will also perform mechanical testing at both ambient and cryogenic temperatures, including fracture toughness assessments, and conduct failure analyses when required. Your responsibilities: Investigate the behaviour, properties and failure mechanisms of engineering materials and components. Characterise materials using advanced analytical techniques, including light and electron microscopy (SEM), Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS), Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD), Focused Ion Beam (FIB), X-ray diffraction (XRD), automated image analysis and instrumented indentation, including nanoindentation and atomic force microscopy (AFM). Plan and perform mechanical testing at room and cryogenic temperatures, and help in the development of dedicated test facilities, experimental procedures, and data analysis protocols. Lead the execution of failure analyses of materials and components, combining microstructural and mechanical characterisation with non-destructive examination methods, including visual inspection (VT), penetrant testing (PT), ultrasonic testing (UT), radiographic testing (RT) and computed tomography (CT). Develop testing strategies and communicate results by defining appropriate test programmes, improving characterisation methodologies and presenting findings to CERN project teams, industrial partners and research institutes. Your profile: Experience in materials engineering, with a strong background in performing experimental materials characterisation and mechanical testing at cryogenic temperatures. Experience working in a multidisciplinary materials laboratory equipped for metallurgical analysis and mechanical testing. Would be considered as an asset: Experience in advanced mechanical testing in liquid helium (fracture toughness, fatigue), including experimental implementation and evaluation of test results. Experience in interpretation of NDT results (RT, PT, CT, UT) applied to assess material soundness. Skills: Hands-on experience in mechanical testing of structural materials in liquid helium. Ability to integrate complementary materials characterisation methods (SEM/EDS, XRD, EBSD) to address complex technical materials challenges. Ability to process and interpret experimental data using scientific software and scripting tools. Strong organisational skills to coordinate experimental campaigns. Clear technical communication and reporting skills. Analytical thinking and effective problem-solving abilities. Ability to work independently and collaboratively. Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French. Eligibility criteria: You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State . You have a professional background in Materials / Mechanical Engineering (or a related field) and have either: a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience; or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience. You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before. Qualifications Additional Information Job closing date: 06.12.2026 at 23:59 CET. Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum. Working hours: 40 hours per week Job flexibility: Fully Onsite Target start date: 01-April-2027 This position involves: A valid driving licence. Job reference: EN-MME-MM-2026-175-GRAP Field of work: Chemical, Materials & Process Engineering Benchmark job: 200080 - Material Science/Chemical Engineer/Chemist Global Benefits A monthly net stipend of either 6372 or 7004 Swiss Francs per month depending on your degree. 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure. Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund. Family, child and infant monthly allowances depending on your individual circumstances. A relocation package (installation grant and travel expenses) depending on your individual circumstances. Our groundbreaking work brings together not only physicists but also a diverse range of professionals from engineering, technical, scientific, and administrative fields. Together, we foster an environment where innovation and collaboration thrive. Every day, we face exciting new challenges and opportunities to contribute to cutting-edge research that shapes our understanding of the universe. We meet these challenges through the diverse perspectives within our teams, ensuring every contribution is valued and driving our shared sense of inclusion and purpose. Diversity is a core value of CERN since its foundation, and it remains central to our mission and continued success. About the Country/Multi-Country Office The East Asia and Pacific Multi-Country Office (EAPMCO), headquartered in Bangkok, supports UNOPS operations across 24 countries in Southeast Asia, Northeast Asia, and the Pacific. Established in January 2023, EAPMCO provides strategic direction, operational support, and quality assurance to ensure the efficient and effective delivery of projects across its portfolio. EAPMCO implements initiatives in priority areas such as energy transition, climate change, and sustainable development, drawing on UNOPS' core expertise in human resources, procurement, infrastructure, fund management, and programme management. About the Project Office UNOPS has supported Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2016, initially partnering with the Global Fund to strengthen public health services. In 2020, a dedicated country office was established to manage UNOPS’ growing portfolio, which spans infrastructure, procurement, and project management. UNOPS currently works with the Government of PNG, the World Bank, the European Union, and the Governments of Australia and New Zealand on initiatives in health, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), and sustainable energy, supporting the country’s development priorities through tailored, results-driven solutions. Job Specific Context Organizational Context The South East Asia and Pacific Multi Country Office (EAPMCO)  supports, develops and oversees the UNOPS portfolio of projects in South East Asia and the Pacific. EAPMCO was established in January 2023 following the merger of the Thailand Multi-Country Office, which covered 20 countries across  North East Asia, South East Asia and the Pacific, and the Cambodia Multi-Country Office, which covered 4 countries South East Asia - 3 countries in the Mekong Sub-region (Cambodia, Lao PDR and Vietnam) and the Philippines.  EAPMCO currently covers 24 countries across North East Asia, South East Asia and the Pacific. With its head office in Bangkok, the Multi-Country Office comprises nine business units: EAPMCO Thailand, EAPMCO Indonesia,  EAPMCO Pacific Operations Cluster, EAPMCO Papua New Guinea, EAPMCO China, EAPMCO Vietnam, EAPMCO Mekong, and EAPMCO Philippines. In 2022, the UNOPS EAPMCO implemented projects worth more than USD 95.7 million, in the areas of Energy Transition, Digital Transformations, Sustainable Environmental Management, Climate Change, Waste Management, Rule of Law and Access to Justice, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Post Conflict Reintegration, Emergency Relief, Post COVID19 Economic Transformations, and Health, through HR, procurement, construction, contract management, fund and program management services.   The Multi Country Office head office in Bangkok provides strategic direction, operational support, delivery oversight and assurance of the excellence of business processes and quality standards across all of the entire Multi Country Office locations. It is also responsible for developing, delivering and managing the portfolio of engagements in the country of the MCO location itself. UNOPS in Papua New Guinea The EAPMCO Papua New Guinea was established in early 2020 to support the implementation of design and construction of infrastructure, sustainable procurement, capacity development to support technical and governance excellence, programme management, and to facilitate access to funding sources in Papua New Guinea.   As an established office since 2022, EAPMCO PNG is demonstrating significant growth and portfolio diversification potential in a short period of time. Working with an increasing number of development partners, in 2023 EAPMCO PNG is quickly being recognised as a responsive and quality partner in climate change resilient infrastructure, sustainable procurement and governance support to the Government of PNG in its service delivery obligations to the people. There are a number of projects currently in the pipeline which will expand the portfolio of existing projects for the office Background Information – Impact Health Phase 2 The “Improving Access to and Value from Health Services in PNG: Financing the Frontlines Project” (IMPACT Health Project) aims to address critical challenges in Papua New Guinea (PNG), including the lack of key infrastructure, medical instruments, and supplies necessary for effective health service delivery. The objective of the IMPACT Health Project is to increase the utilization of quality essential health services in the supported provinces: East New Britain, East Sepik, Central, and Chimbu. The government, through this initiative, plans to upgrade primary health care facilities by conducting comprehensive needs assessments and setting priorities for rehabilitation and equipment upgrades. Additionally, the IMPACT Health Project will strengthen the assessment and supervision of health facilities by implementing an integrated facility supportive supervision checklist. This engagement contributes to Component 1 - Increase service delivery readiness and community-based service delivery, and Component 2 - Improve frontline service delivery performance of the IMPACT Health Project. The specialist will also perform business analysis to support innovative workflows and system integrations. Using the world's largest and most complex scientific instruments, they study the basic constituents of matter - fundamental particles that are made to collide together at close to the speed of light. The process gives physicists clues about how particles interact, and provides insights into the fundamental laws of nature. Work during nights, Sundays and official holidays, when required by the needs of the Organization. Job grade: 4-5 Job reference: EN-IM-CEP-2026-224-LD Field of work: Mechanical Engineering Benchmark Job Title: Computing Technical Engineer Global Benefits A competitive salary  (tax free), increasing in line with your years of relevant experience. 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure. Your work will focus on the needs of the HL-LHC. You will help keep NXCALS fast, reliable and scalable as particle accelerator data volumes grow and the machine moves toward the High-Luminosity LHC era. You will work on a real production system alongside experienced engineers, with plenty of opportunities to learn and take ownership. They will work closely with the UN Women Georgia team and ensure that the meaning of the content remains intact during the editing process. This is a home-based consultancy position with no travel required. Candidate Requirements: Native Georgian speaker Excellent editing and proofreading skills Strong attention to detail Knowledge of editorial standards Ability to ensure clarity and quality of written materials Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security.  UN Women aims to enhance its communication and outreach efforts through the development of targeted and diverse digital visual materials and publications. Introduction Recrutement d’un consultant national en Suivi-Évaluation, Gestion Axée sur les Résultats (GAR), Qualité de Service et Satisfaction des Usagers pour appuyer le Ministère de la Sécurité Publique (MSP) et la Direction Générale du Trésor (DGT) 1. Contexte À la suite d’une demande officielle de la Présidence, le PNUD a soutenu l’établissement de la Facilité d’assistance technique (FAT) pour la Refondation de Madagascar au moyen d’un financement interne destiné à la phase de démarrage et aux premières interventions prioritaires. La FAT, officiellement lancée le 20 juillet 2026, constitue désormais un mécanisme gouvernemental piloté par la demande et structuré autour de trois objectifs globaux : (i) améliorer la gestion et la performance de l’administration publique ; (ii) accroître la rapidité et la qualité de la prestation des services publics, notamment par la numérisation ; et (iii) soutenir les réformes et transformations structurelles prioritaires. Avant le lancement, le PNUD a formé, pendant une série de formations de quatre jours, 218 points focaux à l’auto-évaluation de la fonction publique selon le Cadre d’auto-évaluation des fonctions publiques (CAF) et à l’élaboration de plans d’amélioration. Au total, 58 ministères et institutions publiques ont finalisé des plans d’amélioration couvrant une période de deux ans et ont soumis 210 projets sollicitant l’appui de la FAT. La gouvernance de la FAT est assurée par un Comité de pilotage interministériel chargé de fournir les orientations stratégiques, d’examiner et de prioriser les demandes d’assistance technique, et de veiller à leur alignement sur les priorités nationales. Présidé par la Présidence de la République, ce Comité est composé de représentants de la Primature, du ministère de l’Économie et des Finances (MEF), du ministère des Affaires étrangères (MAE) et du ministère de l’Intérieur et de la Décentralisation (MID). Le PNUD assure le secrétariat du Comité et apporte l’appui technique et opérationnel nécessaire à la préparation, à l’organisation et au suivi de ses travaux. Lors de sa session du 1er octobre 2026, le Comité de pilotage de la FAT a examiné ce portefeuille et retenu 64 projets dont 5 projets prioritaires pour une mise en œuvre immédiate. Il a reporté 130 projets en vue d’un examen, d’une maturation ou d’un financement ultérieur, tandis que 16 projets n’ont pas été approuvés. Ces décisions fournissent à la FAT une base opérationnelle concrète pour programmer l’assistance technique, mobiliser les ressources et suivre les résultats institutionnels. Les 5 projets prioritaires retenus pour une mise en œuvre immédiate sont ceux des institutions suivantes : Centre de Fusion Maritime rattaché à la Primature, Ministère de la Sécurité Publique, Direction Générale du Trésor, Ministère de la Justice et Fond du Développement Local rattaché au Ministère de l’Intérieur et de la Décentralisation. Le présent recrutement répond aux besoins de la Ministère de la Sécurité Publique et la Direction Générale du Trésor. 1. Profil recherché: - Titulaire d’un Bac+5 minimum en suivi-évaluation, gestion de projet, statistiques, économie, administration publique, sciences sociales ou domaine connexe. - Au moins 7 ans d'expérience professionnelle en suivi-évaluation, Gestion Axée sur les Résultats (GAR), qualité de service ou mesure de performance. - Expérience confirmée dans la conception et l'animation de formations en suivi-évaluation et renforcement des capacités. - Expérience dans la conception et la mise en œuvre d'enquêtes de satisfaction des usagers ou de dispositifs d'amélioration de la qualité de service. - Bonne connaissance du fonctionnement de l'administration publique et des projets de développement. - Excellentes capacités d'analyse, de rédaction et de facilitation d'ateliers. - Excellentes capacités rédactionnelles en français et en malgache. postings.text: UN Women National Consultant - Technical Coordinator – Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan | UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Skip to main content UN Women National Consultant - Technical Coordinator – Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Karachi National Mid level Speaks English, Urdu Apply Summary by Impactpool UN Women is seeking a National Consultant - Technical Coordinator in Karachi, Pakistan, to enhance coordination and collaboration among provincial women's machineries, government institutions, and civil society organizations. The consultant will facilitate stakeholder engagement, support implementation follow-up, and contribute to gender-responsive governance. This role involves maintaining knowledge of relevant legislation, tracking progress, and preparing documentation. The consultant will report to the Portfolio Manager and work closely with various stakeholders to ensure effective delivery of UN Women’s programs. Candidate Requirements: Master's degree in gender studies, law, social sciences, or related field 3 years of experience in program coordination or gender equality Understanding of Pakistan's gender equality context Familiarity with provincial government structures and women's machineries Experience in stakeholder engagement and coordination Strong communication and organizational skills Fluency in English and Urdu UN Women is the United Nations entity dedicated to advancing gender equality and the empowerment of women (GEWE), with a unique triple mandate integrating normative support, UN system coordination, and operational engagement. This enables UN Women to support governments in aligning national frameworks with international human rights commitments, while also strengthening implementation through coordinated, multi-stakeholder approaches. By linking policy development with practical interventions, UN Women advances progress across key priority areas, including women’s economic and social empowerment, legal reform, political participation, access to justice, and gender-responsive service delivery. In Pakistan, UN Women’s work is guided by its Strategic Note (2023–2027), which prioritizes inclusive governance, women’s leadership and participation, ending violence against women and girls, and women’s economic empowerment. As the lead agency for Outcome 2 of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework, UN Women plays a central role in ensuring that gender equality is systematically integrated across UN programming, while providing technical and policy support to government counterparts. At the institutional level, UN Women partners with national and provincial women’s machineries including Women Development Departments, Commissions on the Status of Women, Offices of the Ombudspersons, Women Parliamentary Caucuses, parliamentarians and legislative bodies, to strengthen capacities for developing, implementing, and monitoring gender-responsive laws and policies. These efforts are complemented by engagement with civil society and academia to promote inclusive, evidence-based policymaking and accountability. The objective of this consultancy is to strengthen coordination, collaboration and information-sharing among provincial women’s machineries, government institutions, civil society organizations and other relevant provincial stakeholders, in support of the effective implementation of gender equality and women’s empowerment commitments. The consultant will facilitate stakeholder engagement, support implementation follow-up, strengthen institutional linkages, and contribute to coordinated approaches that advance women’s rights, access to services, and gender-responsive governance at the provincial level.  Reporting to the Portfolio Manager, the Technical Coordinator will support UN Women’s engagement with provincial women’s machineries, government departments, civil society organizations and other stakeholders. The consultant will facilitate coordination processes, support implementation follow-up, strengthen stakeholder engagement, document progress and contribute to the effective delivery of UN Women’s programme interventions at the provincial level. Strategic Institutional Coordination Act as the liaison between provincial women’s machineries, including the Commission on the Status of Women, Women Development Department (or equivalent), Women Parliamentary Caucus, Ombudsperson's Office and other relevant stakeholders. Support coordination among provincial women’s machineries and relevant stakeholders to promote alignment between policy, legislative, oversight and service delivery functions. Maintain a working knowledge of provincial pro-women and gender-related legislation and policies, including on domestic violence, protection against harassment at the workplace, anti-rape, child marriage restraint, women’s property and inheritance rights, and home-based workers. Track the status of related rules, regulations, and implementation mechanisms, and use this understanding to support coordination, follow-up, policy dialogue, and advocacy with women’s machineries and relevant stakeholders.  Support the establishment and/ or strengthening of a standing provincial coordination mechanism (e.g., a joint coordination forum or inter-institutional working group) that brings together women’s machineries and relevant stakeholders to institutionalize coordination, moving beyond informal to regular, structured joint planning, review, information sharing, and accountability. Facilitate coordination meetings, technical consultations and stakeholder engagements, including preparation of agendas, documentation of proceedings and follow-up on agreed actions. Government and Civil Society Engagement Serve as the central point of contact for UN Women for coordination with women’s machineries to streamline communication. Support engagement between women’s machineries, civil society organizations, networks and relevant stakeholders to strengthen collaboration on GEWE priorities. Create structured pathways for Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and the EVAW Alliance to collaborate directly with government bodies. GEWE implementation & Monitoring Support monitoring and follow-up of agreed actions, commitments and programme activities related to gender equality and women’s empowerment. Develop and maintain implementation trackers, action matrices and coordination tools to monitor progress against agreed priorities. Proactively identify bottlenecks in provincial coordination and propose practical, efficient solutions. Knowledge Management & Reporting Prepare meeting minutes, briefing notes, consultation summaries and event reports. Maintain organized records of stakeholder engagements, coordination activities and programme documentation. Develop periodic updates highlighting progress, challenges and recommendations. Support preparation of knowledge products, advocacy materials and communication outputs, as required. Ensure documentation and reporting are aligned with UN Women standards and requirements. Reporting: The consultant will report to the Portfolio Manager, EVAW, Governance and Human Rights, with guidance from the Portfolio Manager, WEE and Humanitarian Affairs. Day-to-day technical coordination will be provided by the designated Provincial Focal Point, in close collaboration with the relevant UN Women programme teams. The consultant will work closely with provincial government counterparts, women’s machineries, civil society organizations and other stakeholders, as required for the effective implementation of the assignment. The consultant will maintain regular communication with UN Women and provide periodic updates on progress, challenges and follow-up actions. All deliverables shall be submitted to UN Women for review and approval in accordance with the agreed workplan and payment schedule. UN Women will provide relevant background materials, technical guidance and facilitate introductions with key institutional counterparts, as required. The consultant will be responsible for arranging their own office space, equipment and communication tools necessary for the assignment. Official travel undertaken as part of the assignment and approved in advance by UN Women will be covered in accordance with UN Women’s applicable travel policies and procedures. Where required, UN Women may facilitate access to meeting venues and institutional coordination platforms for consultations, meetings and stakeholder engagement activities. Duration: The assignment will be from 15 December 2026 to 31 March 2027 Education: Master's degree in gender studies, women’s studies, law, social sciences, development studies, international relations or another relevant field. A Bachelor’s degree with two additional years of relevant experience may be accepted in lieu of a Master’s degree. Experience: A minimum of three (3) years of relevant professional experience in programme coordination, stakeholder engagement, governance, gender equality, human rights, social development, public policy, or related fields. Sound understanding of Pakistan's gender equality, women’s empowerment and human rights context, including familiarity with relevant national frameworks and international commitments such as CEDAW, the Beijing Platform for Action and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Familiarity with provincial government structures, women’s machineries and institutional mechanisms related to gender equality and women’s empowerment. Working knowledge of provincial pro-women and gender-related legislation and its implementation status, including the associated rules, regulations, oversight bodies, enforcement arrangements, and redress mechanisms governing key laws related to women’s rights, protection, empowerment, and gender equality. Experience working with government institutions, commissions, ombudsperson offices, civil society organizations, development partners, academia, or other relevant stakeholders. Experience coordinating meetings, consultations, workshops and stakeholder engagement processes, including preparation of presentations, meeting minutes, briefing notes, reports and other documentation. Experience supporting programme implementation, coordination, monitoring, reporting and follow-up of agreed actions. Experience engaging and coordinating with multiple stakeholders and building effective working relationships. Experience in gender equality, women’s empowerment, governance, human rights, access to justice, social protection or related areas will be an asset. Previous experience working with the United Nations system or other international development organizations will be an asset. Competencies: Strong interpersonal and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with diverse partners. Strong organizational, coordination and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple assignments simultaneously. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including drafting reports, meeting minutes and correspondence. Ability to work independently and proactively while maintaining close coordination with supervisors and team members. Ability to identify challenges, propose practical solutions and support follow-up actions. Ability to work effectively in multicultural and multidisciplinary environments. Familiarity with coordination mechanisms, referral pathways, governance structures or institutional strengthening processes will be an asset. Language Requirements: Fluency in English and Urdu. postings.text: IT Service Officer | EC - European Commission Skip to main content IT Service Officer EC - European Commission Luxembourg Both national and international FG IV, Function Group 4, Contract Agent level Speaks English Application deadline: November 27, 2026 (11 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The European Commission is seeking an IT Service Officer to support governance, risk, compliance, communication, and awareness in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI). This role involves leading a team in Luxembourg and Brussels, ensuring compliance with the EU AI Act, and developing corporate-level communication and training initiatives. The position requires collaboration with various departments to promote the use of secure AI and manage AI-related stakeholders. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in AI technologies and project management, along with excellent communication skills. Candidate Requirements: Practical experience in AI systems development Knowledge of AI technologies Experience in regulatory supervision Experience in IT/AI governance preparation Project management and team leadership experience Professional experience in an international environment Master's degree in IT or related field At least one year of relevant technical experience Excellent English communication skills Experience in delivering trainings and presentations Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities High customer orientation and flexibility VACANCY NOTICE FOR A CONTRACT AGENT SELECTION Job title IT Service Officer Reference EC-2026-DIGIT-456893 Application deadline 27.11.2026 - 12.00 (noon, Brussels time) Directorate-General (full name) DG Digital Services Unit DIGIT.B.1, 'Data, Artificial Intelligence & Web' Place of assignment Luxembourg Domain* Information technology Contract type and Function Group Contract Agent 3b FG IV Other useful information (contract duration, other ...) *please use one of the standardised domains that can be found here About us This is an opportunity to work in a collaborative team withing the Directorate-General for Digital Services ( DG DIGIT ) in the European Commission. DIGIT serves leading authority on IT enablers and drivers, overseeing the Commission's digital transformation and the evolution of its IT delivery model. The directorate is particularly focused on harnessing emerging technologies, utilizing data, and leveraging internal expertise. Through its digital technology and services DIGIT ensures that the digital environment in which the Commission operates is robust, resilient and secure, supports digital-ready policy making across the Commission and facilitates stronger collaboration between Europe and Public administrations. DIGIT.B.1 Data, Artificial intelligence and Web mission is to provide digital enablers for the transformation of the Commission ICT domain in the areas of data, artificial intelligence and web presence. Additionally, the unit fosters innovation at corporate level through the management of the digital innovation policy framework. Regarding Artificial Intelligence the unit oversees and leads the implementation of the AI@EC Communication that articulates the Commission's strategic vision to foster the development and adoption of lawful, safe and trustworthy Artificial Intelligence system within the Commission and provides supporting services on AI Governance, compliance and risk. About the role Unit B.1 of DG DIGIT is seeking to hire one IT Service Officer for the activities of the Data, AI and Innovation policy sector. The position will consist of providing services that support governance, risk, compliance, communication and awareness raising in the field of AI. The services also relate to the development and execution of the AI@EC Communication programme that establishes the AI governance in the Commission and the practical measures to promote the use of secure AI. This entails visibility and contact with all the Departments (DGs) in the Commission from the most advanced on AI, to the ones that want to increase their AI usage. The role offers visibility across all Commission DGs, from those with advanced AI capabilities to those seeking to expand their use of AI. Your role is to lead a team in Luxembourg and Brussels to support Commission AI governance, ensure compliance with the EU AI Act, other relevant regulations, and internal guidelines of Commission's AI solutions, and develop corporate-level communication, collaborate in the creation of trainings and awareness initiatives for general staff, managers, and AI specialists. You will establish the technical vision, oversee and participate in team activities, create business cases and deliver models for the services—sometimes with external partners. Additionally, you will liaise with other AI related stakeholders via the management of the Interservice Steering Group on AI and the different AI related interservice working groups, and prepare reports for the Unit, the management of the Directorate and corporate boards. Relevant topics to follow are high-risk use cases, transparency, AI explainability, cybersecurity, risk management, etc. Qualifications, experience and skills We are looking for a candidate who will demonstrate some of the following required skills and characteristics: Practical experience in the development of AI based systems, AI models development and evaluation including alignment. Knowledge/understanding of AI technologies Knowledge/experience of regulatory supervision and enforcement in any related domain. Knowledge/experience in the preparation of IT/AI governance, guides, instructions and procedures. Project management, team leadership and budget management experience Additional expertise or academic background on real matters. Professional experience in an international and multicultural environment. The ideal candidate will possess some, or all of the following: A master's degree in IT, computer science, engineering/science or other relevant domain. At least one year of experience as a research scientist, computer scientist, software and data engineer, hardware specialist or other technical staff. Project management, team leadership and budget management experience. Experience working in complex public or private environments. Excellent written and spoken English communication skills. Experience delivering trainings and public presentations. Commitment to ongoing technical and personal development. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, able to manage multiple tasks and large volumes of information under time constraints. High customer orientation, commitment, and flexibility. postings.text: Procurement Associate II | ILRI - International Livestock Research Institute Skip to main content Procurement Associate II ILRI - International Livestock Research Institute Nairobi HG11 level Application deadline: November 24, 2026 (8 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI) is seeking a Procurement Associate II to provide day-to-day procurement support for Nairobi operations. This role involves routine purchasing, quotation administration, purchase order preparation, and supplier documentation management. The successful candidate will maintain accurate electronic records and assist with compliance and audit support. The position requires a diploma in procurement or a related field and at least three years of relevant experience. Candidate Requirements: Diploma in procurement or related field At least three years in purchasing support Relevant procurement training or certification Understanding of procurement documentation Accurate data entry and record keeping Ability to use spreadsheets and procurement systems Clear communication skills Strong organizational skills Integrity and confidentiality awareness The International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI) seeks to recruit a Procurement Associate II to provides day-to-day procurement support for Nairobi operations, reporting to the Procurement Officer. The role supports routine purchasing, quotation administration, purchase order preparation, supplier documentation, delivery follow-up and accurate electronic records, within delegated authority. ILRI is an international organisation working for better lives and better planet through livestock. ILRI’s mission emphasises the interconnections between people, animals, and the environment, aiming to improve the lives of more than 300 million people in low- and middle-income countries through livestock science that supports equitable and resilient livestock systems, ultimately contributing to food systems transformation with climate and environmental benefits. This mission is delivered through two core strategic objectives: co-designing and deploying sustainable, science-based livestock solutions, and leveraging science to inform and influence policy and investment decisions. ILRI is a member of the CGIAR, a global research alliance that works to transform food, land and water systems in a climate crisis and is the only CGIAR centre dedicated to addressing multiple development challenges through sustainable livestock solutions. Key Responsibilities: A. Procurement Operations & Planning Check requisitions for completeness, specifications and required approvals before processing or referral. Process assigned routine purchases within delegated authority and approved procedures; refer exceptions to the supervisor. Maintain procurement trackers and assist with compiling departmental procurement requirements. B. Sourcing & Tender Management Prepare routine requests for quotations using approved templates and guidance. Collect quotations and compile comparison schedules for review without assuming approval authority. Support tender administration, supplier communications and evaluation documentation while maintaining confidentiality. C. Contract & Supplier Management Collect supplier onboarding and due-diligence documents for review. Prepare purchase orders and routine contract documentation for checking and approval. Maintain supplier and contract records, flagging missing documents, expiry dates and delivery issues. D. Digital Procurement & Data Management Enter and update approved procurement transactions and supplier information in designated systems. Maintain electronic procurement files and routine order-status reports. Check records for completeness and accuracy and refer discrepancies for correction. E. Compliance, Risk & Audit Support Follow applicable procurement procedures, approval requirements and segregation of duties. Flag missing approvals, incomplete specifications, conflicts of interest and unusual supplier requests. Retrieve and organise supporting records for compliance checks and audits. F. Logistics & Order Fulfilment Follow up purchase orders and delivery schedules with suppliers and Stores/Logistics. Help reconcile order, receipt and invoice documentation and escalate discrepancies. G. Stakeholder Engagement & Service Delivery Provide routine updates to requesters on quotations, orders and deliveries. Explain standard documentation requirements and refer technical or policy queries to the supervisor. H. Continuous Improvement & Other Duties Suggest practical improvements to trackers, filing and routine procurement administration. Perform other related duties as assigned within the scope of the role. Requirements Diploma in procurement, supply chain management, business administration or a related field At least three years in routine purchasing support, quotation administration, order tracking, supplier records and electronic procurement filing. Relevant procurement or supply chain professional training; certification level Understanding of routine purchasing and procurement documentation. Accurate data entry, record keeping and attention to detail. Ability to use spreadsheets and designated procurement systems. Clear communication and responsive service to internal customers. Organisation, follow-up and ability to prioritise routine tasks. Integrity, confidentiality and awareness of approval boundaries. Post location : The position will be based in Nairobi, Kenya Terms of Appointment This position is at job level HG11 and it is only open to Kenyan nationals. The position is on a 1 Year fixed term contract. ILRI offers a competitive salary and benefits package which includes pension, medical and other insurances. We thank all applicants for their interest in working for ILRI. Due to the volume of applications, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted . ILRI does not charge a fee at any stage of the recruitment process (application, interview meeting, processing or training). postings.title: Vacancy notice – Political Officer - Contract Agent FGIV - EU DELEGATION TO LIBYA - Job No 383103 EEAS - European External Action Service Tripoli FG IV, Function Group 4, Contract Agent - Consultancy
postings.text: Vacancy notice – Political Officer - Contract Agent FGIV - EU DELEGATION TO LIBYA - Job No 383103 | EEAS - European External Action Service Skip to main content Vacancy notice – Political Officer - Contract Agent FGIV - EU DELEGATION TO LIBYA - Job No 383103 EEAS - European External Action Service Tripoli Both national and international FG IV, Function Group 4, Contract Agent level Speaks Arabic, English, French Application deadline: November 30, 2026 (14 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The European External Action Service (EEAS) is seeking a Political Officer to join the Political, Press and Information Section of its Delegation in Tripoli, Libya. The successful candidate will coordinate the EU's political relations with Libya, monitor and analyze political developments, and provide advice on policy issues. This role requires strong interpersonal skills, the ability to work under tight deadlines, and experience in diplomatic relations. Candidates must have passed the EPSO CAST exam and meet specific educational and language requirements. Candidate Requirements: Passed EPSO CAST in FG IV or registered in EPSO Permanent CAST Completed university studies of at least three years or equivalent professional training Capacity to work in English and French Strong interpersonal skills Ability to analyze and report on political matters Experience in diplomatic relations and political developments Knowledge of EU institutions and CFSP Good knowledge of Libya and regional political dynamics Contract type: Contract Agent Deadline for applications is 30/11/2026 at 12.00 hours (midday, Brussels time) . WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. WE PROPOSE The position of Political Officer, contract agent FGIV as per Article 3a of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (hereafter, the “CEOS”).  Subject to having passed the CAST exam, the successful candidate will be offered a contract agent position (Function Group IV), as per Article 3a of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS), on the basis of a contract with an initial duration of 3 years. This contract may be renewed not more than once for a fixed period of not more than 5 years. Any further renewal shall be for an indefinite period. PLACE OF EMPLOYMENT City, COUNTRY:                             Tripoli, LIBYA  LCA:                                                   40% POST AVAILABLE:                           Immediately LEGAL BASIS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THIS POSITION The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions foreseen in the relevant provisions of the CEOS, in particular Article 82 thereof.  WE LOOK FOR A highly motivated and dynamic colleague to work to join the Political, Press and Information Section of the Delegation. Under the authority of the Head of Section, the selected candidate will contribute to the work of the Delegation in coordinating the EU's political relations with the host country and in representing the Delegation as necessary. She or he will be required to monitor and contribute to analysis and reporting on the overall situation and development in Libya, including on regional level and on political relations with the EU and Member States. The Political Officer will liaise regularly with Headquarters and provide advice, as appropriate, on policy issues, as well as briefing dossiers, speeches, statements, press releases and articles, as requested. Eligibility criteria According to the conditions set out in Article 82 of the CEOS and in the  Commission Decision C(2017) 6760 , which is applicable to the EEAS by virtue of the  Decision ADMIN(2018) 4 of the High Representative , in order to be eligible for this post of contract agent FG IV, candidates must: have passed a valid EPSO CAST in FG IV; or be registered in the EPSO Permanent CAST for FG IV ( https://epso.europa.eu/en/job-opportunities/open-for-application ). In the latter case, while the registration will render the candidate eligible for the selection procedure, the recruitment of a candidate on this vacant post will be subject to his/her successfully passing the CAST exam; meet the minimum qualifications for engagement as contract agent FG IV: (i) have a level of education which corresponds to completed university studies of at least three years attested by a diploma, or (ii) where justified in the interest of the service, professional training of an equivalent level (related to the nature of the tasks and qualifications indicated in the job description); have the capacity to work in languages of CFSP and external relations (English and French) necessary for the performance of their duties; be a national of one of the Member States of the EU and enjoy full rights as a citizen . Selection criteria The candidates should have: Strong interpersonal skills; Capacity to analyse and structure information; Demonstrated ability to accurately report on sensitive political matters under strict and tight deadlines; Ability to maintaining and further developing a positive work environment; Ability to work in a different socio-cultural environment and to adapt quickly to evolving situations; Experience in reaching out to and working with foreign governments, diplomatic representations, international organisations and the civil society on matters related to political developments, especially human rights; Expert knowledge of EU institutions, policies, decision-making processes and instruments, particularly related to the CFSP;  Proven experience as political officer or manager of political files; Good knowledge of Libya and political dynamics of the wider region; Ability to work in a crisis-prone environment, with composure and adaptation to stressful situations. Furthermore: Experience in EU external relations; Experience on bilateral economic and trade files; Experience in handling secure communications and classified information; Knowledge of IT tools used in EU institutions; Experience of working in a team in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural environment; Capacity to work in languages of the CFSP and external relations necessary for the performance of their duties (EN and FR); Knowledge of Arabic will be considered as assets. POSTING POLICY EEAS career development policy places the need for staff to develop a mix of competences at its core, e.g. working in various fields of expertise and responsibilities in the course of a person's career, including postings at Headquarters and Delegations.  Contract staff in Delegations is usually posted for 2, 3, 4 or 6 years in a given EU Delegation. Call for interest to apply for postponement or early mobility will be launched annually prior to the publication of the mobility exercise. Staff are reminded that extension and early mobility are not a right. Contract staff assigned to a post where the living conditions allowance (LCA) determined in accordance with Article 10 of Annex X to the Staff Regulations of Officials of the EU (SR) is 30% or 35% may participate in the mobility exercise after 4 years . Contract staff assigned to a post where the LCA is 40% may participate in the mobility exercise after 3 years . Contract staff assigned to a non-family post may participate in the mobility exercise after 2 years .  For candidates currently posted in compound-confined, non-family posting, please refer to Article 6, point (2)(g) of the Decision ADMIN(2024) 20 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 24/07/2024 on the periodic serving of Officials and Temporary Agents in Union Delegations and repealing Decision ADMIN(2021) 221 of 1 July 2021ADMIN(2021) 221. Within the mobility exercise, contract staff may be temporarily assigned to the EEAS Headquarters in Brussels; such assignment shall remain exceptional and depends on the availability of posts. The assignment shall be for no less than two years, unless a derogation is granted by the Head of the Division RM.BHR.3 ‘Selection and Recruitment’ in the interest of the service. The assignment shall be for no more than four years, in accordance with Article 118 of the CEOS and Article 3 of Annex X to the SR. The member of contract staff temporarily assigned to the EEAS Headquarters shall be included in the mobility exercise in time to be reassigned to a Union Delegation before he/she reaches the maximum period of 4 years. Candidates currently in the EEAS Headquarters are expected to have served at least three years in the Headquarters by the expected time of posting in Delegation. Derogation to this rule may only be granted by the Authority Authorised to Conclude Contracts of Employment (hereafter, “AACC”) in the interest of the service. External candidates may also apply to any vacancy position published for posts in Delegations. It is in the interest of the service to ensure that staff members in Delegations are able to complete full postings before reaching the age of retirement. Before taking its decision on recruitment, the AACC will ensure on a case-by-case basis, in accordance with the SR and CEOS, that the successful candidates will be able to complete the relevant full posting for the post for which they are selected. Applications from candidates not fulfilling this requirement will be examined by the AACC for exceptional and justified reasons and in the interest of the service. CONDITIONS OF RECRUITMENT AND EMPLOYMENT CONFLICT OF INTEREST AND SECURITY RISKS As a matter of policy, applications of individuals who have dual nationality, including one of a non-EU country or of the host country, or whose spouse or partner has the nationality of the host country, will be considered on a case-by-case basis. In that regard, the EEAS also examines if there could be a conflict of interest and shall also take into account any specific local and global-security-context, diplomatic or other concerns about the personal security of the candidate or to the security interests of the Union. In this context, candidates shall fill in with their application a declaration of potential conflict of interest . PERSONNEL SECURITY CLEARANCE The requested level of security clearance for this post is: SECRET UE/EU SECRET. A description of the EU classified information levels is available under Article 2 of Annex A of the  Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS . The selected candidate should hold, or be in the position to obtain, a valid Personnel Security Clearance (hereafter, the PSC) issued by the competent authority of the Member State concerned.  Ca

postings.text: Consultant Administration and Communication | ILRI - International Livestock Research Institute Skip to main content Consultant Administration and Communication ILRI - International Livestock Research Institute Guwahati Junior level Speaks English Application deadline: November 23, 2026 (7 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI) is seeking a Consultant for Administration and Communication to support the project aimed at enhancing the livelihoods of pig farmers in Northeast India. The role involves providing technical guidance, designing communication materials, coordinating events, and maintaining effective communication with stakeholders. The consultant will also assist with administrative and financial tasks related to the project. This position is open to Indian nationals and offers a competitive consultancy fee based on qualifications and experience. Candidate Requirements: Master’s degree in relevant field At least two years of relevant work experience Strong knowledge of communication strategies Ability to design and format communication materials Experience in organizing meetings and workshops Excellent interpersonal skills Strong verbal and written communication skills in English Ability to handle administrative tasks Ability to multitask with minimal supervision Willingness to travel within India Excellent computer skills The International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI) seeks to recruit a Consultant Administration and Communication to provide administrative and communication support for the implementation of the project “Reviving and Protecting Piggery Farmers’ Livelihoods in Northeast India”. ILRI is an international organisation working for better lives and better planet through livestock. ILRI’s mission emphasises the interconnections between people, animals, and the environment, aiming to improve the lives of more than 300 million people in low- and middle-income countries through livestock science that supports equitable and resilient livestock systems, ultimately contributing to food systems transformation with climate and environmental benefits. This mission is delivered through two core strategic objectives: co-designing and deploying sustainable, science-based livestock solutions, and leveraging science to inform and influence policy and investment decisions. ILRI is a member of the CGIAR, a global research alliance that works to transform food, land and water systems in a climate crisis and is the only CGIAR centre dedicated to addressing multiple development challenges through sustainable livestock solutions. Scope of Work of the Consultant Provide technical guidance and support to the field staff in running awareness and knowledge and behavioural change communication at community level. Design, draft, review, edit, and format communication products, including reports, awareness materials, and other communication products. Contribute to the preparation of progress reports, technical reports, research papers, and other project-related documents, as required. Coordinate training sessions, meetings, workshops, and events, ensuring their smooth organisation and effective communication. Undertake basic administrative and financial tasks related to the project. Maintain effective communication with partners, donors, and stakeholders. Organise and coordinate logistical arrangements for project staff. Support the Country Representative, India, in leading the project. Consultancy Fee: Competitive, based on qualifications and experience. Post Location: ILRI, Guwahati, Assam. Duration: Eighteen months (maximum of 220 working days per year). Terms of Appointment: This consultancy is open to Indian nationals only . Essential Skills and Qualifications The applicant should possess: Master’s degree in Veterinary Sciences, Mass Communication, English Literature, Social Work (MSW), Business Administration (MBA), or a related discipline. At least two years of relevant work experience. Strong knowledge of communication strategies and tools. Demonstrated ability to design, draft, review, edit, and format high-quality communication materials in English. Ability to organise and coordinate meetings, training sessions, workshops, and seminars, including anchoring and facilitating such events. Excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrated experience working in a multicultural team environment. Strong verbal and written communication skills in English. Ability to undertake basic administrative and financial tasks and coordinate logistical arrangements. Ability to multitask with minimal guidance and supervision. Willingness and ability to travel within India. Excellent computer skills to perform the responsibilities outlined above. How to Apply: Applicant should send his/her CV stating their qualification and experience in the relevant areas expected for the position with a covering letter justifying the candidature for the position to the Head of People and Culture, by clicking on the  "Apply Now " tab below on or before 23 November 2026 .   The position title and reference number  REF: 2363/11/206 should be clearly marked on the subject line of the cover letter. We thank all applicants for their interest in working for ILRI. Due to the volume of applications received, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. ILRI does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process, including application, interviews, processing, or training. ILRI also does not request applicants’ bank account information. To learn more about ILRI, please visit www.ilri.org . ILRI is an equal opportunity employer.
