postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) FEDERAL DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA LOWLANDS LIVELIHOOD RESILIENCE PROJECT – PHASE II (LLRP-II) Credit No.: 7519-ET Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Hydrogeological and Geophysical Investigation for Groundwater Development at Nine (9) Drilling Locations in Dunyar, Shilabo (two sites), Dambel, Guradhamole, Lagahida, Mayamuluko, Harawo and Hadhagala Woredas, Somali Regional State Reference No .: ET-SOM-RPCU-570299-CS-QCBS The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank and the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) for the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase II (LLRP-II) and intends to use part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include hydrogeological and geophysical investigations to identify, assess and recommend technically feasible, sustainable, climate-resilient, environmentally sound and socially acceptable groundwater drilling sites for water supply (domestic and livestock) and, where applicable, irrigation development at nine (9) drilling locations in eight (8) woredas of Somali Regional State, namely: Dunyar Woreda, Siti Zone (Asli kebele); Shilabo Woreda, Korahey Zone (Qudha’shir and Miyir Kaynan kebeles – two sites); Dambel Woreda, Siti Zone (Dalamane kebele); Guradhamole Woreda, Liban Zone (Dektah kebele); Lagahida Woreda, Erer Zone (Busa kebele); Mayamuluko Woreda, Erer Zone (Magaalacad kebele); Harawo Woreda, Siti Zone (Darcade kebele); and Hadhagala Woreda, Siti Zone (Geedwayn kebele). The Client may adjust the final locations and number of sites during implementation depending on field conditions and project priorities. The Services comprise: review of existing information and preparation of an Inception Report (including a data gap register, stakeholder engagement plan and security management plan); reconnaissance survey and baseline assessment, including mapping of seasonal livestock migration routes, grazing areas, existing water points and customary water rights; stakeholder consultation, conducted in the Somali language, with pastoral and agro-pastoral communities, customary institutions, women, youth and vulnerable groups; hydrogeological mapping, including assessment of transboundary aquifers; estimation of groundwater potential, recharge and likely yields using empirical and analogue methods; geophysical surveys (a minimum of three Vertical Electrical Soundings per site, i.e. at least twenty-seven (27) VES) and their interpretation, with a primary and at least one alternative drilling point for each site; sampling of existing water points and laboratory analysis for drinking, livestock and irrigation suitability; environmental and social impact assessment in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and IFAD requirements, including preparation of Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs); uncertainty, data gap and risk management, including site confidence classification, site risk registers and a decision matrix presented at a validation workshop; groundwater development planning; establishment of a GIS database and maps; capacity building of Client staff; estimation of the drilling contract period; and preparation of preliminary engineering recommendations, draft bidding documents based on the World Bank Standard Procurement Documents (technical specifications, drawings and bills of quantities, including drilling-risk provisions) and the Engineer’s cost estimate for the subsequent borehole drilling and test pumping works. The assignment is a pre-drilling investigation based on desk study, field reconnaissance, hydrogeological mapping, geophysical surveys, sampling of existing water points and empirical estimation. It does not include test well (exploratory borehole) drilling, borehole construction or pumping tests, which will be procured under a separate works contract. The implementation period is three (3) calendar months from the date of commencement, and the assignment is expected to start in December 2026. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below. Somali Regional State, Office of the President, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: (a)  Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business shall be in groundwater/hydrogeological investigation and water resources consultancy services. Provide the company profile, certificate of registration, and number of years in business. (b)  General experience: experience in consultancy services for water supply, irrigation and/or water resources development during the last ten (10) years. (c)  Specific experience: experience in assignments of similar nature and complexity, i.e. hydrogeological and geophysical investigations for groundwater development, borehole siting, groundwater quality assessment and preparation of drilling recommendations, bills of quantities and bidding documents, preferably in arid, semi-arid or pastoral/agro-pastoral areas with sedimentary, karstic or basement aquifer settings (such as the Ogaden basin and other lowland areas of Ethiopia), and under projects financed by the World Bank or other international development partners, including application of environmental and social (ESF/safeguard) requirements and in remote or security-constrained areas. For each assignment, indicate the client, location, contract value, duration, scope of services, and the firm’s role, supported by contract or completion certificates. Where available, indicate the drilling outcome (success rate) of boreholes drilled on sites recommended by the firm. (d) Technical and managerial capability of the firm: organizational structure, geophysical survey equipment (e.g. resistivity meters for VES/ERT), GPS and field logistics, hydrogeological and GIS software, access to accredited water quality laboratories, quality assurance systems, and capacity to mobilize multidisciplinary field teams, including Somali-speaking staff, to remote and geographically dispersed areas of Somali Region, and to manage field security, health and safety risks. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 8:00 A.M. to 5:30 P.M. local time, on working days. Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form to the address below (in person, in hard copy) by 4, December, 2026 at 9:00 P.M. local time. Somali Regional State, Office of the President Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Somali Regional Project Coordination Unit (RPCU) Attn: Procurement Officer, Room No. 3 Jigjiga, Somali Region, Ethiopia Asphalt road leading to Jigjiga University to the right/near the traffic light or behind SRS Research Institute Tel: +251 915077890 E-mail: bashirhaji173@gmail.com

postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) FEDERAL DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA LOWLANDS LIVELIHOOD RESILIENCE PROJECT – PHASE II (LLRP-II) Credit No.: 7519-ET Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Hydrogeological and Geophysical Investigation for Groundwater Development at Nine (9) Drilling Locations in Bil’inbur, Goljano, Danot (two sites), Daror, Mula, Kohle, Dhagaxmadow and Shebeley Woredas, Somali Regional State Reference No .: ET-SOM-RPCU-570292-CS-QCBS The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank and the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase II (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include hydrogeological and geophysical investigations to identify, assess and recommend technically feasible, sustainable, climate-resilient, environmentally sound and socially acceptable groundwater drilling sites for water supply and, where applicable, irrigation development at nine (9) drilling locations in eight (8) woredas of Somali Regional State, namely: Bil’inbur Woreda, Jarar Zone (Boholaley kebele); Goljano Woreda, Fafan Zone (Kebele 01); Danot Woreda, Dollo Zone (Tanole and Qorile kebeles – two sites); Daror Woreda, Jarar Zone (Rabaso kebele); Mula Woreda, Fafan Zone (Cididowga kebele); Kohle Woreda, Afdher Zone (Kebele 01); Dhagaxmadow Woreda, Jarar Zone (Tantomi kebele); and Shebeley Woreda, Fafan Zone (Baladka kebele). The actual locations and number of sites may be adjusted by the Client during implementation depending on field conditions and project priorities. The Services comprise: review of existing information and preparation of an Inception Report; reconnaissance survey and baseline assessment; stakeholder consultation with authorities, pastoral and agro-pastoral communities, women, youth and vulnerable groups; hydrogeological mapping; geophysical surveys (e.g. VES, ERT, electromagnetic, seismic refraction and magnetic methods) and their interpretation to recommend drilling locations and depths; assessment of groundwater potential, recharge, aquifer characteristics and safe yield; water sampling and laboratory analysis for drinking, livestock and irrigation suitability; environmental and social impact assessment in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), applicable ESSs and IFAD requirements, including preparation of Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs); groundwater development planning; establishment of a GIS database and maps; capacity building of Client staff; estimation of the drilling contract period; and preparation of preliminary engineering recommendations, draft bidding documents based on the World Bank Standard Procurement Documents (technical specifications, drawings and bills of quantities) and the Engineer’s cost estimate for the subsequent borehole drilling works. The implementation period is three (3) calendar months from the date of commencement, and the assignment is expected to start in December 2026. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below. Somali Regional State, Office of the President, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: (a)  Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business shall be in groundwater/hydrogeological investigation and water resources consultancy services. Provide the company profile, certificate of registration and number of years in business. (b)  General experience: experience in consultancy services for water supply, irrigation and/or water resources development during the last ten (10) years. (c)  Specific experience: experience in assignments of similar nature and complexity, i.e. hydrogeological and geophysical investigations for groundwater development, borehole siting, groundwater quality assessment and preparation of drilling recommendations, bills of quantities and bidding documents, preferably in arid, semi-arid or pastoral/agro-pastoral lowland areas of Ethiopia, and under projects financed by the World Bank or other international development partners, including application of environmental and social (ESF/safeguard) requirements. For each assignment, indicate the client, location, contract value, duration, scope of services and the firm’s role, supported by contract or completion certificates. (d) Technical and managerial capability of the firm: organizational structure, geophysical survey equipment (e.g. resistivity meters for VES/ERT), GPS and field logistics, hydrogeological and GIS software, access to accredited water quality laboratories, quality assurance systems, and capacity to mobilize multidisciplinary field teams, including Somali-speaking staff, to remote and geographically dispersed areas of Somali Region, and to manage field health, safety and security risks. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 8:00 A.M. to 5:30 P.M. local time, on working days. Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form to the address below (in person, in hard copy) by 4, December, 2026 at 9:00 P.M. local time. Somali Regional State, Office of the President Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Somali Regional Project Coordination Unit (RPCU) Attn: Procurement Officer, Room No. 3 Jigjiga, Somali Region, Ethiopia Asphalt road leading to Jigjiga University, to the right/near the traffic light or behind the SRS Research Institute Tel: +251 915077890 E-mail: bashirhaji173@gmail.com

postings.text: Programme Associate (School Meals/Feeding), G6, Mogadishu | WFP - World Food Programme Skip to main content Programme Associate (School Meals/Feeding), G6, Mogadishu WFP - World Food Programme Mogadishu National GS-6, General Service - No need for Higher Education - Locally recruited position level Speaks English, Somali Application deadline: November 29, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The World Food Programme (WFP) is seeking a Programme Associate for its School Meals Programme in Mogadishu. This role involves supporting the implementation, monitoring, and reporting of school meals activities, ensuring compliance with WFP policies and operational guidelines. The Programme Associate will collaborate with government counterparts, schools, and community stakeholders to enhance program effectiveness and accountability. The position requires strong organizational and communication skills, as well as a commitment to improving education and nutrition outcomes in Somalia. Candidate Requirements: Secondary school education or university degree in relevant field At least 6 years of experience with secondary school certificate or 2 years with university degree Fluency in English and Somali Understanding of school meals and community-based programming Experience in program implementation and stakeholder coordination Strong data management and report writing skills Ability to work under pressure and manage multiple priorities DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS 29 November 2026-23:59-GMT+03:00 East Africa Time (Mogadishu) WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability. ABOUT WFP The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks. At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves. To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org  and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube , LinkedIn , Instagram , Facebook , Twitter , TikTok . WHY JOIN WFP?   WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate. WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment. WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities. A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe. We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement). BACKGROUND: The United Nations World Food Programme is the world's largest humanitarian agency fighting hunger worldwide. The mission of WFP is to help the world achieve Zero Hunger in our lifetimes. The WFP Somalia Country Strategic Plan (CSP) 2026–2030 is focused on supporting Somalia's transition from recurring humanitarian crises toward greater resilience, self-reliance, and nationally led development. The CSP combines humanitarian assistance with investments in human capital, food systems, climate resilience, and institutional capacity. WFP aims to address immediate food, and nutrition needs while strengthening government systems and local capacities to reduce vulnerability to shocks, improve nutrition outcomes, enhance sustainable livelihoods, and build more resilient communities. (WFP) advances human capital development by integrating nutrition, social protection and school meals into a comprehensive approach where all activities contribute to one overall objective. Somalia faces recurring food insecurity, climate shocks, conflict-related displacement, and high levels of malnutrition, which continue to negatively affect school attendance, learning outcomes, retention, and the wellbeing of children. School Meals represent a key investment in human capital development and provide an effective platform for improving education outcomes, nutrition, social protection, gender equality, and community resilience. WFP, in close collaboration with the Federal Government of Somalia, State Ministries of Education, development partners and local communities, is supporting the expansion and strengthening of a nationally owned school meals programme. This includes transitioning from direct implementation towards government leadership, strengthening local food systems, improving programme quality and accountability, and integrating school meals within broader social protection and human development frameworks. The Programme Associate (School Meals) will support the implementation and day-to-day management of WFP Somalia's School Meals Programme under the supervision of the Programme Policy Officer (School Meals) and the guidance of Head of Human Capital Development. The position will contribute to the effective delivery, monitoring, reporting, coordination, and administration of school meals activities across Somalia. The incumbent will work closely with government counterparts, Area Offices, cooperating partners, schools, community structures, service providers, and other stakeholders to ensure efficient programme implementation and compliance with WFP policies, procedures, and quality standards. The position supports WFP's efforts to strengthen nationally owned school meals systems and contributes to broader education, nutrition, social protection, and human capital development objectives. PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT: To provide specialized programme and administrative support for the planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, coordination, and operational follow-up of school meals activities. The position will ensure accurate programme information management, effective stakeholder coordination, timely reporting, and support to field implementation and systems-strengthening initiatives. KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority) Support the implementation of school meals activities in accordance with approved workplans, budgets, operational guidelines, donor commitments, and WFP procedures. Assist in the preparation of implementation plans, activity schedules, operational updates, and programme tracking tools. Coordinate day-to-day implementation with Area Offices, government counterparts, schools, cooperating partners, and community structures to ensure timely delivery of programme activities. Participate in monitoring visits, school assessments, verification exercises, and field missions to assess programme performance, compliance, and implementation progress. Consolidate monitoring findings and support follow-up on recommendations arising from monitoring activities, evaluations, audits, and reviews. Support accountability and beneficiary engagement processes, including feedback and complaints mechanisms, ensuring concerns are documented and addressed appropriately. Maintain accurate programme records and databases, and compile, verify, and analyze implementation data received from field offices and partners. Ensure timely and accurate reporting of programme activities and results in WFP corporate systems, including COMET, SCOPE, and other relevant platforms. Prepare periodic and ad hoc reports, briefing notes, presentations, factsheets, and other programme information products. Support performance monitoring, indicator tracking, results reporting, and documentation of lessons learned and good practices. Organize meetings, workshops, consultations, training sessions, and field missions, including preparation of agendas, minutes, action points, and follow-up actions. Support capacity strengthening activities for government counterparts, schools, community education committees, parent associations, and cooperating partners. Liaise with relevant WFP units, including Supply Chain, Finance, Administration, Partnerships, Monitoring and Evaluation, and Area Offices, to facilitate effective programme implementation. Support operational and administrative processes related to school meals activities, including follow-up on requisitions, contracts, invoices, service requests, and programme documentation. Promote the integration of gender, protection, disability inclusion, and accountability to affected populations considerations throughout programme implementation and monitoring. Perform any other duties as assigned by the supervisor. undefined QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS REQUIRED Education: Completion of secondary school education OR University degree (Diploma/Bachelor) in degree in Education, Social Sciences, Nutrition, Public Health, administration, Development Studies, Agriculture or other related in functional area is desirable. Experience: At least Six (6) years of experience with a Secondary School Certificate OR University Degree (Diploma/Bachelor’s) with a minimum of two (2) or more years of relevant experience in programme implementation, project management support, education, social protection, food security, nutrition, humanitarian assistance,  development programming or any other related field. Language Proficiency:  Fluency (level C) in English language and Somali Language. Knowledge & Skills: Good understanding of school meals, education, nutrition, and community-based programming. Experience in programme implementation, monitoring, reporting, and stakeholder coordination. Strong data management, analytical, and report writing skills. Ability to work effectively with government institutions, development partners, and community stakeholders. Strong organizational, planning, communication, and interpersonal skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities, work under pressure, and meet deadlines. Ability to communicate clearly and concisely both orally and in writing. This position is open to qualified Somali national candidates only. Female candidates are highly encouraged to apply. WFP Somalia offers female friendly spaces in the workplace. WFP LEADERSHIP FRAMEWORK   WFP Leadership Framework guides to the common standards of behavior that guide HOW we work together to accomplish our mission. Click here to access WFP Leadership Framework REASONABLE ACCOMMODATION   WFP is committed to supporting individuals with disabilities by providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process. If you require a reasonable accommodation, please contact:  global.inclusion@wfp.org NO FEE DISCLAIMER   The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web. postings.text: Officer, Planning, Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting | IFRC - International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies Skip to main content Officer, Planning, Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting IFRC - International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies Dakar, Saint-Louis National Staff level Speaks Arabic, English, French, Spanish Application deadline: November 17, 2026 Closing soon Apply Summary by Impactpool The MEAL/PMER Officer will establish and manage the project's performance monitoring, data management, evaluation, learning, and reporting system. This role involves ensuring data reliability and completeness, providing technical advice, and enhancing project quality and impact through effective PMER practices. The Officer will collaborate with various teams to develop monitoring tools, conduct data quality assessments, and support capacity-building efforts. The position requires strong analytical skills and the ability to produce high-quality reports and dashboards. Candidate Requirements: Bachelor's degree in relevant field Minimum 3 years of experience in MEAL/PMER Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and data management tools Experience in data collection and analysis Fluent in English and another IFRC language Strong communication and training skills Officer, Planning, Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting Vacancy No.S19170Category of ContractNationalPosition TypeNationalApplication Deadline17/11/2026Job Posted On04/11/2026Duty StationDakar, SenegalCountrySENEGALGradeNational StaffDuty Station StatusN/AAccompanied StatusN/ADuration12 months Organizational Context The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. Senegal occupies a strategic position along the Atlantic migration route and experiences movements of people that may generate significant humanitarian needs, particularly in health, food, water, temporary accommodation, hygiene, protection, psychosocial support and restoring family links. In this context, IFRC, in collaboration with the Senegalese Red Cross (SRC), is implementing humanitarian assistance within the Temporary Care Centres for Migrants Rescued at Sea (CPCT-MSM) in Dakar and Saint-Louis. The intervention aims to ensure that people accommodated in the centres have equitable, dignified and non-discriminatory access to essential services, while ensuring the identification of vulnerabilities, referrals and adaptation of interventions to identified needs. The overall purpose of this position is to enhance and fortify the quality, accountability, performance and impact of programmes and operations supported by IFRC. This entails collaborating closely with the National Society (NS), providing technical assistance and guidance on PMER-related matters. Responsibilities include conducting reliable planning, monitoring, evaluation and reporting on the Project, donor reporting, establishing a MEAL/PMER framework and bolstering NS programmes and operations through capacity-building efforts. Job Purpose The MEAL/PMER Officer is responsible for establishing and managing the project's performance monitoring, data management and quality, evaluation, learning and reporting system. The Officer ensures the reliability, completeness, traceability and protection of data and ensures that data are effectively used to improve the quality of interventions and support decision-making. This includes offering technical advice to IFRC country teams. The position aims to elevate project quality, performance, and impact through specialized technical assistance and direction in PMER practices. Job Duties and Responsibilities A. PLANNING, MEAL/PMER System and Performance Monitoring The Officer will: Participate in the development, updating and operationalization of the project MEAL/PMER plan; Update the indicator tracking system; Develop and maintain the results and indicator matrix, MEAL Plan, indicator tracking tables (ITTs), to monitor objectives, indicators, and activities, as per IFRC guidelines and in line with the contractual requirements. Ensure appropriate methods and tools for data collection, verification, consolidation and analysis; Harmonize monitoring tools between Dakar and Saint-Louis; • Ensure the availability and traceability of sources of verification; Maintain physical and electronic archives; Conduct Data Quality Assessments (DQAs); Plan and conduct field monitoring visits and joint monitoring missions with NS programme staff and PNSs, based on the set M&E framework, documenting findings and following up on recommendations. Support teams in the correct use of monitoring tools; Regularly monitor indicators, compare achievements against targets and identify performance gaps. Provide technical advice to the Delegation and NS staff on regularly monitoring their projects, programmes and plans to facilitate results-based management, strengthen accountability, and produce evidence-based results. B. Data Management, Analysis and Quality Coordinate data collection, consolidation, cleaning and analysis across the project centres ; Ensure the completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness and traceability of project data; Conduct data quality checks, identify anomalies and duplicates, and triangulate data from relevant sources ; Develop and maintain data quality assurance mechanisms and conduct regular Data Quality Assessments (DQAs); Document DQA findings, develop corrective action plans and follow up on their implementation; Support project teams to strengthen data management practices and ensure compliance with data protection and confidentiality requirements. C. Dashboards, Analysis and Reporting Produce and update operational dashboards; Maintain secure, updated and well-organized databases and ensure appropriate data archiving; Provide analysis to identify trends, constraints, emerging needs and performance gaps ; Alert coordination teams to key challenges ; Support teams in defining and monitoring corrective actions; Consolidate data from both centres ; Contribute to monthly, quarterly, semi-annual and final reports as required; Verify consistency between data, sources of verification and reported results; Contribute to reports for partners, authorities and donors requirements; Where relevant and in compliance with data protection requirements, the Officer will produce disaggregated analyses, including by sex, age and nationality. D. Evaluation, Learning and Knowledge Management Support the planning, coordination and implementation of baseline, mid-term and final evaluations, as well as satisfaction surveys and other learning exercises; Participate in monthly and quarterly performance reviews and facilitate the identification and documentation of good practices, innovations, challenges and operational adaptations ; Analyse monitoring and evaluation findings and translate them into practical recommendations to inform programme improvement and decision-making; Track the implementation of evaluation and learning recommendations and document lessons learned; Support the systematic use of evidence and evaluation findings within the project and contribute relevant learning to IFRC processes at country, regional and global levels; Contribute to the development and dissemination of learning products, case studies and other knowledge-management outputs, as appropriate. E. Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA) In collaboration with relevant teams, the Officer contributes to the functioning of the feedback and complaints mechanism. The Officer will: Job Duties and Responsibilities (continued) Monitor the number, nature, handling and status of feedback received; Analyse concerns raised by people accommodated in the centres; Contribute to satisfaction surveys; Document adaptations resulting from feedback; Ensure that people accommodated in the centres are aware of complaints and feedback mechanisms; Ensure the confidentiality of sensitive information. F. Capacity Strengthening and general Support Train and support staff and volunteers on data collection, management and analysis tools, as well as indicator monitoring and reporting. Contribute to developing a culture of data- and evidence-based decision-making within the project. Provide PMER-related technical assistance and guidance for assessments of the programme. G. Coordination & Collaboration The MEAL/PMER Officer will work closely with the Project Manager, IFRC Migration Delegate, CPCT-MSM managers, health, protection, PSS and RFL teams, SRC volunteers, IFRC technical teams, and logistics and administrative/finance functions. The Officer will participate in coordination meetings and performance reviews and provide the data and analysis required for decision-making. H. Knowledge & Skills Good proficiency in the following tools is expected: Microsoft Excel, including advanced functionalities; KoboToolbox and/or ODK; Electronic data collection and data management tools; Databases and reporting systems. Knowledge of Power BI and Power Query is an advantage. The ability to develop or adapt simple data collection, quality control and data visualization tools will also be considered an asset. I. Data Protection & Confidentiality The Officer must strictly adhere to the principles of confidentiality and data protection. The Officer will ensure, in particular, that access to sensitive data is restricted to authorised personnel, aggregated and anonymised data are prioritised for reporting, databases and sensitive documents are securely maintained, and consent and information-sharing procedures are respected. Any data protection incident or risk must be reported in accordance with applicable procedures. J. Key Deliverables Key deliverables include: MEAL/PMER plan; Indicator matrix and performance tracker; Harmonised data collection and monitoring tools; Updated and quality-checked databases; Operational dashboards; Monthly reports and contributions to quarterly, semi-annual and final reports; DQA reports and corrective action plans; Satisfaction and feedback analysis; Trend and performance-gap analyses; Contributions to evaluations; Learning and knowledge-management briefs. Education University degree at bachelor’s level or above in monitoring and evaluation, statistics, economics, development studies, social sciences, project management or a related field. Master's degree in one of these fields. Additional training in MEAL/PMER, data management or statistica

postings.title: Field Research Coordinator - Eastern Africa CIMMYT - International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center Lodwar Mid - Mid level
postings.text: Field Research Coordinator - Eastern Africa | CIMMYT - International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center Skip to main content Field Research Coordinator - Eastern Africa CIMMYT - International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center Lodwar Both national and international Mid level Speaks English Apply Summary by Impactpool CIMMYT is seeking a Field Research Coordinator for Eastern Africa to oversee climate-smart agriculture research services in Kenya, Uganda, and Rwanda. The role involves coordinating project activities, establishing learning sites, and ensuring effective data collection and community engagement. The coordinator will also support farmer learning initiatives and monitor project implementation while adhering to safety protocols. This position requires frequent travel and driving in rural areas. Candidate Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in Agriculture or related field At least five years of relevant experience Experience in agricultural research and community-based projects Valid Kenyan driving license Strong coordination and communication skills Good written and spoken English Description CIMMYT is a cutting-edge, non-profit, international organization dedicated to solving tomorrow’s problems today. It is entrusted with fostering improved quantity, quality, and dependability of production systems and basic cereals such as maize, wheat, triticale, sorghum, millets, and associated crops through applied agricultural science, particularly in the Global South, through building strong partnerships. This combination enhances the livelihood trajectories and resilience of millions of resource-poor farmers, while working towards a more productive, inclusive, and resilient agrifood system within planetary boundaries. CIMMYT is a core CGIAR Research Center, a global research partnership for a food-secure future, dedicated to reducing poverty, enhancing food and nutrition security, and improving natural resources. For more information, visit https://www.cimmyt.org/careers/jobs/ CIMMYT is seeking a Field Research Coordinator – Eastern Africa, to provide technical and operational coordination for the implementation of climate-smart agriculture research services supporting home-grown school feeding programmes across Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda. The role will ensure the establishment and effective utilization of learning sites, reliable data collection, farmer learning, partner engagement and consistent project implementation across the three countries. The position will also involve undertaking project-related driving and field transport duties, where required, in accordance with organizational safety and vehicle-use policies. Key Responsibilities; Multi-Country Project Coordination and Partner Engagement Coordinate approved workplans, activities, partner commitments and schedules across Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda. Support the development, harmonization and tracking of project implementation plans, as instructed by the Principal Investigator (PI), maintaining comparability across countries while allowing adaptation to local conditions and priorities. Serve as an operational link among CIMMYT, National Agricultural Research Systems (NARS) and local implementation partners. Convene coordination reviews, track milestones and actions, and escalate risks, delays and implementation issues. Align field activities with agricultural seasons, school calendars, procurement and data collection schedules. Learning Site Establishment and Technical Quality Under the direction of the Project PI, participate fully booth technically and through local engagement in the identification, selection, validation, establishment, management and documentation of learning sites, in collaboration with CIMMYT, NARS teams and local community partners. Support land access arrangements, land preparation, planting, demonstrations, indigenous crop trials and field operations. Ensure learning sites follow agreed scientific, social and operational criteria and protocols, applied consistently across sires with appropriate local adaptation. Monitor site performance, management, risks and learning outputs, and ensure sites support evidence generation, farmer exchange and partner learning. Work with project scientists (CIMMYT and NARS) to adapt and apply protocols for climate-smart agriculture, indigenous crops, natural resource management, postharvest practices and school-feeding linkages. Identify partner capacity gaps and facilitate the technical support needed for effective implementation. Farmer Learning, Country Teams and Community Engagement Provide day-to-day coordination and technical support to country coordinators and last-mile partners, clarifying roles, timelines, reporting, learning-site management and data collection requirements, while helping resolve implementation challenges. Coordinate farmer field days, exchanges, training, reflection sessions and school-community engagement. Promote gender-responsive and youth-inclusive participation, alongside transparent communication with communities. Ensure that communities, farmers, schools and local leaders understand the purpose of learning sites, expected benefits, respective responsibilities and the limits of project support. Support mechanisms for receiving, documenting and addressing community feedback and concerns, referring unresolved issues to project leadership. Data Collection, Monitoring, Reporting and Learning Coordinate field surveys, site monitoring, farmer feedback and partner reporting across all three countries. Support the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) team in applying approved data protocols, quality assurance, ethics and safeguarding standards. Support the training of country teams and partners on digital tools, data integrity and field documentation. Prepare monthly progress reports covering workplans, milestones and partner commitments, compliance and implementation matters, deviations and their causes, corrective actions, emerging evidence and lessons, as well as priorities for the following month. Include updated action plans, activities, timelines and guidance required. Document lessons from learning sites and incorporate them into project planning and reporting. Prepare field and mission reports and learning notes and contribute to technical briefs and case studies. Field Logistics, Driving, Safety and Compliance Be able to safely operate and drive a field (terrain) vehicle under authorization from CIMMYT in the support of project vehicles to learning sites, partner meetings and field activities as required. Maintain a valid, AA-certified Kenyan driving license and comply with road safety, vehicle-use and journey management requirements. Carry out routine vehicle checks, maintain accurate trip and mileage records, and promptly report defects or incidents. Coordinate field logistics and comply with safeguarding, health, safety, environmental and inclusion requirements. Other Responsibilities  Identify and mitigate potential risks within the area of responsibility. Take reasonable care of own occupational health and safety, as well as that of others, in accordance with applicable CIMMYT Occupational Health and Safety policies and relevant country legislation. Participate in other team projects and activities as required. Requirements Education and Work Experience Bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Agronomy, Agricultural Development, Environmental Sciences, Rural Development or a related discipline. An advanced degree will be an added advantage. At least five (5) years of relevant experience coordinating agricultural research, climate-smart agriculture, field demonstrations or community-based projects. Experience working with partners and field teams, collecting and assuring the quality of data, and preparing progress reports is required. A valid Kenyan driving license appropriate for the assigned project vehicles is mandatory . AA-certified is an added advantage. Demonstrated practical driving experience, including driving in rural and remote field conditions, and the ability to travel frequently are required. Experience driving Manual four-wheel-drive vehicles on difficult terrain will be an added advantage. Required Skills Thinking Challenge; Demonstrate sound judgment in resolving field-level issues, prioritizing activities and escalating risks. Interpersonal Skills: Possess strong coordination, communication and stakeholder engagement skills. Level of English Language Required: Good written and spoken English is required. Knowledge of relevant local languages will be an added advantage. Autonomy: Ability to work independently on field assignments within approved plans and safety protocols. Impact: Ensure timely and consistent delivery of learning sites, credible field evidence and productive partner engagement. Additional Information This is a one-year, fixed-term position requiring frequent travel to project sites across Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda. This role involves collaborating with the Ministry of Health and stakeholders to assess vaccination coverage and the quality of campaign implementation. The consultant will develop guidelines, train data collectors, manage data analysis, and prepare reports with recommendations. The position requires a strong background in vaccination and public health research. Candidate Requirements: Degree in medicine or health statistics/biostatistics Over 5 years of experience in survey planning and implementation Experience in vaccination and public health Knowledge of WHO sampling methods Strong analytical and organizational skills Proficient in statistical software (R, Stata, SPSS) Excellent French language skills Intermediate English language skills (desirable) | Job Description - Consultant international/Vaccination (2605011) Consultant international/Vaccination-(2605011) Grade:No grade Contractual Arrangement:External consultant Contract Duration (Years, Months, Days):3 mois Job Posting: Nov 15, 2026, 3:30:29 PM Closing Date: Nov 28, 2026, 5:59:00 PM Primary Location: Niger-Niamey Organization: AF_NER Niger Schedule: Full-time IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device's system settings. .. Domaine d’expertise Vaccination Objet de la consultation Réalisation de l’évaluation post-campagne nationale préventive contre la fièvre jaune - Phase2 au Niger.     Background Le Niger a obtenu en mars 2024 le soutien de Gavi pour la mise en œuvre d’une campagne nationale préventive contre la fièvre jaune. Le pays demeure en effet à haut risque pour cette maladie à potentiel épidémique aux graves conséquences, dont le risque de propagation internationale représente une menace potentielle pour la sécurité sanitaire mondiale. Entre 2022 et 2023, quatre foyers épidémiques ont été enregistrés dans le pays, nécessitant la conduite de deux campagnes de vaccination réactive en décembre 2022 dans les districts sanitaires (DS) de Doutchi, Kéita et Tchirozérine, et en mai 2023 dans le DS de Gazaoua. La campagne nationale préventive contre la fièvre jaune a été planifiée en deux phases ciblant chacune quatre régions du pays. La première phase de la campagne a été conduite dans les régions d’Agadez et de Maradi (en janvier 2025), de Tahoua (octobre - novembre 2025) et Dosso (janvier 2026), permettant de vacciner 12.054.736 personnes âgées de 9 mois à 60 ans, soit 99% de la cible attendue pour l’ensemble des quatre régions.  Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de la deuxième phase de la campagne, organisée du 15 au 21 Octobre 2026 dans les quatre autres régions du pays et qui a pemis de vacciner 95% des personnes attendues (11 613 659  / 12 199 252), le Ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène Publique (MS/HP) à travers la Direction des Immunisations (DI), a planifié la réalisation d’une évaluation post-campagne, conformément au plan de travail de la subvention validé par Gavi. Cette évaluation, déjà conduite pour la phase 1 de la campagne, vise à apprécier la qualité de la mise en œuvre et les résultats de la campagne, et plus spécifiquement à : (i) estimer les couvertures vaccinales obtenues au terme de la campagne selon les caractéristiques socio-démographiques des personnes ciblées, (ii) évaluer la qualité de la préparation et la mise en œuvre des activités de la campagne aux différents niveaux de la pyramide sanitaire, (iii) évaluer le statut vaccinal de routine des enfants de moins de moins de 5 ans, et (iv) analyser les facteurs sociaux et comportementaux de la vaccination. Résultats attendus Le consultant travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le Ministère de la santé et les autres parties prenantes, sous la supervision du Team Lead DPC du Bureau pays de l’OMS. Il apportera un soutien technique à l’organisation de l’enquête de couverture post campagne, et accomplira en collaboration avec toutes les parties prenantes les tâches suivantes : Élaboration des directives et les matériels de formation ; Sélection et formation des enquêteurs, des superviseurs, des gestionnaires de données et des coordonnateurs ; Collecte et la saisie des données ; Gestion technique et analyse des données d'enquête ; Formulation de recommandations et d'activités pertinentes pour assurer une meilleure couverture vaccinale dans le pays ; Préparation du rapport d'évaluation final axé sur les résultats obtenus à partir de l'enquête et décrivant clairement les domaines de préoccupation et les recommandations, entre autres ; Organisation de l'atelier national / séance de débriefing sur les résultats et les recommandations de l'enquête ; Toute autre tâche pertinente liée à l'enquête de couverture pouvant être assignée par le superviseur. Les livrables attendus de la consultation sont les suivants : Protocole d'enquête ; Outils de collecte validés Directives, matériels et rapport de formation du personnel d’enquête ; Dictionnaire des variables ; Base de données sur support électronique ; Codes et syntaxe d’analyse ; Rapport intermédiaire à la fin de la collecte des données ; Présentation des résultats de l’évaluation sous format PowerPoint ; Rapport final validé sous format Word. Qualifications, experience, compétences et langues Qualification Essentielle Diplôme en médecine ou en statistique de la santé/biostatistique dans une université reconnue. Souhaitable Formation spécifique en vaccinologie, épidémiologie, et recherche en santé publique. Experience Essentielle Avoir plus de cinq (5) ans d’expériences dans la planification et de la mise en œuvre des enquêes (enquêtes de couverture PEV, enquêtes de couverture post-campagne, EDS) ; Expérience pertinente dans le domaine des maladies évitables par la vaccination et de la santé publique ; Expérience de travail avec des parties prenantes nationales en matière d’enquête. Souhaitable  Expérience avec l'OMS ou d'autres agences du Système des Nations Unies. Compétences et connaissances  Compétences essentielles Expertise approfondie des méthodes d'échantillonnage probabiliste de l'OMS ; Connaissance des systèmes de vaccination et de leur fonctionnement ; Compétences fonctionnelles Solides compétences analytiques et organisationnelles ; Excellentes compétences en matière de rédaction de rapports ; Compétences informatiques  Parfaite Maîtrise d'un logiciel de programmation / analyse de données statistiques (R, Stata, SPSS) ; Excellente connaissance des logiciels Microsoft Office (Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.). Langues et niveau requis (Elémentaire/Intermediaire/Expert) Essentiel Excellente connaissance du Français ; Désirable Connaissance intermédiaire de l’anglais. Lieu d’affectation Niamey Voyages Aucun déplacement en dehors du lieu d’affectation n’est prévu au cours de la consultation. Only candidates under serious consideration will be contacted. A written test and/or an asynchronous video assessment may be used as a form of screening. In the event your candidature is retained for an interview, you will be required to provide, in advance, a scanned copy of the degree(s)/diploma(s)/certificate(s) required for this position. postings.text: Programme Policy Officer - School Meals/Feeding (NOB)- Mogadishu | WFP - World Food Programme Skip to main content Programme Policy Officer - School Meals/Feeding (NOB)- Mogadishu WFP - World Food Programme Mogadishu National NoB level Speaks English, Somali Application deadline: November 29, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Programme Policy Officer for School Meals in Mogadishu will lead the operational planning, implementation, monitoring, and expansion of school meals activities across Somalia. This role involves strategic engagement with key stakeholders and operational partners to ensure alignment with WFP corporate priorities and national school feeding objectives. The officer will provide technical oversight, support policy dialogue, and coordinate with government authorities to strengthen local food systems. The position requires a commitment to improving education outcomes and community resilience through effective school meal programs. Candidate Requirements: Advanced University Degree in relevant field or First University Degree with additional experience At least 3 years of relevant experience with Advanced Degree or 5 years with First Degree Fluency in English and Somali Knowledge of food and nutrition security concepts Experience in program design and implementation with multiple stakeholders Strong interpersonal and leadership skills DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS 29 November 2026-23:59-GMT+03:00 East Africa Time (Mogadishu) WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability. ABOUT WFP The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks. At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves. To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org  and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube , LinkedIn , Instagram , Facebook , Twitter , TikTok . WHY JOIN WFP?   WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate. WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment. WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities. A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe. We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement). BACKGROUND: The United Nations World Food Programme is the world's largest humanitarian agency fighting hunger worldwide. The mission of WFP is to help the world achieve Zero Hunger in our lifetimes. The WFP Somalia Country Strategic Plan (CSP) 2026–2030 is focused on supporting Somalia's transition from recurring humanitarian crises toward greater resilience, self-reliance, and nationally led development. The CSP combines humanitarian assistance with investments in human capital, food systems, climate resilience, and institutional capacity. WFP aims to address immediate food and nutrition needs while strengthening government systems and local capacities to reduce vulnerability to shocks, improve nutrition outcomes, enhance sustainable livelihoods, and build more resilient communities. (WFP) advances human capital development by integrating nutrition, social protection and school meals into a comprehensive approach where all activities contribute to one overall objective. Somalia faces recurring food insecurity, climate shocks, conflict-related displacement, and high levels of malnutrition, which continue to negatively affect school attendance, learning outcomes, retention, and the wellbeing of children. School Meals represent a key investment in human capital development and provide an effective platform for improving education outcomes, nutrition, social protection, gender equality, and community resilience. WFP, in close collaboration with the Federal Government of Somalia, State Ministries of Education, development partners and local communities, is supporting the expansion and strengthening of a nationally owned school meals Programme. This includes transitioning from direct implementation towards government leadership, strengthening local food systems, improving Programme quality and accountability, and integrating school meals within broader social protection and human development frameworks. Purpose: This position is based in our Country Office in Mogadishu, Somalia and entails operations management as well as strategic engagement with key stakeholders and operational partners and teams. The Programme Policy Officer (School Meals) will lead the operational planning, implementation, monitoring, coordination and expansion of school meals activities across Somalia, ensuring alignment with WFP corporate priorities, the Country Strategic Plan, Government education priorities, and national school feeding objectives. Under the supervision of the Head of HCD, the PPO- School Meals will lead the school feeding team within the HCD portfolio to lead improvements in programming quality implementation and building government capacity. KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority) Provide strategic and operational leadership on WFP's school meals portfolio, ensuring alignment with national development priorities, WFP strategies, and donor commitments. Provide technical inputs to Programme and project design, including concept notes, project documents, operational plans, implementation strategies, and results frameworks Lead the integration and linkages between school meals programmes and broader social protection and nutrition in general and ECCT pilot in particular. Provide technical oversight and quality assurance for Programme implementation, ensuring compliance with WFP standards, government requirements, and donor commitments. Support policy dialogue and technical discussions on social protection reforms, expansion pathways, and shock-responsive social protection. Represent WFP in technical working groups, policy forums, interagency platforms, sector coordination, and partner meetings, positioning WFP as a leading partner in school meals. Coordinate strategic engagement with federal, state, and district authorities and promote collaborative and complementary approaches across stakeholders. Support preparedness, contingency planning, and the integration of shock-responsive approaches within school meals systems. Support resource mobilization efforts through the preparation of concept notes, project proposals, investment cases, donor reports, presentations, and engagement strategies. Lead the development and implementation of research, learning, and evidence-generation agendas that strengthen school meals programming. Provide technical assistance and institutional capacity strengthening to government counterparts, WFP Country and Area Offices, and implementing partners. Contribute to annual, quarterly, and monthly reports, briefing notes, activity summaries, presentations, and strategic communications materials. Perform other related duties as required or delegated by supervisor.   QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS REQUIRED: Education: Advanced University Degree in Development, Education, Public Policy, Nutrition, Agriculture, Social Sciences, Economics, or any other related field. OR First University Degree with additional years of related work experience and/or relevant training courses.   Experience: At least three (3) years of relevant professional experience with an Advanced University Degree OR a First University Degree with a minimum of five (5) years preferably in post-conflict and fragile settings, in one or more of the following areas: project and Programme management, strategic planning, strategic engagement, networking, coordination, partnership development, and stakeholder engagement. Language Proficiency:  Proficiency: Fluency (level C) in English and Somali language. Knowledge & Skills: Knowledge of food and nutrition security-related concepts and programmes; Skills or experience in designing and implementing programmes with multiple stakeholders. Specific experience in or knowledge of school feeding or school health and nutrition is an added advantage. Understanding of government capacity strengthening and technical assistance. Strong interpersonal and leadership skills and ability to deal patiently and tactfully with people of different national and cultural backgrounds and to manage a team. Ability to communicate clearly and concisely both orally and in writing. This position is open to qualified Somali national candidates only. Female candidates are highly encouraged to apply. WFP Somalia offers female friendly spaces in the workplace. If you require a reasonable accommodation, please contact:  global.inclusion@wfp.org NO FEE DISCLAIMER   The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web. REMINDERS BEFORE YOU SUBMIT YOUR APPLICATION All applications must be submitted exclusively through our online recruiting system. We do not consider CVs or applications sent by email, LinkedIn, or any other channel. Once your profile is completed, please apply, and submit your application. If you experience technical issues while submitting your application, you may contact us at global.hrerecruitment@wfp.org . Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and invited to proceed to the next stage of the recruitment process. All employment decisions are made on the basis of organizational needs, job requirements, merit, and individual qualifications. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.  IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. Organizational Context and Scope IOM Ecuador is a key partner in supporting the Government of Ecuador and other stakeholders in addressing migration challenges and harnessing the opportunities of human mobility for sustainable development. As part of the International Organization for Migration (IOM), the UN Migration Agency, IOM Ecuador works to advance safe, orderly and regular migration through comprehensive approaches that include protection and assistance, socioeconomic inclusion, regular pathways, institutional strengthening, and data and evidence. Aligned with its 2022–2026 strategy, IOM Ecuador emphasizes sustainable, community-based interventions and strong coordination with national and local authorities, communities and other stakeholders to strengthen migration governance, promote inclusive development, and uphold the rights and dignity of migrants. Under the general supervision of the Chief of Mission, and direct supervision of the Head of the program Support Unit , the Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant is responsible for supporting the implementation of Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) processes established by IOM. Responsibilities 1.    Assist in the use and adaptation of methodological tools, data collection, and information systematization, in line with needs and guidelines. 2.    Compile and organize information, both at individual and aggregated levels, on assistance programs; support collaboration with IOM partners when needed; and prepare reports to support program reviews and informed decision-making. 3.     Support the implementation of Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) tools in coordination with the Information Management System established by the mission. 4.    Maintain and update information products and basic data visualization tools, such as dashboards, charts, and tables, according to needs. 5.    Provide general support to integrate the MEAL approach across all OPORTUNIDADES and office activities, in line with IOM principles and standards. 6.    Contribute to the preparation of monitoring reports and assist in responding to information requests from internal and external counterparts, including OPORTUNIDADES counterparts 7.    Support communication and documentation activities related to project monitoring. 8.    Provide assistance on MEAL-related administrative and logistical tasks, in coordination with relevant units.  9.    Perform other related duties as assigned. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education Bachelor’s degree in fields related to Engineering, Business Administrations, Computer Science, Social Sciences, Economics, Statistics, or another relevant area, with proven experience in data collection, data management, information consistency, and quantitative methodologies, with two years of professional experience; or  School diploma with four years of relevant professional experience.     Accredited Universities are those listed in the  UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Experience in research, monitoring, and evaluation of international cooperation programs or projects. Experience with Kobo Toolbox or other tools for data collection. Experience in advanced data visualization and information design. Experience in handling confidential data. Experience with international organizations and/or humanitarian action is an advantage. Experience in preparing reports for donor partners and presenting indicators through dashboards. Experience in using the Information Management System (desirable)   Skills Knowledge of software packages such as Power BI, R, and other data analysis tools. Proven ability to communicate required information through (but not limited to) dashboards, charts, tables, as well as strong writing skills. Experience in collecting and consolidating quantitative and qualitative information from international cooperation projects.   Languages All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).
