postings.title: RESEARCH TEAM LEAD UNIRMCT - United Nations International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals Nairobi BG09
postings.text: RESEARCH TEAM LEAD | UNIRMCT - United Nations International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals Skip to main content RESEARCH TEAM LEAD UNIRMCT - United Nations International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals Nairobi BG09 level Speaks English, French Application deadline: November 20, 2026 Closing soon Apply Summary by Impactpool The Research Team Leader - M&E at IITA Kenya will provide technical and coordination support for monitoring, evaluation, learning, and performance management within the Technologies for African Agricultural Transformation (TAAT) Programme. This role involves designing and implementing M&E systems, tracking program performance, and ensuring the quality and reliability of data. The leader will work closely with various stakeholders to facilitate evidence-based learning and adaptive management. The position requires strong expertise in M&E, data management, and stakeholder engagement to enhance program effectiveness. Candidate Requirements: Master’s degree in relevant field 8+ years in agricultural research coordination 10+ years in M&E and data analysis Experience in multi-country projects Strong data management and analytical skills Proficiency in digital data tools Excellent technical writing and reporting skills Ability to work in multicultural teams Fluency in English; French is a plus Job Description RESEARCH TEAM LEADER- M&E IITA KENYA THE ORGANIZATION The Alliance of Bioversity International delivers research-based solutions that harness agricultural biodiversity and sustainably transform food systems to improve people’s lives. Alliance solutions address the global crises of malnutrition, climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental degradation. The Alliance works with local, national and multinational partners across Latin America and the Caribbean, Asia and Africa, and with the public and private sectors. The Alliance is part of CGIAR, a global research partnership for a food-secure future, dedicated to reducing poverty, enhancing food and nutrition security, and improving natural resources and ecosystem services. THE INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTE OF TROPICAL AGRICULTURE (IITA) The International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA) is a not-for-profit institution that generates agricultural innovations to meet Africa’s most pressing challenges of hunger, malnutrition, poverty, and natural resource degradation. Working with various partners across sub-Saharan Africa, we improve livelihoods, enhance food and nutrition security, increase employment, and preserve natural resource integrity. IITA is a member of CGIAR, a global agriculture research partnership for a food secure future. Please visit http://www.iita.org/ for more information on IITA. ABOUT THE POSITION The Research Team Leader- M&E role is established to provide hands-on technical and coordination support for the monitoring, evaluation, learning, and performance management functions of the Technologies for African Agricultural Transformation (TAAT) Programme. The Research Team Leader will support the design, implementation, coordination, tracking, analysis, and reporting of TAAT results, ensuring that programme activities, outputs, outcomes, and impacts are systematically measured and documented in line with the TAAT results framework and reporting requirements. Given the breadth, complexity, and multi-country nature of the TAAT portfolio, the role combines strong expertise in monitoring and evaluation, data management and analysis, results measurement, and performance reporting with effective programme coordination and stakeholder engagement. The role will work closely with the TAAT Programme Management Unit, Compacts, country teams, implementing partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen the quality, timeliness, and use of programme data; track progress against targets and key performance indicators; identify implementation gaps and emerging risks; and facilitate evidence-based learning and adaptive management. The role will contribute to ensuring that TAAT has credible, timely, and actionable evidence on programme performance, including the adoption and scaling of agricultural technologies, beneficiary reach, productivity and production outcomes, employment and livelihood effects, gender and youth results, and other programme-level indicators. The post holder will also support the preparation of high-quality M&E products, dashboards, analytical reports, performance updates, and donor reports, helping ensure coherence, accountability, and evidence-based decision-making across the TAAT portfolio. MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE: STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS AND PROGRAMME COORDINATION The position will work across a complex, multi-country and multi-partner portfolio, requiring close coordination with the TAAT Programme Management Unit, TAAT Compacts, implementing CGIAR Centers and non-CGIAR international agricultural institutions, the TAAT Clearinghouse, National Agricultural Research and Extension institutions, government agencies, private-sector partners, and other implementing partners. The Research Team Leader - M&E will help ensure that reliable and timely evidence on programme implementation, outputs, outcomes, and impacts is generated, quality-assured, analyzed, and effectively used for programme management and decision-making. The role will: Lead the translation of TAAT results frameworks into actionable M&E plan and elaborate Performance Indicator Reference Sheets (PIRS) including indicator definitions, data sources, collection methods, reporting schedules, responsibilities, milestones, and verification requirements. Contribute to the implementation of TAAT's M&E system, applying appropriate M&E approaches, tools, methodologies, and digital data systems aligned with the TAAT Results Framework. Track programme performance across all TAAT Compacts and countries, monitoring progress against set baselines, targets, and milestones for the programme’s indicators. Coordinate the collection, compilation, validation, analysis, and reporting of data, ensuring that data submitted by Compacts and implementing partners are complete, accurate, consistent, timely, and adequately supported by evidence. Provide technical guidance on data quality assurance and verification processes, including consistency checks, field-level verification, and other appropriate data quality assessment mechanisms to strengthen the credibility and reliability of reported results. Maintain and continuously update TAAT performance tracking systems, databases, dashboards, and other M&E tools for real-time visibility of implementation progress. Prepare periodic performance reports on TAAT outputs and outcomes indicators and submit them within stipulated donor and programme timelines. Provide technical guidance to Compacts and implementing partners on M&E methodologies and tools, including indicator measurement, data collection, digital data management, sampling, surveys, outcome monitoring, technology adoption measurement, beneficiary tracking, and results reporting. Support the design and implementation of outcome case studies, impact assessments, and other M&E studies as required to generate credible evidence of TAAT's contribution to agricultural transformation. Contribute to programme reviews, learning events, supervision missions, and performance discussions, providing evidence and analytical insights to inform management decisions and adaptive implementation. Lead capacity strengthening of Compact and partner M&E teams, including development and use of M&E tools, indicator guidance, data collection protocols, reporting templates, data quality procedures, and results. Contribute to the coordinatiom of M&E activities of TAAT addendums and country engagement initiatives to ensure their alignment to TAAT’s Result Framework. M&E LEADERSHIP AND PROGRAMME COORDINATION The M&E Lead will serve as a key coordination and technical focal point for monitoring, evaluation, learning, and results measurement across the TAAT programme. The role will facilitate effective engagement and information flow between the TAAT Programme Management Unit, Compacts, country teams, implementing partners, technical institutions, the TAAT Clearinghouse, national stakeholders, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure timely generation, validation, use, and reporting of programme results. The role will: Coordinate routine M&E engagement across TAAT Compacts and participating countries, ensuring that M&E requirements, reporting schedules, indicators, targets, and evidence requirements are clearly understood and consistently applied. Lead the flow of M&E information between implementing partners, Compacts, the TAAT PMU, the TAAT Clearinghouse, and other relevant stakeholders. Provide technical guidance and constructive feedback to implementing teams and partners on indicator measurement, data collection, reporting formats, evidence requirements, and compliance with the TAAT Results Framework. Support coordination with the TAAT Clearinghouse and relevant technical partners on the tracking and verification of technology dissemination, adoption, scaling, beneficiary reach, and other key TAAT results. Contribute to cross-Compact learning and knowledge exchange, facilitating sharing of M&E approaches, lessons, good practices, and innovative tools across compact teams and countries. PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND PERFORMANCE MONITORING The M&E Lead will deliver timely, credible, and actionable monitoring, evaluation, and performance information to support effective implementation, accountability, learning, and evidence-based decision-making across the TAAT programme. The role will: Lead the consolidation and synthesis of routine M&E updates from TAAT Compacts, countries, and implementing partners, ensuring that progress against indicators, targets, milestones, and deliverables is accurately captured. Prepare and maintain programme performance dashboards, trackers, databases, and analytical tools that provide up-to-date information on TAAT implementation and results. Ensure the completeness, accuracy, consistency, and quality of reported results through systematic data validation, quality assurance, verification, and follow-up with Compacts and implementing partners. Lead the preparation of annual, quarterly, and other periodic reports, ensuring that results across all Compacts and countries are accurately consolidated. Document and synthesize lessons, good practices, innovations, and emerging evidence from programme implementation to support learning, knowledge management, and adaptive management. Provide timely M&E inputs for programme reviews, supervision missions, management meetings, donor engagements, and strategic planning processes. Maintain an organized and auditable repository of M&E data, reports, tools, supporting documentation, and evidence, ensuring that programme results can be readily verified and traced to their sources. REQUIREMENTS: Education and Experience A Master’s degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Agricultural Economics, Development Studies, Statistics, Data Science, Agricultural Sciences, Social Sciences, or a related field from a recognized university.At least eight years of progressively responsible experience coordinating agricultural research for development, extension, agribusiness, digital agriculture, innovation scaling, or related programs. At least 10 years of professional experience in monitoring, evaluation, learning, results measurement, performance management, data analysis, or related fields, preferably within agricultural development or international development programmes. Demonstrated experience in designing, implementing, and strengthening M&E systems and Results Measurement Frameworks. postings.title: National Non-Technical Survey/ Explosive Ordnance Risk Education Manager DRC - Danish Refugee Council Damascus MF2
postings.text: National Non-Technical Survey/ Explosive Ordnance Risk Education Manager | DRC - Danish Refugee Council Skip to main content National Non-Technical Survey/ Explosive Ordnance Risk Education Manager DRC - Danish Refugee Council Damascus National MF2 level Speaks Arabic, English Application deadline: November 30, 2026 (14 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The National Non-Technical Survey/Explosive Ordnance Risk Education Manager at the Danish Refugee Council leads and oversees NTS, Community Liaison, and EORE activities in Syria. This role ensures compliance with international standards and DRC procedures while managing the planning, implementation, and quality of operations. The manager will contribute to the strategic development of the Humanitarian Mine Action program and ensure integration with broader recovery efforts. This position offers a unique opportunity to shape operational approaches during a critical phase of program expansion. Candidate Requirements: Minimum 5 years in EORE and NTS within humanitarian mine action At least 2 years supervising teams or managing EORE/NTS activities NTS and EORE qualified Strong knowledge of IMAS and SOPs for NTS, CL, and EORE Experience in developing and implementing SOPs and methodologies Solid understanding of EO contamination patterns in Syria Experience integrating HMA with other humanitarian sectors Strong coordination and representation skills Relevant university degree or technical qualification Strong working English and fluent in Arabic Who are we? The Danish Refugee Council assists refugees and internally displaced persons across the globe: we provide emergency aid, fight for their rights, and strengthen their opportunities for a brighter future. We work in conflict-affected areas, along the displacement routes, and in the countries where refugees settle. In cooperation with local communities, we strive for responsible and sustainable solutions. We work toward successful integration and – whenever possible – for the fulfillment of the wish to return home. The Danish Refugee Council was founded in Denmark in 1956 and has since grown to become an international humanitarian organization with more than 7,000 staff and 8,000 volunteers. Our vision is a dignified life for all displaced. All of our efforts are based on our value compass: humanity, respect, independence and neutrality, participation, and honesty and transparency. DRC Syria DRC has been operating in Syria since 2008, initially responding to the Iraqi refugee crisis before pivoting to a full-scale response to the Syria crisis from 2011 onwards. Our work encompasses the full cycle of displacement—responding to life-saving humanitarian needs and supporting community recovery until durable solutions can be achieved. DRC Syria takes an area-based approach to supporting internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities across our key sectors: Economic Recovery and Resilience, Protection, WASH, Shelter and Infrastructure, and Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (including Humanitarian Mine Action). With an established rapid response mechanism, DRC can rapidly respond to emerging crises and shocks to meet acute emergency needs. Recognizing the significant need for early recovery and resilience programming to ensure dignified, sustainable, and cost-effective solutions for fragile communities, DRC’s programmes foster resilience for individuals and communities in situations of protracted displacement and during the initial stages of post-conflict recovery, towards a durable solution of their choice. With active portfolios in the neighboring countries of Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye and Iraq, DRC offers a cross-border, regional response to the Syria crisis, through cross-border protection monitoring, advocacy, and trends analysis. Overall purpose of the role : The NTS/EORE Manager leads and oversees DRC’s Non-Technical Survey (NTS), Community Liaison (CL), and Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) activities in Syria, ensuring full compliance with International Mine Action Standards (IMAS), national standards, and DRC Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). The role is responsible for the planning, implementation, quality management, and continuous improvement of NTS/EORE operations, while contributing to the strategic development of DRC’s Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA) programme. This includes developing and adapting SOPs, tools, and methodologies in line with the evolving operational context. A key function of the role is to ensure strong integration of NTS/EORE with DRC’s broader recovery portfolio, including HLP, livelihoods, shelter, WASH, and protection, so that mine action activities directly enable safe, sustainable, and area-based recovery outcomes. The NTS/EORE Manager ensures that DRC effectively maps EO contamination through systematic identification, recording, and analysis of hazardous areas, while delivering targeted EORE to reduce risk-taking behavior among affected populations. This is a twelve-month, country-wide role designed to support the scale-up, consolidation, and standardization of NTS/EORE operations across Syria. The position offers a unique opportunity to shape operational approaches, systems, and tools during a critical phase of programme expansion. Key Responsibilities and Accountabilities: Technical Management and Implementation Lead the planning, implementation, and oversight of NTS, CL, and EORE activities in assigned areas Ensure activities are conducted safely, efficiently, and in line with IMAS, national standards, and DRC SOPs Oversee tasking, deployment, and daily management of NTS/EORE teams Ensure systematic integration of NTS/EORE outputs into clearance prioritization and broader HMA programming Ensure that NTS/EORE activities are aligned with and support DRC’s recovery interventions, including livelihoods, shelter, infrastructure, WASH, and protection Lead the development, revision, and contextualization of SOPs, guidelines, and tools for NTS, CL, and EORE Develop and refine data collection tools, prioritization tools, and methodologies Ensure alignment of operational tools with IMAS and evolving national standards Promote continuous improvement and adaptation of approaches based on operational learning Develop monthly team workplans linked to project targets, locations and available resources; coordinate implementation with Technical Field Managers and Area Managers and escalate delivery gaps to the HMA Operations Manager. Ensure deployment readiness in accordance with approved safety, communications and medical procedures; suspend unsafe activities and immediately report concerns to the HMA Operations Manager. Lead EORE needs assessments, adapt and pre-test messages and materials for different at-risk groups, and work with MEAL to assess understanding and safer behavior. Strategy and Programme Development Contribute to the strategic development and expansion of DRC’s HMA programme in Syria Provide technical inputs to proposal development, concept notes, and donor engagement Actively promote area-based and nexus approaches, ensuring mine action enables and is integrated with recovery and development outcomes Identify operational gaps and opportunities for scale-up and cross-sector collaboration Staff Management & Capacity Development Line manage and supervise NTS/EORE team leaders and field teams Design and deliver initial and refresher training in NTS, CL, and EORE Lead capacity development of national staff, including substantial training, mentoring and on-the-job training Lead EORE/ NTS capacity development of national authorities (e.g. NMAC) and relevant stakeholders Quality Management, Monitoring & IM Ensure strong quality assurance (QA) and quality control (QC) of all NTS/EORE activities Oversee data collection, verification, and analysis related to EO contamination Track progress against targets and indicators Ensure data is accurately captured, stored, and shared with relevant stakeholders (e.g. SNMAC, MA AoR) Strengthen linkages between operations and Information Management (IM) Document QA findings and non-conformities, assign corrective actions and deadlines, and verify closure. Coordinate with IM and MEAL on indicator definitions, disaggregated beneficiary reporting and prevention of double counting; protect personal and sensitive information and share it only through approved procedures. Coordination & External Liaison Liaise with Mine Action AoR, relevant working groups and other operators to ensure alignment and avoid duplication Engage with local authorities, community leaders, and civil society actors Represent DRC in relevant coordination forums as required Support coordination on tasking, prioritization, and information sharing Budget Management, Reporting & Compliance Manage EORE/NTS budgets and track expenditures against targets as well as progress Prepare and oversee high-quality internal and donor reporting (weekly, monthly, and ad hoc) Ensure timely submission of field reports and data Contribute to donor reports with technical inputs and analysis  Exercise budget responsibilities within delegated authority, coordinating expenditure forecasts and procurement planning with the HMA Operations Manager and the Head of HDP Integrated Programming and Housing, Land and Property (HLP) Strengthen operational linkages between NTS/EORE and DRC's Protection, HLP, Economic Recovery, Shelter and WASH programmes, ensuring that contamination data and risk assessments inform integrated, area-based interventions. Facilitate joint assessments, operational planning and referral pathways with other DRC sectors, enabling mine action to support safe access to land, infrastructure, essential services and livelihoods. Act as the HMA technical focal point for a HLP consultancy, supporting the development, field-testing and operationalization of harmonized HLP due diligence guidance, tools and procedures for Syria's mine action sector. Ensure HLP considerations, including land ownership, tenure, access, competing claims and potential land-related disputes, are systematically integrated into NTS, community liaison, prioritization and land release planning. Coordinate with DRC's HLP specialists, the HLP Technical Working Group, Mine Action AoR and relevant national stakeholders to support the adoption of harmonized HLP approaches and their potential integration into National Mine Action Standards. Promote conflict-sensitive approaches to survey and land release, ensuring that HMA interventions do not inadvertently exacerbate land disputes, exclusion or community tensions. Refer land disputes and legal questions to qualified HLP specialists; provide operational input to HLP processes within the manager’s technical competence and delegated authority. Safeguarding, Inclusion and Accountability Ensure compliance with DRC’s Code of Conduct, safeguarding and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse requirements; report concerns through designated channels. Ensure inclusive participation and accessible community complaints and feedback channels, and coordinate appropriate referrals with Protection and Accountability colleagues. Undertake any other tasks as required by HMA Operations Manager and Head of HDP . Experience and technical competencies: Minimum 5 years of experience in EORE and NTS within humanitarian mine action (HMA) programmes At least two years of experience supervising teams or managing EORE/NTS activities. NTS and EORE qualified QMS qualified (is an asset) Demonstrated experience in managing and training NTS, Community Liaison (CL), and EORE teams, including capacity development of national staff and authorities Strong knowledge of IMAS and SOPs applicable to NTS, CL, and EORE, including quality management (QA/QC) Proven experience in developing, adapting, and implementing SOPs, tools, and methodologies Solid understanding of EO contamination patterns and operational context in Syria or similar env

Organizational Setting The Fisheries and Aquaculture Division is one of FAO's core technical divisions under the Natural Resources and Sustainable Production stream at FAO headquarters in Rome, Italy. The Division collaborates with Members and partners to promote for the responsible and sustainable management of aquatic food systems, aiming for better production, better nutrition, a better environment, and a better life. To fulfil its mandate, the Division focuses on the global development of fisheries and aquaculture through the implementation of its Blue Transformation a strategic approach that outlines a vision for sustainable and resilient aquatic food systems. Additionally, it extends support to Members through normative instruments and in collaborations with regional fishery bodies (RFBs) established within the framework of the FAO Constitution. The position is either home-based or located at FAO headquarters, Viale delle Terme di Caracalla, Rome, Italy. The New Aquatic Food Value Chains development project (NAVAC), funded by the European Union (EU) aims to promote sustainable healthy diets for the most vulnerable in fragile contexts. The project will specifically focus on the development of new aquatic products that can provide key nutrients to vulnerable populations, provide livelihoods, and generate jobs through the development of sustainable aquatic food value chains. Reporting Lines The NAVAC Programme Specialist reports to the relevant NFI officers and collaborate with relevant NFI staff. postings.title: Closing tomorrow: Senior Planning, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer IFRC - International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies Remote | Kyiv National Staff
postings.text: Senior Planning, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer | IFRC - International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies Skip to main content Senior Planning, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer IFRC - International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies Remote | Kyiv National Staff level Application deadline: November 17, 2026 Closing soon Apply Summary by Impactpool The Senior Planning, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (PMEAL) Officer will support the Danish Red Cross Ukraine Country Office and the Ukrainian Red Cross Society in project development and implementation. This role involves providing technical assistance in planning, monitoring, evaluation, and accountability to ensure high-quality program delivery. The officer will also support the DRC Nepal Country Office remotely, focusing on operationalizing Theories of Change and developing monitoring systems. The position requires collaboration with various stakeholders to maintain accountability and promote learning across both country programs. Candidate Requirements: Bachelor’s or graduate degree in relevant field At least 5 years of experience in MEAL, Grant-writing, Project Management Experience in data collection in humanitarian settings Strong analytical and report writing abilities Solid understanding of humanitarian programming Good communication skills Flexibility and adaptability Valid driving license Senior Planning, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer Vacancy No.S18402Category of ContractIntegrationPosition TypeIntegrationApplication Deadline17/11/2026Job Posted On11/11/2026Duty StationKyiv, UkraineCountryUKRAINEGradeNational StaffDuty Station StatusN/AAccompanied StatusN/ADuration12 months Organizational Context The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian ‎network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience ‎and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally ‎led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and ‎environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental ‎principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our ‎work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of ‎strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. ‎ IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the ‎Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, ‎service centres and delegations across the globe.‎ The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and ‎Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, ‎abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also ‎adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. ‎ Based in Kyiv, the Senior PMEAL Officer supports the Danish Red Cross (DRC) Ukraine Country Office and the ‎Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) in the development and implementation of projects and operations (70% of ‎the role). The position also provides remote PMEAL support to the DRC Nepal Country Office and the Nepal Red ‎Cross Society (NRCS) (30% of the role), with in-country support in Nepal if needed. The Senior PMEAL Officer is ‎responsible for implementing PMEAL frameworks for DRC programmes and strengthening the quality of PMEAL ‎systems and functions by providing technical assistance and guidance across all relevant areas of PMEAL – ‎planning, monitoring, evaluation/review, learning and accountability. The position will strengthen the PMEAL ‎capacity of URCS and NRCS and provide capacity-building support to the DRC teams in both country offices. The Senior PMEAL Officer will work in close cooperation with URCS and NRCS counterparts and DRC programme, project ‎and support staff.‎ Job Purpose The Senior PMEAL Officer will, together with the Senior PMEAL Delegate, serve as the focal point for strategic, portfolio and programmatic Planning, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (PMEAL) across the assigned portfolio, providing 70% support to the DRC Ukraine Country Office and Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) operations and 30% support to the DRC Nepal Country Office and Nepal Red Cross Society (NRCS) operations. Support to Nepal will primarily be provided remotely, with in-country support undertaken as required. The core purpose of the role is to ensure that DRC remains accountable to the communities served through its National Society partners, as well as to donors and key stakeholders across both country programmes. This includes supporting programme teams to ensure that DRC programmes are designed and implemented in accordance with DRC Project Management Standards, Standard Operating Procedures, the Core Humanitarian Standard and other relevant sector standards. The role will support the design, implementation, monitoring, learning and reporting functions across both country offices, ensuring consistency in quality standards, accountability commitments and evidence-based decision-making. The role will maintain a specific focus in Ukraine on leading assessments, baseline and endline studies, Post-Distribution Monitoring exercises, beneficiary surveys, reviews, evaluations and other analytical exercises conducted by DRC, URCS or external consultants to inform programme quality and strategic engagement. In Nepal, a key priority will be to provide technical PMEAL leadership to operationalise country-level Theories of Change and accompanying Operational Frameworks, translating them into practical monitoring systems, measurable results frameworks and evidence-based programme management approaches, while contributing to the high-quality design of new programmes and proposals. postings.text: UN Women National Consultant to Facilitate Training for Women in Seafood Processing and Value Addition, Cross River State, Nigeria. | UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Skip to main content UN Women National Consultant to Facilitate Training for Women in Seafood Processing and Value Addition, Cross River State, Nigeria. UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Nigeria National Mid level Speaks Chinese, Arabic, English, French, Russian, Spanish Application deadline: November 28, 2026 (12 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool UN Women is seeking a National Consultant to facilitate training for women in seafood processing and value addition in Cross River State, Nigeria. The consultant will deliver hands-on training focused on safe seafood handling, processing, preservation, and basic enterprise practices. The goal is to enhance the technical and enterprise capacities of women, improve product quality, and increase their competitiveness and incomes. The trainer will work closely with UN Women and local stakeholders to ensure the training is relevant and effective. Candidate Requirements: Minimum diploma or bachelor's degree in relevant field At least 5 years of experience in seafood processing or food safety Experience training women or community groups Practical knowledge of seafood handling and preservation techniques Strong communication and facilitation skills Fluency in English; knowledge of local language is an advantage Background: UN Women Nigeria supports women’s economic empowerment through improved skills, productive livelihoods, market access and more resilient value chains. In Cross River State, women play important roles in the fisheries and seafood value chain, including handling, processing, preservation, packaging and marketing. However, limited access to improved processing techniques, food-safety practices, appropriate equipment, business skills and higher-value markets can constrain productivity and incomes. UN Women therefore seeks a qualified local trainer to deliver practical, hands-on training for women on safe and hygienic seafood handling, processing, preservation, value addition, packaging and basic enterprise practices. The assignment should prioritize locally available seafood and technologies that are affordable, energy-efficient and appropriate for women-led micro and small enterprises. The trainer will work under the overall guidance of UN Women Nigeria and the designated programme focal point, in coordination with relevant state/local authorities, community leadership and participating women’s groups as applicable. All deliverables are subject to UN Women review and acceptance. Objective of the Assignment The overall objective is to strengthen the technical and enterprise capacities of participating women to process seafood safely, reduce post-harvest losses, improve product quality and shelf life, diversify value-added products, and enhance their competitiveness and incomes. Specific Objectives Assess participants’ existing practices, skills gaps and locally available seafood products. Provide practical training on hygienic handling, cleaning, sorting, preparation and preservation of seafood. Demonstrate improved processing techniques suited to local products, including smoking, drying and other safe value-addition methods where appropriate. Build practical skills in food safety, quality control, packaging, labelling, storage and waste minimization. Strengthen basic costing, pricing, record-keeping, customer orientation and market-readiness skills. Equip participants to operate and maintain relevant small-scale processing equipment safely. Scope of Work and Responsibilities Conduct an inception meeting with UN Women and relevant local stakeholders and submit a concise training plan. Carry out a rapid pre-training needs/skills assessment and adapt the curriculum to participants’ literacy levels, local seafood species and market context. Develop simple participant-friendly training materials, practical demonstrations and job aids in English and, where useful, locally understandable language. Deliver competency-focused sessions combining demonstration, supervised practice and peer learning. Cover good hygiene practices, prevention of cross-contamination, safe water use, temperature/time control, clean work surfaces, appropriate protective clothing and safe storage. Demonstrate seafood processing and preservation methods applicable to the target products, such as improved smoking, drying, chilling/freezing or other methods agreed with UN Women. Train participants in packaging and labelling fundamentals, product presentation, basic quality assurance and compliance awareness for market access. Integrate occupational health and safety, energy efficiency, responsible use of fuel and water, by-product utilization and environmentally sound waste disposal. Introduce simple business modules covering product costing, pricing, production records, stock control, customer service and market linkages. Administer post-training competency checks, document lessons learned and provide coaching/mentoring during practical application. Submit complete training documentation and a final assignment report with recommendations for sustainability and follow-up support. Indicative Training Modules Module 1: Seafood value chain, participant assessment and good hygiene practices Module 2: Raw material selection, handling, cleaning and preparation Module 3: Improved processing and preservation: smoking, drying and context-appropriate cold preservation Module 4: Food safety, contamination prevention, quality control and safe storage Module 5: Processing equipment: safe operation, routine cleaning and basic maintenance Module 6: Value-added product development, portioning, packaging and labelling Module 7: By-product utilization, waste management, energy/water efficiency and workplace safety Module 8: Costing, pricing, record-keeping, customer requirements and market readiness Module 9: Practical production exercises, competency assessment and coaching Training Approach The trainer will use an adult-learning and learning-by-doing approach. Training should be predominantly practical, with demonstrations followed by supervised participant practice. Examples, measurements and job aids should be simple and locally relevant. The trainer will ensure safe use of knives, heat/smoking equipment, cold-storage equipment and other tools; promote hygienic workstations; and make reasonable adaptations that enable equitable participation by women. Expected Deliverables  Inception report and training plan: Methodology, schedule, stakeholder engagement approach and materials/equipment list. Needs assessment and adapted training package: Baseline findings, session plans, participant materials and practical exercises. Practical training delivered: Attendance records, photos where consent and UN Women protocols permit, practice logs and competency observations. Coaching and post-training assessment: Follow-up coaching, post-assessment results and identified support needs. Final report: Activities, participant profile, pre/post results, achievements, challenges, lessons learned and recommendations, with annexes. Performance Indicators Training delivered according to the approved plan and within 20 working days. Participants demonstrate improved knowledge and practical competence based on pre/post assessment and observation. Participants can apply key hygiene, processing, preservation, packaging and basic costing practices. Complete, accurate and timely training records and reports submitted. Positive participant feedback and clear recommendations for post-training coaching and market support. Competencies : Core Values: Integrity; Professionalism; Respect for Diversity. Core Competencies: Awareness and Sensitivity Regarding Gender Issues; Accountability; Creative Problem Solving; Effective Communication; Inclusive Collaboration; Stakeholder Engagement; Leading by Example. Please visit  this link  for more information on UN Women’s Values and Competencies Framework:  Functional Competencies: Strong practical facilitation skills. Respect for diversity, gender equality and women’s economic empowerment. Ability to work effectively with adult learners of different literacy levels. Commitment to food safety, occupational safety, safeguarding and respectful engagement. Results orientation, integrity and timely delivery. Required Qualifications  Minimum diploma or bachelor’s degree, technical certificate or recognized vocational qualification in fisheries, aquaculture, food science/technology, catering/food processing, agribusiness or a related field. Experience At least 5 years of relevant practical experience in seafood/fish processing, preservation, food safety or fisheries value-chain development; strong hands-on experience may be considered alongside formal qualifications. Demonstrated experience training women, community groups, cooperatives or micro and small enterprises using participatory and practical adult-learning methods. Practical knowledge of hygienic seafood handling, smoking/drying or other preservation techniques, packaging, storage, basic equipment maintenance and post-harvest loss reduction. Knowledge of applicable Nigerian food-safety and market requirements and ability to translate these into practical guidance for small-scale processors. Experience in Cross River State or comparable coastal/fisheries communities is an asset. Strong communication, facilitation, documentation and basic reporting skills; ability to communicate in English and a relevant local language is an advantage. Language Requirements Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of another official UN language is desirable (French, Arabic, Chinese, Russian or Spanish). Statements : In July 2010, the United Nations General Assembly created UN Women, the United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women. The creation of UN Women came about as part of the UN reform agenda, bringing together resources and mandates for greater impact. It merges and builds on the important work of four previously distinct parts of the UN system (DAW, OSAGI, INSTRAW and UNIFEM), which focused exclusively on gender equality and women's empowerment. Diversity and inclusion: At UN Women, we are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. UN Women recruits, employs, trains, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, ability, national origin, or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, competence, integrity and organizational need. If you need any reasonable accommodation to support your participation in the recruitment and selection process, please include this information in your application. UN Women has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UN Women, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination. All selected candidates will be expected to adhere to UN Women’s policies and procedures and the standards of conduct expected of UN Women personnel and will therefore undergo rigorous reference and background checks. (Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check.) Note: Applicants must ensure that all sections of the application form, including the sections on education and employment history, are completed. If all sections are not completed the application may be disqualified from the recruitment and selection process . postings.text: Research Associate (PSA) | UNU - United Nations University Skip to main content Research Associate (PSA) UNU - United Nations University Pretoria Mid level Speaks English, French, Portuguese Application deadline: December 14, 2026 (28 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The United Nations University (UNU) is seeking a Research Associate to contribute to its domestic revenue mobilization initiatives, particularly focusing on taxation and digital transformation. The role involves conducting policy-relevant research, developing knowledge products, and supporting capacity development activities in collaboration with African partner institutions. The Research Associate will also engage in policy dialogues and disseminate research findings to various stakeholders. This position is based in Pretoria, South Africa, and requires a commitment to the principles of the United Nations. Candidate Requirements: PhD in Economics or related field (completed or near completion) Minimum of 2 years relevant research or professional experience Strong quantitative analytical skills Experience with Stata, R, or Python Excellent drafting skills in English Knowledge of taxation and development challenges Ability to work independently in a multicultural environment Readiness to travel internationally United Nations University (UNU) The United Nations University (UNU) is a global think tank and postgraduate teaching organization within the United Nations System. UNU engages in policy-relevant research, capacity development, and knowledge dissemination in furtherance of the purposes and principles of the United Nations. The work of UNU contributes to solving pressing global problems that are the concern of the United Nations and its Member States. For the past five decades, UNU has been a source of impartial research on sustainability, human security, and economic development. With hundreds of researchers working at institutes in 12 countries, UNU's expertise spans the full breadth of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals, generating policy-relevant knowledge to effect positive global change. UNU collaborates closely with other UN entities and leading research institutions across the globe. For more information, please visit About UNU-WIDER UNU-WIDER is one of 13 research and training Institutes that comprise the think tanks in the UNU system.  UNU-WIDER is a leading international development economics research institute. The Institute provides economic analysis and policy advice with the aim of promoting sustainable and equitable development for all. The Institute began operations in 1985 in Helsinki, Finland, as the first research centre of the United Nations University. Today, it is a unique blend of think tank, research institute, and UN agency — providing a range of services from policy advice to governments, as well as open-access original research. More information on UNU-WIDER and its current work programme is available at . Domestic Revenue Mobilisation and Tax Research for Development Strengthening domestic revenue mobilisation is an important area of UNU-WIDER’s research and policy engagement. Through its Tax Research for Development work and related partnerships, the Institute collaborates with governments, tax administrations, researchers, and international partners to generate rigorous evidence and strengthen the use of research and administrative data in tax policy and administration. As part of this broader agenda, the African-Finnish Partnership for Tax and Digital Transformation project examines how digital technologies and data-driven approaches can contribute to more effective and sustainable tax systems and strengthen domestic revenue mobilisation in Africa. The project is implemented through UNU-WIDER’s partnership with the African Tax Administration Forum (ATAF) and HAUS Finnish Institute of Public Management, combining research, capacity development, and technical cooperation. UNU-WIDER’s work under the partnership focuses particularly on generating policy-relevant empirical evidence on digital transformation, tax administration, taxpayer behaviour, and public finance outcomes, drawing on administrative tax data and other sources. This position is based in Pretoria, South Africa and thus requires the incumbent to be based in Pretoria for the duration of the assignment. Responsibilities Under the supervision of the Research Fellow, the Research Associate will contribute to the implementation of UNU-WIDER’s portfolio on domestic revenue mobilization, with a particular focus on research on taxation and digital transformation, capacity development, policy engagement, and partnerships. The Research Associate will undertake policy-relevant research, contribute to the development and dissemination of knowledge products, and support capacity development activities and engagement with African partner institutions, including the African Tax Administration Forum (ATAF) and African revenue authorities. 1. Conduct research and contribute to the management of commissioned research on taxation and digital transformation. Conduct policy-relevant research on digital transformation of tax administrations, domestic revenue mobilisation, and related development challenges; Undertake quantitative analysis using administrative tax data and other relevant datasets; Prepare and contribute to technical notes, working papers, policy reports, and journal articles; Support the translation of research findings into practical tools and capacity development activities; Contribute to identifying research opportunities for collaboration between researchers, policymakers, and practitioners. 2. Contribute to the design and delivery of capacity development activities with partner institutions, including teaching and technical advice. Contribute to the development of training materials and other capacity-development resources; Support the design and delivery of workshops, webinars, policy dialogues, training courses, and other learning events; Provide technical input and advice to partner institutions, drawing on project research and evidence. 3. Support policy engagement, partnerships, and knowledge mobilization. Prepare policy briefs, blogs, presentations, and other knowledge products tailored to academic, policy, and practitioner audiences; Support the dissemination and uptake of research findings through policy dialogues, webinars, roundtables, conferences, and other stakeholder engagement activities; Contribute to the synthesis, editing, and dissemination of programme outputs, evidence, and lessons learned; Develop and maintain effective working relationships with partner institutions, including tax administrations, universities, regional organisations, and other project partners. 4. Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor. Key Performance Indicators Timely production of high-quality research outputs in accordance with agreed workplans. Effective contributions to policy and knowledge products that translate research findings for different audiences. Active contributions to workshops, webinars, and capacity development activities. Effective collaboration and  engagement with project partners, researchers, policymakers and other stakeholders. Competencies Values: Inclusion — take action to create an environment of dignity and respect for all, regardless of age, culture, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, gender expression, geography, grade, language, nationality, racial identity, religion, sex, sex characteristics, sexual orientation, social origin or any other aspect of identity Integrity — act ethically, demonstrating the standards of conduct of the United Nations and taking prompt action in case of witnessing unprofessional or unethical behaviour, or any other breach of UN standards Humility — demonstrate self-awareness and willingness to learn from others Humanity — act according to the purposes of the United Nations: peace, dignity and equality on a healthy planet Behaviours: Connect and collaborate — build positive relationships with others to advance the work of the United Nations and work coherently as One UN Analyse and plan — seek out and use data from a wide range of sources to understand problems, inform decision-making, propose evidence-based solutions and plan action Deliver results with positive impact — hold oneself and others accountable for delivering results and making a positive difference to the people and causes that the United Nations serves Learn and develop — pursue own learning and development and contribute to the learning and development of others Adapt and innovate — demonstrate flexibility, agility and the ability to think and act in novel ways 1) Education and certification PhD (completed or near completion) in Economics, Development Economics, Public Finance, Statistics, Public Policy, or a related discipline 2) Required skills and experience A minimum of two (2) years of relevant research or professional experience is required.  Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality research outputs. Strong quantitative analytical skills. Experience using Stata, R, or Python. Experience in project management is an asset. Knowledge of taxation and development challenges and experience in capacity development are assets. Excellent team player with strong interpersonal skills and ability to work independently in a multi-cultural, multi-ethnic environment with sensitivity and respect for diversity. Readiness to travel internationally, including extended stays in developing countries when collaborating with local partners. 3) Language Requirements: Excellent drafting skills and fluency in both oral and written English. Knowledge of French or Portuguese would be an asset. Remuneration The successful candidate will be employed under PSA contract. UNU offers an attractive compensation package including an annual gross salary of ZAR 1,241,097.00, commensurate with the experience and qualifications of the candidate. Benefits include 30 days annual leave and a health insurance scheme. UNU is not liable for any taxes that may be levied on the remuneration you receive under this contract. Assessment Evaluation of qualified candidates may include an assessment exercise which may be followed by a competency-based interview, background checks, and references. postings.text: Agronomist | FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Skip to main content Agronomist FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Georgia International Consultant - Contractors Agreement level Speaks English, Russian Application deadline: November 27, 2026 (11 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The FAO is seeking an Agronomist to provide technical guidance and support for agronomic work in conflict-affected communities in western Georgia. The role involves managing Farmer Field Schools, training farmers in fruit and vegetable production, and conducting data collection and analysis on various crops. The Agronomist will work under the supervision of the FAO Senior Programme Coordinator and contribute to the implementation of sustainable agrifood systems. Candidates should have a strong background in agronomy and relevant experience in agriculture. Candidate Requirements: Advanced university degree in Agronomy 3 years of relevant experience in agriculture Working knowledge of English National of Georgia or resident with valid work permit Demonstrated understanding of agronomy focused on fruits and vegetables Excellent communication skills Good community mobilization skills Ability to work as an effective team member Problem-solving skills Computer literacy with spreadsheets and databases Working knowledge of Russian is a strong asset IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that Closure Date and Time displayed above are based on date and time settings of your personal device FAO is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, background and culture Qualified female applicants, qualified nationals of non-and under-represented Members and person with disabilities are encouraged to apply Everyone who works for FAO is required to adhere to the highest standards of integrity and professional conduct, and to uphold FAO's values FAO, as a Specialized Agency of the United Nations, has a zero-tolerance policy for conduct that is incompatible with its status, objectives and mandate, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks All applications will be treated with the strictest confidentiality FAO’s commitment to environmental sustainability is integral to our strategic objectives and operations. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) contributes to the achievement of the 2030 Agenda through FAO Strategic Framework by supporting the transformation to MORE efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agrifood systems, for better production, better nutrition, a better environment, and a better life, leaving no one behind. Organizational Setting The main aim of the FAO country offices, which are headed by the FAO Representative, is to assist governments to develop policies, programmes and projects to achieve food security and to reduce hunger and malnutrition, to help develop the agricultural, fisheries and forestry sectors, and to use their environmental and natural resources in a sustainable manner. Reporting Lines The Agronomist will work in various locations across western Georgia under the overall guidance and responsibility of the FAO Regional Programme Leader and the direct supervision of the FAO Senior Programme Coordinator. Technical Focus Provide technical guidance to FAO agronomic work across the conflict affected communities on both sides of the ABL, with a focus on supporting the implementation of Farmer Field School (FFS) activities. Tasks and responsibilities • Lead the field support in agronomy related to the management of Farmer Field Schools in Vegetable and Fruit production • Provide technical support to the management of grape vines, blueberries and citrus plots, and support the training of farmers with hands on demonstration of management of blueberries and citrus. • Provide technical support to the management of greenhouses and train farmers on counter-season production of vegetables under greenhouse conditions. • Support the data collection and analysis of new citrus, grapes, blueberry and vegetable varieties introduced by FAO, and support the process of delivering these varieties to farmers associated to the FFS. • Lead the implementation of vegetable production Farmer Field Schools (FFS), in main and counter season production. • Lead the implementation of master classes on different agronomic topics to be chosen based on farmers’ interests. • Lead the technical guidance to farmers beneficiaries of the project the implementation of demonstration plots for extension purposes under the FFS methodology. • Introducing experimental diversification of high potential crops in target regions. • Organize and participate in the activities of monitoring and data collection, adding the data of the FAO activities on FAO’s records. • Lead the data collection of the agricultural season and provide analytical opinions on the different crops. • Support data collection on the performance of new grape varieties, as well as rootstock/scion compatibility of the plants. • Provide technical inputs for the different partial or final narrative reports of different projects. postings.text: CONSULTANT FOR IPCC GUIDELINE TRAINING (FACILITATOR) | GGGI - Global Green Growth Institute Skip to main content CONSULTANT FOR IPCC GUIDELINE TRAINING (FACILITATOR) GGGI - Global Green Growth Institute Semarang, Bandung, Jakarta 2 level Speaks English Application deadline: November 20, 2026 Closing soon Apply Summary by Impactpool The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is seeking a Consultant to facilitate IPCC Guideline Training aimed at improving Indonesia's capacity to measure methane emissions. The training will be conducted in-person for university students in Jakarta, Bandung, and Semarang, focusing on GHG inventories and the application of IPCC methodologies. The Consultant will be responsible for preparing training materials, coordinating logistics, and delivering the training sessions. This role requires strong communication skills and experience in capacity-building activities related to climate change. Candidate Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in environmental science or related field Minimum 4 years of experience in capacity-building activities Experience in international development programs related to climate change Good communication and facilitation skills Fluency in Bahasa Indonesia and working proficiency in English Consultancy Level: 2 Consultancy Type: Deliverable Application Deadline: 20 November 2026 11:59 PM (KST) Project Background ASEAN-Korea Cooperation for Methane Mitigation (AKCMM) is a 3-year project to help reduce methane emissions in ASEAN countries. Funded by the ASEAN-Korea Cooperation Fund (AKCF), the project provides technical and financial support in the following four outputs: Developing enabling policies and institutions, Improving the measurement of methane emissions, Designing, financing, and implementing methane reduction projects, and Promoting regional dialogue and partnership The AKCMM project period is from November 2024 to November 2027, with activities at the regional and national level. In Indonesia, the AKCMM project is implemented in cooperation with the Ministry of Environment (MoE), which serves as the ASEAN Working Group for Climate Change Focal Point for Indonesia. Based on the direction of the MoE, municipal solid waste (MSW) has been selected as the priority focus for AKCMM implementation in Indonesia, reflecting its significant contribution to national methane emissions. Objective of the Assignment The Term of Reference (ToR) are prepared under Output 2 of the AKCMM project “Improving the measurement of methane emissions”, which aims to strengthen Indonesia’s capacity to accurately quantify, report, and verify methane emissions. In this context, Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) refers to tracking and documenting emissions levels to ensure reliable and transparent national greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories.  Reliable waste sector inventories depend on a pool of skilled practitioners who understand the IPCC methodologies and can apply them using inventory software. Indonesia’s GHG inventory system draws on the IPCC Guidelines (2006 and the 2019 Refinement), which also underpin reporting obligation. To contribute to this goal, GGGI plans to organize an IPCC Guideline Training for university students in Jakarta, Bandung and Semarang, tentatively scheduled for November 2026. The training will be conducted in person in Jakarta. It is expected to run for two days, with up to [30] participants per session, drawn from relevant study programs such as environmental science, environmental engineering, and chemical engineering. All training materials and delivery will be in Bahasa Indonesia. Resource people may be drawn from relevant government institutions, academia, and GGGI’s existing individual consultants. The training will introduce the fundamentals of GHG inventories, the IPCC Guidelines (2006 and the 2019 Refinement), and the UNFCCC reporting framework. It will also explain the IPCC Guidelines (2006 and the 2019 Refinement) and the basic principles of emission estimation, including activity data, emission factors, and the use of default values. Particular emphasis will be placed on the waste sector, especially methane emissions from solid waste disposal. A demonstration session will show how the IPCC Inventory Software is used to calculate waste sector emissions, from data input to the generation of results and reports, using sample data to illustrate the process. The training will also include interactive discussions and short exercises and will offer participants a view of career and research opportunities related to GHG inventories. GGGI seeks to engage an individual consultant (the “Consultant”) to support the preparation and delivery of these training activities, in accordance with the scope of work outlined below Preparation of training plan, materials, and stakeholder engagement  Develop a training plan covering the training schedule, venue, delivery modality, resource person availability, and alignment with universities’ academic calendars. Reach out to universities and student organizations in Jakarta and surrounding areas to share participant invitations and registration information. Support venue preparation and arrange required logistics for resource persons, including transportation and honorarium arrangements. Coordinate with resource persons in developing training materials (presentations, hands-on exercises, and sample waste sector datasets), compile all final materials.. Ensure that participants have access to the IPCC Inventory Software and the technical set-up needed for hands-on sessions, such as installation guidance and pre-training checks. Design pre- and post-training assessments to evaluate participant learning outcomes, in line with AKCMM project requirements. Execute training delivery Facilitate and coordinate with resource persons throughout the training sessions to ensure effective delivery. Manage the day-to-day implementation of training execution in accordance with the agreed training plan, including ensuring smooth execution of the agenda, guiding discussions, maintaining participant attendance records, conducting pre- and post-training assessment surveys, and supporting resource persons during delivery. Documentation and reporting Support the preparation of a training summary report, documenting implementation progress, key outputs, and outcomes. Compile and analyze participant feedback, including pre- and post-training assessments where applicable. Document key lessons learned, challenges, and recommendations to inform future capacity-building activities. Deliverables and Payment Schedule This assignment is expected to start November 2026 and will be completed in 5 months. The expected deliverable, delivery timeline, and milestone payment are as follows: No. Deliverable* Percentage of maximum amount Due date 1. Inception report, with the following scopes: Summary of consultations and coordination with resource persons and Directorate GHG Inventory and MRV   Detailed training workplan, including schedule , delivery modality, coordination and logistic arrangement approach Detailed training agenda outlining key sessions, topics, and methodologies Pre-post assessment tools/survey  40% of contract value i.e. USD 4,000  1 week after the signing the contract, i.e. 3 November 2026 2. Training package, with the following scope:  Compiled training materials from resource persons, Materials prepared in English and Bahasa Indonesia and formatted for replication and future use 40% of contract value i.e. USD 4,000 1 week prior to training delivery (estimated 13 November 2026) 4. Final training report with the following scope,   Comprehensive summary of all training activities and outcomes across locations Consolidated list of participants and participating institutions (disaggregated where relevant, e.g., by gender or institution type) Summary and analysis of participant feedback and lessons learned including key trends and capacity improvement observations (if applicable) 20% of contract value i.e. USD 2,000 1 month after the training delivery (estimated 15 December 2026) Note: *The organization of the training events, including the provision of meeting venues and catering, will be arranged in coordination with GGGI.  All costs related to the Consultant’s participation, including but not limited to domestic travel (airfare and local transportation), accommodation, daily allowance, and other incidental expenses, shall be the responsibility of the Consultant and inclusive in the contract. The Consultant’s  contract fee shall be inclusive of all costs associated with  resource persons from MoE, for a maximum of three persons per training event: travel cost (airfare), local transport, airport transfer,  honorarium, and per diem aligned with the latest Indonesia’s regulation.   Expertise Required Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, social sciences, communication, public administration, or other relevant studies Minimum of 4 years’ experience  in supporting or facilitating capacity-building activities, such as workshops, stakeholder consultations, or training sessions.  Proven experience working in international development program , particularly relates to the climate change. Good communication and facilitation skills with the relevant stakeholders Fluency in Bahasa Indonesia and working proficiency in English Administrative Information Interested consultant must meet the minimum qualification listed below. Consideration and selection will be based on a panel evaluation of the evaluation criteria factor below. Please note that only shortlisted/finalist applicants will be interviewed or contacted. GGGI does not pay for any expenses associated with the interviews unless expenses are pre-authorized. Reference check will be conducted on those candidates selected for an interview. The applicant’s references must be able to provide substantive information about his/her past performance and abilities. Interviews and a writing exercise may be requested. Applicants are required to prepare a brief narrative demonstrating how prior experience and/or education and training address selection criteria factors listed below: 1) Professional competencies 2) Technical knowledge 3) Communication skills  Selection criteria: 1) Professional Competency (40 points):  Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, social sciences, communication, public administration, or other relevant studies  2) Technical Knowledge (30 points):  Minimum of 4 years’ experience  in supporting or facilitating capacity-building activities, such as workshops, stakeholder consultations, or training sessions.  Proven experience working in international development program , particularly relates to the climate change. 3) Communication skills (30 points):  Good communication and facilitation skills with the relevant stakeholders Fluency in Bahasa Indonesia and working proficiency in English Maximum Points Available : 100 At GGGI’s discretion, reference checks and interviews may be conducted as part of the evaluation process. Applicants must also include in their application package as follows: A cover letter of no more than 3 pages that demonstrates how the candidate’s qualifications meet the work requirements; A curriculum vitae which, at a minimum, describes education, latest experience and career achievements; Names, current and accurate contract numbers (email and phone) of three professional references that have knowledge of the applicant’s abilities to perform the duties set forth in the solicitation. All of the above information must be included in the application package in order for the package to considered complete. postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) FEDERAL DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA LOWLANDS LIVELIHOOD RESILIENCE PROJECT – PHASE II (LLRP-II) Credit No.: 7519-ET Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Route Selection and Survey, Feasibility Study, Detailed Engineering Design, ESIA and Tender Document Preparation for a Package of Six (6) Gravel Access Roads and Four (4) Medium Span Bridges in Hararey, El-Ogaden, Dambal, Mubarek, Shilabo, Guradamole, Aware, Qubi, Hadagala and Hamaro Woredas, Somali Regional State Reference No .: ET-SOM-RPCU-570309-CS-QCBS The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase II (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include route selection and survey, feasibility study, detailed engineering design, Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and preparation of tender documents for six (6) gravel access roads and four (4) medium span bridges in Somali Regional State, as follows: Gravel access roads: (1) Duhun–Garasley–Hararey (49 km), Hararey Woreda, Nogob Zone; (2) Adaley–El-Ogaden (23 km), El-Ogaden Woreda, Korahey Zone; (3) Dulcad–Dambal–Araabi (35 km), Dambal Woreda, Siti Zone; (4) Kukubanya–Buurfuley (50 km), Mubarek Woreda, Dawa Zone; (5) Shilabo–Higloley (50 km), Shilabo Woreda, Korahey Zone; and (6) Berdo–Adeley (15 km), Guradamole Woreda, Liban Zone (total about 222 km). Medium span bridges: (7) Falfal Bridge (120 m), Aware Woreda, Jarar Zone; (8) Erer River Bridge (80 m), Qubi Woreda, Erer Zone; (9) Habaqo Bridge (65 m), Hadagala Woreda, Siti Zone; and (10) Af-dhagah Bridge (70 m), Hamaro Woreda, Erer Zone. The Services will be carried out in two phases, following the latest Ethiopian Roads Administration (ERA) design manuals, standard specifications and Quality Manual, the LLRP-II environmental and social instruments (ESMF, RF, SEP, SA, LMP and GBV Action Plan), the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and the World Bank Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) Guidelines: (a)  Phase I – Route Selection and Survey, and Feasibility Study: identification and comparison of at least three alternative routes in technical, economic, environmental, social and strategic terms; site reconnaissance and investigation; stakeholder consultation; classified traffic counts and axle load surveys; full topographic survey and 3D Digital Terrain Model; preliminary design; ESIA of the selected route; preliminary cost estimates (80–85% accuracy) and preliminary bill of quantities; and economic evaluation (EIRR, NPV and sensitivity analysis, using HDM-4 or a similar package). (b)  Phase II – Detailed Engineering Design, ESIA and Preparation of Bidding Documents: materials and site investigation; geometric, drainage, pavement, geotechnical and bridge/structural design; road safety design and audit, including “Green Road” measures; utilities, private accesses and right-of-way demarcation; climate and natural hazard vulnerability assessment and climate-resilient design; risk assessment; estimate of the construction contract period; final ESIA and Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP); and preparation of bidding documents based on the World Bank Standard Procurement Documents, including technical specifications, drawings, bills of quantities and the Engineer’s cost estimate. The implementation period is three (3) months from the date of commencement, and the assignment is expected to start in December 2026. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below. The Somali Regional State, Office of the President, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: (a)  Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business shall be in road/highway engineering consultancy services. Provide the company profile, certificate of registration and number of years in business. (b)  General experience: experience in civil engineering consultancy services (studies, design and/or construction supervision of roads, bridges or other civil infrastructure) during the last ten (10) years. (c)  Specific experience: experience in assignments of similar nature and complexity, i.e. route selection, feasibility studies and detailed engineering design of roads (new construction, rehabilitation or upgrading, including gravel/low-volume roads) and of bridges (medium span bridges and major drainage structures), covering topographic surveys, traffic and economic evaluation, hydrology and drainage, geotechnical and structural design, ESIA and preparation of bidding documents, preferably in arid, semi-arid or pastoral lowland areas and under projects financed by the World Bank or other international development partners. For each assignment, indicate the client, location, road length and/or bridge span, contract value, duration, scope of services and the firm’s role, supported by contract or completion certificates. (d) Technical and managerial capability of the firm: organizational structure, survey equipment (e.g. survey-grade GPS and total stations), access to soil, materials and geotechnical testing laboratories, road design software (e.g. MX Road, InRoads or Eagle Point), hydrological and structural analysis software, economic evaluation software (e.g. HDM-4), quality assurance systems, and capacity to mobilize multidisciplinary field teams to remote and geographically dispersed areas of Somali Region. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 8:00 A.M. to 5:30 P.M. local time, on working days. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, in hard copy) by 4, December, 2026 at 9:00 P.M. local time. Somali Regional State, Office of the President Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Somali Regional Project Coordination Unit (RPCU) Attn: Procurement Officer, Room No. 3 Jigjiga, Somali Region, Ethiopia asphalt road leading to Jig jiga university to the right/near traffic light or behind SRS research institute Tel: +251 915077890 E-mail: bashirhaji173@gmail.com
