Candidates will also provide guidance and training to support staff while maintaining accurate financial records. This position offers an opportunity to contribute to humanitarian efforts in a diverse and inclusive environment. Candidate Requirements: Completion of secondary school education Post-secondary certificate in finance desirable Experience in collecting and monitoring financial data Fluency in English (level C) Intermediate knowledge of another official language may be required DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS 29 November 2026-23:59-GMT+04:30 Afghanistan Time (Kabul) WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability. ABOUT WFP The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks. At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves. To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org  and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube , LinkedIn , Instagram , Facebook , Twitter , TikTok . WHY JOIN WFP?   WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate. WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment. WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities. A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe. We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement). THE ROLE To support effective delivery of finance, budget and administration support services in order to facilitate transparent and efficient utilization of financial resources. postings.text: Social Media Consultant - Influencer Engagement | UNFPA - United Nations Population Fund Skip to main content Social Media Consultant - Influencer Engagement UNFPA - United Nations Population Fund New York City International P-3, International Professional - Internationally recruited position level Speaks English, French, Spanish Application deadline: November 29, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) is seeking a Social Media Consultant for Influencer Engagement to enhance its digital communications strategy. The consultant will lead engagement with digital creators, manage influencer partnerships, and support social media content creation. Responsibilities include influencer mapping, content co-creation, and performance measurement across various platforms. The role requires collaboration with multiple teams to ensure alignment with UNFPA's priorities and effective communication with creators. Candidate Requirements: Advanced degree in Communications, Digital Marketing, or related field Minimum 5 years of experience in digital communications and social media management Proven experience in creator campaigns and digital storytelling Proficiency in data analytics and visualization tools Fluency in English; knowledge of French or Spanish is a plus Job description Location: Headquarters (New York)  Duration: 11 months (renewable) Contract Type: Individual Consultant (P-3 equivalent) 1. Background UNFPA, the United Nations Population Fund, is the sexual and reproductive health agency of the United Nations. Under its Strategic Plan 2026–2029, the organization works across 150+ countries to achieve four transformative outcomes: ending unmet family planning needs, ending preventable maternal deaths, eliminating gender-based violence and harmful practices, and strengthening demographic resilience. The UNFPA Digital Communications Strategy 2026–2029 prioritizes an audience-first, social-by-design approach. As platform algorithms favor creator-led spaces, reaching Millennials and Generation Z requires expanding values-aligned influencer partnerships and platform-native storytelling to build trust, counter misinformation, and mobilize support across development and humanitarian settings. 2. Purpose of the Assignment Under the direct supervision of the Head of Digital Communications and in close collaboration with the Media / Goodwill Ambassador Specialist, the Consultant leads UNFPA HQ’s engagement with digital creators while supporting social media content creation for corporate accounts. The Consultant identifies, vets, and cultivates creator partnerships that bring visibility and credibility to UNFPA’s mandate, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and safeguarding standards. In parallel, the Consultant manages influencer activations, executes hands-on content creation, and integrates creator-led assets into corporate advocacy moments, the global editorial calendar, and supporter journeys. 3. Duties and Responsibilities Influencer Mapping, Scouting, and Due Diligence Maintain a global roster of creators and expert voices aligned with UNFPA priorities and target audiences (Gen Z, Millennials, youth communities). Map creators across macro, mid-tier, and micro tiers to programmatic and humanitarian priorities. Conduct risk assessments, safeguarding checks, and due diligence using established vetting tools and AI workflows. Creator Engagement and Partnership Management Serve as global focal point for creator collaborations, liaising with Regional Communications Advisors, Country Offices, the Individual Giving Programme team, the Multimedia team and the Goodwill Ambassador / Media team. Manage communication with creators and agencies, preparing creative briefs and narrative guardrails. Secure collaborations in accordance with UNFPA's influencer compensation guidelines.  Content Co-Creation and Quality Assurance Co-create platform-native formats (collaborative Reels, explainer videos, carousels) with creators and in close collaboration with the Multimedia team. Ensure deliverables adhere to accessibility, inclusive language, and visual identity standards. Global Social Media Planning and Channel Operations Execute audience-first copywriting and multi-platform content production across global corporate channels (TikTok, Instagram, LinkedIn, X/Twitter, Facebook, and YouTube). Coordinate and draft social media packages for corporate and campaign moments (State of World Population, 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence, UNGA, CSW, etc.). Monitoring, Analytics, and Performance Measurement In close collaboration with the Business Intelligence and Data Analyst, track channel metrics, video engagement (watch time, shares, saves), and sentiment via Sprout Social, native analytics, and Upfluence. Conduct social listening to monitor narrative pull-through and emerging digital trends. 4. Expected Deliverables Maintained influencer roster with documented due diligence assessments. Campaign-ready activation plans, briefs, and signed agreements. Cleared collaborative assets published across global channels. Weekly scheduled global social content with audience-optimized copy. Performance reports detailing reach, engagement, and audience growth. 5. Qualifications and Experience Education: Advanced university degree (Master's) in Communications, Digital Marketing, Journalism, International Relations, or related field; or a Bachelor’s degree with additional qualifying experience. Professional Experience: Minimum five (5) years of progressively responsible professional experience in digital communications, global social media management, and creator/influencer marketing. Proven experience delivering creative creator campaigns and digital storytelling; expertise in talent vetting and safeguarding; proficiency in data analytics and data visualization, translating Sprout Social and Upfluence metrics into actionable insights; hands-on experience with Meta Business Suite, Canva, Figma, and creator management platforms. Strong understanding of UNFPA's core mandate (maternal health, family planning, gender-based violence, demographic resilience, and humanitarian response.) Languages: Fluency in English required; working knowledge of another official UN language, particularly French and/or Spanish is an asset. Applicants are required to submit a cover letter and CV by e-mail to social@unfpa.org , by 29 November 2026 with subject: "Social Media Consultant - Influencer Engagement" At Impactpool we do our best to provide you the most accurate info, but closing dates may be wrong on our site. Please check on the recruiting organization's page for the exact info. Candidates are responsible for complying with deadlines and are encouraged to submit applications well ahead. Before applying, please make sure that you have read the requirements for the position and that you qualify. Applications from non-qualifying applicants will most likely be discarded by the recruiting manager. postings.title: Consultant - Institutional Capacity Assessment Methodology Development and Validation WHO - World Health Organization Congo-Brazzaville Band level B
postings.text: Consultant - Institutional Capacity Assessment Methodology Development and Validation | WHO - World Health Organization Skip to main content Consultant - Institutional Capacity Assessment Methodology Development and Validation WHO - World Health Organization Congo-Brazzaville International Band level B level Speaks English, French, Portuguese Application deadline: November 27, 2026 (11 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The consultant will provide technical and methodological leadership for the development and validation of the Institutional Capacity Assessment (ICI) methodology. This role involves translating the ICI Concept Note into a coherent methodology, developing a prototype assessment package, and overseeing pilot testing. The consultant will work closely with various stakeholders, including National Malaria Programmes and WHO technical teams, to ensure the methodology is scientifically credible and operationally feasible. The position requires strong analytical skills and experience in disease prevention and control, particularly in malaria and other vector-borne diseases. Candidate Requirements: Degree in medicine and advanced degree in public health or related field At least 7 years of experience in disease prevention and control Experience in developing or validating assessment frameworks Strong analytical skills in quantitative and qualitative methods Expert knowledge of public health program management Excellent technical writing and facilitation skills Fluent in English or French | Job Description - Consultant - Institutional Capacity Assessment Methodology Development and Validation (2604969) Consultant - Institutional Capacity Assessment Methodology Development and Validation-(2604969) Contractual Arrangement:External consultant Contract Duration (Years, Months, Days):3 Months Job Posting: Nov 13, 2026, 4:18:20 AM Closing Date: Nov 27, 2026, 5:59:00 PM Primary Location: Congo-Brazzaville Organization: AF/DPC Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Control Schedule: Full-time IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device's system settings. .. Purpose of consultancy To provide overall technical and methodological leadership for the development, testing, validation and documentation of the ICI, resulting in a scientifically credible, operationally feasible and regionally applicable methodology and Version 1.0 of the ICI Technical Development Manual. Background The Tropical and Vector-borne Diseases (TVD) programme of the Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Control (DPC) Cluster, WHO Regional Office for Africa (AFRO), supports Member States to implement regional frameworks for the control, elimination and eradication of malaria, neglected tropical diseases and other vector-borne diseases. Its objectives include providing technical support and institutional capacity building to national disease programmes. Specific objectives 1. Translate the ICI Concept Note and approved Framework into a coherent methodology, including the conceptual model, domains, indicators, evidence requirements, assessment criteria and scoring approach. 2. Develop a prototype ICI methodology and assessment package, informed by evidence synthesis and country co-design with National Malaria Programmes and partners. 3. Design and technically oversee pilot testing and methodological validation of the ICI. 4. Consolidate the validated methodology into Version 1.0 of the ICI Technical Development Manual and prepare recommendations for its operational implementation. Scope of Work Under the direct supervision of the TVD Team Lead, and within the governance arrangements established by the Framework, the consultant will work closely with the Ad hoc Technical Working Group (TWG), WHO technical teams, National Malaria Programmes and technical partners to: A. Evidence synthesis and methodology development •    Review relevant normative guidance, institutional capacity assessment methodologies, measurement approaches and existing malaria and health-system assessment mechanisms, and identify opportunities for adaptation, integration and added value. •    Translate the ICI Concept Note and approved Framework into a coherent methodological approach, refining the conceptual model, domains, indicators, evidence requirements, assessment criteria and scoring approaches. •    Develop the prototype ICI methodology and assessment package, including domains, indicators, evidence requirements, scoring methodology, assessment instruments and guidance for pilot implementation. B. Technical coordination, country co-design and consensus-building •    Work with the TWG and relevant specialists to develop and progressively refine the ICI methodology, indicators, assessment tools and supporting technical documentation. •    Design and facilitate structured engagement with National Malaria Programmes, Ministries of Health, WHO country offices and technical partners, so that country experience and operational realities inform the methodology. •    Prepare methodological products and evidence for TWG review, document areas of agreement and methodological uncertainty, and incorporate agreed recommendations into successive versions. C. Pilot testing and validation •    Develop pilot protocols and tools, support pilot implementation, assess feasibility and usability, analyse findings and identify required methodological modifications. •    With the TWG and relevant specialists, define and apply approaches for assessing the validity, reliability, reproducibility, feasibility and fitness for purpose of the ICI. D. Documentation, traceability and transition •    With the project secretariat, document all significant methodological decisions, evidence considered, stakeholder inputs, modifications and validation findings. •    Maintain the ICI Technical Development Manual as a living document throughout development, and consolidate the validated methodology into Version 1.0 after final approval. •    Prepare technical recommendations for the institutionalization, maintenance, future revision and potential digital implementation of the ICI. Deliverables 1. Inception, work planning and reporting        • Inception report with a detailed workplan aligned with the Framework and Operational Roadmap, the methodology development approach and agreed formats for all outputs, approved by the supervisor.         • Monthly progress reports against the workplan, including decisions taken and pending decision-gate reviews.         • Final consultancy report with results, lessons learned and recommendations. 2. Evidence synthesis and conceptual framework        • Evidence synthesis report reviewing normative guidance, existing institutional capacity and health-system assessment approaches, and methodological options.         • Refined ICI conceptual framework: domains, definitions and proposed measurement architecture, reviewed by the TWG. 3. Indicator and prototype methodology development        • Draft indicator framework with indicators, evidence requirements, assessment criteria and preliminary scoring approach.         • Prototype methodology package: draft assessment tools, scoring system, evidence guidance and first draft of the ICI Technical                      Development Manual. 4. Country co-design and scientific review        • Country co-design report consolidating feedback from National Malaria Programmes, WHO country offices and partners, with resulting methodological modifications.        • TWG review packages and records of agreements, methodological uncertainties and decisions for each decision gate. 5. Pilot testing and validation        • Pilot protocol and tools for the selected pilot country or countries.         • Pilot report analysing feasibility, usability and findings, with recommendations for refinement.         • Validation package: validation approach, supporting evidence and consolidated findings for TWG review. 6. Finalization, documentation and transition        • Methodological decision log documenting decisions, evidence, stakeholder inputs and modifications.         • Pre-final methodology incorporating pilot and validation findings.         • ICI Technical Development Manual, Version 1.0: final validated methodology and supporting technical guidance.         • Transition package with recommendations for operationalization, stewardship, maintenance, future revision and potential digital implementation.  Quality and acceptance of deliverables Deliverables should be technically sound, consistent with the ICI Methodology Development and Validation Framework and applicable WHO guidance, and traceable to the evidence, stakeholder inputs and decisions on which they are based. They should be accompanied by editable source files and, where relevant, datasets and analysis files. The consultant will lead and coordinate the technical development but will not independently determine or approve the methodology: major methodological decisions and progression between development stages are subject to TWG review and the decision-gate arrangements in the Framework, and final approval rests with the TVD programme. Country data will be used and shared in line with WHO and national data governance arrangements. Qualifications, experience, skills and languages Educational qualifications Essential: degree in medicine and an advanced university degree (master’s or equivalent) in public health, epidemiology, health systems, health policy and management, implementation science, monitoring and evaluation, measurement science, organizational or institutional development, or another field directly relevant to the assignment. Desirable: doctoral degree in a relevant discipline and/or advanced training in measurement, psychometrics, programme evaluation, implementation science or health systems research. Experience Essential: •    At least seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in disease prevention and control at national and/or international levels, particularly in malaria, other vector-borne diseases or infectious diseases, including substantial experience in low- and middle-income countries. •    Demonstrated experience leading the development or validation of multidimensional assessment frameworks, indices, scorecards, maturity models or comparable measurement methodologies. •    Strong experience in indicator development, measurement frameworks, evidence synthesis, and quantitative and qualitative assessment methods. Desirable: •    Experience in malaria programme management, or in Malaria Programme Reviews or comparable national programme review processes. •    Experience in health-system institutional capacity strengthening, institutional maturity models or index development. Technical skills and knowledge •    Expert knowledge of the management of at least one public health programme, notably malaria, other vector-borne diseases or infectious diseases. •    Methodological leadership, sound scientific judgement, and strong conceptual and systems thinking. •    Strong quantitative and qualitative analytical skills, with the ability to integrate multiple sources of evidence. •    Excellent technical writing skills and the ability to translate complex methodological concepts into clear, operational guidance. •    Strong facilitation and consensus-building skills, and the ability to engage effectively with senior technical, government and country stakeholders. •    Strong planning, coordination and risk-management skills, and the ability to work independently within formal governance and quality-assurance arrangements. Languages and level required Essential : Expert level of English or French.  Desirable : Intermediate knowledge of the other or Portuguese.  Location On site: WHO Regional Office for Africa, Brazzaville, Republic of Congo. postings.text: TERMS OF REFERENCE National Individual Consultant Site Engineer (One Position)   Title Site Engineer Contractual Arrangement Local Recruitment Expected Start Date December 9th 2026 Contract Duration Eight (8) months (December 2026 – August 2027), with possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance, project needs, and availability of funding. Level of Input Full-time Project Nurturing Early Skills through Technology (NEST) Project Financing Partner The World Bank Hiring Organization Shanti Volunteer Association (SVA) Duty Station Battambang Province (covering project sites in Kos Kralar, Ek Phnom and Thmar Kaul Districts) Contract Type Time Based   1.  Background The Nurturing Early Skills through Technology (NEST) Project is funded by the Japan Social Development Fund (JSDF) and administered by the World Bank. The Project is implemented by Shanti Volunteer Association (SVA) in close collaboration with the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (MoEYS) of Cambodia. The Project aims to enhance access to and quality of Early Childhood Education (ECE) through the promotion of learning through play and the integration of digital technology in target districts in Cambodia. The Project supports teacher professional development, establishment of an ECE digital resource platform, parental and community engagement, improvement of preschool learning environments through construction and renovation, and implementation of pilot school meal programs. The Project is implemented in selected districts in Battambang, Banteay Meanchey, and Pailin provinces, targeting public preschools with the objective of strengthening equitable access to quality ECE services for young children aged 3–5 years. Under Component 2 of the Project, SVA will implement phase 1 of civil works activities, comprising: (i) construction of 8 new preschool buildings, toilets, water tanks and 6 kitchen facilities; (ii) renovation of 17 existing preschool buildings; and (iii) outdoor environment improvements at  25 targeted preschools. These works are spread across three districts in Battambang province and one district in Banteay Meanchey Province, and procured through Request for Bids (RFB) and Request for Quotations (RFQ) methods. To strengthen day-to-day site supervision during the main construction period, SVA seeks to recruit a Site Engineer based in Battambang Province. The Site Engineer will provide full-time, on-site supervision of the prime contractor(s) at project sites in Battambang Province, under the technical guidance of the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer.   2.  Objectives The objective of this assignment is to ensure that the prime contractor’s civil works at project sites are executed in accordance with the approved drawings, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities (BoQ), and contract requirements, through on-site supervision by the Site Engineer. Specifically, the Site Engineer will: Provide full-time, day-to-day on-site supervision of the prime contractor’s works at project sites in the assigned province. Ensure quality of materials and workmanship are complied with specification, approved drawing, method statement and schedules. Ensure that the prime contractor executed all work in compliance with approved Environmental and Social(E&S) document Maintain accurate and complete site records, including site diaries, inspection checklists, measurement records, and photo documentation. Provide verified site-level information (progress, quantities, defects) to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer to support progress monitoring, payment certification, and completion.   3.  Scope of Work Under the technical guidance of the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer, the Consultant shall undertake the following tasks at project sites: a.  Site Mobilization and Pre-Construction Become familiar with the approved drawings, technical specifications, BoQs, contract documents, and contractors’ work programs for each assigned site, and report any discrepancies to the Civil Engineer and SVA Engineer. Participate in site handover to contractors and in pre-mobilization meetings with contractors, school representatives, and the SVA project team. Sites readiness: coordinate with contractor’s supervisor and relevant stakeholders at target schools during contractor mobilization. Prepare and submit updated sites plan including photos Confirm that contractors have mobilized the required personnel, equipment, materials, site signage, and safety arrangements before works begin. b.  Day-to-Day Site Supervision and Quality Control Conduct full-time, day-to-day supervision of civil works at assigned sites, prioritizing site visits according to construction schedules and critical activities. Inspect and verify key construction stages before contractors proceed (e.g., reinforcement and formwork inspection prior to concreting), using standard inspection checklists. Verify that materials delivered to site comply with approved samples and technical specifications, and reject and record non-compliant materials. Witness and record field and material tests (e.g., concrete slump tests, sampling of concrete test cubes, compaction checks), and follow up on test results. Issue site instructions to contractors on quality and workmanship issues within delegated authority, and refer matters beyond this authority, including design changes and variations, to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.   c.  Site Records, Progress Monitoring and Reporting Maintain a site diary for each site, recording daily activities, workforce and equipment, weather conditions, materials delivered, inspections, instructions issued, visitors, and issues. Maintain photo documentation (before, during, and after works) and inspection records for each site. Monitor actual progress against contractors’ approved work programs, and report delays together with proposed corrective measures. Prepare weekly site progress reports and monthly reports, and submit them to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer. Participate in regular site meetings and record minutes and agreed actions, as required. d.  Measurement and Payment Support Verify at sites the actual completed works in Activity Schedule submitted by contractors Prepare measurement sheets and supporting documentation for contractors’ payment applications, for review by the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer. Record and report site conditions or instructions that may give rise to variations or claims, with supporting evidence, for review by the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer. e.  Environmental, Social, and Safety Compliance Monitor contractors’ daily implementation of occupational health and safety (OHS) measures, including use of personal protective equipment (PPE), site fencing and barricading, safety signage, safe working at height, and first aid, with particular attention to the safety of children, teachers, and community members at operating preschools. Monitor implementation of E&S mitigation measures at construction sites, including dust and noise control, waste management, drainage, and agreed working hours, in coordination with the E&S Specialist. Monitor contractor compliance with labor management requirements, including workers’ code of conduct and prevention of child labor. Report E&S incidents, accidents, and non-compliance to the E&S Specialist and SVA Project Manager immediately, and in any case within 24 hours, and follow up on corrective actions. Liaise with school directors, School Management Committees (SMCs), and local authorities on site-level matters, and refer community concerns and grievances to the Project Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM). f.  Completion and Handover Participate in pre-completion and final inspections, and prepare defect (snagging) lists for each site. Monitor rectification of defects by contractors and confirm completion of rectification works. Compile site-level completion documentation, including as-built mark-ups, photo records, test records, and site diaries. Support the handover of completed facilities to schools, School Management Committees (SMCs), and relevant government counterparts.     4.  Expected Outputs and Deliverables The following deliverables are expected over the course of the assignment. Timelines are indicative and subject to adjustment based on project implementation progress and construction schedules. # Deliverable Timeline 1 Inception Work Plan and site supervision schedule for assigned sites Within two (2) weeks of contract signing 2 Site diaries and inspection checklists for each site Daily (submitted with weekly reports) 3 Weekly site progress report (progress, quality issues, instructions issued, E&S/OHS observations, and photos)   Weekly 4 Monthly report, including progress against work programs and E&S compliance Monthly 5 Material inspection and test records, and measurement sheets supporting contractors’ payment applications   As required, in line with contractors’ payment schedules 6 E&S and OHS incident reports Within 24 hours of occurrence 7 Defect lists and pre-completion inspection reports for each site Prior to practical completion at each site 8 Site completion documentation package and Final Report Upon practical completion of each site; Final Report at end of contract 5.  Work Supervision The Consultant will work under the overall supervision of the SVA Project Manager and will receive day-to-day technical guidance from the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer. The Consultant will coordinate and liaise with: The Civil Engineer and the SVA Engineer to ensure a consistent supervision approach across provinces; PMU members and field staff; The E&S Specialist and other technical consultants engaged under the Project; Contractors, site supervisors, and construction personnel at project sites; School directors, School Management Committees (SMCs), community representatives, and sub-national authorities at project sites. The Consultant shall submit site records and weekly reports to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer, and monthly reports to the SVA Project Manager through the SVA Engineer, for review and approval. The Consultant shall participate in regular coordination meetings, site meetings, and World Bank supervision missions, as required. 6.  Contract Term and Location of Assignment The contract period is eight (8) months, from December 2026 to August 2027, with possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance, project needs, and availability of funding. The Consultant will be engaged as a full-time Individual Consultant (IC) under the NEST Project and is expected to be present at project sites on a daily basis throughout the assignment period. Key arrangements are as follows:   Duty Station: Battambang Province (covering project sites in Kos Kralar, Ek Phnom and Thmar Kaul Districts) Contract Modality: The contract will be time-based, with remuneration at a fixed monthly rate for the duration of the assignment. Working Arrangements: Full-time, in accordance with SVA working hours. Work outside regular working hours may be required in line with construction activities, subject to SVA policy. The Consultant is expected to work primarily at project sites and to make their own arrangements for workspace. No office space will be provided by SVA; however, the Consultant may use the SVA Battambang Office for meetings or as required. The Consultant is expected to provide their own computer, smartphone for photo documentation, and personal working equipment. Payment Modality: Payment shall be made on a monthly basis upon submission and approval of monthly reports and agreed deliverables. Travel costs directly rel

postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST Region: Central Asia, Aral Sea Basin Countries: Republic of Kazakhstan (the Executive Committee of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea and the Project Implementation Unit are currently based in Astana; on 1 January 2027, the three-year chairmanship of IFAS will be transferred from Kazakhstan to Uzbekistan, and the Project Implementation Unit is expected to be established in Uzbekistan under the Executive Committee of IFAS no later than 1 May 2027), Republic of Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Republic of Uzbekistan. Project: Central Asia Water Efficiency Cooperation Project under Phase 3 of the Multiphase Programmatic Approach (hereinafter referred to as the “Project” or “CAWEC”) Grant No.: E709-7C Assignment Title: Environmental and Social Consultant for the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) Contract No.: CAWEC-4-CS-IND-4.2 The Executive Committee of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea (EC IFAS) received funding from the International Development Association (World Bank) for implementation of the Central Asia Water Efficiency Cooperation Project (CAWEC) and intends to use the funds to pay for advisory services under the Project. The Executive Committee of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea (EC IFAS) is the Implementing Agency of the Project (hereinafter referred to as “EC IFAS”). The Project Development Objective is to facilitate climate-resilient investments and strengthen the capacity of regional water resources management institutions in Central Asia. The Project is part of a Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA) and comprises three components: (i) Preparation of Transboundary Projects; (ii) Information Support and Digitalization for Improved Regional Water Resources Management and Climate Resilience; and (iii) Institutional Strengthening and Capacity Building. The Project aims to strengthen and expand cooperation among countries in the Aral Sea Basin.            To ensure efficient implementation of the Project, EC IFAS intends to hire an individual consultant for the position of Environmental and Social Consultant         The objective of the assignment is to ensure effective and integrated support of the Project implementation, including evaluation of risks to environment and society, including relevant vulnerable groups, to build capacity in member countries' water resources management and irrigation sectors, and implementation of principles and standards of International and Industry Best Practice and promoting sustainable practices in the water resources management and irrigation sectors.           Qualification Requirements: university degree in environmental studies, social sciences, or a related field; knowledge of the environmental and social standards of international financial institutions, including the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF); experience in environmental and social risk assessment, stakeholder engagement, reporting, and the delivery of training activities; experience working on projects in the water sector, climate change adaptation, or regional cooperation; and proficiency in MS Office. Experience with Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and familiarity with the institutional framework of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea (IFAS) will be considered an advantage.   The Consulting Services (the "Services") include the following main functions : Identifying and promptly addressing environmental and social issues arising during Project implementation; Compliance with applicable national laws and World Bank Group rules, procedures and standards; Participation in the preparation of the Project Operations Manual (POM) within the scope of their responsibilities; Reviewing, as necessary, the Project Procurement for Development Strategy (PPSD), Environmental and Social Commitment Plan, (ESCP), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP); Preparation of Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) where required in accordance with the Project requirements; Preparing relevant reports; Maintaining regular communication and coordination with the environmental and social specialists of the national Project Implementation Units (PIUs) on matters related to compliance with the Project’s environmental and social requirements; Other related tasks (detailed information is attached in the Terms of reference).      The Environmental and Social Consultant is expected to carry out preparations and deliver the following results: 1. Develop, coordinate, review, submit, and, where necessary, revise environmental and social documentation in accordance with the approved Work Plan and decisions of the Regional Steering Committee (RSC). 2. Develop and implement relevant documents and procedures in accordance with the World Bank’s operational policies and Environmental and Social Standards, including the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment (SESA), and Labour Management Procedures (LMP), as well as applicable national legislation. 3. Develop training materials and deliver training programmes, including training on the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), Project documentation, and issues related to gender-based violence (GBV), sexual exploitation and abuse, and sexual harassment (SEA/SH). 4. Prepare timely reports on capacity-building activities and the results achieved. 5. Prepare coordination plans and reports on engagement with relevant stakeholders and national project implementation teams.            6. Maintain timely and constructive engagement with the World Bank and obtain the necessary clearances and approvals. 7. Assess environmental and social complaints and grievances in a timely manner in accordance with World Bank procedures and prepare periodic reports for the World Bank.  8. Monitor, document, and report on the impacts, risks, and outcomes of Project implementation. 9. Provide recommendations on environmental and social matters, stakeholder engagement, and institutional processes within the Project.  10. Establish and maintain a comprehensive electronic archive of environmental and social documentation, including spatial data. The duration of the assignment is 6 months from the contract signing date (but no later than May 1, 2027). Terms of employment: part-time (8-10 working days per month). Duty station: Astana.  The full Terms of Reference, including qualification requirements, are available on the EC IFAS website at the following link: https://ecifas.kz/publication/ The Executive Committee of International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea (the "Client") invites eligible individual consultants ("Consultants") to express interest in providing consulting services for the position of CAWEC Procurement Specialist. Interested Consultants should provide information confirming necessary qualifications and experience to perform the Services, including a current CV, details of similar assignments, and other documentation evidencing qualifications and professional experience. Expressions of interest should include the following: An up-to-date CV; description of the experience with performing similar assignments; Information on projects financed by international financial institutions (if any); Letters of recommendation and customer feedback (if any). The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.13, 3.15 and 3.16 of Section III of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers , version September 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), which describe the World Bank's policy regarding conflict of interest. postings.text: National Consultant on Coordination and Monitoring | UNESCO - United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization Skip to main content National Consultant on Coordination and Monitoring UNESCO - United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization Tashkent National Level 3 - Senior level Speaks English, Russian, Uzbek Application deadline: November 30, 2026 (14 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The National Consultant on Coordination and Monitoring will support the UNESCO Office in Uzbekistan's Education Unit in implementing project activities related to teacher quality and professional development. The role involves planning, monitoring, reporting, and coordinating with various stakeholders to ensure timely delivery of project outcomes. The consultant will analyze project data, provide strategic guidance, and contribute to quality assurance processes. This position requires strong communication and coordination skills, along with extensive experience in monitoring and evaluation of education projects. Candidate Requirements: Advanced university degree in education or related field Minimum 10 years of experience in M&E of education projects Strong knowledge of project monitoring and results-based management Proven experience in data collection and report writing Excellent coordination and communication skills Professional experience in Uzbekistan's education sector Fluency in English, Uzbek, and Russian National Consultant on Coordination and Monitoring JOB DETAILS Type of contract : Consultant Contract Level : Level 3 - Senior Hiring Unit : Education Sector (ED) Duty Station : Tashkent Work location : On site Duration of contract : 6 months Hiring open to : External candidates Application deadline (Midnight UTC+5 Time) : 30/11/2026 UNESCO Core Values: Commitment to the Organization, Integrity, Respect for Diversity, Professionalism OVERVIEW The UNESCO Office in Uzbekistan’s Education Unit supports the Government of Uzbekistan in strengthening teacher quality and professional development across both pre-service and in-service education systems. Working closely with the Ministry of Education and Science, pedagogical universities, and teacher training institutions, UNESCO contributes to the development of teacher professional standards, competency frameworks, curricula, practicum models, and continuous professional development systems. The Unit supports reforms aimed at modernizing teacher education through competency-based approaches, digital and ICT skills development, inclusive education, STEM education, and innovative pedagogies. Through technical assistance, capacity-building programmes, policy dialogue, and international knowledge exchange, UNESCO seeks to ensure that prospective and practicing teachers are equipped with the skills and competencies required to deliver quality, equitable, and future-oriented education for all learners. ASSIGNMENTS National expert will support the effective implementation of project activities by ensuring timely planning, monitoring, reporting, and stakeholder coordination. The expert will track progress against approved workplans, results frameworks, and implementation timelines; monitor the achievement of outputs, outcomes, and key performance indicators; and identify implementation challenges and propose corrective actions as needed. The role includes coordinating communication and collaboration among government counterparts, educational institutions, experts, development partners, and project teams to ensure alignment and timely delivery of activities. The expert will compile and analyze project data, and monitoring updates, and provide the strategic guidance during coordination meetings, technical consultations, workshops, and field missions. Furthermore, the expert will contribute to quality assurance processes, maintain project documentation and records, support risk management and follow-up on agreed actions, and ensure that project implementation remains consistent with donor requirements, national priorities, and UNESCO's programme and reporting standards. Long Description DELIVERABLES Deliverable 1: Strategic Monitoring and Performance Analysis Develop and implement a strategic monitoring framework to assess progress toward project outcomes and objectives. Analyze implementation performance against key indicators, identify emerging risks and bottlenecks, provide evidence-based recommendations for adaptive management, and prepare strategic progress reports to support decision-making by UNESCO and national stakeholders. Deliverable 2: Strategic Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement Lead the coordination and alignment of project implementation among government counterparts, development partners, implementing institutions, and technical experts. Facilitate strategic review meetings, monitor the implementation of agreed actions, and support high-level stakeholder engagement to ensure coherence, partnership effectiveness, and achievement of project results. Deliverable 3: Results Reporting, Knowledge Management, and Quality Assurance Produce consolidated analytical reports on project performance, results achievement, lessons learned, and good practices. Maintain oversight of project documentation and reporting processes, support quality assurance of deliverables and activities, and provide strategic insights to inform programme planning, resource allocation, and future interventions. Long Description COMPETENCIES - Core (C) & Managerial (M) Communication (C) Accountability (C) Innovation (C) Knowlegde sharing and continuous improvement (C) Planning and organizing (C) Results focus (C) Teamwork (C) For detailed information, please consult the UNESCO Competency Framework . REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS EDUCATION Advanced university degree in education, social sciences, development studies, or related field. WORK EXPERIENCE Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible experience in M&E of education or development projects. Strong knowledge of project monitoring, results-based management (RBM), and performance measurement frameworks. Proven experience in data collection, analysis, and report writing. Excellent coordination and communication skills with government and partners. Professional experience in Uzbekistan and familiarity with national education sector priorities, institutions, and stakeholders are highly desirable. Long Description SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES Demonstrated ability to conduct strategic analysis, monitor progress against indicators, identify implementation risks, and provide evidence-based recommendations for decision-making. Excellent coordination and stakeholder engagement skills, with experience working with government institutions, development partners, educational institutions, and technical experts. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, including the capacity to synthesize complex information and translate findings into actionable recommendations. LANGUAGES Fluency in English, Uzbek and Russian. Long Description SELECTION AND RECRUITMENT PROCESS Please note that all candidates must complete an on-line application and provide complete and accurate information, by the above deadline. To apply, please visit the UNESCO Careers website . No modifications can be made to the application once submitted.  The process may include pre-recorded video interviews and/or written assessments, interviews with a Panel, as well as reference checks. In addition, candidates may be requested to provide additional information which may be pertinent to the position’s qualifications.   Please note that all candidates, whether selected or not, will be informed of the outcome of their application in due course.  Short-listed candidates may also be added to Talent Pools; subject to their consent (i.e. Data Privacy Statement). ADDITIONAL INFORMATION UNESCO recalls that paramount consideration in the appointment of personnel shall be the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, technical competence and integrity. UNESCO applies a zero-tolerance policy against all forms of harassment. lndividuals from minority groups and indigenous groups and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the highest level of confidentiality. UNESCO does not charge a fee at any stage of the hiring process. postings.text: Consultant - Laboratory Scientist in Isotopic Applications | IAEA - International Atomic Energy Agency Skip to main content Consultant - Laboratory Scientist in Isotopic Applications IAEA - International Atomic Energy Agency Seibersdorf, Monaco, Vienna Mid level Speaks Chinese, Arabic, English, French, Russian, Spanish Application deadline: November 27, 2026 (11 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The IAEA is seeking a Consultant - Laboratory Scientist in Isotopic Applications to enhance the capacity of Member States in animal production and health. The role involves optimizing, validating, and standardizing stable isotope methodologies for applications in animal nutrition, health, antimicrobial resistance detection, and traceability. The consultant will review existing methodologies, develop analytical protocols, and prepare training materials to strengthen laboratory capabilities. This position requires a strong background in stable isotope techniques and experience in laboratory quality assurance. Candidate Requirements: University degree in biological, agricultural, environmental, or health sciences Minimum two years' experience in stable isotope techniques or nuclear-related technologies Experience in preparing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) Familiarity with laboratory quality assurance and control systems Experience with isotope ratio mass spectrometry (IRMS) is desirable Strong communication skills in English; knowledge of other IAEA languages is an asset Ability to manage time effectively and meet deadlines Self-motivated with attention to detail Organizational Setting The Department of Nuclear Sciences and Applications implements the IAEA's Major Programme 2, "Nuclear Techniques for Development and Environmental Protection". This Major Programme comprises individual programmes on food and agriculture, human health, water resources, environment and radiation technologies. These programmes are supported by laboratories in Seibersdorf, Monaco and Vienna. The Major Programme's objective is to enhance the capacity of Member States to meet basic human needs and to assess and manage the marine and terrestrial environments through the use of nuclear and isotopic techniques in sustainable development programmes. The Joint FAO/IAEA Centre of Nuclear Techniques in Food and Agriculture assists Member States of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and the IAEA in using nuclear techniques and related technologies to improve food security, alleviate poverty and promote sustainable agriculture. The Joint Centre consists of five Sections, each with an associated laboratory (located in Seibersdorf, 45 km south-east of Vienna), in the areas of: animal production and health; plant breeding and genetics; insect pest control; soil and water management and crop nutrition; and food and environmental protection. The Animal Production and Health Section and Laboratory assist Member States in improving livestock productivity through the efficient use of locally available feed resources, reproduction and breeding practices, and disease diagnostic tools and control measures. Main Purpose Within the framework of its activities to support sustainable livestock development and food security, the Animal Production and Health Laboratory (APHL) of the Joint FAOjlAEA Centre of Nuclear Techniques in Food and Agriculture is engaged in strengthening Member States' capacities to address key constraints affecting animal production and health, including poor feed and nutrient utilization, low reproductive efficiency, environmental stress, infectious and transboundary animal diseases, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), and inadequate animal identification and traceability systems. APHL seeks to advance the use of nuclear and isotope techniques to improve animal production and health through enhanced assessment of nutrition, productivity, genetics, disease surveillance, traceability of animals and their products, and AMR, thereby supporting evidence-based decision-making and effective interventions .. The purpose of this consultancy is to provide technical expertise with regards to the optimization, validation, and standardization of stable isotope methodologies for applications in animal nutrition, animal health, AMR detection, and animal traceability with the key objective to establish technical and analytical capacity at the animal production and health laboratory of the Joint FAOjlAEA Centre. Functions / Key Results Expected Review and evaluate existing stable isotope methodologies used in animal nutrition, animal health, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), and animal traceability applications, and identify opportunities for optimization and sta nda rd ization. Define analytical applications of stable isotope techniques for assessing feed intake, nutrient utilization efficiency, AMR detection and surveillance, and traceability of animals and animal products. Develop and optimize analytical protocols for selected stable isotope methodologies applicable to animal production and health research and services. Carry out validation studies to assess the accuracy, precision, reproducibility, robustness, and fitness-for-purpose of optimized stable isotope methods. Prepare detailed research protocols for the application and evaluation of stable isotope techniques in animal nutrition, animal health, AMR detection, and animal traceability. Prepare Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for validated stable isotope methodologies, including sample collection, preparation, analysis, quality assurance, quality control, and data interpretation procedures. Provide technical recommendations on laboratory workflows, analytical requirements, equipment utilization, and quality management systems to support implementation of validated methodologies. Prepare training and reference materials to strengthen technical and analytical capacity of the Animal Production and Health Laboratory staff in the application of stable isotope techniques. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Animal Diseases Qualifications and Experience University degree (bachelor) in biological, agricultural, environmental, or health sciences. Minimum two years' experience in the development and application of stable isotope techniques and/or nuclear-related technologies in animal production, animal health, food systems, or related fields. Proven experience in the preparation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), laboratory quality assurance and quality control systems, and method verification/validation. Experience with laboratory procedures, quality assurance and quality control practices, and analytical techniques. Experience working with isotope ratio mass spectrometry (IRMS) and other stable isotope analytical platforms would be highly desirable. Exposure to stable isotope analysis, including isotope ratio mass spectrometry (IRMS), would be considered an advantage. Experience in research within animal, agricultural, environmental, veterinary, biological, or related life sciences, with demonstrated application. of stable isotope, nuclear, or other advanced analytical techniques to address challenges in production systems, health, traceability, or resource utilization. Experience in technical training, capacity building, and technology transfer for laboratory personnel, particularly in developing countries, is an asset. Strong communication skills, both written and oral, with proficiency in English. Excellent oral and written command of English. Knowledge of other official IAEA languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian and Spanish) is an asset. Ability to manage time effectively and meet deadlines. Self-motivated with keen attention to detail and thorough documentation skills. postings.text: Humanitarian Affairs Officer (Monitoring) | UN OCHA - Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs Skip to main content Humanitarian Affairs Officer (Monitoring) UN OCHA - Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs Bangui International P-3, International Professional - Internationally recruited position level Speaks English, French Application deadline: November 26, 2026 (10 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Humanitarian Affairs Officer (Monitoring) position is located in Bangui, Central African Republic, within the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). The role involves managing and coordinating the Country Based Pooled Fund, ensuring compliance with monitoring and reporting requirements, and supporting project management and evaluation. The officer will liaise with various stakeholders, conduct field visits, and analyze humanitarian financing information. This position requires strong analytical skills, teamwork, and the ability to work under pressure in a humanitarian context. Candidate Requirements: Advanced university degree in relevant field Minimum five years of experience in humanitarian affairs or related area Experience in project management and evaluation Humanitarian experience in emergency situations Fluency in English and French Org. Setting and Reporting This position is located in the Crisis Response Division (CRD) of the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), based in Bangui, Central African Republic (CAR). OCHA is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention, and facilitate sustainable solutions. This temporary job opening is being advertised for the position of Humanitarian Affairs Officer (Monitoring) in Bangui, Central African Republic (CAR). Under the overall supervision of the OCHA Head of Office in the Central African Republic (CAR), the incumbent reports to the Head of the Humanitarian Financing Unit. Responsibilities Within delegated authority, the Humanitarian Affairs Officer (Monitoring) will be responsible for the following duties: I. Fund Management and Coordination: • Under the supervision of the Pooled Fund Manager and Head of CAR Humanitarian Financing Unit, support and advise the HC on the overall management of the Country Based Pooled Fund vis-à-vis the humanitarian context (i.e. priorities and critical needs). • Support and advise the Pooled Fund Manager on the overall management and administration of the Fund on issues related to monitoring and reporting and liaise as necessary with relevant OCHA HQ sections. • Manage and supervise Fund-related support staff. • Participate in the process of strategic (project selection) and technical review during CAR HF allocations. • Support the process of review, selection, and quality control of proposals. • Liaise with NGOs, UN partners as well as clusters and OCHA field offices to follow-up on project progress and overall Fund progress. II. Monitoring, Reporting and Evaluation: • Ensure compliance with monitoring and reporting requirements in place for the Fund; • Support the Fund’s reporting processes, ensuring evidence-based analysis of the performance and results achieved through activities undertaken by implementing partners, in accordance with the Fund’s accountability framework. • Develop a monitoring plan and carry out monitoring activities in relation to funded projects. • Monitor funded projects portfolio, based on the Operational Modalities considering the level of risk associated with each implementing partner, project timeframes, reporting schedules and other criteria as relevant. • Conduct periodic field visits to promote the knowledge and support the appropriate use of the Fund in line with its Terms of Reference, field visits should focus on key actors (i.e. OCHA field colleagues, recipient organizations, local governments, communities). • Strengthen CAR HF planning, monitoring, and reporting processes through knowledge sharing and the synthesis of lessons learned, in support of improved decision-making. • Systematically provide information on project status to the Pooled Fund Manager for further transmission to the HoO and the HC, donors and relevant governing bodies of the Fund; • Ensure timely overall project reporting, including acting as the lead for the pooled fund annual report exercise as required. • Assist in the preparation of evaluations or other research activities and studies in consultation with relevant HQ sections (CBPF Section, EGS). III. Analysis, communications and public information: • Ensure proper communication and support during the allocation process to all stakeholders. • Liaise with and provide necessary support to recipient organizations of the Fund throughout the life-cycle of the projects, promoting coherence between humanitarian needs and response. • Advise the recipient organizations and stakeholders on measures to mitigate foreseeable operational risks. • Research, analyze and present humanitarian financing information, in particular monitoring and reporting funding trends and requirements, gathered from diverse sources. • Assist in policy development, including the review and analysis of humanitarian issues and funding trends at the country level, ensuring proper coordination with FCS. • In collaboration with other OCHA units and field offices, as well as with support from relevant OCHA HQ sections, document and disseminate results, best practices and results of the Fund across internal and broader audiences through information and communication products/pieces (i.e. bulletins, feature stories, photographs/videos, websites, etc.). • Perform other duties as assigned by the Head of CAR Humanitarian Financing Unit. Competencies • Professionalism: Sound knowledge of and exposure to a range of humanitarian assistance, emergency relief and related humanitarian issues. Knowledge of institutional mandates, policies and guidelines pertaining to humanitarian assistance. Strong analytical capacity, in particular the ability to analyze and articulate the humanitarian and protection dimension of issues which require a coordinated UN response. Good knowledge of the UN common system and humanitarian NGOs. Ability to identify issues and to use sound judgment in applying technical expertise to resolve a wide range of problems. Strong research skills, including ability to evaluate and integrate information from a variety of sources and assess impact on the humanitarian rights and protection situation in assigned country/area. Ability to work under extreme pressure, on occasion in a highly stressful environment (e.g. civil strife, natural disasters and human misery). Ability to provide guidance to new/junior staff. Excellent drafting skills and strong computer literacy (MS Word and Excel). Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. • Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. • Planning & Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. Education Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in political science, social science, international studies, public administration, economics, engineering, earth sciences or a related field. A first-level university degree in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Work Experience A minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible professional experience in humanitarian affairs, emergency preparedness, crisis/emergency relief management, project management, budget management, or related area is required. Humanitarian experience in the field (actual setting where a mission and/or project is being implemented) in emergency situations (complex emergency or natural disaster) is required. Experience in program/project management, including monitoring and evaluation is required. Experience in humanitarian financing (e.g. grant management, fundraising, or donor relations for humanitarian programmes) is desirable. Experience in a humanitarian context within the UN Common System or other comparable international organization is desirable. Experience in the design of policies and guidelines pertaining to humanitarian assistance is desirable. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. postings.text: Project Consultant - EdTech and AI at Central Square Foundation - PurposePhil Career Info Close Jobs search Project Consultant - EdTech and AI Central Square Foundation • Full-time • Tamil Nadu, India • 4d ago About Central Square Foundation Founded in 2012, Central Square Foundation is a non-profit philanthropic foundation working with the vision of ensuring quality school education for all children in India. We believe that effective foundational learning is essential for better learning outcomes for all children in school. The development of foundational literacy and numeracy skills by Class 3 can help children progress to higher levels of learning and is an essential building block in a child's life. We are driven by our mission to enable the school education system to adopt solutions that are scalable, sustainable and effective, so that all children get equal access to opportunities needed for leading a better life. CSF has prioritised 4 critical areas of work: Foundational Literacy & Numeracy (FLN); EdTech; Early Childhood Education (ECE); and Schools Governance. Read more about our work here: https://www.centralsquarefoundation.org . About EdTech at CSF CSF's EdTech initiative focuses on leveraging technology to enhance teaching and learning, both in classrooms and at home, through student-focused and teacher-directed interventions. Our goal is to improve foundational learning in primary grades and provide remediation support in middle school using evidence-based, scalable technology solutions. Since 2012, CSF has played a pivotal role in shaping India's EdTech ecosystem by bridging demand and supply, backed by rigorous research. We drive impact by: Supporting EdTech organisations to build contextually relevant, pedagogically sound products for low-income learners. Generating evidence on what works, how it works, and how to scale effective EdTech interventions. Partnering with governments to implement EdTech solutions and influence policy. Funding public goods to drive innovation and strengthen the ecosystem. In the last five years, CSF has collaborated with 15+ EdTech organisations, 11+ state governments, and leading academic institutions, reaching 2.5 million learners across India. Join us to shape the future of learning for India's children and help build an EdTech ecosystem that is evidence-driven, tech-enabled, scalable and equitable. Position Summary Central Square Foundation aims to work closely with the Department of School Education, Tamil Nadu, by providing support for the adoption and implementation of EdTech programs for the K-12 schooling system in the state. This position is a full-time assignment as part of the CSF's EdTech and AI team for this purpose. The consultant will be expected to support the execution of live projects and help start new projects by working closely with senior and junior officers in the department towards commonly aligned milestones. ﻿ Location Chennai, Tamil Nadu Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to: ﻿ Engage with relevant stakeholders within DSE-TN, including state, district, block, and school-level officials, to understand implementation progress and challenges. Coordinate with relevant stakeholders to ensure timely execution and resolution of implementation challenges. Undertake school visits, lead consultations with stakeholders to identify any implementation gaps, challenges, opportunities, and provide actionable recommendations for strengthening EdTech initiatives in the state. Support DSE-TN in the end-to-end planning, implementation, monitoring, and scale-up of EdTech and AI education initiatives. This would include, but not limited to, developing pilot proposals whenever necessary, defining objectives, creating implementation roadmap and strategies, identifying resource requirements, aligning stakeholders, creating monitoring framework, and defining expected outcomes. Analyze data and glean meaningful insights for driving adoption, student engagement, EdTech platform usage, and uptake of EdTech programs by students and teachers in schools Coordinate with CSF internal teams, technology partners, academic institutions, and implementation agencies to drive project execution, under the supervision of the team lead Prepare analytical reports, progress updates, meeting notes, presentations to inform departmental decision-making. Required Qualifications, Skills, and Abilities: ﻿ Bachelor's or equivalent degree required Minimum 4 years of work experience demonstrating strong project delivery Proficiency in English and Tamil (Written and Verbal) is mandatory Strong solution-oriented mindset with continuously seeking ways to move tasks forward despite challenges to achieve project goals efficiently and effectively. Ability to independently address and resolve issues by leveraging data, considering alternative approaches, and weighing their pros and cons meticulously Comfort with large-scale data, its analysis and reporting as per the audience profile Ability to build and maintain positive and collaborative relationships both within and outside the organisation, including with government stakeholders across hierarchies, EdTech product vendors, donor organisations, colleagues, researchers, and any other relevant stakeholders Ability to conduct and facilitate meetings with confidence, ensuring discussions are productive, objectives are met, and follow-ups are clearly defined. Ability to conduct and facilitate meetings with confidence, ensuring discussions are productive, objectives are met, and representing CSF to external audiences Ability to create detailed presentations, reports, and documentation that are thorough, accurate, and tailored to audience needs. Strong execution, planning, and organisational skills, and an ability to be able to set priorities, plan timelines and meet deadlines Compensation Remuneration will be competitive with Indian philanthropy pay scales and will depend upon the candidate's experience level Application Process ﻿Interested candidates are requested to submit an updated resume tailored to the role, a brief Statement of Purpose (not exceeding 500 words) outlining how their past experience and future aspirations align with the role, and details of two references through the CSF Careers Portal by 30th November 2026. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an initial HR call to discuss the role in detail and align on the next steps in the hiring process.﻿ Central Square Foundation Apply for this job Share this job Apply to Central Square Foundation
