postings.text: Independent Consultant (Microbiologist) | CHAI - Clinton Health Access Initiative Skip to main content Independent Consultant (Microbiologist) CHAI - Clinton Health Access Initiative Patna Both national and international Mid level Speaks Hindi, English Application deadline: December 13, 2026 (27 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool WJCF is seeking an Independent Consultant (Microbiologist) to lead technical laboratory work related to tuberculosis testing in Bihar. The consultant will assess laboratories, train staff, and support the scale-up of open RT-PCR testing for TB. This role requires collaboration with state health authorities and involves travel within Bihar. The position is for six months with the possibility of extension, focusing on improving laboratory practices and ensuring quality control. Candidate Requirements: Postgraduate degree in microbiology or related field At least 5 years of experience in molecular testing for TB Hands-on real-time PCR experience Experience in assessing or setting up laboratories Fluent in Hindi and English Ability to work independently and handle workstreams Independent Consultant (Microbiologist) Country India Type Independent Contractor Program (Division) Country Programs - India Overview WJCF is an Indian non-profit organisation committed to saving lives by reducing the burden of disease and strengthening government-owned, high-quality health systems. Since 2007, WJCF has combined data-driven approaches and deep public health expertise with strong government partnerships to design, implement, and scale solutions across India’s national and state health programmes. We work for and at the service of governments — supporting the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and State Departments of Health to build systems that are strong, sustainable, and led by Indian institutions. As an Indian organisation, WJCF brings an unmatched depth of contextual understanding of India’s health system architecture, policy landscape, and implementation realities across diverse geographies and population groups. This local institutional credibility, combined with global technical rigour, is central to WJCF’s effectiveness as a partner to governments and donors. Our work is built around four complementary roles: as a Trusted Government Partner, co-designing programmes and strengthening health system architecture; as an Operational Partner, translating strategies into effective on-the-ground delivery; as a Market Shaper, improving the availability and affordability of health commodities; and as an Ecosystem Catalyst, convening governments, development partners, academia, and the private sector to drive solutions at scale. WJCF’s programme portfolio spans thematic areas like hepatitis, HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, vector-borne diseases), syphilis, cervical cancer, diabetes, maternal and childhood anaemia, immunisation, under-5 diarrhoea and pneumonia, sexual and reproductive health, Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri – Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), hypoxemia and oxygen, safe drinking water, sickle cell disease, presbyopia, lead poisoning, and cross cutting thematic areas like AI and Health, integrated disease surveillance, and climate and health. We currently support programmes across 19 states and union territories, with teams working at national, state, district, and sub-district levels. Our people are our greatest asset. WJCF brings together a talented, diverse team of professionals from public health, analytics, consulting, healthcare, the development sector, and academia, all united by a shared commitment to improving health outcomes for the people of India. We are entrepreneurial, action-oriented, and deeply grounded in the communities and systems we work in. Our field teams collectively bring hundreds of years of experience managing public health programmes across the country. WJCF collaborates with a range of international and domestic partners and donors to advance its mission, including an affiliation with the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI), a global health organisation with which WJCF shares a common mission and values. Programme Overview India has the world's highest burden of tuberculosis (TB). The National TB Elimination Program (NTEP), led by the Central TB Division (CTD), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, aims to end TB, and expanding access to rapid molecular testing is central to that goal. WJCF has supported the CTD and state health departments on TB since 2012, across case detection, access to diagnostics, preventive therapy, private-sector engagement and technical support to governments. India built a large network of RT-PCR laboratories during COVID-19, and much of it now sits underused. With ICMR having validated an open RT-PCR kit for TB, this network could substantially expand rapid molecular testing for TB. Since July 2026, WJCF has supported the Central TB Division's operational feasibility assessment of open RT-PCR for TB, including at IGIMS Patna and Siwan District Hospital. Before the feasibility assessment was conducted, s ites collocated with o pen r eal t ime PCR and NAAT ( currently used under the programme ) were identified by the State and CTD . These facilities were individually assessed on site by a team of technical experts using a detailed structured checklist . The non -conformities were addressed ; kits and consumables were procured ; the lab personnel trained subsequently on laboratory practices by the microbiologist followed by demonstration and hands on practice facilitated jointly by a microbiologist and the manufacturer's technical representative . Learnings from the feasibility assessment encourage scale up of Open Real Time PCR - based testing for TB to other 42 poten tial sites across the state . To do this , it is vital to assess the readiness at the identified fac ility . A two - step approach with initial self - assessment by the site through a structured questionnaire will be followed by a detailed - on site assessment by technical expert is intended . The recommendations based on the findings during the assessment w ould be provided to the State health authorities for addressing non- conformities. Consequently , training of laboratory staff will be facilitated jointly by the microbiologist and the manufacturer's technical personnel . Position Summary: WJCF is looking for a microbiologist to lead the technical laboratory work cited above . Location: Patna (preferred), flexible to other base locations as well, however must be willing to t ravel within Bihar as required ( up to 20-25 days a month ) Duration: Six months, with the possibility of extension Guided by : Advisor, Diagnostics Responsibilities The work falls into four areas. The balance between them will shift over the six months, as the State's plan moves from assessment to training and rollout. Assess laboratories and plan what each need Review the self-assessment checklists already returned by labs, and follow up on gaps with respect to key metrics (AMC status, working equipment, staff in post) as required Lead on- site assessments of open RT-PCR labs across Bihar, including infrastructure, biosafety, equipment and AMCs, staffing, current workload, quality control and linkage to NAAT . Complete the assessment checklist, recommend corrective actions. Share the recommendations with the state health authorities and foll o w up o n the remedial actions taken . Estimate the quantum of kits, consumable and reagent requirements for each facility . Train and support laboratory staff Facilitate training laboratory personnel on good laboratory practices , Real time PCR principles , Biosafety ( including unidirectional workflow, use of PPE , spill management ), sample packaging and transport , equipment maintenance , quality control , contamination mitigation methods etc . Co- facilitate ( with the manufacturer's technical personnel ) on - site demonstration and hands on practice on open RT - PCR testing for TB , recording & reporting , and trouble shooting . Plan and run in-person training s for microbiologists and lab technicians with WJCF and the State, through hands-on sessions at a running lab followed by supervised testing Make mentoring visits to newly started labs, stay available for troubleshooting by phone and make supervisory visits to ensure smooth functioning Help labs put internal quality control in place, investigate contamination, interpret results correctly, and resolve results that disagree with NAAT Support the State on the systems scale-up depends on Advise on staffing norms and roles for the new microbiologist, lab technician and lab attendant posts , including job descriptions and key responsibilities S upport with designing suitable sample collection , storage and transport mechanism s Learn from the pilot labs Stay closely involved with the open RT-PCR assessment at IGIMS Patna and Siwan District Hospital, use what works there to shape the state rollout, and help these labs serve as reference and training sites Write up site visits and lessons learnt, and contribute to WJCF's operational playbook for open RT-PCR. Outputs We expect the following outputs: Readiness a ssessment findings and a readiness status for each lab visited;  Support to the State's equipment, procurement and staffing plans;  Bihar-adapted SOPs and training materials; T raining delivery; Supportive supervisory visits; S hort monthly updates; and A closing report with recommendations.  Much of this work depends on government processes, so priorities and timelines will be agreed with the Advisor, Diagnostics and reviewed every mont h. Qualifications Who we are looking for A postgraduate degree in microbiology (MD Microbiology, or MSc or PhD in Medical Microbiology / Applied Microbiology / Biotechnology/General Microbiology ) or related field . At least 5 years of relevant experience in molecular testing for TB , ideally including work with NTEP, a t IRL or NRL , or national or state governments , o r non- profit organizations . Hands-on real-time PCR experience, with a good grasp of laboratory quality systems, BSL-2 biosafety and quality assurance Experience assessing or setting up laboratories, training lab staff, and working with state government teams; knowledge of Bihar is a plus Fluent Hindi and English, and comfortable travelling across Bihar and working independently Ability to independently handle workstreams and meet deliverables in a fast-paced environments. Terms of engagement: This is an independent consultancy based in Patna. Fees will be paid monthly against invoices for progress agreed with the Advisor, Diagnostics and the State Lead, and all travel will be invoiced as per WJCF policy. All outputs belong to WJCF and the Government of Bihar, and are confidential. Last Date to apply: 13 December, 2026 At Impactpool we do our best to provide you the most accurate info, but closing dates may be wrong on our site. postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST ( LEARN-2.5-EUE-7-R1 – Senior Expert on Optimizing the Network of Vocational Training Institutions)   UKRAINE Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program GPE TF0D0613   Assignment Title: Senior Expert on Optimizing the Network of Vocational Training Institutions No . LEARN-2.5-EUE-7-R1 Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation). LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system. The objective of this assignment is to provide expert and analytical support to the MoES in coordinating activities for preparing regional plans for the formation of the network of vocational and professional pre-higher education institutions by local authorities, according to the Methodological Guidelines for Forming the Network of Institutions of Vocational and Professional Pre-higher Education, approved by the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine Order No. 216-r of March 4, 2026 . The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”).  The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.   The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest. The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 Kyiv time December 04, 2026. TERMS OF REFERENCE Consulting Services (Individual Consultant) Senior Expert on Optimizing the Network of Vocational Training Institutions Contract No. LEARN-2.5-EUE-7-R1 Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project GPE TF0D0613 Background   Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation). LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan). The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School” stipulated in the Strategic Plan. The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$737 mln  provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) – US$675.9 mln and Investment Project Financing (IPF) – US$61.1 mln. The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million. On June 9, 2026, a Loan Agreement (Third Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) was signed between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (Loan No. K019-UA) in the amount of $286 million. Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million. More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171 The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by: • financing activities for the development of preschool education; • providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms. In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning. II. OBJECTIVE OF THE TASK The purpose of this assignment is to provide expert and analytical support to the MoES in coordinating activities for preparing regional plans for the formation of the network of vocational and professional pre-higher education institutions by local authorities, according to the Methodological Guidelines for Forming the Network of Institutions of Vocational and Professional Pre-higher Education, approved by the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine Order No. 216-r of March 4, 2026. The expert will ensure that each region moves forward with the preparation of regional plans for formation of the network of vocational and professional pre-higher education institutions during the assignment period. III. SCOPE OF SERVICES The Consultant will provide the following services, including but not limited to: Coordinate engagement with regional teams and support the work of regional working groups; Conduct consultations and working discussions with representatives of regional administrations, education departments, and other relevant stakeholders; Provide guidance on the application of the Methodological Recommendations; Deliver training on the use of analytical dashboards and tools for education network planning; Provide advisory support to regional working groups responsible for developing regional plans for the establishment and optimization of vocational and professional pre-higher education networks, including guidance on the collection, analysis, and interpretation of data related to education networks, demographic trends, and labour market needs; Develop and substantiate strategic recommendations for the optimization of education institution networks; Monitor the progress of regional plan preparation and provide regular reports to the Project team. IV. REPORTING The Consultant will report to and cooperate with the Project Coordinator (Co-Coordinator) and work under the supervision of the General Director of the Directorate. For operational matters, the Consultant will coordinate his/her activities with the Head of the World Bank Operations Management Unit, ensuring effective interaction and support during project implementation. The onsultant will prepare: Monthly reports on services provided within the project execution; Regular progress reports on the work with regions; Analytical notes on the status of regional plans preparation. V. RESOURCES PROVIDED The MoES will provide the onsultant with the necessary information in a timely manner to carry out his/her duties. The MoES will also ensure the Consultant has a work station, including the necessary equipment to perform his/her functions (e.g., PC, communication tools, and office equipment). VI. QUALIFICATIONS Minimum requirements (mandatory): Master’s degree or higher in education, public administration, economics, regional development, sociology, information technology, computer science, applied mathematics, statistics, data science, systems analysis, or another related field; At least 3 years of experience working with government authorities and local self-government bodies; At least 2 years of experience in project management in the education or public administration sector; Knowledge of the regulatory and legal framework in the education sector; Proficiency in English at a minimum level of B1; Fluency in Ukrainian. Desirable skills and qualifications: Experience working with international organizations providing international technical assistance; Leadership skills and ability to work effectively in a team; Experience in drafting regulatory acts would be an advantage; Strong interpersonal communication and consensus-building skills; Ability to adapt to changing circumstances and priorities; Experience in crisis management would be an advantage.   VII. DURATION AND LOCATION The Consultant shall provide his/her services until  October 30, 2027. The contract may be extended subject to satisfactory performance and mutual agreement between the Consultant and the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine during the Project financing period. The Consultant is expected to provide services under this Agreement on an ongoing basis throughout its term at a level of engagement equivalent to full-time employment, to the extent necessary to properly perform the tasks specified in the Terms of Reference. The Consultant shall provide services primarily in Kyiv, Ukraine, and may take business trips to other regions of Ukraine to support implementation of the Project.   VIII. postings.text: Junior Electrical Systems Asset Manager (EN-EL-MO-2026-253-GRAE) | CERN - European Organization for Nuclear Research Skip to main content Junior Electrical Systems Asset Manager (EN-EL-MO-2026-253-GRAE) CERN - European Organization for Nuclear Research Geneva Junior level Speaks English, French Application deadline: December 03, 2026 (17 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Junior Electrical Systems Asset Manager will support the management of electrical equipment throughout its lifecycle at CERN. Responsibilities include managing supply contracts, preparing technical specifications, and contributing to the Computerised Maintenance Management System (CMMS). The role requires collaboration with maintenance managers and the Asset Management team to improve equipment data and work management processes. Candidates should have a strong interest in electrical assets and project management, along with good organizational and communication skills. Candidate Requirements: Knowledge of electrical assets like transformers and MV/LV switchgear Experience or interest in Computerised Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS) Understanding of project management and procurement processes Familiarity with technical documentation and engineering drawings Strong interest in electrical equipment lifecycle and maintenance Effective communication skills with stakeholders Willingness to learn and improve processes Attention to detail and organizational skills Teamwork and communication skills in English or French Company Description Job Description The Engineering Department (EN) pushes back the limits of technology so that physicists can carry out their research. Within the Electrical Engineering (EL) group of the EN department, you will join the Maintenance and Operation (MO) section, which operates and maintains CERN's electrical distribution network. Your responsibilities Contribute to the management of electrical equipment throughout its lifecycle, from procurement and installation to maintenance activities. Manage supply contracts for low-voltage switchboards: coordinate with suppliers and follow up on orders, deliveries, warranties and after-sales services. Prepare technical specifications and tender documents and contribute to the correspondent procurement activities. Contribute to define and improve equipment data models in CERN's Computerised Maintenance Management System (CMMS), so that technical information, drawings and as-built documentation are organised and kept up to date. Coordinate and follow up on site surveys, from data collection and verification to process and update the corresponding information in the CMMS. Work with maintenance managers to define preventive and corrective maintenance activities in the CMMS, including maintenance task plans, standard work orders, required resources and spare parts. Support engineers, technicians and contractors in using the CMMS through training, user guides and technical assistance. Contribute to developing dashboards and KPIs that monitor maintenance activities, equipment performance and data quality. Collaborate with the Asset Management team to improve and harmonise equipment data and work management processes across equipment families in the CMMS. More information here . Your profile Good knowledge of electrical assets such as transformers and MV/LV switchgear. First experience with, or a strong interest in, Computerised Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS). Good understanding of project management and procurement processes. Familiarity with technical documentation, specifications and engineering drawings. Skills Strong interest in electrical equipment, its lifecycle and maintenance processes. Interest in procurement and contract management, with the ability to communicate effectively with different stakeholders and follow up on commitments. Willingness to learn and to help improve existing methods and processes. Structured approach to work, with strong attention to detail. Good organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks and manage responsibilities. Positive and collaborative attitude, with strong teamwork and communication skills. Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the other language. Eligibility criteria: You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State . By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Electrical/Industrial Engineering (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree . You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before. Applicants without University degree are not eligible. Applicants with a PhD are not eligible. Qualifications Additional Information Job closing date: 03.12.2026 at 23:59 CET. Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum. Working hours: 40 hours per week Job flexibility: Fully Onsite Target start date: 01-March-2027 This position involves: Work in Radiation Areas. Interventions in underground installations. A valid driving licence. Job reference: EN-EL-MO-2026-253-GRAE Field of work: Electrical Engineering Benchmark job: 200030 - Electrical Engineer Global Benefits A monthly net stipend of either 5266 or 5793 Swiss Francs per month depending on your degree. 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure. Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund. Family, child and infant monthly allowances depending on your individual circumstances. A relocation package (installation grant and travel expenses) depending on your individual circumstances. Possibility to extend your contract up to 36 months. On-the-job and formal training including language classes. Overview of CERN - Discover a world where the impossible is made possible! At CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research, we are pushing the frontiers of science and technology. Our groundbreaking work brings together not only physicists but also a diverse range of professionals from engineering, technical, scientific, and administrative fields. Together, we foster an environment where innovation and collaboration thrive. Every day, we face exciting new challenges and opportunities to contribute to cutting-edge research that shapes our understanding of the universe. We meet these challenges through the diverse perspectives within our teams, ensuring every contribution is valued and driving our shared sense of inclusion and purpose. Diversity is a core value of CERN since its foundation, and it remains central to our mission and continued success. If you are ready to be part of a dynamic, inclusive community pushing the boundaries of knowledge, CERN is the place where your curiosity and skills can thrive. Be part of our mission to uncover what lies at the heart of the universe!  TAKE PART! postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES) Country: Pakistan Project: Getting Results: Access and Delivery of Quality Education Services in Balochistan (GRADES-B) Project Number: P507512 Assignment Title: Hiring of Consulting Firm for Engagement of a Third-Party Validation (TPV) Firm for Verification of Community-Based School Sites Identified by District Education Groups (DEGs) under GRADES-Balochistan Reference No . PK-PMU-SED GOB-576103-CS-CQS The Government of Balochistan, through the Government of Pakistan, has secured USD $100 Million funded through IDA capital credit financing from the World Bank to implement the Getting Results: Access and Delivery of Quality Education Services in Balochistan (GRADES-B) project. The project is designed to increase girls’ and boys’ enrollment in pre-primary and primary grades, and to improve reading and numeracy proficiency in primary grades, all in project-supported schools. The GRADES-B project aims to address educational disparities in Balochistan by enhancing access, quality, and equity in education. The initiative focuses on foundational literacy and numeracy, increased enrollment, and sustainable systemic reforms. The proposed project is structured around four components to address systemic challenges in the education sector of the province. They focus on improving access to education and enhancing teaching quality, strengthening data-driven accountability, building resilience to climate change , and introducing emergency preparedness mechanisms to minimize disruptions. Project Management Unit (here and after as the Client) intends to apply part of the proceeds to cover eligible payments for hiring the services of Consulting Firm for Engagement of a Third-Party Validation (TPV) Firm for Verification of Community-Based School Sites Identified by District Education Groups (DEGs) under GRADES-Balochistan (here and after as the Consulting Firm). The consulting services (“the Services”) include provision of Engagement of a Third-Party Validation (TPV) Firm for Verification of Community-Based School Sites under GRADES-Balochistan, ensuring full consistency with the TOR’s referred to in this REOI. The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment can be found at the following website:  https://pmubesp.gob.pk/  or can be obtained at the Office Address, House # 74-A Chaman Housing Scheme, Airport Road Quetta. The Project Management Unit, Balochistan Education Support Project now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A consulting firm(s)/ Joint Venture(s) will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification based Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” September, 2023. Required Expertise and Qualifications of the Firm The Firm must be a legally registered organization (in Pakistan) with demonstrated technical capacity to conduct large-scale, geographically dispersed field verification exercises. The Firm should have: At least 10 years of experience of working in Social Sector particularly Education; Must have completed at least 3 similar experiences of conducting Third Party Validations in GIS-based geo-tagging, mapping and spatial/distance analysis; Demonstrated experience in digital/mobile data collection (e.g., KoBoToolbox, ODK, SurveyCTO or similar platforms); Proven capacity to mobilize and manage field teams across multiple, geographically remote and hard-to-access districts of Balochistan (including Sherani, Chaman, Washuk, Duki, Kohlu, Barshore, Jhal Magsi, Kachhi, Sohbatpur, Chaghi, Kharan and Musa Khel); Experience of working with government departments, education projects or development partners in Balochistan or similar rural contexts; Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, i.e. 0900 to 1700 hours. Expressions of Interest (EOI) may be delivered in written form to the address given below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by 27th November, 2026 16:00 Hrs. EOI can be transmitted electronically by email to the email address ps.gradesb@gmail.com  and couriered subsequently.   Project Management Unit, Balochistan Education Support Project House # 74-A Chaman Housing Scheme Quetta Quetta, Pakistan Tel: +92812864295-6 Fax: +92812864297

postings.text: Consultoría Coordinador de innovación para la unidad de habilidades para la vida y el trabajo | UNESCO - United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization Skip to main content Consultoría Coordinador de innovación para la unidad de habilidades para la vida y el trabajo UNESCO - United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization Remote | Santiago Level 2 - Middle level Speaks English, Portuguese, Spanish Application deadline: November 27, 2026 (11 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool UNESCO is seeking a Coordinator of Innovation for the Life and Work Skills Unit to support the design and development of innovative components in digital transformation projects. The role involves establishing mechanisms for project development, designing monitoring frameworks, and coordinating with educational ministries. The consultant will also facilitate capacity-building actions and manage learning communities. This position is remote and is contracted for 11 months, focusing on enhancing educational innovation and digital skills. Candidate Requirements: Bachelor's degree in education or related field Master's degree in educational policies or digital education 4 years of project management experience 2 years in educational innovation projects Experience in developing training methodologies Experience in writing project reports Experience in coordinating with government and international entities Understanding of the 2030 Agenda and SDG4 Excellent communication skills in Spanish and English Consultoría Coordinador de innovación para la unidad de habilidades para la vida y el trabajo JOB DETAILS Type of contract : Consultant Contract Level : Level 2 - Middle Hiring Unit : Education Sector (ED) Duty Station : Santiago Work location : Remote Duration of contract : 11 months Hiring open to : External candidates Application deadline (Midnight UTC−4 Time) : 27/11/2026 UNESCO Core Values: Commitment to the Organization, Integrity, Respect for Diversity, Professionalism Requisitos para aplicar La UNESCO le invita a presentar por escrito propuestas técnica y económica de consultoría para la asignación del trabajo descrito en el numeral 3. Para la preparación de estas propuestas, además de completar la aplicación en línea (obligatoria), deberá enviar: Una propuesta técnica en la que se integre el currículum vitae detallado y actualizado del postulante; y su propuesta metodológica para el desarrollo de las funciones (numeral 3 del Término de Referencia) y productos de la consultoría (numeral 4 del Término de Referencia). Una propuesta financiera, expresada en USD y Pesos Chilenos, que considere los honorarios de esta consultoría con distribución de pagos mensual y total, incluyendo todos los costos asociados a la implementación logística de la consultoría. La UNESCO pone gran énfasis en asegurar que se cumplan los objetivos de la asignación de trabajo, como se describe en los Términos de Referencia. En consecuencia, al evaluar las propuestas para la tarea, la atención se centrará principalmente en los elementos técnicos. De las propuestas que se consideren adecuadas en función de los Términos de Referencia, la UNESCO seleccionará la propuesta que ofrezca a la Organización la mejor relación calidad-precio. Las propuestas deben enviarse, por separado (un correo electrónico para la propuesta técnica y otro correo para la propuesta económica), a la dirección roster.santiago@unesco.org hasta las 17H00 pm (hora de chile) el 20 de noviembre de 2026 . Por favor, cite en el asunto del correo electrónico lo siguiente: “Ref: STG/2026/CIC/17 Coordinador de innovación ". Debe tomar en cuenta estas condiciones para aplicar, en caso contrario las propuestas no serán consideradas. Es responsabilidad de cada postulante asegurarse de que su propuesta sea recibida antes de la fecha límite. Gracias por su interés en esta oportunidad de consultoría de la UNESCO; y esperamos recibir su propuesta. Por favor, tenga en cuenta que todos los postulantes también deben completar un formulario de postulación en línea y proveer información completa y precisa. Para postular, visite la página de Carreras UNESCO (https://careers.unesco.org/) . No se podrán hacer modificaciones una vez que la postulación haya sido enviada. La evaluación de los postulantes se basa en los criterios del Término de Referencia, y puede incluir testes y/o evaluaciones, así como una entrevista basada en competencias. La UNESCO utiliza tecnología de comunicación tales como vídeo o teleconferencia, correspondencia de e-mail, etc., para la evaluación de los candidatos. Por favor, tenga en cuenta que sólo los postulantes seleccionados serán contactados y los candidatos en la selección final estarán sujetos a verificación de referencias sobre la base de la información suministrada. 1. CONTEXTO La UNESCO conecta la educación con el mundo del trabajo en rápida evolución mediante la promoción de las competencias para el trabajo y la vida . La Educación y Formación Técnica y Profesional (EFTP) contribuye al ODS 4 y al ODS 8 sobre trabajo decente y crecimiento económico, ayudando a los jóvenes y adultos a desarrollar las competencias, habilidades, conocimientos, valores y actitudes necesarias para encontrar un trabajo digno y construir un mundo pacífico, sano, justo y sostenible. En todo el mundo, 267 millones de jóvenes de 15 a 24 años no tienen ningún tipo de empleo, educación o formación. En América Latina y el Caribe (LAC), cerca de 28 millones de jóvenes y adultos mayores de 15 años son analfabetos, y 16,4% de los jóvenes de 15 a 24 años no estudian ni trabajan. Las competencias para el trabajo y la vida se refieren a una serie de experiencias de aprendizaje que son pertinentes para el mundo del trabajo y más allá, incluyendo el estudio de tecnologías y ciencias relacionadas y la adquisición de habilidades prácticas, actitudes, comprensión, y el conocimiento que ayudan a las personas a vivir vidas sanas y satisfactorias. Desarrollar habilidades que se adapten a un mercado de trabajo cambiante a lo largo de toda la vida es crucial para el crecimiento inclusivo y sostenible, la productividad y la innovación. La transformación digital y el cambio ecológico están impulsando profundos cambios, y las economías solo pueden beneficiarse de ellos si los alumnos desarrollan las habilidades y competencias adecuadas. Por otro lado, las economías de todo el mundo se vieron afectadas por la pandemia de la COVID-19, millones de personas perdieron sus empleos o parte de sus ingresos, y se elevó el desempleo juvenil y la desproporción de cualificaciones. La UNESCO apoya a los países en la identificación de las competencias y habilidades necesarias para servir a las economías digitales y verdes, abordar el desempleo y reducir la brecha de competencias entre los géneros. Las tecnologías digitales han cambiado la forma en que se accede a los conocimientos y a la información, se comparten y se producen. La pandemia del COVID-19 aumentó significativamente la transmisión digital del conocimiento, por lo que las competencias digitales son cruciales para la participación social, incluidas las oportunidades de aprendizaje y empleo a lo largo de toda la vida. Sin embargo, durante la pandemia, los países que carecían de infraestructura suficiente para mantener sus sistemas digitales de aprendizaje sufrieron las mayores interrupciones de la educación. Esta situación dejó a más de un tercio de los estudiantes del mundo sin acceso al aprendizaje durante el cierre de las escuelas por más de un año. América Latina y el Caribe experimentó la interrupción de la educación presencial más prolongada del mundo. Entre febrero de 2020 y marzo de 2022, las escuelas estuvieron completamente cerradas durante 33 semanas y parcialmente cerradas por 37 semanas, afectando a más de 170 millones de estudiantes y sus familias.  La UNESCO apoya el uso de la innovación digital para ampliar el acceso a las oportunidades educativas y promover la inclusión, mejorar la pertinencia y la calidad del aprendizaje, construir vías de aprendizaje permanente mejoradas por las TIC, fortalecer los sistemas de educación y gestión del aprendizaje, la formación continua y el aprendizaje. Para alcanzar estos objetivos, la UNESCO trabaja en el desarrollo de la alfabetización y las competencias digitales, centrándose en los maestros y en los estudiantes. A nivel regional, en mayo de 2024, nace la Alianza Regional para la Transformación e Innovación Educativa (ARTIE) como una de las resoluciones del Comité Directivo Regional del ODS 4 para promover acciones conjuntas que apoyen a los países a institucionalizar sus procesos de innovación, acompañar la transformación digital de la educación, el desarrollo de capacidades y el intercambio de evidencia. El objetivo de ARTIE es favorecer el logro de las metas educativas de calidad e inclusión, y contribuir a la construcción de sistemas educativos más resilientes, sostenibles y adaptativos. Esta iniciativa coordinada por la UNESCO Santiago, integra la red de puntos focales de innovación educativa de los ministerios de educación de América Latina y el Caribe como un espacio de diálogo político y técnico para abordar los retos de la innovación, como es el abordaje de IA en los procesos de enseñanza aprendizaje. Adicionalmente, la UNESCO Santiago desarrolla múltiples proyectos para promover las competencias para el trabajo y la vida , apoyando a los ministerios de educación en su labor para promover la innovación educativa, fortalecer la enseñanza de competencias digitales, con un enfoque de inclusión, y énfasis en la Educación y Formación Técnico Profesional y la Educación de Jóvenes y Adultos.  El apoyo de la UNESCO Santiago a los países de la región en estas esferas ha integrado como enfoque transversal el uso de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la educación y promueve la participación de niñas y mujeres en las áreas STEAM.  La IA tiene el potencial de abordar muchos desafíos significativos en la educación, así como de llevar la innovación a las prácticas de enseñanza y aprendizaje. Al mismo tiempo, la aplicación de estas tecnologías debe guiarse por los principios de inclusión y equidad. La UNESCO apoya a los Estados Miembros en el aprovechamiento del potencial de la IA para lograr la Agenda 2030 para la Educación, utilizando un enfoque centrado en las personas. Asimismo, la UNESCO está prestando especial atención a la disparidad de género en las carreras de STEM mediante investigaciones, políticas y actividades de creación de capacidad como parte de sus esfuerzos por promover el empoderamiento de las niñas y mujeres a través de la educación. 2. Objetivo de la consultoría Apoyar el diseño y desarrollo de los componentes de innovación en las actividades y proyectos de transformación digital, Educación Técnica y Educación de Jóvenes y Adultos que la UNESCO Santiago ejecuta a través de su Unidad de Habilidades para la Vida y el Trabajo, en el marco de la Alianza Regional para la Transformación e Innovación Educativa (ARTIE) . 3. FUNCIONES DE LA CONSULTORÍA Bajo la autoridad del Jefe de Educación de UNESCO Santiago y la supervisión del Especialista en Educación a cargo de la Unidad de Competencias para el trabajo y la vida , el consultor realizará las siguientes tareas: Establecer un mecanismo para el diseño y desarrollo de los componentes de innovación en los proyectos de transformación digital, Educación Técnica y Educación de Jóvenes y Adultos que la UNESCO Santiago ejecuta a través de su Unidad de Habilidades para la Vida y el Trabajo. Diseñar líneas de base y marcos de indicadores de seguimiento para monitorear el desempeño de los componentes de innovación educativa en las actividades y proyectos de transformación digital, Educación Técnica y Educación de Jóvenes y Adultos de la Unidad de Habilidades para la Vida y el Trabajo . Sobre la base de esta información, elaborar informes técnicos, de avance y finales de los referidos proyectos. Adaptar los enfoques me

postings.text: Human Resources Specialist | FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Skip to main content Human Resources Specialist FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Haiti International Consultant - Contractors Agreement level Speaks English, French Application deadline: November 27, 2026 (11 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The FAO is seeking a Human Resources Specialist to provide technical advice and coordinate HR services for its Representation in Haiti. The role involves managing recruitment, workforce planning, performance management, and HR operations in line with FAO policies. The incumbent will also support HR reporting, process improvements, and collaborate with various stakeholders on complex HR matters. This position requires a commitment to integrity and professional conduct, as well as adherence to FAO's values. Candidate Requirements: Advanced University degree in relevant fields At least 5 years of relevant HR experience Full proficiency in English Work experience in recruitment planning and selection processes Ability to interpret and apply HR rules and regulations Experience in managing international and local travel CALL FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST - VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT : IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that Closure Date and Time displayed above are based on date and time settings of your personal device FAO is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, background and culture. Qualified female applicants, qualified nationals of non-and under-represented Members and person with disabilities are encouraged to apply; Everyone who works for FAO is required to adhere to the highest standards of integrity and professional conduct, and to uphold FAO's values FAO, as a Specialized Agency of the United Nations, has a zero-tolerance policy for conduct that is incompatible with its status, objectives and mandate, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks All applications will be treated with the strictest confidentiality FAO’s commitment to environmental sustainability is integral to our strategic objectives and operations. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) contributes to the achievement of the 2030 Agenda through FAO Strategic Framework by supporting the transformation to MORE efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agrifood systems, for better production, better nutrition, a better environment, and a better life, leaving no one behind. Organizational Setting The FAO Office in Haiti is responsible for developing, promoting, supervising, and implementing agreed strategies to address national priorities in food security, agriculture, and rural development in Haiti. It develops and maintains relations with the relevant ministries at the national level. The main objective of FAO country offices, led by an FAO Representative, is to assist governments in developing policies, programs, and projects to achieve food security, reduce hunger and malnutrition, support the development of the agriculture, fisheries, and forestry sectors, and ensure the sustainable use of their environmental and natural resources. Reporting Lines Under the overall supervision of the FAO Representative in Haiti, the direct supervision of the Head of Administration, in close collaboration with the Programme, Administration and Procurement Units. The incumbent will also work closely with the other teams within the FAO Representation. Technical Focus The Human Resources Specialist will provide technical advice and coordinate the delivery of HR services for the FAO Representation in Haiti, covering recruitment, workforce planning, performance management and HR operations, in accordance with FAO rules, regulations, policies and procedures. The incumbent will also support HR reporting, contribute to process improvements and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to address complex HR matters. Tasks and responsibilities • Support annual recruitment planning for the FAO Representation in Haiti. • Monitor and analyze filled and vacant positions, including data on post occupancy, personnel categories and grades, funding sources and gender distribution. • Manage the day-to-day operations of the HR Unit in Haiti and ensure the efficient and effective delivery of HR services. • Participate in internal and external meetings on HR-related matters, as required. • Coordinate with the Human Resources Division, the Shared Service Centre and other relevant stakeholders on HR strategies, policies, guidelines and the implementation of corporate HR initiatives in Haiti. • Support the smooth implementation of HR initiatives within the FAO Representation in Haiti. • Advise hiring managers on matters concerning staff and affiliate personnel. • Prepare briefing notes on relevant HR matters for senior management visits and missions. • Support the recruitment and hiring of staff and affiliate personnel. • Coordinate post management actions for the FAO Representation in Haiti. • Support internal and external audits on HR-related matters and follow up on the implementation and closure of agreed actions and recommendations. • Identify capacity gaps and training needs within the HR team and propose appropriate capacity development and knowledge-sharing opportunities. • Maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information with discretion. • Lead and take overall responsibility for international travel management, including planning, authorization, entitlements, and coordination for national and international personnel, ensuring compliance with FAO policies, security requirements, and L3 duty station procedures. • Supervise and oversee local travel operations, including mission planning, approvals, coordination with security and logistics of travel requests, ensuring efficiency, and compliance. • Participate in interview panels for the recruitment of affiliate personnel (but not staff members) • Exercise supervisory functions over other affiliate personnel (but not staff members) • Perform other duties as required. CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING Minimum Requirements • Advanced University degree from an institution recognized by the International Association of Universities (IAU)/UNESCO in Human Resources Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, Management, Organizational Development, Industrial/Organizational Psychology, Labour Relations, Social Sciences, Labour/Employment Law, Economics or any other discipline relevant to the work of the Organization. Consultants with bachelor's degree need two additional years of relevant professional experience. • At least 5 years of relevant experience in Human Resources, Administration and/or related areas. • Full proficiency/Working knowledge of English. FAO Core Competencies • Results Focus • Teamwork • Communication • Building Effective Relationships • Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement Technical/Functional Skills • Work experience in more than one location or area of work. • Full proficiency/Working knowledge of French is desirable. • Work experience in in recruitment planning, selection processes, hiring of staff and affiliate personnel, and post management. • Ability to interpret and apply HR rules, regulations and procedures, advise hiring managers, and support audits and follow-up on recommendations • Ability to interpret and apply HR rules, regulations and procedures, advise hiring managers, and support audits and follow-up on recommendations • Experience in managing international and local travel, including planning, authorizations, entitlements, and coordination with security and logistics, in compliance with organizational policies and L3 duty station procedures. Please note that all candidates should adhere to FAO Values of Commitment to FAO, Respect for All and Integrity and Transparency ADDITIONAL INFORMATION FAO does not charge any fee at any stage of the recruitment process (application, interview, processing) Please note that FAO will only consider academic credentials or degrees obtained from an educational institution recognized in the IAU/UNESCO list Please note that FAO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU) / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed at http://www.whed.net/ For more information, visit the FAO employment website Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, and security clearances. HOW TO APPLY • To apply, visit the recruitment website at Jobs at FAO and complete your online profile. We strongly recommend that your profile is accurate, complete and includes your employment records, academic qualifications, and language skills • Candidates are requested to attach a letter of motivation to the online profile • Once your profile is completed, please apply, and submit your application • Please note that FAO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU) / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – SELECTION OF INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS)   Republic of Uzbekistan Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project Credit No.: 7425-UZ   Assignment Title: Social Specialist for the construction and renovation of ITES Centers Reference No.: UZ-DIP-581363-CS-INDV   The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the International Development Association toward the cost of the Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project. “Administration of Technology Park of Software and IT” LLC (IT Park), as the Implementing Agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds to engage an individual consultant as Social Specialist for Component 2.2 of the Project. Under Component 2.2, the Project finances the construction and the reconstruction of ITES Centers in the regions. To meet the requirements of the Project’s Environmental and Social Commitment Plan, IT Park will engage three individual consultants under separate contracts: an Environmental Specialist (including Occupational Health and Safety), a Social Specialist and a Stakeholder Engagement Specialist. This Request for Expressions of Interest concerns the Social Specialist. The Social Specialist will support IT Park as the lead specialist for social risk management at the construction sites: labour and working conditions of contractor and subcontractor workers, the workers’ grievance mechanism, prevention of and response to sexual exploitation and abuse / sexual harassment, social aspects of community impacts and accessibility for persons with disabilities, in line with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework and the labour legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan. The consulting services (“the Services”) include, but are not limited to: social screening of Project activities and land plots, including any economic or physical displacement under World Bank Environmental and Social Standard 5 (ESS5) review and preparation of the social parts of the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment / Environmental and Social Management Plans, including measures for building users during works; review of designs for accessibility for persons with disabilities and social inputs to the public consultations on the ESMPs; preparation of the labour, community health and safety and SEA/SH parts of the environmental and social requirements, the Code of Conduct for contractor personnel and the bidder declaration for each works tender, and verification that the signed works contracts include them; review of the social sub-plans of each contractor’s Environmental and Social Management Plan and induction of the contractor’s management on the Labour Management Procedures, the Code of Conduct, the workers’ grievance mechanism and SEA/SH requirements. The assignment is expected to start in December 2026 and to continue until the taking-over of the last of the construction sites and acceptance of the final report, currently expected in the first half of 2029. To obtain the Terms of Reference for the assignment, please send your request to the following e-mail address: udip@it-park.uz. “Administration of Technology Park of Software and IT” LLC now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services: a curriculum vitae in the English language, copies of diplomas and contact details of references. The evaluation criteria are: 1) Education University degree in social sciences, sociology, development studies, law, public administration or a related field. 2) Experience At least 5 years of experience in social risk management and labour issues; At least 3 years of experience on projects financed by the World Bank or other international financial institutions; Proven experience in implementing LMP and workers’ grievance mechanisms and monitoring contractors’ labour practices; Experience with SEA/SH prevention and response and with construction projects is an advantage. 3) Knowledge World Bank ESF (ESS1, ESS2, ESS4; ESS10 as relevant), including SEA/SH requirements; Labour Code and related legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan; Gender and inclusion issues; work with mahalla committees and local authorities. 4) Language Fluent Uzbek and Russian; Good working English. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Fifth Edition, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest, and to paragraph 3.21 on eligibility. The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations, based on a comparison of qualifications and experience. Shortlisted candidates may be interviewed. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours: 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Tashkent time. postings.text: E T Consultant - Nature Based Solutions Specialist | World Bank Group Skip to main content E T Consultant - Nature Based Solutions Specialist World Bank Group New Delhi Both national and international EC3 - Extended Term Consultant Appointment level Speaks Hindi, English Application deadline: November 26, 2026 (10 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The World Bank is seeking an ET Consultant - Nature-Based Solutions Specialist to provide technical and operational support for coastal resilience projects in South Asia. The role involves advising on the design and implementation of nature-based solutions (NBS) for coastal ecosystems, including mangrove and coral reef conservation. The consultant will engage with stakeholders, support capacity building, and contribute to knowledge sharing on NBS practices. This position requires a strong background in marine ecology, coastal management, and relevant professional experience in sustainable development. Candidate Requirements: Master's degree in marine ecology, coastal engineering, or related field Minimum 8 years of relevant experience in nature-based solutions Knowledge of mangrove restoration and coastal ecosystem management Strong technical skills in remote sensing and GIS Excellent analytical and writing skills Experience in South Asia and familiarity with Coastal Regulation Zone framework Ability to work in multi-disciplinary teams Strong results orientation and ability to work under tight timelines E T Consultant - Nature Based Solutions Specialist Job #: req39138 Organization: World Bank Sector: Environment Grade: EC3 Term Duration:  1 year 0 months Recruitment Type: Local Recruitment Location: New Delhi,India Required Language(s): English, Hindi Preferred Language(s): Closing Date: 11/26/2026 (MM/DD/YYYY) at 11:59pm UTC Description At the World Bank, a member of the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. For more information, visit  https://www.worldbank.org/en/who-we-are/ibrd India's 11,099-kilometer coastline is home to 250 million people and supports key blue economy sectors including fisheries, tourism, agriculture, and transport. Despite its ecological richness, India's coastal ecosystems face mounting pressure from climate-induced hazards, coastal erosion, pollution, and land-use change. One-third of India's coastline is reported as vulnerable to erosion, threatening livelihoods, settlements, and biodiversity of global significance. The SHORE MPA has begun implementation in the states of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka under Phase 1 and will be expanded to other coastal states such as Goa, Maharashtra, Puducherry and West Bengal under subsequent phases. It aims to increase the resilience of targeted coastal communities and ecosystems, focusing on four components: (i) strengthening institutions for Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM); (ii) shoreline management, coastal protection and conservation; (iii) improving livelihoods for natural resource-dependent communities; and (iv) enhancing marine pollution management and plastic circularity.  Nature-based solutions (NBS) are central to Component 2, which supports mangrove, seagrass and coral reef conservation management and restoration, along with shelter belts, bio-shields, and hybrid coastal erosion management measures such as beach nourishment, sand dune stabilization, artificial reefs, and others. Where relevant, NBS investments should be coordinated with livelihood activities such as eco-tourism and mangrove-friendly value chains to ensure that conservation-livelihood tradeoffs are managed. The project also involves establishment of Centers of Excellence for coastal ecosystem management, long-term biodiversity monitoring, and eco-tourism.  The Environment (ENV) Department in South Asia seeks to recruit a highly skilled and motivated ET Consultant (Nature-based Solutions Specialist) to provide technical, operational, and analytical support to the World Bank task team and the state-level implementing agencies in planning, implementing, and monitoring nature-based solutions for coastal resilience under the SHORE MPA. The ET Consultant will report to the ENV Practice Manager for the South Asia Region (SAR) and work under the supervision of the SHORE Task Team Leaders. The South Asia Region comprises six countries (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, and Sri Lanka) that range in size from India (with a population of over 1 billion) to Maldives (with 0.3 million people). The region has experienced a long period of robust economic growth, averaging 6% a year over the past 20 years. It was the second-fastest growing region in the world in the aftermath of the global crisis. This strong growth has translated into declining poverty and impressive improvements in human development. The percentage of people living below the poverty line fell in South Asia from 56% to 16% between 1981 and 2013. Still, the region remains home to a third of the world’s poorest, with 216 million people living below $1.9/day.  The South Asia Region:  https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/sar The Environment Department (ENV), located within the World Bank’s Planet Practice Group has been established to deliver on the opportunities, benefits and outcomes offered by enhanced management of the environment and natural resources. ENV provides expertise, technical assistance and financing to help countries manage land, sea and freshwater natural resources in a sustainable way to help create jobs, improve livelihoods, enhance ecosystem services, decrease pollution and increase resilience to climate change. Over 360 ENV staff working across the globe help set developing countries on a clean, green growth trajectory for resilient economies and healthy communities. The SSAE1 unit comprises around 30 staff, with 95 percent based in Country Offices. The rest of the team is based in Washington DC. Our Sri Lanka country office is a joint World Bank/International Finance Cooperation office, comprising approximately 100 staff, including an ETC working on environment, providing a vibrant, collegial working environment. Duties and accountabilities: The ET Consultant will have the following tasks: 1)Technical Advisory and Operational Support  •Provide technical guidance to the task team and clients on the design, siting, and implementation of NBS interventions including mangrove, coastal sandy-soil & cliff forests, seagrass and coral reef conservation and restoration, bio-shields and shelter belts, and hybrid erosion management. •Support preparation and quality review of sub-project-level technical designs for NBS activities, including for e.g. Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), and Biodiversity Management Plans (BMPs). •Advise on screening of NBS sub-project sites to avoid ecologically sensitive areas, no-go zones, and areas with high biodiversity value in line with State Coastal Zone Management Plans (CZMP) and Shoreline Management Plans (SMP). •Contribute to Implementation Support Missions and progress report reviews from implementing agencies related to NBS design and implementation. 2)Global Knowledge and Technical Expertise •Support the implementation of nature-based solutions-related advisory services and knowledge products, including through technical inputs, guidance materials, and planning for the timely delivery of analytical products.  •Generate and curate knowledge, such as by identifying best practices and lessons learned on NBS for coastal protection, and promote dissemination at the national and global levels. •Support the team in technical assessments/analyses related to NBS e.g. cost-benefit analysis frameworks for NBS interventions, assessment of ecosystem services and livelihoods benefits. •Support the design and operationalization of long-term NBS/ecosystem monitoring programs in line with project results frameworks. 3)Stakeholder Engagement and Capacity Building •Contribute to the engagement and policy dialogue with government counterparts and other collaborators in the NBS space. •Support capacity building and knowledge sharing activities for state officials, community groups, and technical staff on NBS principles, implementation, and adaptive management. This may include knowledge exchange between SHORE state teams, with national institutions (e.g., NCSCM, NIOT, NCCR, IIT-Madras, SDMRI), and with other countries that are implementing coastal NBS projects. •Engage with local natural-resource dependent communities and Self-Help Groups (SHGs) in the design of community-driven NBS interventions. Selection Criteria • Master's (or higher) degree in marine ecology, coastal engineering, forestry, environmental science, natural resource management, geography, or a closely related field. • Minimum of 8 years of relevant professional experience in nature-based solutions, forestry/mangroves, coastal ecosystem management, coastal resilience, natural resource management, and/or sustainable development fields with demonstrated experience in World Bank operations and analytics. • Demonstrated knowledge and expertise on nature-based solutions, which may include mangrove restoration, coral reef rehabilitation, seagrass conservation, shelter belts, bio-shields, or green-grey hybrid coastal protection. • Strong technical skills with remote sensing, coastal modeling tools, or GIS as applied to coastal ecosystem management. • Strong analytical skills, ability to think strategically, analyze and synthesize diverse qualitative and quantitative data and information. Ability to develop, conduct, or review assessments of NBS design and implementation is an advantage. • Excellent writing skills and ability to produce high-quality analytical and advisory outputs for both technical and non-technical audiences. • Experience working on South Asia and familiarity with the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notification framework and ICZM principles in the Indian context is an advantage.  • Good team player who can work as a member of a multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural team, motivate and lead group efforts and network effectively across boundaries.  • A drive for results while working with limited supervision and under tight timelines. Additional Considerations: As the World Bank Group continues to evolve, we value candidates who: • Demonstrate the ability to collaborate effectively across teams, disciplines, cultures, and institutional boundaries. • Responsibly leverage digital and AI-enabled tools to enhance productivity, learning, and decision-making. • Bring experience working on fragile, conflict-affected, and violent (FCV)-related contexts and are encouraged to highlight relevant experience in their application materials, where applicable. Empowerment and accountability: Empower yourself and others to act and hold each other accountable for results. The consulting services (“the Services”) include route selection and survey, feasibility study, detailed engineering design, Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and preparation of tender documents for Lot I:  Feasibility study & detail design of Key kokab - Gelkem- Kelt Rural Access Roads (30 Km) in Maji Woreda &  Duku-Tulgit-Haro Rural Access Roads (20 Km) in Surma Woreda  Lot II: Feasibility study & detail design of Nada-Kumba-Bunanta- Meshgebezh-Shallo Rural Access Roads (50 Km) in Goba Woreda & Shasha-Kira- Aduba Rural Access Roads (35 Km) in Meanit Shasha Woreda.  Lot III:  Feasibility study & detail design of Turga River Medium span bridge (16m) Goba woreda & Kibish River Large span bridge (70m) in Anjo Kebele, Surma Woreda. The Services will be carried out in two phases, following the latest Ethiopian Roads Administration (ERA) design manuals and quality manual, the LLRP-II environmental and social instruments and the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF): (a)   Phase I – Route Selection and Survey, and Feasibility Study: identification and multi-criteria comparison of at least three alternative routes; site reconnaissance and investigation; stakeholder consultation; traffic counts and axle load surveys; full topographic survey and Digital Terrain Model; preliminary design; ESIA of the selected route; preliminary cost estimates; economic evaluation; and climate and natural hazard vulnerability assessment. (b)  Phase II – Detailed Engineering Design, ESIA and Preparation of Bidding Documents: materials and site investigation; geometric, drainage, pavement, geotechnical and bridge/structural design, including an independent bridge design check; road safety design and audit; utilities and private accesses; estimate of the construction contract period; final ESIA and Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP); and preparation of bidding documents based on the World Bank Standard Procurement Documents, including technical specifications, drawings, bills of quantities and the Engineer’s cost estimate. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. Provide training and on-the-job training for procurement management to MOH staff and provincial and district-level personnel. Support the finance team in financial planning to ensure it aligns with procurement schedules and that funds are available when payments are due. Execute procurement of health products as per the approved procurement plan. Responsible for processing importation and shipping documents required for customs clearance. Monitor procurement and budget/expenditure to identify savings and/or overspending. Coordinate with the finance team to ensure that any revisions to the health products budget are reflected in the detailed budget. Perform other duties as may be requested by the Project Manager and Directors.   Duration and Place of Work   The consultant will work on a full-time basis at the DPF, Ministry of Health situated in Vientiane.  Adequate space and equipment will be provided to perform the work. The duration of the contracts is xxx years. However, the consultant performance will be reviewed annually and only upon satisfactory performance the continuation of the contract for the next year will be approved.   Reporting The consultant will report to the DPF, DHP, and HPC will be responsible for monitoring the Consultant’s performance, reviewing deliverables, providing technical guidance, coordinating with relevant departments and stakeholders, and ensuring that the services are implemented in accordance with the contract requirements and the Terms of Reference.   Qualifications   The Ministry of Health (MOH) proposes to recruit a Senior Procurement Consultant to support procurement activities under the project due to the complexity of procurement processes, the need for coordination with multiple health departments, and the requirement to comply with the procurement procedures of international development partners.
