postings.text: Greening Agriculture Knowledge Management, Monitoring and Reporting Specialist | FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Skip to main content Greening Agriculture Knowledge Management, Monitoring and Reporting Specialist FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Multiple locations International Consultant - Contractors Agreement level Speaks English Application deadline: November 28, 2026 (12 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The FAO is seeking a Greening Agriculture Knowledge Management, Monitoring and Reporting Specialist to support the Greening Agriculture Team in the Near East and North Africa region. The role involves monitoring and reporting on the implementation of the regional work programme, enhancing knowledge management, and facilitating collaboration among various stakeholders. The incumbent will develop monitoring tools, prepare progress reports, and coordinate regional knowledge-sharing events. This position aims to strengthen the delivery of FAO's strategic objectives related to sustainable agrifood systems. Candidate Requirements: Advanced university degree in relevant fields 1-10 years of relevant experience in knowledge management, monitoring, and reporting Working knowledge of English Experience in organizing regional meetings and workshops Ability to analyze and synthesize information Proficient in Microsoft Office applications CALL FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST - VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT : IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that Closure Date and Time displayed above are based on date and time settings of your personal device FAO is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, background and culture. Qualified female applicants, qualified nationals of non-and under-represented Members and person with disabilities are encouraged to apply; Everyone who works for FAO is required to adhere to the highest standards of integrity and professional conduct, and to uphold FAO's values FAO, as a Specialized Agency of the United Nations, has a zero-tolerance policy for conduct that is incompatible with its status, objectives and mandate, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks All applications will be treated with the strictest confidentiality FAO’s commitment to environmental sustainability is integral to our strategic objectives and operations. Organizational Setting The Regional Office for the Near East and North Africa (RNE) leads FAO's support to countries in the region in transforming their agrifood systems to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It identifies regional priorities for food security, agriculture and rural development and ensures the planning and implementation of FAO's strategic response in the region through a multidisciplinary approach. It implements approved programmes and projects, monitors programme implementation and ensures that they contribute to addressing regional priorities. RNE also advises on the incorporation of regional priorities into the FAO Strategic Framework and Programme of Work and Budget. RNE supports regional policy dialogues, facilitates the emergence of regional partnerships, and supports knowledge exchange, capacity development and resource mobilization for food security, agriculture and rural development in the region. It develops and maintains relations with region-wide institutions including the Regional Economic Integration Organizations (REIOs). To strengthen the delivery and demonstrate the results of its regional priorities, RNE places particular importance on effective monitoring, knowledge management and reporting. Regional Priority 3 (RP3), focusing on Greening Agriculture, Water Scarcity and Climate Change, is one of the key priorities guiding FAO's support to countries in the region. A coherent regional monitoring approach is essential to tracking progress against the Greening Agriculture Agenda, measuring results and impact across countries and interventions, consolidating evidence and lessons learned, and identifying gaps and opportunities for scaling up successful approaches. It also provides an important basis for evidence-informed policy and programming, accountability, and communicating FAO's contribution to sustainable and climate-resilient agrifood systems. The assignment will be carried out under the Greening Agriculture Team, Near East Regional Office (RNE). The assignment aims to provide support to the Greening Agriculture Team in monitoring and reporting on the implementation and results of the regional work programme, supporting work planning and reporting processes, and strengthening knowledge management and knowledge exchange across the region. The assignment will contribute to FAO's strategic objectives and the implementation of the regional priority on Greening Agriculture, including through improved monitoring of results, knowledge sharing, and regional coordination. Reporting Lines The incumbent will report to the Greening Agriculture Team Leader – Senior Programme Officer. Technical Focus The incumbent will contribute to the development and maintenance of monitoring and reporting tools and processes, consolidation of information from technical teams and FAO country offices, preparation of progress reports and management updates, and documentation of results, good practices and lessons learned. The incumbent will also support regional coordination mechanisms and networks, including the organization and follow-up of meetings, webinars, workshops and consultations, and facilitate collaboration and information exchange between FAO country offices and the Regional Office. Tasks and responsibilities • Support the monitoring and reporting of the Greening Agriculture work programme, including tracking activities, outputs, milestones, results and achievements against postings.text: MINISTRY OF TRANSPORTS AND LOGISTICS MAPUTO METROPOLITAN AREA URBAN MOBILITY PROJECT Grant No.: IDA-E0660-MZ REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTANCY SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) Assignment Title:  CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR DETAILED ENGINEERING DESIGN FOR CONSTRUCTION OF MUNICIPAL ROADS AND STORMWATER SYSTEM Reference No.:  107/CONS/MMAUMP/26 INTRODUCTION The Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) is inviting Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified and experienced Consultancy Firms to provide “Consultancy Services for Detailed Engineering Design for Construction of Municipal Roads and Stormwater System”. The EOI will lead to a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the below-mentioned Consultancy Services package from the short-listed Consultants. BACKGROUND The Government of Mozambique, represented by the Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Maputo Metropolitan Area Urban Mobility Project (PMUAMM), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The specific objective of the assignment is to provide The Maputo Metropolitan Area Urban Mobility Project (PMUAMM) intends to hire Consulting services for detailed engineering design for the construction of 6 municipal roads and a stormwater system. The consulting services (the Services) include , but not limited to (1) Conducting all field surveys, investigations, and specialized studies including topographic, geotechnical, hydrological, and traffic surveys necessary to underpin a robust and technically sound detailed engineering design for the municipal road corridors covered under this assignment, in full compliance wih the principles of technical, social, and environmental sustainability; (2) Preparing the detailed engineering design for each road corridor, including geometric alignment options, typical cross-sections, preliminary drainage layouts, pavement structure alternatives, and landscaping and road furniture proposals, with sufficient detail to allow the Client to validate the design direction before committing to detailed design; (3) Providing design support during the procurement phase of the civil works contracts, including responses to technical queries raised by bidders, preparation of addenda where design clarifications or corrections are required, and participation in bid evaluation on technical matters, to ensure the integrity of the design is preserved through to contract award. SCOPE OF SERVICES  The Ministry of Transport and Logistics now invites eligible consulting firms (Consultants) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.  The consulting firm that is to be selected shall have it’s core business and experience as consultancy in design of roads, particularly in urban or peri-urban environment and stormwater systems. Must be an officially registered consulting firm on it’s country of origin. The short-listing criteria will be as follows: (i) Core Business:  Proven experience in the various stages required, namely technical and economic feasibility studies, preliminary design (preliminary project), executive project (detailed) designs and preparation of tender documents (specifications and bills of quantities); (ii) Demonstrated experience of having prepared, in the last 5 to 10 years, a minimum number of road engineering projects (3 completed projects with at least 10.0 km long) with technical characteristics equivalent to the object of the competition. At least one such project should be in an urban environment; (iii) Demonstrated experience in designing roads with public transport facilities; (v) Experience in conducting watershed studies and dimensioning of stormwater drainage (ditches, aqueducts and bridges); (vi) Experience in soil prospecting, laboratory tests and structural design of the pavement (Geotechnics and Paving) and experience in plan and altimetric and cadastral surveys ((Topography and Geodesy). Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The Consultancy will have a duration of 8 months, from the effectiveness day of the assignment.  Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. Any party to the association, either joint venture member’s or sub-contractor’s experience will count on the qualifications criteria. In the case of a Joint Venture (JV), the Consultant shall specify the lead partner and all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14 to 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated July 2016, revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2023, February and September 2025 setting forth the World Bank’s Policy on Conflict of Interest. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. Only shortlisted Consultants will be approached directly by Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) to submit proposals for the services required in the RFP phase. The EOI document shall be prepared and submitted in a written form to the address below (in person or by e-mail) until 10:00 h (Maputo time), November 27, 2026. Ministério dos Transportes e Logística Projecto de Mobilidade Urbana na Área Metropolitana de Maputo Rua de Mukumbura 164 (Recinto do INAM), Cidade de Maputo Email: aquisicoes@movemaputo.gov.mz Maputo – Mozambique

postings.text: E T Consultant - Environmental Engineer | World Bank Group Skip to main content E T Consultant - Environmental Engineer World Bank Group Dhaka Both national and international EC2 - Extended Term Consultant Appointment level Speaks English Application deadline: November 26, 2026 (10 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The World Bank is seeking an Environmental Engineer to support its environment portfolio in Bangladesh. This role involves providing technical implementation support, reviewing engineering designs, and assisting in project preparation and delivery. The candidate will work closely with task teams and clients to ensure effective project execution and coordination. The position requires a strong engineering background and the ability to manage multiple work-streams effectively. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. For more information, visit   https://www.worldbank.org/en/who-we-are/ibrd The Environment (ENV) Department in South Asia seeks to recruit a highly capable Environmental Engineer to provide operational, coordination, and implementation support across the World Bank's environment portfolio in Bangladesh. The role spans both lending operations and analytical and advisory work, focused on four areas: pollution management and air quality, centered on implementation of the Bangladesh Clean Air Project (BCAP); resource efficient and cleaner production through Sustainable Microenterprise and Resilient Transformation Project; sustainable coastal resilience, centered on preparation of the Bangladesh Coastal Resilience Program (BCRP); and carbon pricing and market-based instruments. This position will be based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The Environmental Engineer will report to the ENV Practice Manager for the South Asia Region (SAR) and work as part of the World Bank Bangladesh Country Unit. Locally recruited staff are remunerated on a local pay scale. The Environmental Engineer will play a technical role, not a general program-management role in supporting specific operations within the environment portfolio, which includes significant infrastructure investments, such as buildings, laboratories, waste management facilities and rural infrastructure. The Specialist will therefore be expected to bring a strong engineering background, ideally in civil, environmental, or related discipline, with hands-on experience in the design of infrastructure projects. The Specialist will specifically review designs, technical specifications, and bills of quantities. They will also help assess the quality and feasibility of engineering work and advise teams and counterparts on technical issues that arise during preparation and implementation. The role is operationally focused. Working under the guidance of the relevant Task Team Leaders, the Specialist will help teams move operations and advisory activities through preparation, effectiveness, and implementation, keeping coordination, procurement and disbursement follow-up, counterpart engagement, and delivery of analytical outputs on track. The position is suited to a proven operator with engineering design skills who can manage multiple work-streams in parallel, troubleshoot bottlenecks, and deliver results with limited supervision.  The South Asia Region comprises six countries (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, and Sri Lanka) that range in size from India (with a population of over 1 billion) to Maldives (with 0.3 million people). The region has experienced a long period of robust economic growth, averaging 6% a year over the past 20 years. It was the second-fastest growing region in the world in the aftermath of the global crisis. This strong growth has translated into declining poverty and impressive improvements in human development. The percentage of people living below the poverty line fell in South Asia from 56% to 16% between 1981 and 2013. Still, the region remains home to a third of the world’s poorest, with 216 million people living below $1.9/day.  The South Asia Region:  https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/sar The Environment Department (ENV), located within the World Bank’s Planet Practice Group has been established to deliver on the opportunities, benefits and outcomes offered by enhanced management of the environment and natural resources. ENV provides expertise, technical assistance and financing to help countries manage land, sea and freshwater natural resources in a sustainable way to help create jobs, improve livelihoods, enhance ecosystem services, decrease pollution and increase resilience to climate change. Over 360 ENV staff working across the globe help set developing countries on a clean, green growth trajectory for resilient economies and healthy communities. The SSAE1 unit comprises around 30 staff, with 95 percent based in Country Offices. The rest of the team is based in Washington DC. Our Sri Lanka country office is a joint World Bank/International Finance Cooperation office, comprising approximately 100 staff, including an ETC working on environment, providing a vibrant, collegial working environment. Duties and accountabilities: The Extended Term Consultant will, under the guidance of the relevant Task Team Leaders: • Support WB clients and task teams to accelerate project implementation and design. • Provide technical implementation support to clients and task teams by reviewing/providing guidance on engineering designs, drawings, technical specifications, bills of quantities, cost estimates, and related technical documentation prepared by implementing agencies or their consultants. Supervise field activities as needed. • Support the preparation and implementation of WB-financed projects by reviewing and supporting the implementation of operational documents such as Project Operational Manuals, terms of reference, results data, Management Information Systems, etc. and providing feedback drawing on experience from other relevant programs including previous WB-financed projects. • Support delivery of analytical and advisory activities, including working with consultants, firms and clients to ensure timely and high-quality delivery, monitoring/supervising deliverable timelines, providing feedback on data or draft reports/products, and organizing meetings/consultations/discussions and other items as prioritized by PM and supervising TTLs. • Support mission preparation and delivery, including logistics, consultation meetings, and drafting of mission technical notes, management letters, and any agreed actions and its follow ups. Travel to remote field sites will be required.  • Contribute to written products and communications, including components of ISRs, briefs, technical notes, concept notes, and project documents. • Support coordination and liaison with government, development partners, NGOs, civil society, private sector, and academia, including organizing and supporting events, workshops, and meetings. • Perform other operational tasks assigned by the PM and/or Task Team Leaders. Selection Criteria • Master's degree in engineering (civil, environmental, structural, or a closely related discipline). A bachelor's degree in engineering combined with significant relevant experience may be considered. Additional qualifications in project management, public policy, or environmental management are an advantage. • 8+ years of proven, relevant experience in the design, review, or supervision of infrastructure projects, such as buildings, laboratories, waste management facilities, and rural infrastructure. Experience with development projects, ideally with the World Bank or other multilateral development banks, is strongly preferred. • Demonstrated, hands-on engineering design skills, including the ability to review architectural and engineering designs, technical specifications, drawings, and bills of quantities. The candidate should be able to assess technical quality, cost estimates, and constructability, and to advise on design standards and construction supervision. • Demonstrated experience in procurement of works, goods, and consulting services, and in contract management and disbursement monitoring for donor-financed projects. Familiarity with financial management oversight is an advantage • Experience with private sector engagement and public-private partnerships is an advantage.   • Proven ability to follow up multiple work-streams simultaneously and deliver results under tight timelines with limited supervision.  • Working knowledge of the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework and Bank operational procedures, or the ability to acquire it quickly.  • Familiarity with the environment, climate, air quality, coastal and water, or carbon markets agendas in Bangladesh is an advantage.  • Ability to work well with a range of stakeholders, including government officials, project-affected parties, non-governmental organizations and civil society, development partners, and private sector.   • Excellent writing and communication skills in both Bangla and English are required. • Strong interpersonal and team skills, and the ability to work as a member of a multidisciplinary and multicultural team. • Ability and willingness to travel frequently to project sites domestically is required. Additional Considerations: As the World Bank Group continues to evolve, we value candidates who: • Demonstrate the ability to collaborate effectively across teams, disciplines, cultures, and institutional boundaries. • Responsibly leverage digital and AI-enabled tools to enhance productivity, learning, and decision-making. • Bring experience working on fragile, conflict-affected, and violent (FCV)-related contexts and are encouraged to highlight relevant experience in their application materials, where applicable. postings.text: Private Markets Risk Senior Research Intern | UNJSPF - United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund Skip to main content Private Markets Risk Senior Research Intern UNJSPF - United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund Remote | New York City Both national and international Internship level Speaks English, French Application deadline: November 25, 2026 (9 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund is seeking a Private Markets Risk Senior Research Intern to support the Investment Risk and Performance team. This remote internship will focus on enhancing the assessment and monitoring of private-market investments. Responsibilities include researching industry dynamics, assessing investment risks, and developing a Private Markets Risk Assessment Framework. The intern will document findings and participate in knowledge-sharing sessions with the team. Candidate Requirements: Enrolled in or completed a graduate program or final year of a bachelor's degree Good knowledge of MS Word and MS PowerPoint Interest in investment management, finance, or related fields Knowledge of investment analysis and risk management is desirable Ability to conduct independent research and communicate findings clearly Fluency in spoken and written English Work Location Remote Expected duration 4-6 months Duties and Responsibilities The United Nations Secretary-General is responsible for the investment of the assets of the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund (UNJSPF). The Secretary-General has delegated this responsibility to the Representative of the Secretary-General for the investment of the assets of the UNJSPF (RSG). The RSG heads the Office of Investment Management (OIM), which manages approximately $100+ billion multi-asset class, global investment portfolio, about 80% of which is actively managed in-house. Asset classes under management comprise global equities, fixed income, foreign exchange, private equity, real estate, infrastructure, timber and commodities. OIM’s staff are all based in New York but come from over 30 countries. For more information please visit OIM's website at https://oim.unjspf.org/. This internship position is located in Investment Risk and Performance within Risk and Compliance of the Office of Investment Management (OIM), United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund. The Investment Risk and Performance team provides independent risk analysis, performance oversight and challenge across OIM’s investment activities, including the assessment and monitoring of portfolio, market, liquidity, valuation, manager and private-market investment risks. The incumbent reports to the Chief, Investment Risk and Performance. This is a part-time, fully remote internship. Private Markets Investment Risk Research and Framework Development The intern will support the Investment Risk and Performance team in strengthening its independent assessment and monitoring of private-market investments. The work will focus on developing a practical and repeatable approach for assessing specialized industries, investment managers and complex private-market transactions, and for linking pre-investment assumptions with ongoing risk and performance monitoring. Tasks will include: • researching the economics, value chains, competitive dynamics and principal risk and return drivers of specialized industries; • identifying material industry and business-model risks, including technological, regulatory, commercial, financing and execution risks; • researching approaches for assessing private-market transactions, including valuation, leverage, liquidity, capital structure, downside risk and exit assumptions; • reviewing investment underwriting assumptions and identifying factors that could materially weaken or invalidate the original investment thesis; • researching approaches to investment-manager assessment, including investment process, portfolio construction, diversification, governance, valuation practices and monitoring; • supporting the development of a Private Markets Risk Assessment Framework for evaluating industry, company, manager, portfolio and transaction-specific risks; • developing practical due-diligence questions to support independent risk review and challenge of new industries, strategies, managers and transactions; • identifying quantitative and qualitative risk and performance indicators that connect investment assumptions, business fundamentals and subsequent performance; • developing potential early-warning indicators and monitoring triggers to identify deterioration in an investment thesis before it is fully reflected in reported valuations or performance; • applying the proposed methodology to a specialized industry as an initial case study and identifying lessons that may be applied to other private-market industries and transactions; • documenting methodologies, findings and recommendations in analytical materials and a final research paper and presentation; and • participating in periodic virtual knowledge-transfer and working sessions with relevant Risk and Compliance staff. Applicants who have graduated as defined in (a) or (b) above, if selected, must commence the internship within a one-year period of graduation. postings.title: Consultant for Government Preparedness and Response to the Potential Impacts of El Niño in the State of Rio de Janeiro UNHABITAT - United Nations Human Settlements Programme Rio de Janeiro CON
postings.text: Consultant for Government Preparedness and Response to the Potential Impacts of El Niño in the State of Rio de Janeiro | UNHABITAT - United Nations Human Settlements Programme Skip to main content Consultant for Government Preparedness and Response to the Potential Impacts of El Niño in the State of Rio de Janeiro UNHABITAT - United Nations Human Settlements Programme Rio de Janeiro CON level Speaks English, French, Portuguese, Spanish Application deadline: November 20, 2026 Closing soon Apply Summary by Impactpool The United Nations Human Settlements Programme is seeking a Consultant for Government Preparedness and Response to the Potential Impacts of El Niño in the State of Rio de Janeiro. The consultant will work closely with various teams to support project objectives related to urban resilience and disaster risk management. Responsibilities include reviewing the State Contingency Plan, assessing resource availability, identifying institutional gaps, and developing actionable roadmaps for preparedness. The role requires a strong background in climate risk management and collaboration with government agencies. Candidate Requirements: Post-Graduation in relevant fields or 5 years of experience 8 years in climate risk management or disaster preparedness Experience with Brazilian state or municipal governments Familiarity with meteorological and disaster risk information Strong technical writing skills Fluency in Portuguese Result of Service The incumbent will work in close collaboration with programme, operations and project teams to support the achievement of project objectives and organizational priorities. Work Location Rio de Janeiro (RJ), Brazil Expected duration Two (2) months Duties and Responsibilities Background The main mandate of the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is to promote sustainable development of human settlements and policies conducive to adequate housing for all. Within this framework, UN-Habitat supports central and state governments, as well as local authorities and other partners for the implementation of the Habitat Agenda, the 2030 Agenda with the Sustainable Development Goals and the New Urban Agenda. UN-Habitat helps the urban poor by transforming cities into safer, more inclusive, compact, integrated, resilient and connected places with better opportunities where everyone can live with dignity. It works with organizations at every level, including all spheres of government, civil society, and the private sector to help build, manage, plan and finance sustainable urban development. The Regional Office for Latin American and the Caribbean – ROLAC – is based in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The Agency puts emphasis on developing and managing activities in the host country. Indeed, for the past years, UN-Habitat has expanded its portfolio in Brazil by working with the three tiers of government to support the formulation and implementation of more effective, sustainable, participative, and socially fairer urban economic, social, and environmental policies. In this context, “Inclusive and Sustainable Rio” is a project between UN-Habitat and the Government of the State of Rio de Janeiro (Governo do Estado do Rio de Janeiro - GERJ), through the State Secretariat for the Environment and Sustainability (SEAS) which aims to strengthen urban resilience in the State of Rio de Janeiro, based on the implementation of the 2030 Agenda and the principles of the New Urban Agenda. El Niño is a climate phenomenon associated with the abnormal warming of surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean, which can alter rainfall patterns and temperatures across Brazil. In the state of Rio de Janeiro, its potential impacts include higher temperatures, more frequent heatwaves, and an increased risk of drought and water scarcity, particularly during periods of reduced rainfall. At the same time, El Niño can influence atmospheric circulation and contribute to episodes of intense rainfall, increasing the risk of flash floods, landslides, and urban flooding, especially in densely populated areas and informal settlements. These impacts may affect public health, water and energy security, agriculture, biodiversity, and infrastructure. The severity and location of these effects depend on the intensity and timing of the phenomenon, regional climate conditions, and interactions with other climate drivers; therefore, climate monitoring, early warning systems, and integrated disaster risk management are essential. To properly implement the above-mentioned project, a Consultant for Government Preparedness and Response to the Potential Impacts of El Niño in the State of Rio de Janeiro is required. Report to UN-Habitat Manager The Consultant for Government Preparedness and Response to the Potential Impacts of El Niño in the State of Rio de Janeiro reports to the Head of Brazil Office, who will evaluate him/her. Responsibilities The Consultant for Government Preparedness and Response to the Potential Impacts of El Niño in the State of Rio de Janeiro will support the implementation of the project, and its activities, with the following responsibilities: a) Review and assess the existing State Contingency Plan, including its proposed measures, response arrangements, institutional responsibilities and operational protocols, verifying their current status and level of implementation. b) Assess the actual availability and readiness of the resources and arrangements required to implement the existing Contingency Plan, including contracts, procurement processes, personnel assignments, equipment, financial resources, institutional agreements and technical capacities. c) Identify gaps between the measures envisaged in the Contingency Plan and the actual institutional, operational and logistical capacity available to ensure an effective response, highlighting pending arrangements, bottlenecks and actions requiring immediate attention. d) Identify and assess the roles and responsibilities of relevant state government agencies, municipalities and institutional partners, including the institutional arrangements required for implementation, interinstitutional engagement, monitoring and communication, as well as opportunities for cooperation with federal agencies, universities, utility providers and civil society organizations. e) Develop a prioritized and actionable roadmap for preparedness and response measures, distinguishing immediate, short-term and structural actions, and identifying measures that can be implemented through existing resources and institutional arrangements, as well as additional requirements in terms of personnel, equipment, financing and technical learning environment. l) Perform any other duties assigned by the supervisor, consistent with the functions of the position. The consultant will be responsible for his/her own security, so the person should get familiarized with United Nations security mechanisms and comply with them according to the Framework of Accountability for the United Nations Security Management System. Outputs/Work Assignment The objective of the deliverable below is to Identify and propose practical measures to prepare the State Government for the potential impacts of El Niño, taking into account existing instruments, the mandates of state agencies, municipal actions, and institutional coordination. The consultant shall assist the implementation of the project, according to the stated responsibilities and the delivery of the following products: Product 1 — Review of the Existing Contingency Plan and Preparedness Arrangements Description: Define institutional responsibilities and establish a prioritized, actionable roadmap for preparedness and response measures, including implementation timelines, resource requirements, monitoring indicators, and institutional capacity gaps. postings.title: Climate debt haircut – macroeconomic and sovereign debt modelling expert (Consultant) UNECA - United Nations Economic Commission for Africa Remote | Rabat CON
postings.text: Climate debt haircut – macroeconomic and sovereign debt modelling expert (Consultant) | UNECA - United Nations Economic Commission for Africa Skip to main content Climate debt haircut – macroeconomic and sovereign debt modelling expert (Consultant) UNECA - United Nations Economic Commission for Africa Remote | Rabat International CON level Speaks English, French Application deadline: November 19, 2026 Closing soon Apply Summary by Impactpool The Economic Commission for Africa is seeking a consultant with expertise in macroeconomic and sovereign debt modeling to develop methodologies for assessing climate-related debt impacts in North Africa. The consultant will produce a technical report that includes a debt-attribution methodological review, a framework for future climate-related debt modeling, and a climate debt haircut methodology. The role involves collaboration with another expert to evaluate data requirements and feasibility for empirical implementation in African countries. This consultancy is expected to last for four months and will be conducted remotely. Candidate Requirements: Advanced university degree in economics or related field PhD in relevant field (desirable) At least 7 years of professional experience in quantitative economics Experience in sovereign-debt or public-finance modeling (desirable) Fluency in English Knowledge of French (desirable) Result of Service The consultant will submit the following deliverables in electronic form, in English: • A final technical report comprising: o Debt-attribution methodological review and recommended options o Technical specifications for historical debt reconstruction attributable to global warming o Future Climate-Related Debt Modelling Framework: Methodology for estimating additional debt arising from global warming reaching +2°C, including adaptation financing. o Climate Debt Haircut Methodology: Integrated framework for determining sustainable debt levels and calculating the historical and forward-looking haircut components. o Feasibility Assessment and Implementation Roadmap: Assessment of data needs, uncertainties, validation options and next steps for empirical application in African countries. o documented illustrative calculations for 2 selected countries Work Location Remotely Expected duration 4 months Duties and Responsibilities Background and rationale for support Climate change is already affecting productive capacity and public finances through reduced economic output and tax revenues, reconstruction and adaptation costs, and higher financing risks. These effects can aggravate existing sovereign-debt vulnerabilities, particularly in climate-exposed developing economies with constrained fiscal space. North Africa is among the regions most vulnerable to climate change. According to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO, 2024), the subregion experienced the fastest warming in Africa, at approximately 0.4°C per decade between 1991 and 2023. North Africa also recorded the highest temperature anomalies across African subregions in 2025 (WMO, 2026). Rising temperatures, increasingly severe droughts, water scarcity, extreme weather events and sea-level rise threaten the subregion's economic and social development, particularly through their impacts on agriculture, food security, labour productivity, infrastructure and water-dependent economic activities. The economic consequences of climate change are already significant and are expected to intensify. The World Bank's Country Climate and Development Report for Morocco estimates that a 25% decline in water availability, combined with climate-related reductions in crop yields, could reduce GDP by 6.5%. The same report estimates that approximately US$78 billion in investment, in present-dollar terms, would be required to place Morocco on a climate-resilient and low-carbon development pathway by the 2050s (World Bank, 2022). In Tunisia, failure to address climate-related challenges could generate GDP losses of up to 3.4% by 2030 (World Bank, 2023), while a more recent assessment estimates that water scarcity alone could reduce GDP by 6.4% by 2050 (World Bank, 2026). In Egypt, the World Bank estimates that insufficient climate action could lead to GDP losses of between 2% and 6% by 2060 (World Bank, 2024). Although these scenario-based estimates are not directly comparable, they illustrate the potentially substantial macroeconomic consequences of climate change across North Africa. In a recent paper, UNECA (2025) estimated that a 1°C increase in global temperatures would lead to a 11% drop in GDP per capita in the subregion. These climate pressures are emerging in a context of significant fiscal constraints and public debt vulnerabilities. In Egypt, central government debt stood at 82.5% of GDP at the end of fiscal year 2024/25, while interest payments reached 10.6% of GDP, considerably restricting fiscal space (World Bank, 2026). In Tunisia, public debt was estimated at 82.2% of GDP in 2025, compared with 67.8% in 2019, while the fiscal deficit reached 5.2% of GDP (World Bank, 2026). Morocco recorded central government debt of 67.1% of GDP and a fiscal deficit of 3.5% of GDP in 2025 (IMF, 2026). In Algeria, the fiscal deficit remained particularly elevated at 10.5% of GDP in 2025, while government debt increased to 52.1% of GDP, reflecting substantial financing needs and the depletion of fiscal buffers (IMF, 2026). Climate change could further aggravate these fiscal and debt vulnerabilities through several interconnected channels. Climate-related reductions in economic output and productivity weaken government revenues, while extreme weather events and growing adaptation needs increase public expenditures for reconstruction, water security, infrastructure, health and social protection. Additional borrowing requirements may consequently increase public debt and debt-servicing costs, further reducing the resources available for investment in resilience and sustainable development. The resulting climate–debt trap risks becoming particularly severe in economies facing already constrained fiscal space, high borrowing costs or limited access to external financing. Although the nature and magnitude of these vulnerabilities differ across North African countries, climate change could progressively undermine their capacity to maintain fiscal sustainability while financing their development and adaptation needs. Against this background, the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA) has developed a paper entitled “Debt in a Warming World: The Case for a Climate Debt Haircut for Africa”. The paper argues that the existing international debt architecture insufficiently accounts for the economic consequences of climate change, the historical responsibility for global warming and the financing needs associated with resilience and sustainable development. It proposes a one-off climate debt haircut based on two components: first, the share of existing public debt attributable to the historical economic and fiscal impacts of climate change; and second, an additional debt reduction, where necessary, to place countries on a sustainable debt trajectory under future climate conditions while preserving sufficient fiscal space for adaptation and essential public expenditure. The proposed approach requires a rigorous quantitative methodology capable of estimating historical climate-attributable debt and assessing future debt sustainability under alternative climate and financing scenarios. The present consultancy aims to develop and operationalize this methodology, providing an empirical basis for assessing the proposed climate debt haircut and its potential application to African countries. ECA's concept paper, 'Debt in a Warming World: The Case for a Climate Debt Haircut for Africa', proposes an exploratory one-off debt reset combining two distinct assessments: (i) the portion of today's debt attributable to the historical economic and fiscal effects of anthropogenic global warming; and (ii) the additional debt adjustment, where necessary, to restore debt sustainability under future warming while safeguarding essential development and adaptation expenditure. Historical attribution and future debt assessment require different methods. Historical attribution involves credible counterfactuals without anthropogenic warming and the identification of fiscal responses and borrowing decisions. The forward-looking component requires integrated climate-economy scenarios and debt sustainability analysis, including a pathway reaching +2°C and alternative adaptation and financing assumptions. ECA therefore intends to commission two complementary methodological studies, one led by an expert in macroeconomics, fiscal policy and sovereign debt modelling and the other by an expert in integrated climate-economy modelling and climate impact attribution. The present phase is intended to develop, compare and specify feasible methodologies, not to deliver definitive debt estimates for all African countries. Scope and tasks of work for the consultant Under the overall guidance of the Director of ECA SRO-NA and the direct supervision of the Economic Affairs Officer responsible for the study, the consultant will undertake the following tasks, in coordination with the other expert: - Develop and assess methodological options to estimate the proportion of today's public debt attributable to the historical macroeconomic and fiscal consequences of anthropogenic global warming, - Assess the data requirements, feasibility, uncertainties and limitations of the proposed debt methodologies for African countries, and contribute to a joint implementation roadmap with the climate–economy expert. - Develop a framework for estimating additional future public borrowing and debt arising from the economic impacts of a warming pathway reaching +2°C, including the implications of future adaptation financing. - Develop a methodology for determining the maximum current public-debt stock compatible with debt sustainability under future climate conditions, while protecting essential development expenditure and adaptation needs. - Assess the feasibility, uncertainties, debt and fiscal data requirements, and potential validation of these methodologies in African countries; identify next steps for their empirical implementation in coordination with the climate–economy expert. - Propose an integrated quantitative framework for calculating a climate debt haircut from the historical debt attribution and, when necessary, an additional forward-looking sustainability adjustment, avoiding double counting. The main expected deliverables and their timelines are: D1: Inception note (work plan, selection of the two countries); debt-attribution methodological review and recommended options (end of month 1) D2: Technical specifications for historical debt reconstruction attributable to global warming; future climate-related debt modelling framework (+2°C, including adaptation financing) (end of month 2) D3: Climate debt haircut methodology (sustainable debt levels, historical and forward-looking haircut components); draft illustrative calculations for the two countries (end of month 3) D4: Feasibility assessment and implementation roadmap; final documented calculations for the two countries; final technical report consolidating all components and reflecting ECA comments (end of month 4) Qualifications/special skills An advanced university degree (Master's degree at least) in economics, macroeconomics, public finance or a closely related field is required. A PhD in a relevant field is desirable At least 7 years of professional experience in quantitative economic is required Experience in sovereign-debt or public-finance modelling and applied econometrics is desirable Languages English and French are the working languages of the UN Secretariat. For this consultancy, Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of French is desirable Additional Infor

postings.text: MINISTRY OF MINERALS AND ENERGY PROJECTS AND ENERGY DEVELOPMENT UNIT (PEDU) Invitation for Expression of Interest Consulting Services- Firms Selection Topographic, Hydrological and Route Survey Studies for A Wind Farm Site in Botswana Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Topographic, Hydrological Studies and Route Survey for a Wind Farm Site in Botswana. Reference: EOI/MME-PEDU/003/26-27 BACKGROUND Botswana plans to harness its renewable energy (RE) resources and accelerate renewable energy development through the implementation of its Integrated Resource Plan (IRP). The Government of Botswana is currently developing renewable energy projects at several pre-selected sites. The Projects and Energy Development Unit (PEDU), under the Ministry of Minerals and Energy (the Client), is responsible for the development of these projects. A feasibility consultant has identified a proposed site for a wind farm based on a multi-criteria assessment considering preliminary wind resource data, transmission infrastructure, land use and ownership, and preliminary environmental and social considerations. The site studies will support the development of a proposed 100MW wind farm located north of Letlhakane. The final coordinates and boundaries of the area to be surveyed will be confirmed by the Client prior to commencement of the assignment. SCOPE OF WORK The assignment will comprise three principal components: a topographic survey of the proposed wind farm site and associated areas; a hydrological study , including assessment of drainage and flood risks relevant to the proposed development; and a route survey to assess feasible transport routes for the delivery of wind turbine components and other oversized equipment to the project site. The detailed scope, survey areas, technical requirements and deliverables will be set out in the Terms of Reference provided at the next stage of the selection process. The consultant shall also provide a capacity-building seminar on how to understand and use the study reports when their first versions are issued. QUALIFICATIONS PEDU invites eligible consulting firms/consortiums ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are: Core Business: minimum of ten (10) years of experience providing surveying, engineering and or technical consulting services relevant to the scope of the assignment. Demonstrate experience in undertaking topographic surveys, hydrological studies and route/transport surveys for utility-scale energy or comparable infrastructure projects. In addition, the Consultant (directly or through a named sub-consultant/joint venture partner) shall demonstrate: (i) minimum 3 topographic survey assignments of comparable scale completed in the preceding 5 years; (ii) minimum 2 hydrological/drainage assessment assignments completed in the preceding 5 years. The Consultant to demonstrate experience in undertaking comparable assignments in accordance with applicable technical, environmental and occupational health and safety standards. The Consultant shall demonstrate experience working on assignments financed by International Financial Institutions (IFIs), and its eligibility including but not limited to meeting the debarment and sanctions standard, financial and commercial capability and fiduciary and system compliance. The Consultant shall have no conflict of interest and pass integrity check. The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Paragraphs 3.14 to 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for Borrowers, dated July 2016, revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2023, setting forth the World Bank's Policy on Conflict of Interest. CONSULTANT QUALIFICATIONS EVALUATION CRITERIA Interested bidders who have submitted expression of interest will be evaluated according to the following criteria: - Overall years of consulting experience (20 points) Number of similar assignments (70 points) Availability of key experts to carry the assignment (10 points)   Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications. When firms are associating, the submission must include verifiable evidence of association from all the parties   A Bidders workshop will be held virtually to discuss the assignment overview on 21 October 2026. Details will be announced via MME and World Bank platforms . A consultant will be selected in accordance with the CS-CQS method set out in the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated July 2016, revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2023. Interested consultants may obtain further information in writing at the address below during office hours, that is, 0730 hours to 16:30 hours. In case of clarifications, do not hesitate to contact Mr Franz Mafoko at frmafoko@gov.bw; Cell No.: +267 72794446.   Expressions of Interest clearly labelled "Expression of Interest - Consultancy Services for Topographic, Hydrological and Route Studies for a Wind Farm in Botswana ," must be hand-delivered or emailed at the address below by 11 November 2026 at 12:00 hours (CAT). Electronic submissions should be password protected. Attention:         The Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Minerals and Energy Block D, Third Floor, Office No DT 10, Plot No. 50676 Fairgrounds Office Park, Gaborone Republic of Botswana. postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION)   Country:                                             Independent State of Samoa Name of Project:                              Samoa Finance Sector Resilience and Development Project (SFSRDP) 2025 – 2029 (World Bank Financed Project P181456) Loan No./Credit No./Grant No.:      IDA – E3780 Assignment Title:                              Diagnostic assessment for a National Retail Payment Switch Reference No.:                                   CBS/CS/004   1. Introduction: The Government of Samoa has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the SFSRDP P181456 and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The Central Bank of Samoa invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing consulting services to conduct a diagnostic assessment for a national retail payment switch. The objective of this assignment is to undertake a diagnostic assessment of Samoa's retail payments ecosystem and evaluate the need, feasibility, and potential design options for establishing a National Retail Payment Switch. Interested consulting firms should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. This REOI is being issued for the purpose of establishing a shortlist of qualified consulting firms who will subsequently be invited to submit detailed technical and financial proposals under the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method.   2. Background: The Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) is the monetary authority responsible for maintaining financial stability, managing currency issuance, and overseeing the payment systems in Samoa. Under the Samoa Finance Sector Resilience and Development project supported by the World Bank, the CBS is pursuing initiatives to strengthen the national payments ecosystem, increase digital financial inclusion, improve payment efficiency, and support the country's broader digital transformation agenda. As electronic payment channels continue to expand across banks, mobile money operators, government agencies, merchants, and consumers, the need for more efficient interoperability arrangements has become increasingly important. Currently, retail payment transactions may be processed through bilateral arrangements, proprietary networks, or international payment schemes, resulting in potential inefficiencies, higher transaction costs, limited interoperability, and constraints on innovation. A National Retail Payment Switch could provide a shared infrastructure enabling seamless, secure, and real-time interoperability among payment service providers. Before making investment and policy decisions, CBS seeks the services of a consultancy firm to conduct a comprehensive diagnostic assessment to determine whether a National Retail Payment Switch is necessary, feasible, and economically viable, and if so, to identify the most appropriate implementation model for Samoa   3. Objective of the Assignment: The objectives of the assignment include: Assess the current state of retail payment systems and interoperability arrangements. Identify gaps, inefficiencies, and constraints within the existing payment ecosystem. Evaluate current and future demand for interoperable retail payment services. Assess the business, technical, operational, regulatory, and financial viability of a National Retail Payment Switch. Examine alternative interoperability models and determine whether a national switch is the most appropriate solution. Provide recommendations and an implementation roadmap, if deemed necessary.   4. Scope of Services: The Consultant will be expected to undertake activities including, but not limited to: Task 1: Inception Phase and stakeholder consultation Task 2: Assessment of the current payment ecosystem Task 3: Gap Analysis Task 4: Assessment of the Need for a National Retail Payment Switch Task 5: Evaluation of Alternative Models Task 6: Design Considerations (If a Switch is Recommended) Task 7: Implementation Roadmap   5. The detailed Terms of Reference for the Assignment is provided in the Annex of this document.   6. The Central Bank of Samoa now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.   7. A consulting firm is allowed to submit the expression of interest alone if it considers itself to be fully qualified on its own for the assignment, as it is not mandatory for consultants to associate with any other firm(s), whether foreign or local. Alternatively, if consultants themselves choose to associate to enhance their qualifications and capability for the assignment, then such associations may either be as a Joint Venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally responsible) and/or Sub-consultants (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant). In case of an association, the Consultants must explain in the EOI submission (a) the rationale for forming the association and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture and/or of each subconsultant for carrying out the assignment, to justify the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants in the association. Failure to provide the above explanation in the Expression of Interest may risk the association not being shortlisted for the assignment. Please note that in the evaluation of EOIs of associations for shortlisting purposes, only the qualifications of the JV members will be taken into account whereas the qualifications of proposed sub-consultants will not be considered.     8. The shortlisting criteria are as follows, in which specific experience of the Consultant relevant to the assignment will be considered of paramount importance: Demonstrated experience in assignments of comparable scope, specifically in conducting diagnostics and advisory services for national or regional payment systems, with a focus on retail payment switch design, implementation, or assessment within the last 10 years. Proven track record in supporting the modernization of payment systems to enhance efficiency, security, and interoperability of digital financial services, including experience with regulatory and supervisory frameworks for payment systems in developing country contexts. Experience advising central banks, financial sector regulators, or payment system operators on the development, evaluation, or integration of payment infrastructure, including interoperability standards (e.g., API, QR) and digital financial services ecosystems. Familiarity with financial inclusion strategies and demonstrated capacity to assess payment system use cases that promote access to formal financial services and reduce remittance costs Documented organizational systems and methodologies for conducting diagnostics, stakeholder consultations, and technical assessments in the context of payment system modernization. Capacity to address data protection, cybersecurity, and business continuity considerations relevant to payment system infrastructure, as required for robust and resilient digital financial services. Ability to coordinate with the Central Bank of Samoa and other relevant stakeholders, reflecting experience in multi-institutional environments and government-led financial sector reforms. Sufficient organizational resources to field a multidisciplinary team with expertise in payment systems, digital finance, regulatory analysis, and IT systems, appropriate to the assignment’s scope and complexity Compliance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Fifth Edition, September 2023) and absence of conflict of interest or debarment If joint ventures or subconsultants are proposed, the lead firm must be clearly identified, and the proposal must specify how relevant experience will be aggregated to meet the above requirements. The Consultants should demonstrate availability of and/or access to the key experts for the performance of the services described in the TOR (e.g., by providing a list of key experts they are working with). The Consultants should demonstrate sound administrative and financial capacity. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.   9. Eligibility and Shortlisting Criteria: Interested consulting firms must: Be legally registered entities. Have been in operation for at least 15 years. Have no conflict of interest related to this assignment. Not be subject to suspension, debarment, or ineligibility by any applicable authority, development partner, or international financing institution. Expressions of Interest will be evaluated based on the following criteria: Criterion Weight (%) Relevant experience in similar assignments 40 Technical expertise in the subject matter 25 Experience working with central banks, regulators, governments, or financial institutions 15 Regional experience, particularly in Pacific Island countries or comparable jurisdictions 10 Organizational capacity and availability of appropriate resources 10 Total 100 Only the highest ranked firms will be shortlisted and invited to participate in the subsequent RFP process.   10.  Information to be Submitted : To demonstrate their qualifications and experience in meeting the above shortlisting/selection criteria, Consultants are requested to submit, at a minimum, the supporting documentation listed below (also refer to Annexes 2-4) A consultant firm can only use its own qualifications and experience and not of its parent, sister or subsidiary companies or its employees. Cover letter – a signed letter expressing interest in undertaking the assignment Company profile – including legal name of firm, country of incorporation, year established, ownership structure, office locations, number of professional staff Relevant experience  Completed Form-1 (Annex 2) to provide information of up to 5 similar contracts within the last 10 years. This should include: the name and reference number of the contract, brief description of the scope of work, contract amount, period of the contract, name of the client country of assignment, role of the Consultant in the contract. outcomes achieved Copies of completion certificates/references of Clients of completed contracts are not required to be submitted with the EoI. In the subsequent stage at the time of submission of proposals, the Client may request the shortlisted consultants to submit such supporting completion certificate 4. The firm’s company brochures detailing: Technical Capability Provide information on – areas of expertise, key technical competencies, internal quality assurance systems Regional and Sector Experience Describe experience in – financial sector development, financial inclusion, digital financial services, consumer protection, regulatory and supervisory framework, pacific island cou

postings.title: Consultant - Digital and AI Safety for Women Entrepreneurs UNESCAP - United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific Remote | New Delhi CON
postings.text: Consultant - Digital and AI Safety for Women Entrepreneurs | UNESCAP - United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific Skip to main content Consultant - Digital and AI Safety for Women Entrepreneurs UNESCAP - United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific Remote | New Delhi CON level Speaks Hindi, English Application deadline: November 30, 2026 (14 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific is seeking a Consultant for Digital and AI Safety for Women Entrepreneurs. The consultant will develop training materials, prepare policy recommendations, and deliver training focused on the safe use of digital technologies and AI for women entrepreneurs in India. Responsibilities include conducting needs assessments, creating a training manual, and providing workshops. The role requires a commitment to high integrity and accountability in delivering outputs as per the agreed terms of reference. Candidate Requirements: Advanced degree in cybersecurity, IT, computer science, or digital policy 10 years of experience in cybersecurity or digital safety Experience in evidence-based policy analysis on digital safety Practical experience with online fraud and AI risks Experience designing training materials for non-technical audiences Support for women entrepreneurs in digital commerce Knowledge of South Asia's digital business environment Fluency in English; knowledge of Hindi or another South Asian language is desirable Result of Service The consultant shall commit to performing the tasks stated above with high integrity and dedication to delivering the outputs as per plan. He/she shall be professionally accountable to Economic Affairs Officer, SRO-SSWA. Within the overall parameters set out in this agreement, the Consultant will work according to the agreed ToR. Work Location Remotely Expected duration 5.5 months Duties and Responsibilities Under the supervision of the Economic Affairs Officer responsible for the women’s entrepreneurship programme at SRO-SSWA, the consultant will develop practical training materials, prepare policy recommendations and deliver training on the safe use of digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI). The assignment will begin with women entrepreneurs in India. Its core materials will be designed for later adaptation across South Asia. The consultant will undertake the following tasks: 1. Review programme materials and consult women entrepreneurs, trainers and relevant institutions to identify priority safety risks in everyday business use of digital platforms, e-commerce, digital payments and AI tools. 2. Develop and test a plain-language training manual that helps women use these tools to promote their businesses while protecting their money, business information, personal safety and families. 3. Prepare evidence-based policy recommendations for a safer and more inclusive digital and AI environment for women entrepreneurs, drawing on the India pilot and selected South Asian experience. 4. Deliver practical workshop sessions, introduce the manual to participants and trainers, and revise the materials using feedback and learning assessments. 5. Submit all agreed outputs, source files and supporting evidence to the Economic Affairs Officer in charge of the women’s entrepreneurship programme at SRO-SSWA. The following are the activities and engagements for the consultant: All month references are measured from the contract start date. The scope below provides for three training engagements: two workshops in India and one regional session. Workshop dates and formats will be confirmed in the inception plan. Output 1 Inception report By the end of Month 1, submit an inception report of approximately 6–8 pages, excluding annexes, to outline the proposed methodology and analysis. The inception report should include a review of relevant literature available from ESCAP, UN and governments and other institutions in India and South Asia and a list of government institutions and women entrepreneurs in India and representatives of training partners, women’s business networks and relevant digital safety institutions to consult in the needs assessment. Output 2 Needs assessment and Draft training manual and teaching materials Undertake consultations with identified stakeholders to understand the needs of women entrepreneurs and the eco-system of institutions and partners and their potential roles in the support process. The needs assessment report will set out priority learning needs, common business risks, the manual outline, consultation findings, proposed learning assessments and a workplan. It will identify two additional South Asian countries for a focused desk review, selected with ESCAP, and explain which elements require country-specific adaptation. By the end of Month 3, submit a complete draft manual in English, normally 30–40 pages excluding annexes, with a companion slide deck and facilitator notes. Keep modules short, illustrated and suitable for smartphone reading and low-cost printing. Provide step-by-step actions, realistic business examples, checklists, practice exercises and a brief glossary. Avoid technical language and explain essential terms when first used. The manual will cover the following content: • Safe business use of AI: drafting product descriptions, marketing content, translations and customer messages; checking facts and outputs; protecting customer and business information; recognising bias and misleading content; and respecting consent and intellectual property. • Account and device protection: strong passwords or passkeys, multi-factor authentication, recovery options, updates, backups, app permissions and safer use of shared devices. Explain how to separate business and family information where possible. • Safer e-commerce and payments: checking buyers, suppliers and platform messages; recognising fake orders, payment screenshots, refund requests, phishing links, QR-code and UPI fraud; and using official payment and platform support channels. • AI-enabled deception and personal safety: impersonation, cloned voices, deepfake images or videos, fake AI services, harassment and threats involving family members. Teach independent verification and safe reporting rather than relying on visual clues alone. • Responding to an incident: stopping further payments or disclosure, contacting the bank or payment provider promptly, securing accounts, preserving evidence safely and using verified reporting channels. Include a short action card and explain that reporting does not guarantee recovery of funds. Use fictional data and safe demonstrations. Do not request passwords, one-time passcodes, live bank details or sensitive customer records. Include India-specific official reporting guidance in a clearly marked annex, with verification dates. Provide a reusable country annex structure so that Indian procedures are not presented as regional rules. Output 3 Tested manual and finalized training package By the end of Month 4, test the draft with women entrepreneurs with varied levels of digital experience and trainers. Participants may include people consulted for Output 1. Use practical scenarios to check whether participants can recognise risks and follow protective steps. Submit anonymised findings, a summary of changes and a response to ESCAP’s comments. Deliver the revised manual, participant checklists, incident action card, facilitator notes, slides and short pre- and post-session assessments. Include at least one exercise per module and guidance on local-language delivery and accessibility. Translation is outside the proposed scope; editable files must support later translation. ESCAP’s acceptance will depend on accuracy, usability, completeness and incorporation of agreed revisions. Output 4 Policy recommendations for a safer digital and AI environment By the end of Month 5, submit a policy paper of approximately 12–15 pages, excluding references, and a two-page policy brief. Draw on consultations, the India pilot and the focused desk review of two additional South Asian countries. Distinguish findings supported by evidence from issues requiring further investigation. Do not generalise India’s experience to the whole subregion. Assess gaps in prevention, accessible reporting, redress and institutional support. Address data protection, AI-enabled fraud, online harassment, platform and payment-provider responsibilities, digital literacy and support for small and informal women-led businesses. Verify relevant laws and policies against official sources and distinguish measures in force from proposals or measures awaiting implementation. Present a practical action matrix identifying each recommendation, its evidence base, proposed lead institution, partners, priority, indicative resource needs and progress indicator. Separate near-term operational measures from longer-term policy options. Identify opportunities for regional peer learning. Recommendations should support safe participation and avoid unnecessary costs or barriers for women-led enterprises. Incorporate ESCAP’s comments before final submission. Output 5 Training delivery and workshop reports Deliver two workshops in India and one regional session. Plan for at least three hours of facilitated teaching and exercises at each India workshop and a 90-minute regional session. ESCAP will arrange participants, venues, connectivity and local-language support, as required. The regional session will present lessons from India and explain how to adapt the materials. Tailor each session to the participants’ business activities and digital confidence. Introduce and share the manual, demonstrate safe routines and help local trainers reuse the materials. Submit a short report within ten working days of each engagement, including the agenda, materials used, assessment results and recommended changes. Report learning results with their limitations; do not attribute changes in income or fraud losses to a short training session. Output 6 Final package and handover By the end of the consultancy, submit the final manual and teaching materials updated after the workshops, the final policy paper and brief, and a short completion report. Provide an adaptation guide covering language, payment systems, relevant laws, reporting channels and referral services. Include a dated source register and instructions for updating information that may change. Supply editable Word and PowerPoint source files, accessible PDFs and any original illustrations or other assets needed for reuse. All outputs must contain clear references, respect third-party rights and be ready for ESCAP review and subsequent publication clearance. ESCAP will provide consolidated comments. The consultant will submit revisions based on the received comments. The inception plan will allow for these review periods. Changes to deliverables, fees or the contract end date require written agreement under applicable contract procedures. Workshop rescheduling will be addressed promptly through an agreed revised schedule.
