postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – SELECTION OF INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS)   Republic of Uzbekistan Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project Credit No.: 7425-UZ   Assignment Title: Environmental Specialist (including Occupational Health and Safety) for the construction and renovation of ITES Centers Reference No.: UZ-DIP-581360-CS-INDV   The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the International Development Association toward the cost of the Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project. “Administration of Technology Park of Software and IT” LLC (IT Park), as the Implementing Agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds to engage an individual consultant as Environmental Specialist (including Occupational Health and Safety) for Component 2.2 of the Project. Under Component 2.2, the Project finances the construction and the reconstruction of ITES Centers in the regions. To meet the requirements of the Project’s Environmental and Social Commitment Plan, IT Park will engage three individual consultants under separate contracts: an Environmental Specialist (including Occupational Health and Safety), a Social Specialist and a Stakeholder Engagement Specialist. This Request for Expressions of Interest concerns the Environmental Specialist. The Environmental Specialist will support IT Park as the lead specialist for environment, occupational health and safety of workers and physical community safety at the construction sites, in line with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, the World Bank Group General Environmental, Health and Safety Guidelines and the legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan. The consulting services (“the Services”) include, but are not limited to: screening of Project activities, including design changes, for environmental, health and safety risks; preparation, review and update of the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment / Environmental and Social Management Plan; environmental, health and safety review of design documentation, including life and fire safety of the buildings, and identification of hazardous materials (asbestos) in the buildings to be reconstructed, with measures for their safe removal and disposal; review of each contractor’s Environmental and Social Management Plan, occupational health and safety plan, community health and safety plan, risk assessments and emergency response plan, and HSE induction of the contractor’s site management; monthly and quarterly reports, the HSE section of the six-monthly environmental, social, health and safety report to the World Bank; The assignment is expected to start in December 2026 and to continue until the taking-over of the last of the construction sites and acceptance of the final report, currently expected in the first half of 2029. To obtain the Terms of Reference for the assignment, please send your request to the following e-mail address: udip@it-park.uz. “Administration of Technology Park of Software and IT” LLC now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services: a curriculum vitae in the English language, copies of diplomas and of the occupational health and safety certificate, and contact details of references. The evaluation criteria are: 1) Education University degree in occupational health and safety, environmental engineering, civil engineering, environmental science or a related field. 2) Experience At least 5 years of experience in HSE management of construction or infrastructure projects, including supervision of contractors on site; At least 3 years of experience on projects financed by the World Bank or other international financial institutions; Proven experience in preparing and implementing ESMPs, reviewing contractors’ C-ESMPs and occupational health and safety plans, site HSE inspections and accident investigation; Experience with multi-storey building construction, renovation, demolition waste or asbestos management is an advantage. 3) Certification Valid occupational health and safety certificate (national, or international such as NEBOSH or IOSH). NEBOSH International General Certificate or equivalent is an advantage. 4) Knowledge World Bank ESF (Environmental and Social Standards ESS1–ESS4) and World Bank Group General EHS Guidelines; Legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan on environmental protection and state environmental expertise, labour protection, fire safety and construction safety; Ability to integrate HSE requirements into designs, cost estimates, tender documents and contracts. 5) Language Fluent Uzbek and Russian; Good working English. postings.text: E T Consultant - Coastal Infrastructure Engineer | World Bank Group Skip to main content E T Consultant - Coastal Infrastructure Engineer World Bank Group New Delhi Both national and international EC2 - Extended Term Consultant Appointment level Speaks Hindi, English Application deadline: November 26, 2026 (10 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The World Bank is seeking a highly skilled Extended Term Consultant (Coastal Engineering Specialist) to support various task teams in preparing and providing technical assistance for coastal infrastructure projects in South Asia. The role involves engineering oversight on civil works related to coastal protection, rehabilitation, and integrated management. The consultant will assess infrastructure investments, provide guidance on environmental and social risks, and ensure compliance with technical designs. This position is based in New Delhi, India, and requires collaboration with project stakeholders to enhance coastal resilience. Candidate Requirements: Master's degree in coastal engineering or civil/hydraulic engineering At least 5 years of experience in coastal and maritime engineering Three references in coastal protection or maritime works design Five experiences in monitoring coastal protection works Knowledge in climate change, hydrology, and coastal oceanography Familiarity with coastal dynamics software Understanding of World Bank environmental and social safeguards Experience in South Asia and knowledge of CRZ Notification framework Ability to work in multi-disciplinary teams Strong results-driven approach E T Consultant - Coastal Infrastructure Engineer Job #: req39137 Organization: World Bank Sector: Environment Grade: EC2 Term Duration:  1 year 0 months Recruitment Type: Local Recruitment Location: New Delhi,India Required Language(s): English, Hindi Preferred Language(s): Closing Date: 11/26/2026 (MM/DD/YYYY) at 11:59pm UTC Description At the World Bank, a member of the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. For more information, visit  https://www.worldbank.org/en/who-we-are/ibrd India's 11,099 kilometer coastline is home to 250 million people and supports key blue economy sectors including fisheries, tourism, agriculture, and transport. Despite its ecological richness, India's coastal ecosystems face mounting pressure from climate-induced hazards, coastal erosion, pollution, and land-use change. One-third of India's coastline is reported as vulnerable to erosion, threatening livelihoods, settlements, and biodiversity of global significance. The Strengthening Coastal Resilience and the Economy (SHORE) program has begun implementation in the states of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka under Phase 1 and will be expanded to other coastal states such as Goa, Maharashtra, Puducherry and West Bengal under subsequent phases. It aims to increase the resilience of targeted coastal communities and ecosystems, focusing on four components: (i) strengthening institutions for Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM); (ii) shoreline management, coastal protection and conservation; (iii) improving livelihoods for natural resource-dependent communities; and (iv) enhancing marine pollution management and plastic circularity. The Position: The Environment (ENV) Department in South Asia seeks to recruit a highly skilled recruit a highly skilled and motivated Extended Term (ET) Consultant (Coastal Engineering Specialist) who would work as part of various task teams involved in preparing and providing technical assistance to World Bank-financed projects/activities involving Coastal hydrodynamic processes, coastal protection/conservation measures and cruise terminal/harbour construction and modernization. This position will be based in New Delhi, India. The candidate is expected to work across several countries in the South Asia Region. The Coastal Engineer will report to the ENV Practice Manager for the South Asia Region (SAR) and work under the supervision of the SHORE Task Team Leaders.   The South Asia Region comprises six countries (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, and Sri Lanka) that range in size from India (with a population of over 1 billion) to Maldives (with 0.3 million people). The region has experienced a long period of robust economic growth, averaging 6% a year over the past 20 years. It was the second-fastest growing region in the world in the aftermath of the global crisis. This strong growth has translated into declining poverty and impressive improvements in human development. The percentage of people living below the poverty line fell in South Asia from 56% to 16% between 1981 and 2013. Still, the region remains home to a third of the world’s poorest, with 216 million people living below $1.9/day.  The South Asia Region:  https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/sar   The Unit The Environment Department (ENV), located within the World Bank’s Planet Practice Group has been established to deliver on the opportunities, benefits and outcomes offered by enhanced management of the environment and natural resources. ENV provides expertise, technical assistance and financing to help countries manage land, sea and freshwater natural resources in a sustainable way to help create jobs, improve livelihoods, enhance ecosystem services, decrease pollution and increase resilience to climate change. Over 360 ENV staff working across the globe help set developing countries on a clean, green growth trajectory for resilient economies and healthy communities. The SSAE1 unit comprises around 30 staff, with 95 percent based in Country Offices. The rest of the team is based in Washington DC. Our Sri Lanka country office is a joint World Bank/International Finance Cooperation office, comprising approximately 100 staff, including an ETC working on environment, providing a vibrant, collegial working environment. Duties and accountabilities: The ET Consultant will have the following tasks: • Support the Bank team by providing engineering oversight and guidance on all infrastructure interventions, technical matters relating to planning, design, and implementation of the civil works activities related to protection, rehabilitation and integrated management of coastal areas. The grey infrastructure interventions may include, but not limited to, coastal protection structures such as submerged reefs, rubble mound breakwaters, concrete sea walls, groynes, pollution treatment/management plants, cruise terminal/ fishing harbors construction and modernization, ecotourism and other livelihoods related infrastructure.  • Assessing the proposed infrastructure investments by the client’s teams and providing guidance on: i) spatial targeting or grouping of the proposed investments; ii) assessing any environmental and social (E&S) risks to be considered and propose alternative technical design to mitigate those risks; iii) recommendations to enhance design to be consistent with overall conceptual framework of the project; iv) assessing technical designs to ensure sustainability and resilience of proposed infrastructure; v) ensuring that technical refinements agreed with the Bank’s team are duly included in the teams’ proposals and designs; • Support the task teams in contributing to the preparation of TORs for studies and technical specifications; reviewing the detailed project reports (DPRs); provide Inputs to the draft reports which are to contribute to the project sub-component designs, and; provide guidance on hydrodynamic, climate change and sediment transport modeling intended for a better understanding of the functioning of the coastline and coastal risks, • Provide assistance to the task team and the clients in advising on contract management such as quality control and ensure consultants’ compliance with contracts for engineering design, works supervision, investments operation and maintenance. • Make site visits with other project officers to project intervention sites to review quality of civil works, material results and monthly progress reports, as well as make recommendations for the project on the overall achievement of the projects’ project and quality of works. • Preparation and conduct of supervision missions from technical and financial partners as well as the monitoring of action plans resulting from said missions; • Engage and collaborate with project stakeholders including beneficiaries for knowledge and skills transfer, relating to the prevention and management of coastal risks;  • Provide other inputs as requested and agreed with the Bank team. Selection Criteria • A master’s degree or its equivalent in coastal engineering discipline or civil/hydraulic engineering, specializing in maritime and/or coastal works, dredging, port works, jetties and large-scale mining of rock for breakwaters. • Have at least 5 years of experience in the field of coastal and maritime engineering or coastal oceanography  • Have at least three (03) references in studies including the design of coastal protection works or maritime works; • Have at least five (05) experiences in the control and monitoring of coastal or maritime protection works; • Demonstrate knowledge in the specific associated fields such as: climate change, hydrology and coastal oceanography, marine environment, hydrodynamics, morphodynamics of coastal zones, digital modeling, measurements, design and construction of port and maritime works, sedimentology, upkeep and maintenance maritime works; • Have a good knowledge of the following common and more specialized software for monitoring and modeling coastal or maritime dynamics will be an added advantage • Have a good knowledge of the environmental and social safeguard measures of the World Bank • Experience working on South Asia and familiarity with the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notification framework and ICZM principles in the Indian context is an advantage.  • Good team player who can work as a member of a multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural team, motivate and lead group efforts and network effectively across boundaries.  • A drive for results while working with limited supervision and under tight timelines. Additional Considerations: As the World Bank Group continues to evolve, we value candidates who: •Demonstrate the ability to collaborate effectively across teams, disciplines, cultures, and institutional boundaries. •Responsibly leverage digital and AI-enabled tools to enhance productivity, learning, and decision-making. •Bring experience working on fragile, conflict-affected, and violent (FCV)-related contexts and are encouraged to highlight relevant experience in their application materials, where applicable. WBG Culture Attributes: 1. Sense of urgency: Anticipate and quickly respond to the needs of internal and external stakeholders. 2. Thoughtful risk-taking: Challenge the status quo and push boundaries to achieve greater impact. 3. Empowerment and accountability: Empower yourself and others to act and hold each other accountable for results. postings.text: Developing the interbank and bond markets in Mauritania (Consultant) | UNECA - United Nations Economic Commission for Africa Skip to main content Developing the interbank and bond markets in Mauritania (Consultant) UNECA - United Nations Economic Commission for Africa Remote | Rabat International CON level Speaks Arabic, English, French Application deadline: November 19, 2026 Closing soon Apply Summary by Impactpool The Economic Commission for Africa is seeking a consultant to develop the interbank and bond markets in Mauritania. The consultant will conduct a diagnostic assessment, create a reform roadmap, and provide capacity-building programs for financial sector stakeholders. Key responsibilities include evaluating liquidity management practices, assessing barriers to interbank lending, and recommending strategies for market development. The position requires remote work for a duration of 10 months. Candidate Requirements: Advanced university degree in economics, finance or related fields Minimum of ten years of experience in economics and finance Experience in analytical policy research in monetary policy in North Africa Experience advising central banks Fluency in French Fluency in English is an advantage Fluency in Arabic is an advantage Result of Service At the conclusion of the assignment: • A prioritized and actionable reform roadmap will be adopted. • Capacity of financial sector stakeholders will be significantly strengthened. • Interbank market activity and liquidity management practices will be enhanced. • Secondary market activity in government securities will increase. • The investor base for government securities will broaden. • Mauritania will be better positioned to develop deeper and more resilient domestic financial markets. Work Location Remotely Expected duration 10 months Duties and Responsibilities Background and rationale for support The Central Bank of Mauritania (Banque Centrale de Mauritanie, BCM) has implemented a range of monetary policy instruments, market infrastructure reforms, and regulatory mechanisms to deepen both the interbank market and the government securities (bonds and treasury bills) market. In the interbank market, the BCM has strengthened liquidity management through open market operations, standing lending and deposit facilities, and regular monitoring and publication of interbank rates and transaction volumes. These instruments enable banks to borrow and lend liquidity among themselves, improve short‑term funding allocation, and enhance the transmission of monetary policy. The BCM has also modernized payment and settlement systems, which facilitate smoother interbank transactions and improve confidence in market operations. A major recent reform was the launch of the interbank foreign exchange market in December 2023, replacing the previous exchange-rate fixing system. To support this market, the BCM introduced an electronic trading platform for interbank transactions, established a network of market makers (teneurs de marché), and conducts foreign-exchange auctions to provide liquidity when necessary. The central bank also clarified its intervention framework and accelerated complementary reforms aimed at facilitating liquidity exchanges between banks and improving the overall functioning of the money market, including the development of instruments compatible with Islamic finance principles. These reforms have contributed to a better alignment of market interest rates with the central bank’s policy rate. Regarding the bond and government securities market, the BCM has supported the development of a structured market for Treasury bills and Treasury bonds by organizing auctions, publishing market data, and providing settlement infrastructure for government securities transactions. The central bank disseminates information on yields and weighted average rates across different maturities, thereby enhancing market transparency and price discovery. Through its role in the payment, clearing, and securities settlement systems, the BCM has also strengthened the institutional framework necessary for the issuance and trading of public debt instruments. These measures help establish a domestic yield curve, provide investment opportunities for banks and institutional investors, and create the foundations for a broader capital market. Despite this progress, significant challenges remain, including limited interbank market activity, low secondary market liquidity for government securities, a narrow investor base, limited market-making capacity, insufficient risk-management capabilities among market participants, underdeveloped money market instruments, and capacity constraints across the banking and financial sectors. These challenges constrain financial sector deepening, market-based monetary policy implementation, and the mobilization of domestic savings for productive investment. To address these constraints, a consultant will be recruited to undertake a comprehensive diagnostic assessment, develop an actionable reform roadmap, provide technical advisory services, and deliver extensive capacity-building programs to financial sector stakeholders. Duties and Responsibilities: Under the direct supervision of the Chief of the Subregional Initiatives Section and the overall supervision of the Director of ECA SRO-NA, the consultant shall undertake the following tasks. 1: Diagnostic Assessment • Review of Interbank Markets including the structure and functioning of the interbank money market. • Assess liquidity management practices in commercial banks. • Evaluate the use and effectiveness of central bank liquidity facilities. • Assess barriers to interbank lending. • Explain why, despite the reforms and market infrastructure already put in place, interbank market activity remains below expectations. Why banks are still not transacting more actively with each other, whether due to the way liquidity is distributed, lack of trust, market incentives, operational constraints, or the way banks currently rely on BCM facilities. Why banks are still not transacting more actively with each other, whether due to the way liquidity is distributed, lack of trust, market incentives, operational constraints, or the way banks currently rely on BCM facilities. When data are available, to look at how the interbank market has actually been used in practice in recent years, including the extent to which banks rely on the Central Bank for their liquidity needs, to identify the main bottlenecks. • Suggest ways and means to translate reforms into deeper market activity • Review of Government Securities and Bond Markets • Assess the primary issuance framework for Treasury bills and bonds. • Analyze auction design and issuance calendars. • Evaluate investor participation patterns. • Assess secondary market activity and liquidity. • Examine the role of primary dealers and market makers. • Identify bottlenecks to bond market development. • Review of Financial Market Infrastructure including payment systems, securities settlement arrangements, trading platforms. • Review relevant laws and regulations and benchmark Mauritania against international good practices. • Identify regulatory gaps. 2. Development of Reform Strategy Based on the diagnostic findings, the consultant shall develop a market development strategy. The strategy shall include: Interbank Market Recommendations • Measures to increase market liquidity. • Introduction or strengthening of repo markets. • Expansion of liquidity management instruments. • Islamic liquidity management instruments where appropriate. Bond Market Recommendations • Measures to increase secondary market liquidity. • Investor base diversification. • Institutional investor participation. • Retail investor development. • Corporate bond market development prospects. Infrastructure and Regulatory Recommendations • Payment and settlement enhancements. • Market transparency measures. • Trading platform improvements. 3. Capacity Building and Training The consultant shall design and deliver a capacity-building program covering: • Interbank Market Development. • Bond Market Development. • Financial Market Infrastructure including trading platforms, settlement systems, market transparency, data reporting and analytics. 4. Advisory Services The consultant shall provide ongoing advisory support throughout the assignment. Qualifications/special skills An advanced university degree (Masters' or PhD) in economics, finance or related fields is required A minimum of ten years of experience in economics and finance is required. Experience in analytical policy research particularly in monetary policy in North Africa is an advantage Experience advising central banks is an advantage Languages English and French are the working languages of the UN Secretariat. For this consultancy, Fluency in French is required. Fluency in the other language is an advantage. Fluency in Arabic is an advantage Additional Information Not available. postings.text: National Consultant for Sustainable Budgeting | UNEP - United Nations Environment Programme Skip to main content National Consultant for Sustainable Budgeting UNEP - United Nations Environment Programme Geneva, Hanoi National CON level Speaks English, Vietnamese Application deadline: November 27, 2026 (11 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is seeking a National Consultant for Sustainable Budgeting to support the implementation of the VN-ADAPT project in Vietnam. The consultant will focus on leveraging public finance for nature-based solutions in agriculture, coordinating with stakeholders, and developing various deliverables related to sustainable budgeting. Key responsibilities include drafting reports, facilitating dialogues, and preparing proposals. The role requires strong project management skills and experience in public finance and environmental policy. Candidate Requirements: Master’s or higher degree in relevant field Minimum two years of project/program management experience Experience with government counterparts, preferably in Viet Nam Experience in multi-stakeholder engagement processes Experience in quality-assuring technical outputs related to public finance Familiarity with UN procedures is desirable Fluency in English and Vietnamese Result of Service The ultimate result of this consultancy is that UNEP’s EFPU delivers on four the sustainable public finance activities committed under Output III: ‘Leveraging private and public innovation and investment in NbSA in agriculture’ of the VN-ADAPT project. Work Location Hanoi, Viet Nam Expected duration 12 Months Part- Time Duties and Responsibilities The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system, and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. The overall objective of UNEP’s Industry and Economy Division is to deliver effective strategic guidance and high-impact action in support of the transition towards inclusive, resource-efficient and environmentally sustainable economies. Its work is guided by ambition, innovation, credible science, and alignment with global climate goals and the specific needs of Member States. Located within the Industry and Economy Division, the Finance and Economics Branch (FEB) examines how economics, finance and public policy interact with the environment and contribute to sustainable development at the local, national, regional and global levels. Within FEB, the Economic and Fiscal Policy Unit (EFPU) conducts analytical research and provides evidence-based policy and capacity-building support to enable the transition towards inclusive and green economies. One area of work for EFPU is implementing part of the IKI-funded Viet Nam Nature-based Solutions for Adaptation in Agriculture through Private Sector Transformation (VN-ADAPT) project. Implemented in partnership with SNV Netherlands Development Organization, which leads the consortium, and the International Center for Environmental Management, the project aims to enhance Viet Nam’s resilience to climate change by scaling up the adoption of nature-based solutions for adaptation (NbSA) in agriculture, particularly in the Mekong Delta and Central Highlands. To this end, UNEP contributes to ‘Output III: Leveraging private and public innovation and investment in NbSA in agriculture’. While UNEP’s Climate Finance Unit contributes to the private sector finance mobilization activities, EFPU implements those related to public finance mobilization, specifically by: •Developing/Testing a Sustainable Budgeting Approach Instrument (SBA Tool) •Creating a toolbox of green public finance instruments for adaptation •Facilitating dialogue between public sector, private sector, and FIs for policy engagement and to scale up finance •Reforming public expenditure & fiscal policies to enhance public investment in NbS/EbA Specific tasks and responsibilities •1st deliverable – by 15 January 2027 – Draft the inception report by conducting stakeholder consultations and a desk review of related national policies to codify the political economy context and UNEP’s potential contributions, complemented by a workplan covering all project activities. Coordinate with related stakeholders to ensure validation of the document. •2nd deliverable – by 15 March 2027 – Draft the concept note on SBA implementation based on a desk review of related green public finance frameworks and consultations with MDAs, which should be mapped to ensure comprehensive coverage. Building on this analysis, propose a preliminary list of national policy priorities to inform the selection of SBA assessment criteria and a proposed data-sharing agreement between the project and relevant MDAs. Coordinate with related stakeholders to ensure validation of the document. •3rd deliverable – by 15 May 2027 – Draft the concept note on the toolbox of green public finance instruments for adaptation by developing the scope of applicable instruments to be included, identifying which instruments have already been supported by existing toolboxes, and proposing entry points. Coordinate with related stakeholders to ensure validation of the document. •4th deliverable – by 15 July 2027 – Preparation and administration of the Call for Proposals (CfP) package. Prepare draft CfP documentation, including the CfP document/form, invitation, annexes of required documentation, assessment tool and Template 11 form, for review and finalization by the Programme Manager. Support the dissemination of the CfP in coordination with UNEP administration; monitor and track submissions; coordinate responses to queries from prospective implementing partners (IPs); verify the completeness of submissions against the CfP requirements; and maintain an organized repository of all submitted documentation. Compile the proposals and prepare an initial assessment summary to support the Programme Manager in the evaluation and selection process. •5th deliverable – by 15 September 2027 – Due diligence support and preparation of the implementation plan and budget. Support the due diligence process for the selected IP through coordination and collection of the required documentation, review of submitted information and preparation of draft due diligence documentation for review by the Programme Manager. In consultation with the selected IP and under the guidance of the Programme Manager, prepare draft implementation plans and corresponding budgets for review and finalization. •6th deliverable – by 15 November 2027 – Draft the final report synthesizing the progress made during phase one of the project and setting out recommendations for phase two of the project, which should include the next steps for national implementation of the SBA, the toolbox and the public-private dialogue as well as related implementation arrangements. Qualifications/special skills •Master’s or higher degree in public policy, development studies, environmental studies, economics, international affairs, sustainable finance, or related field. A first-level university degree with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. •A minimum of two years of project/program management experience in budget analysis, green fiscal policy, and public finance is required. •Experience working with government counterparts, preferably from the Ministry of Finance in Viet Nam, is an advantage. •Experience in coordinating multi-stakeholder engagement processes, preferably in Viet Nam, is an advantage. •Experience in quality-assuring technical outputs related to public finance, fiscal policy, climate adaptation and/or nature-based solutions is an advantage. •Previous experience working with or within the United Nations system, including familiarity with UN administrative procedures and reporting standards, is desirable. Languages English and French are the two working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this post, written and verbal fluency in English and Vietnamese is required. Additional Information Not available. No Fee THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS. postings.title: Development of a National Strategy and Implementation Roadmap for Montenegro's Participation in Euro system TARGET Services
postings.posting_type: Request for Expression of Interest / Consultant Qualification  Selection
postings.text: Central Bank of Montenegro TARGET Instant Payment Settlement Clone – TIPS Clone Project Request for Expressions of Interest Development of a Strategy and Implementation Roadmap for Montenegro’s Participation in TARGET Services Consulting Services: CQS L/C No. P509405-ME Reference No. TIPSC-9858-ME-CS-CQ-26-1.4 November 11, 2026 The Loan Agreement for Montenegro's project ( Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization and its Alignment with SEPA Standards Project (TARGET Instant Payment Settlement Clone Project – TIPS Clone Project )). Project no. P509405 was signed on 30th of July 2025.  The Government of Montenegro aims to modernize payment systems through the improvement of the legal and regulatory framework and the modernization of financial infrastructure.  This Project will assist authorities in supporting the modernization of the payment’s infrastructure. The proposed Project builds directly on the existing engagement and supports authorities with necessary investment activities.   The overall Project have three components: (i)        Providing technical assistance for setting up a new payment system and developing the broader payments ecosystem. (ii)       Supporting the implementation and operation of the new payment system. (iii)      Project Management. The Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) is preparing for future participation in the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and, ultimately, in the Euro system , in line with Montenegro’s broader strategic objective of European Union (EU) accession. This process requires the continued alignment of CBCG’s institutional, operational, legal and technical frameworks with relevant EU standards and practices applicable to central banking and financial market infrastructures. The Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) is the Project Implementing Entity and will have overall responsibility for project implementation and intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for the experienced and qualified Consultancy firm is to ensure the CBCG to development of a clear TARGET Services Accession Strategy and a comprehensive but proportionate implementation roadmap for Montenegro’s participation in relevant TARGET Services . The assessment shall be tailored to Montenegro’s monetary and institutional circumstances and to the practical needs of the CBCG and banking community. The Consultant shall focus on analysis and recommendations at a level sufficient to support strategic decisions and define subsequent implementation work. Detailed system specifications, extensive institution-by-institution audits, drafting of complete legislative instruments, vendor selection, live testing and migration execution are outside the scope unless separately agreed. The Consultant (firm/company) shall perform the required activities in cooperation with CBCG and relevant stakeholders. The ten areas correspond to the required substantive outputs described in ToR.  Findings may be consolidated into coordinated reports rather than duplicated across separate studies. The level of analysis shall be sufficient to identify decisions, implementation prerequisites and indicative costs; detailed implementation design remains a subsequent project stage. The (CBCG) through the Technical Service Unit (TSU) now invites eligible Consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consult-firm (Legal entity) should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services in subject. The Consultant will work closely with relevant stakeholders ensuring compliance with Montenegro’s relevant policies, EU regulations, and international best practices. According to the present timeline it is anticipated that the Consultant should complete their work by the end of the July, 2027.   The Consultancy firm is expected to provide services until defined project activities and deliverables are finalized and formally accepted by the CBCG. The required qualification criteria are:            1. General Qualification and Competences of the consultant (firm) Capacity, competences and organizational structure, of the Consultant firm (Company) The   Consulting firm must be a legal entity :  -------------------------------(Max 20 points on this criteria).           2. Qualification of the consultant (firm) relevant to the assignment : The Consultant should demonstrate proven experience in European payment and settlement infrastructures, preferably including TARGET Services, as well as capacity across legal and regulatory frameworks, payment operations, technical connectivity and financial feasibility analysis. An appropriately multidisciplinary team is expected (Generally available).  Team structure should be proportionate to the assignment, and the same expert may cover more than one area/position where suitably qualified. Relevant experience in central bank and bank migration planning, settlement finality, ISO 20022 and cross-border payment arrangements will be considered particularly valuable. The Consultant should demonstrate the ability to prepare decision-oriented work products and facilitate stakeholder cooperation. --------------------------------------------------------_ (Max 80 points on this criteria). * It is expected that the interested Consultant’s company within the submitted ‘’EoI’’ shall prepare and present a table listing (reference list) which will provide the following information: Contracting authority/client data and contact information to whom the consultancy service was performed, (contract-project detailed description, contract value for performed services and contract implementation period). (name, e-mail, phone numbers for verification purposes). CBCG may decide to verify information provided with the referenced clients. The relevance, similarity and complexity of assignments will be given more weight than their number. *CVs or biodata for Key Expert’s- (staff) are not required and will not be evaluated (at this stage ). The Consultant firm may also submit other documents and which are not listed above in order to justify general qualifications and qualifications relevant to the assignment it considers relevant, such us indicative list of the Key staff or non-key staff that is generally available for this kind of work. Consultants may associate to enhance their qualifications. The associations should clearly indicate the form of the association (Joint-venture, Consortium, sub-consultancy; member in charge; other member/s and or sub- consultants). Joint ventures should submit letter/confirmation, indicating their intent to form a joint venture if awarded the contract and shall provide the above-mentioned information for each member of the joint venture. *Consultant may only submit one expression of interest. If a consultant submits or participates in more than one Expression of Interest, such expression will be disqualified. However, sub-consultants, including individual experts, may participate in more than one expression of interest only in the capacity of sub-consultants.  Qualifications and experience of the sub-consultants will not be considered for evaluation purposes. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment which outlines comprehensively the tasks, duties, deliverables and responsibilities of the Consultant firm can be obtained upon request at the e-mail address given below. A Consultant firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Based Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Sixt Edition; February, 2025.  The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, ‘’3.13 - 3.17’’ setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Interested consultants may obtain further information at the email address below. Expressions of interest must be delivered, only by e-mail to the address below and in subject must clearly indicate project name, subject number : ‘’ Development of a Strategy and Implementation Roadmap for Montenegro’s Participation in TARGET Services’’ Ref.No: TIPSC-9858-ME-CS-CQ-26-1.4 The deadline for submission is November 26, 2026. 10:00h Ministry of Finance /Technical Service Unit Attention: Mr. Zoran Mijovi, Senior Procurement officer Address: Studentska 2 A Floor I                                                                                                                                       City:81000Podgorica Country: Montenegro E-mail: zoran.mijovic@mif.gov.me

postings.title: Consultancy Services to Prepare Site Studies (Geotechnical Investigation Part 1) for Wind Farm Installation In Botswana.
postings.posting_type: Request for Expression of Interest / Consultant Qualification  Selection
postings.text: MINISTRY OF MINERALS AND ENERGY   PROJECTS AND ENERGY DEVELOPMENT UNIT (PEDU)   Invitation for Expression of Interest   Consulting Services- Firms Selection   Geotechnical Studies for a Wind Farm in Botswana   Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Geotechnical Studies for a Wind Farm Site Reference: EOI/MME-PEDU/002/26-27   BACKGROUND   Botswana plans to harness its renewable energy (RE) resources and accelerate renewable energy development through the implementation of the Integrated Resource Plan (IRP). The Government of Botswana is currently developing renewable energy projects at several pre-selected sites. The Project and Energy Development Unit (PEDU) under the Ministry of Minerals and Energy (the Client) is responsible for the development of these projects. A feasibility consultant has identified a proposed site for a wind farm based on a multi-criteria assessment considering preliminary wind resource data, transmission infrastructure, land use and ownership, and preliminary environmental and social considerations.   The geotechnical studies will support the development of a proposed 100 MW wind farm located north of Letlhakane, Botswana. The final coordinates and boundaries of the area to be investigated will be confirmed by the Client prior to commencement of the assignment.   SCOPE OF WORK   The Client is seeking a qualified and experienced consulting firm to undertake geotechnical investigations to support the pre-development of the proposed 100 MW wind farm.   The assignment will include preliminary site-wide geotechnical investigations and, subsequently, location-specific investigations based on the preliminary wind farm layout.   The detailed scope, investigation areas, technical requirements and deliverables will be set out in the Terms of Reference provided at the next stage of the selection process.   QUALIFICATIONS   PEDU invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are: Core Business: Minimum of ten (10) years of experience undertaking geotechnical investigations and related studies. Demonstrated experience in satisfactorily completing geotechnical investigations for utility-scale energy or comparable infrastructure projects. Demonstrated experience in undertaking geotechnical investigations for at least minimum two (2) utility scale projects in Sub- Saharan Africa. The Consultant to demonstrate  experience in undertaking comparable assignments in accordance with applicable technical, environmental and occupational health and safety standards The Consultant shall demonstrate experience working on assignments financed by International Financial Institutions (IFIs), and its eligibility including but not limited to meeting the debarment and sanctions standard, financial and commercial capability and fiduciary and system compliance. The Consultant shall have no conflict of interest and pass integrity check.  The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Paragraphs 3.14 to 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for Borrowers, dated July 2016, revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2023, setting forth the World Bank's Policy on Conflict of Interest.   CONSULTANT QUALIFICATIONS EVALUATION CRITERIA   Overall years of consulting experience (20 points) Number of similar assignments (70 points) Availability of key experts to carry the assignment (10 points)   Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications. Where Consultants propose to associate, the submission shall include evidence of the proposed association from all participating firms.   A Bidders workshop will be held virtually to discuss the assignment overview on 21 October 2026. Details will be announced via MME and World Bank platforms.    A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the CS-CQS method set out in the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated July 2016, revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2023. Interested Consultants may obtain further information in writing at the address below during office hours, that is, 0730 hours to 16:30 hours.   In case of clarifications, do not hesitate to contact Mr Franz Mafoko at frmafoko@gov.bw; Cell No.: +267 72794446.   Expressions of Interest clearly labelled "Expression of Interest - Consultancy Services for Geotechnical Studies for a Wind Farm in Botswana ," must be hand-delivered or emailed at the address below by 11 November 2026 at 12:00 hours (CAT). Electronic submissions should be password protected.   Attention:        The Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Minerals and Energy Block D, Third Floor, Office No DT 10, Plot No. 50676 Fairgrounds Office Park, Gaborone Republic of Botswana. Telephone Nos: (+267) 3656600/6628 Mobile Nos: +267 72794446 Electronic mail address: [frmafoko@gov.bw]

postings.text: REPUBLIQUE DU BURUNDI                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     MINISTERE DES INFRASTRUCTURES, DES LOGEMENTS SOCIAUX, DES TRANSPORTS ET DE L’EQUIPEMENT                                                                    PROJET D’URGENCE SUR LA RESILIENCE URBAINE                                                                                                    APPEL A MANIFESTATIONS D’INTÉRÊT : Consultant Individuel   Pays République du Burundi   Nom du Projet Projet d’Urgence sur la Résilience Urbaine « PRU »   Numéro de Don          IDA-E3520-BI N° du projet   P177146   Intitulé de la Mission  Le recrutement LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN(E) SPECIALISTE EN suivi evaluation   N° de référence (selon le Plan de Passation de Marchés dans STEP) : BI-MIELS- PIU-575330-CS-INDV Le Gouvernement du Burundi a reçu un don de la Banque Mondiale pour renforcer la résilience aux inondations et améliorer la gestion urbaine résiliente au climat à Bujumbura. Le Projet d’Urgence sur la Résilience Urbaine au Burundi (PRU P177146) qui assure la mise en œuvre de ce financement voudrait recruter D’UN(E) SPECIALISTE EN suivi evaluation   Le (la) spécialiste en suivi évaluation du Projet devra avoir le profil suivant : Avoir un diplôme universitaire de niveau Master (bac+5) en statistique, économie, planification, sciences sociales, ingénierie, gestion de projets ou domaine apparenté ; Justifier d’une expérience professionnelle d’au moins 8 ans, dont au moins 5 ans en suivi-évaluation de projets ou programmes de développement ; Avoir au moins 3 ans d’expérience en suivi-évaluation de projets financés par la Banque mondiale ou d’autres partenaires techniques et financiers ; Une expérience en suivi-évaluation de projets d’infrastructures, de développement urbain ou de gestion des risques de catastrophes est un atout ; Avoir un esprit d’initiative et une rigueur dans le traitement des dossiers ; Avoir une excellente qualité de communications interpersonnelles et humaines ; Avoir une excellente connaissance du français et une bonne connaissance de l’anglais ; Avoir une capacité de travailler sous pression et dans une équipe pluridisciplinaire ; Avoir une excellente capacité de rédaction et esprit de synthèse ; Avoir une expérience dans la numérisation de formulaires, la collecte de données et les analyses avec un logiciel adapté ou application similaire ; Solide connaissance informatique des logiciels en suivi-évaluation et analyses statistiques (MS-PROJECT, SPSS, Kobo Collect, etc…) et des logiciels de bureautique usuelle (Word, Access, Excel, Power Point, etc., internet et autres outils de communication) ; La maîtrise d’un logiciel de système d’information géographique (QGIS, ArcGIS) et la connaissance du kirundi sont des atouts ; Aptitude à effectuer régulièrement des missions de terrain. Capacité à initier, gérer et accomplir des tâches variées dans un environnement dynamique ; CONSTITUTION DU DOSSIER Les candidats intéressés devront fournir un dossier composé de : Une lettre de motivation adressée au Coordonnateur du Projet PRT&PRU ; Un curriculum vitae ; Les noms et coordonnées d’au moins trois (3) références professionnelles ; Des copies certifiées conformes à l’original des diplômes, certificats et tout autre document attestant l’expérience professionnelle pourraient être demandés. En cas de nécessité, d'autre document attestant l'expérience professionnelle pourrait être demandés Des informations complémentaires ainsi que les TdRs sont disponibles à l'adresse indiquée, pendant les heures de bureau : du lundi au jeudi de 8h à 12h et de 13h à 17h, et le vendredi de 8h à 12h (heures locales de Bujumbura, GMT+2). Les manifestations d'intérêt, rédigées en français, doivent être soumises par écrit à cette même adresse (en personne, par courrier ou par e-mail) au plus tard le 02  décembre  2026 à 16h (heure de Bujumbura, GMT+2) avec mention :«   D’UN(E) SPECIALISTE EN suivi evaluation  Adresse : Quartier ZEIMET, Avenue MUMIRWA n°101 A l’attention de : Régis MPAWENAYO, Coordonnateur de l’UGP-PRT&PRU Téléphone fixe : + 257 22 21 18 11 Adresse électronique : info@prt.bi avec copie à rmpawenayo@prt.bi , mpawenayoregis@yahoo.fr et tbahori@pru.bi               Pour publication                      Le Coordonnateur de l’UGP-PRT&PRU                                Dr. Ir. Régis MPAWENAYO

postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS)   Country: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia Project : Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase Two (LLRP-II) Credit no/grand no:  7519-ET. Assignment Title : Consultancy Services for Design Review and Construction Supervision of Awadi Geberoch Climate-Resilient Diversion Irrigation and Drainage Scheme in Argoba Woreda Procurement Reference No .: ET-AFR-RPCU-569666-CS-QCBS   The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase II (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.   The consulting services (“the Services”) include : ensure that the proposed irrigation and drainage infrastructure is properly designed, constructed, and completed in accordance with the approved engineering designs, technical specifications, contractual requirements, applicable standards, and environmental and social safeguards.   The service comprises :Review the completed detailed engineering design, verify construction readiness, supervise construction and administer the works contract, and provide completion, commissioning, handover and Defects Liability Period services. Protect the Client’s technical, financial, environmental and social interests while administering the works contract impartially and in accordance with its terms. To ensure the development of a reliable, efficient, and climate-resilient irrigation and drainage system at Awadi Geberoch Climate-Resilient Diversion Irrigation and Drainage Scheme in Argoba Woreda.   The implementation period is 10 (ten ) calendar months from the date of commencement. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.   The Afar National Regional State, Office of the President, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.   The shortlisting criteria are: a) Core business and years in business: The Expression of Interest should focus on the firm’s corporate capability and comparable assignments, and should include, as applicable: A brief profile of the firm, including its legal status, year of establishment, ownership, organizational structure, core business areas and relevant technical capacity. Evidence of experience in irrigation and drainage infrastructure design review, construction supervision and/or contract administration, particularly diversion headworks, canals, hydraulic structures and on-farm irrigation development. Details of comparable assignments completed and/or ongoing, including the assignment name and country/location, client, contract value (where disclosable), scope and relevance, commencement/completion dates, and the firm’s role. Experience on projects financed by the World Bank, IFAD or other development partners, where applicable. Evidence of capacity to manage multidisciplinary engineering and ESHS supervision services, including environmental and social safeguards, occupational and community health and safety, land access/resettlement follow-up and stakeholder engagement. Information on the firm’s availability and capacity to mobilize and maintain a resident supervision team in the project area. For a joint venture or association, details of each member, the proposed form of association, the lead member and the respective roles and responsibilities. Relevant experience of each member should be clearly identified. B) General experience: The Consulting Firm has extensive general experience in providing multidisciplinary engineering consultancy services, including feasibility studies, detailed engineering design, construction supervision, contract administration, and project management of irrigation, drainage, water resources development, and other related civil infrastructure projects. C)    Specific experience: The Firm possesses relevant experience in the supervision and management of irrigation infrastructure development projects, including diversion weirs, river intake structures, irrigation canals, hydraulic structures, drainage networks, flood protection works, and associated civil engineering facilities. The Firm has experience in ensuring construction quality assurance and quality control, monitoring contractors' performance, supervising construction methodologies, reviewing and approving technical submissions, verifying work measurements, preparing progress reports, and ensuring compliance with approved engineering designs, technical specifications, contractual requirements, and applicable environmental and social safeguards. D) Technical and managerial capability of the firm:  organizational capacity and has experience in ensuring construction quality assurance and quality control, monitoring contractors' performance, supervising construction methodologies, reviewing and approving technical submissions, verifying work measurements, preparing progress reports, and ensuring compliance with approved engineering designs, technical specifications, contractual requirements, and applicable environmental and social safeguards. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.   The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.   Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.   A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 7:00 A.M. to 6:00 P.M. ( EAT), on working days.    Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, in hard copy) by  30 November  2026 at 9:00 A.M. East Africa Time (EAT). The address referred above is:                                                         Afar National Regional State, Office of the President,                                                       Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II),                                                      Afar Regional Project Coordination Unit (RPCU)                                                     Attn: Procurement Officer , Tadesse Gebeyehu , Room No. 7                                                      Tel: +251 33 666 0188, /  +251-912- 68- 90- 22/ +251- 933-80-62-                                                      E-mail: afarllrp@gmail.com; llrpafar@gmail.com;                                                                         Semera, Afar, Ethiopia

postings.title: Consultoría de Enlace Sectorial en Cambio Climático y Desplazamiento Interno IOM - International Organization for Migration Lima UG - Ungraded
postings.text: Consultoría de Enlace Sectorial en Cambio Climático y Desplazamiento Interno | IOM - International Organization for Migration Skip to main content Consultoría de Enlace Sectorial en Cambio Climático y Desplazamiento Interno IOM - International Organization for Migration Lima Both national and international UG - Ungraded level Speaks Spanish Application deadline: November 30, 2026 (14 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is seeking a Sectoral Link Consultant to facilitate technical coordination between various governmental entities in Peru regarding internal displacement and climate change. The consultant will be responsible for developing work plans, mapping strategic actors, and providing technical assistance to ensure effective project implementation. This role involves organizing workshops, monitoring progress, and creating normative frameworks to address internal displacement issues. The position is based in Lima, Peru, and requires a commitment of 270 days. Candidate Requirements: University degree in relevant fields Master's degree in Climate Change or related areas Specialization courses in climate change or public policy Knowledge of Peruvian legal frameworks on displacement and climate change Experience in technical document preparation Advanced skills in Office and project management tools Fluency in Spanish Job Description Tipo de consultoría : Consultoría Tipo B Lugar de destino de la consultoría : Lima, Perú WBL (Presupuesto):  NC0249 Nombre de la consultoría:  Consultor de enlace sectorial del Ministerio del Ambiente y Ministerio de la Mujer y Poblaciones Vulnerables para dar acompañamiento técnico, articulación y seguimiento de los resultados, productos y actividades del proyecto. Duración de la consultoría: 270 días calendario Introducción: Fundada en 1951, la OIM es un Organismo Asociado de las Naciones Unidas y la principal agencia de la ONU en el ámbito de la migración. Trabajando en estrecha colaboración con socios gubernamentales, intergubernamentales y no gubernamentales, la OIM promueve una migración humana y ordenada en beneficio de todas las personas. La Organización salva vidas y protege a las personas en movimiento, impulsa soluciones para el desplazamiento y facilita vías para la migración regular, al tiempo que brinda servicios y asesoramiento a gobiernos y migrantes. La OIM está comprometida con el fomento de un entorno laboral respetuoso, inclusivo y de apoyo, donde todas las personas empleadas puedan desarrollarse profesionalmente y sentirse valoradas. Mediante la creación de este entorno, la OIM busca aprovechar mejor todo el potencial de la migración y fortalecer su apoyo a las personas en movimiento. La OIM invita a postularse a personas candidatas de diversos orígenes y ofrece ajustes razonables durante todo el proceso de contratación cuando sea necesario. Obtenga más información sobre la cultura laboral de la OIM en: IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Naturaleza de la consultoría : Consultoría tipo B para el contratar a un profesional de a denominarse Consultor de Enlace Sectorial que se encargara de facilitar la articulación y coordinación técnica e interinstitucional entre la OIM, el MINAM, el MIMP y demás actores involucrados, promoviendo el seguimiento de acuerdos, compromisos, la implementación oportuna y efectiva de actividades, productos y resultados del proyecto. El servicio busca el posicionamiento articulador de la OIM en el proyecto, reforzando las competencias de los sectores o ministerios involucrados para una implementación efectiva y oportuna, y sostenibilidad del proyecto, así como la constitución, acompañamiento y asistencia técnica al Grupo de Trabajo Sectorial conformado Ad Hoc en el marco del proyecto. Contexto y alcance del proyecto:   El Perú ha registrado un incremento del desplazamiento interno asociado a desastres y a los efectos del cambio climático. Según el Observatorio de Desplazamientos Internos (IDMC, por sus siglas en inglés), [1] en el Perú, entre 2008 y 2024, unos 890,208 nuevos desplazamientos internos se registraron por peligros asociados al clima, principalmente lluvias intensas, inundaciones y deslizamientos. A ello, se suman procesos de evolución lenta como sequías prolongadas, degradación de suelos, retroceso glaciar y estrés hídrico que erosionan progresivamente los medios de vida y pueden influenciar procesos de movilidad humana, especialmente en zonas rurales. Asimismo, el Instituto Nacional de Defensa Civil (INDECI), señala que los peligros hidrometeorológicos han afectado a más de 9.3 millones de personas en el Perú durante la última década, siendo las lluvias intensas, inundaciones, deslizamientos y el Fenómeno El Niño (FEN) los más recurrentes. [2] Frente a esta problemática, el Gobierno Peruano cuenta con un marco normativo nacional robusto en materia de cambio climático, como la Ley N.° 30754, Ley Marco sobre Cambio Climático, su reglamento aprobado por Decreto Supremo N.° 013-2019-MINAM y la política climática Estrategia Nacional ante el Cambio Climático (ENCC) al 2050 aprobado por Decreto Supremo N.° 012-2024-MINAM, así como el Plan Nacional de Adaptación aprobado mediante Resolución Ministerial N° 096-2021-MINAM. A nivel global, existe un compromiso climático ante la Convención Marco de las Naciones Unidas sobre el Cambio Climático (CMNUCC) a través de las Contribuciones Determinadas a Nivel Nacional, destacando que el 2025 ha adicionado el área de "desplazamiento interno por efectos del cambio climático". El Perú ya cuenta con el área temática de desplazamiento interno en la NDC, y como tal requiere asumir retos y desafíos para fortalecer dicha área, tales como, definir lineamientos técnicos para robustecer y definir el marco normativo y conceptual, generar y fortalecer los conocimientos y capacidades de los actores directos e indirectos, formulación de la Programación Sectorial, definido como un documento técnico y participativo que contiene información de las medidas de adaptación de las áreas temáticas que conforman la NDC, y que debe ser elaborado en base a la "Guía para la formulación y actualización de medidas de adaptación y mitigación que conforman las NDC" aprobado por Resolución Ministerial N.° 00052-2025-MINAM, y en base a un esfuerzo conjunto con los sectores competentes.  En ese sentido, se requiere contratar a un(a) consultor(a) de Enlace Sectorial para facilitar la articulación y coordinación técnica e interinstitucional entre la OIM, el MINAM, el MIMP y demás actores involucrados, promoviendo el seguimiento de acuerdos, compromisos, la implementación oportuna y efectiva de actividades, productos y resultados del proyecto.  Responsibilities Departamento / Unidad Organizacional al que el Consultor está contribuyendo: Unidad de Emergencias y Asistencia Humanitaria de la Oficina País de la OIM Perú, para el proyecto “Apoyando al Gobierno del Perú en la implementación del componente de desplazamiento interno de la Estrategia Nacional ante el Cambio Climático al 2050 y de la Contribución Determinada a Nivel Nacional (NDC)” financiado por el Fondo de la OIM para el Desarrollo (IDF). Actividades del Consultor de Enlace Sectorial A. Planificación y articulación interinstitucional Elaborar el Plan de Trabajo de la consultoría, que contemple, como mínimo, los antecedentes y contexto del proyecto; objetivos generales y específicos; alcance de la consultoría; metodología de intervención; actividades, subactividades y tareas asociadas a cada producto; productos y entregables; mecanismos y niveles de articulación y coordinación con los sectores y actores estratégicos; cronograma detallado de actividades; y mecanismos de seguimiento, monitoreo y reporte. El plan deberá incluir, como anexos, las herramientas e instrumentos de gestión y seguimiento que serán utilizados durante la consultoría. Elaborar y mantener actualizado un mapa de actores estratégicos y sus niveles de relacionamiento, identificando las instituciones públicas, organismos de cooperación internacional, organizaciones de la sociedad civil, academia y otros actores vinculados con el desplazamiento interno, cambio climático, gestión del riesgo de desastres y protección de poblaciones en situación de vulnerabilidad, incorporando una evaluación de actores estratégicos según poder e interés en un dashboard que identifique su procedencia y tipo de actor.  El mapeo deberá identificar competencias, roles, responsabilidades, niveles de influencia, mecanismos de coordinación y oportunidades de articulación para la implementación del proyecto. Facilitar y fortalecer la articulación técnica e interinstitucional entre la OIM, el MINAM, el MIMP y otras entidades competentes, promoviendo mecanismos de coordinación, intercambio de información, seguimiento de compromisos y generación de acuerdos que contribuyan al cumplimiento oportuno de las actividades, productos y resultados previstos en el proyecto. B. Conformación y funcionamiento del Grupo de Trabajo Técnico Sectorial Brindar asistencia técnica y acompañamiento para la conformación y puesta en funcionamiento del “Grupo de Trabajo Técnico Sectorial de Desplazamiento Interno por Efectos del Cambio Climático”, integrado por representantes y especialistas de las direcciones y unidades orgánicas competentes del MIMP, en coordinación con la OIM y las instancias sectoriales correspondientes, contribuyendo a establecer sus objetivos, composición, funciones y mecanismos de funcionamiento. Brindar asistencia técnica para la elaboración, revisión y puesta en marcha del Plan de Trabajo y los Términos de Referencia del Grupo de Trabajo Técnico Sectorial, asegurando la definición de objetivos, funciones, responsabilidades, actividades, productos, cronograma y mecanismos de coordinación y seguimiento, en concordancia con las competencias institucionales del MIMP y los resultados del proyecto. Organizar, facilitar y brindar acompañamiento técnico a las sesiones y reuniones del Grupo de Trabajo Técnico Sectorial, incluyendo la preparación de agendas, identificación de temas prioritarios, sistematización de aportes, elaboración de ayudas memoria, definición de tareas y responsabilidades, así como el seguimiento de acuerdos y compromisos asumidos por sus integrantes. Desarrollar actividades presenciales de coordinación y asistencia técnica en el MINAM y el MIMP, de acuerdo con un cronograma previamente coordinado y validado por la OIM, con la finalidad de facilitar el intercambio de información, brindar acompañamiento técnico a los funcionarios y especialistas, realizar seguimiento a compromisos institucionales y fortalecer la articulación necesaria para la implementación de los productos del proyecto. C. Asistencia técnica para la elaboración de instrumentos conceptuales y normativos Elaborar el Documento Técnico de Marco Conceptual y Normativo sobre Desplazamiento Interno por Efectos del Cambio Climático, en coordinación con el Grupo de Trabajo Técnico Sectorial y especialistas de las entidades competentes. El documento deberá contribuir a la armonización de conceptos, definiciones y terminología aplicable al contexto peruano, así como al análisis de los instrumentos normativos, políticos e institucionales existentes, la identificación de brechas y la formulación de recomendaciones técnicas para fortalecer el abordaje del desplazamiento interno asociado al cambio climático. Este marco conceptual y normativo debe incorporar los enfoques de igualdad de oportunidades entre mujeres y hombres, interculturalidad, el enfoque intergeneracional y los impactos diferenciados que el proyecto identifica. El documento debe incluir el glosario, clasificación de tipologías y propuesta de mejora normativa. Asimismo, incluir una definición de operativa para las variables correspondientes que permita luego generar información cuantitativa sobre desplazados internos por desastres y cambio climático. También es necesario mencionar explíci

postings.text: Republic of Zambia MINISTRY OF TOURISM GREEN, RESILIENT AND TRANSFORMATIONAL TOURISM DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (GREAT-TDP) CALL FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST SELECTION OF A GRANT MANAGEMENT FIRM TO IMPLEMENT THE MATCHING GRANTS AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM UNDER GREAT-TDP (SUBCOMPONENT 1.3) PROJECT ID: P180337, IDA CREDIT NO. 73380-ZM ZM-MOT-580359-CS-QCBS INDICATIVE ASSIGNMENT DURATION March 2027 – June 2030, Subject to Contract Effectiveness, Financing Availability and The Project Closing Date. Background The Government of the Republic of Zambia has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Green, Resilient and Transformational Tourism Development Project (GREAT-TDP), which is being implemented by the Ministry of Tourism (MoT) through a Project Implementation Unit (PIU). The Project seeks to enhance the sustainability, resilience, and competitiveness of Zambia's tourism sector while promoting inclusive economic opportunities and conservation outcomes in tourism destinations. The GREAT-TDP comprises three components: Component 1:      Strengthening Tourism Competitiveness and Destination Management; Component 2:        Improving Access to Resilient Infrastructure; and Component 3:      Project Administration and Management. Under Component 1, Subcomponent 1.3, Expanding Economic Opportunities through MSMEs and Community-Based Tourism Support, the Project provides financial and technical support to tourism-related Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), Community-Based Enterprises (CBEs), Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), and Tourism Private Sector Associations (TPSAs) through a Matching Grants and Technical Assistance Program. The Program is designed to strengthen business capacity, improve competitiveness, support sustainable tourism development, and expand economic opportunities for participating beneficiaries. Consulting Services The Ministry of Tourism intends to apply part of the proceeds of the financing for consulting services ("the Services"), which include the engagement of a Grant Management Company (GMC) to support the implementation and administration of the Matching Grants and Technical Assistance Program under Component 1 of the GREAT-TDP. The GMC will be responsible for the overall management and administration of the Program, including outreach and communications, beneficiary engagement, application intake and evaluation, grant administration, coordination and delivery of technical assistance activities, monitoring and verification of results, operation of the Management Information System (MIS), reporting, and other related functions as described in the Terms of Reference (TOR). The GMC will support the Ministry of Tourism in ensuring that the Program is implemented efficiently, transparently, and in accordance with the Project's objectives, procedures, and applicable requirements The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at https://greattdp.gov.zm/tenders  or https://www.mot.gov.zm/?page_id=3201  or by writing at the email address given below;     The project coordinator: Green, Resilient and Transformational Tourism Development Project Ministry of Tourism Kwacha House Annex Cairo Road Lusaka Zambia Email: procurementgreattdp@mot.gov.zm Copying:  greattdpprojectcoordinator@mot.gov.zm    The Ministry of Tourism (MoT) now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Service as required in the TOR. The submission should include a cover letter summarizing the relevant experience and indicating its relevance to the assignment at hand. The short-listing criteria are as follows: Comparable program experience. At least 10 years of relevant organizational experience managing grant, matching-grant, or enterprise-support programs. During the 10 years preceding the EOI submission deadline, the firm must have managed at least 2 programs comparable to this assignment in scope, operational complexity, funding value, and number and type of beneficiaries. Technical assistance delivery. Practical experience designing and delivering TA to MSMEs for business development or investment implementation, directly or through specialists managed by the firm. Tourism-sector experience is an advantage. Organizational and managerial capacity. Experience mobilizing multidisciplinary teams and managing geographically dispersed operations. An existing office in Zambia is not required at EOI stage, but the firm must demonstrate capacity to mobilize an effective in-country operation. Systems and controls. Capability to operate grant management informational system (MIS) and maintain audit trails, fiduciary and integrity controls, and environmental and social screening and monitoring procedures. Donor financed and regional experience. Experience in World Bank or other development partner financed programs in the context of developing economies, especially in southern Africa. Conflict of interest. The attention of interested consultancy is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s ‘Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers’ July 2016 revised 7th Edition 2025 [Procurement in investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services], setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Joint venture or sub consultancy Consultants may associate with other consultants in the form of a joint venture or a sub consultancy to enhance their qualifications. The nature of association, whether it is a joint venture or a sub consultancy, should clearly be stated. In case of joint venture, the Consultant leading the joint venture should be mentioned. Selection Method A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) set out in the Consultant Guidelines. Interested Consultant may obtain further information at the email address below: REoI Submission Expressions of interest (EOI) should be delivered in a written (English) form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by 27 November 2026 at 17:00 hours (Zambian time) marked clearly as – “ Expression of Interest for Grant Management Company (GMC) to support the implementation of the Matching Grants and Technical Assistance Program under Component 1 of the GREAT-TDP ” The project coordinator: Green, Resilient and Transformational Tourism Development Project Ministry of Tourism Kwacha House Annex Cairo Road Lusaka Zambia Email: procurementgreattdp@mot.gov.zm Copying:  greattdpprojectcoordinator@mot.gov.zm

Ce programme vise à l’actualisation du Plan directeur de développement de la production, du transport et de la distribution d’électricité du Gabon. La mise en œuvre opérationnelle est assurée par le Ministère de l’Accès Universel à l’Eau et à l’Énergie (MAUEE), en coordination avec les entités techniques concernées, sous la supervision de la CNTIPPEE. Les services de consultant (« les Services ») comprennent le « RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET DE CONSULTANTS POUR LA RÉALISATION DE L’ÉVALUATION ENVIRONNEMENTALE ET SOCIALE STRATÉGIQUE (EESS) DU PLAN DIRECTEUR DE DÉVELOPPEMENT DU SYSTÈME ÉLECTRIQUE DU GABON ».
